  - the kind prefix in every stored event, source and dedupe key, kept byte-for-byte
  - the room-only rule that 'protect' goals rank failed runs too
  - each kind's own leaderboard comparator.
  
  Use runEarnsProgression in the merged function. Add tests that compare the dedupe keys for both kinds before merging. This saves about 300 lines.

### F283: Five separate copies of 'which version of this room is current' have already drifted apart

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The streaming code has to choose which version of a room to use: a local draft, a course's pinned version, someone's live building preview, a just-published copy, or the downloaded one. It makes that choice in five places, each with its own order. Two of them already disagree. The one used for movement assists, room music, the HUD and pit deaths prefers a builder's live preview even after the room is published. The one used to build the room you actually collide with does not. Make one function the single source of truth.

**Technical detail.**

The precedence chains:
- getRoomSnapshotViewForCoordinates (worldStreaming.ts:1225-1251): transient > draft > presence preview > optimistic published > loaded > preview cache. The presence preview is used regardless of summary state.
- getPlayableRoomSnapshotViewForCoordinates (1264-1295): transient > draft > optimistic > presence only if the summary is not published > loaded > current cached full.
- resolveTransitionRenderableRoom (2456-2528): the playable order plus a portal special case.
- refreshVisibleRoomsFromCache inline (2137-2209) and previewCache.collectRenderableRooms (previewCache.ts:399-470): candidate-based, the same rules twice, one sync and one async.
- computeLocalPlayPressure's getRoomSnapshot (worldStreaming.ts:3232-3251): a sixth, shorter variant.

The divergent view accessor feeds:
- movement assists (composition/player.ts:484)
- the HUD (composition/ui.ts:203)
- deadly-pit checks in room transitions (composition/world.ts:656)
- room music

Collision comes from the playable chain. During the window when a room's summary says published but a construction preview or optimistic copy is still held, these readers can see different terrain, music and pit settings than the tilemap the player collides with.

Fix: one pure resolver in worldStreamingModel.ts:

resolveRoomSource(roomId, {transient, draft, presence, optimistic, loaded, cache, summary}, purpose: 'view' | 'playable' | 'preview')

Use it from all six sites, with table-driven tests per purpose. This removes about 150 lines.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1225-1251 — view accessor returns presence preview before optimistic and without a published check
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1264-1295 — playable accessor: optimistic first, presence only when summary not published
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:2456-2528 — transition resolver repeats the playable chain
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:2137-2209 — inline renderable resolution in refreshVisibleRoomsFromCache
- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:399-470 — async copy of the same candidate rules
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3232-3251 — local play pressure has its own lookup order
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/world.ts:656 — room transition (deadly bottom edge) reads the view accessor

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real, but narrower than claimed.
  - **When it happens:** a presence preview only exists for never-published rooms (editor/presence.ts:261-263, server check presenceServer.ts:630-640). So the view and playable accessors only disagree in a short first-publish window, until the editor's clear arrives. That window can stretch to 120 s if the builder disconnects before clearing, because previews persist on the server.
  - **What differs:** in that window the preview content almost always matches what was just published (at most 1.2 s stale). The real difference is status 'draft', a null publishedAt and a draft version. The visible effects are a goal run started on transition that is not leaderboard-eligible (goalRuns.ts:209) and a draft version in the HUD. Terrain, music and pit mismatches are only theoretical.
  - **The divergent orders:** the view accessor (1225-1251) ignores the published check and ranks presence above optimistic. The candidate builder (worldStreamingPolicy.ts:65-95) also ranks presence above optimistic. The playable and transition paths rank optimistic first and gate presence on not-published. The render path prefers the cached published room when the summary is published.
  - **Recommended fix:** a small one. Make the view accessor match the playable order (optimistic before presence, skip presence when the summary is 'published') and update worldStreaming.snapshotView.test.ts.
  - **Optional cleanup:** share one pure resolver across the three sync accessors (view, playable, transition). The async render path (previewCache.collectRenderableRooms) fetches and skips the currency check, and the local-play-pressure lookup only feeds metrics, so neither belongs in the same resolver without parameters. The likely line saving is about 60-100, not 150.

### F269: Expanded Room and Wamp-O-Gram previews use a separate 838-line 'colored blocks' renderer; fold it into the real-art one

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F132

**Summary.** The best levels (Expanded Rooms) and Wamp-O-Gram postcards get their link-preview picture from an older server drawing that uses no real game art. Tiles are colored squares, objects are simple shapes, homemade sprites and objects on the back layer disappear, uploaded backgrounds become a grey checkerboard, and three of the eleven background themes turn forest green. Single rooms already get a real-art picture from a newer drawing module. The API server can load the same art files, so the old file (838 lines, roughly 380 of them copies) can be deleted.

**Technical detail.**

src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts (April 2026, before real-art rendering existed) is still used for:
- every Expanded Room card (share/routes.ts:202-204; the Pages side uses the API image only when cellCount > 1, shareMetadata.ts:406-426)
- every Wamp-O-Gram og:image (wampOGram/routes.ts:101; shareMetadata.ts:248)

What it gets wrong compared with the game:
- **Backgrounds.** Group backgrounds are flat 3-band palettes for 8 hardcoded ids (70-79). jungle_vines, spooky_moon and spooky_mountain fall back to forest (235). Custom photo backgrounds become a checkerboard (243-247).
- **Tiles.** No art at all: colors come from tileset.uiTheme (260-322, 524-537).
- **Objects.** Background-layer objects are skipped (365-367). Custom sprites are dropped, because getObjectById('custom_sprite:…') is undefined (369-372). The NPC Jimothy (category 'npc') becomes a green ellipse via the default branch (403-406, 475).

Duplication: about 380 of its 838 lines copy src/pages/*. fillRect, blendRect, drawTriangle, collectEdgeIntersection, fillEllipse, lighten, darken, hashString and nextSeed are byte-identical after whitespace normalisation. The encoder (722-838) matches roomImagePrimitives.ts:641-771. drawDecoration and drawInteractiveObject (411-476) match drawFallbackObject and drawDecoration (roomImageRenderer.ts:627-829). BACKGROUND_COLORS matches backgroundPalette (281-293). No test imports roomPreviewImage.ts, so renderExpandedRoomSharePreviewPng is never exercised.

The API Worker already has an ASSETS binding over ./dist (wrangler.jsonc:12-17; core/types.ts:71), so it can use the same loader as the Pages renderer (roomImageAssets.ts:79-102).

Plan:
1. Move src/pages/roomImage{Primitives,Assets,Renderer}.ts to a shared src/roomImage/.
2. Give the renderer a layout parameter {left, top, tileSize}, like RoomPreviewLayout (roomPreviewImage.ts:34-49), and an injected asset loader.
3. Port the multi-cell layout and outer border (roomPreviewImage.ts:91-204, about 115 lines) onto it.
4. Delete roomPreviewImage.ts.

Net about -700 lines, and one implementation to fix (the previous finding's fixes then apply everywhere). With the compressed encoder and caching, the extra cost of decoding tilesets (about 100 ms cold per isolate, measured) is paid rarely.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:70-79 — 8 hardcoded background palettes; 11 groups exist in config/backgrounds.ts
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:235 — unknown group falls back to BACKGROUND_COLORS.forest
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:243-247 — custom background drawn as a grey checkerboard
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:298-318 — terrain tiles are colored rectangles, no tileset art
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:365-372 — skips background-layer objects and any id not in GAME_OBJECTS (custom sprites)
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/routes.ts:202-204 — Expanded Room image uses renderExpandedRoomSharePreviewPng
- src/cloudflare/worker/wampOGram/routes.ts:101 — Wamp-O-Gram preview uses the same abstract renderer
- src/pages/shareMetadata.ts:424-426 — Pages uses the API image only for expanded rooms
- wrangler.jsonc:12-17 — API Worker has an ASSETS binding to ./dist

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Every user-facing claim and evidence line holds. The plan needs these changes:
  1. **Keep custom room tiles.** The old renderer draws them correctly (roomPreviewImage.ts:278-296, 324-359) and the Pages renderer does not; they get a colored fallback via roomImageRenderer.ts:409-412. Port that tile drawing into the shared renderer before deleting the file. That also fixes single-room previews.
  2. **Object drawing differs.** drawInteractiveObject and drawDecoration are near-copies of the Pages versions, not matches: the Pages one picks shapes by id regex and has more branches. getTileColor differs too.
  3. **Neither encoder compresses today.** Compression depends on a separate change.
  4. **The API side needs its own custom-background loader.** It should read uploads directly instead of the Pages HTTP + cf.image fetch.
  5. **Net saving** is about -600 to -650 lines, not -700.
- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: Expanded Room (cellCount > 1) and Wamp-O-Gram link previews come from the abstract roomPreviewImage.ts, with every listed visual defect, and about 300 of its lines are byte-identical copies of src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.ts. Four corrections:
  
  1. **Custom tiles.** The real-art Pages renderer has no support for room-local custom tiles (gid >= 10000) and draws them as colored squares. roomPreviewImage.ts draws them properly (lines 278-296 and 324-359). That support must be ported before the old file is deleted, and porting it would also fix single-room cards.
  2. **Not all copies are identical.** drawDecoration differs (Pages adds rock, sun and water). The object code is near-equivalent, not identical.
  3. **Encoder.** Both encoders are uncompressed today.
  4. **Porting effort.** Moving the renderer to the API Worker means decoupling it from PagesWorkerEnv, resolveApiBaseUrl and the cf.image fetch for custom backgrounds, and making the API routes async.
  
  A cheaper alternative: add the multi-cell footprint to the Pages renderer, which reuses its warm asset cache, and point the expanded and Wamp-O-Gram og:image URLs at Pages routes. Then delete roomPreviewImage.ts and the two API image paths.
  
  Reach is small: 27 Expanded Rooms in production as of 2026-10-18, plus draft-only Wamp-O-Grams. The images are fetched only by link-preview crawlers and are cached for 1-24 hours. Impact is medium, not high.
- **partially confirmed.** The fidelity gaps and the duplication are real. Deleting roomPreviewImage.ts as planned would make one thing worse: it is currently the only server renderer that draws per-room custom tiles (gid >= 10000, roomPreviewImage.ts:278-296 and 324-359). The Pages renderer turns them into coloured blocks (roomImageRenderer.ts:409-413), so drawCustomRoomTilePreview and its collision shading have to be ported first.
  
  The custom-background loader cannot be reused as-is in the API Worker. It fetches the API's own /api/background-images route with a cf.image PNG conversion, and uploads can be WebP. The API side needs its own fetch from Cloudflare Images delivery with format conversion.
  
  imageDataCache should get a size bound. Otherwise up to about 37 MB of decoded RGBA (backgrounds plus tilesets) can pile up in the main API isolate.
  
  Net saving is about 600 lines, not 700. Impact is medium: these are link-preview images on two share surfaces, plus a code-health gain. An alternative to weigh: render these two images on the Pages Worker, which already has the asset and background paths, and add an API endpoint for the cell snapshots.

### F267: Each pop-up re-declares the same paper skin by name (~750 duplicate lines); the default is still the old dark one

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F115

**Summary.** WAMP's cream 'paper' pop-up look isn't the default. Each pop-up opts in by name, so the same title, label, error-box and button styles are copied up to 16 times. Two newer pop-ups never opted in and still show the old dark look: Room Insights (builders' play stats) and Room Templates. Disabled buttons in Explore, Leaderboards, Run Rating and WAMP-o-gram also use a different grey from the rest of the game. Making the paper look the default would delete hundreds of copied lines and fix those pop-ups automatically.

**Technical detail.**

Measured with postcss over src/styles: 64 rules / 506 lines in 14 files exist only to restate .history-modal-panel/title/kicker/meta/error for one dialog ID. The title body is identical for 16 IDs, kicker for 15, error box for 14, and the panel for 9+3. Another 92 rules / 636 lines restyle .bar-btn or #btn-* per dialog ID across 27 dialogs: the sky 'Close' button body is copied 10 times and the disabled-state body 8 times. Overall, 178 rules / 1,389 lines in src/styles have declarations identical to an earlier rule in the same media context, and 751 of those lines are dialog-ID-scoped. Root cause: the base rules still carry the pre-retro dark skin. They are room-course.css:31-42 (.history-modal-panel rgba(11,11,11,.96), 8px radius) and history.css:20-59 (light text, #ffd7d7 error), so every dialog must override them by ID. The F115 fix (PR #148) added four more IDs to these lists and explicitly left the consolidation undone. It missed two dialogs that existed by then: Room Insights (room-insights.css:9-16 uses var(--panel) = #0b0b0b and var(--text) = #f3eee2, tokens.css:122/128) and Room Templates (room-templates.css:7, 37-38, 46: #202428, #252a2c, #e8e6d9), so both still render dark. The Publish checklist hard-codes #fff3d9 (clear-check.css:52), a near-miss of --wamp-cream #fff3db. Per-dialog disabled rules use #c2bbb6/#6d6768 (rating-welcome-goals.css:78-79, 743-744, 1310-1311; wamp-o-gram.css:66-67; shared-modal-skin.css:221-222). The shared tokens are --wamp-disabled-surface #d2caba / --wamp-disabled-text #5f5a53 (tokens.css:20-21), used by button-roles.css. Header close buttons carry no data-button-variant (index.html btn-leaderboard-close, btn-explore-close, btn-wamp-o-gram-close), so button-roles.css can't style them. Fix: (1) Put the cream skin in the base selectors (history.css, room-course.css:12-42) and use tokens for disabled. Give `.history-modal-header .bar-btn` the sky look, or add data-button-variant="curate" to the close buttons. (2) Delete the per-ID lists file by file, keeping only per-dialog widths, and check each against the existing screenshot smokes. (3) Once done, have check_shared_styles.mjs reject `#…-modal .history-modal-(panel|title|kicker|meta|error)`. Expected removal: ~750 lines of exact copies plus most of the 506 restatement lines.

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/modals/room-course.css:31-42 — base .history-modal-panel is still the dark rgba(11,11,11,.96), 8px-radius skin
- src/styles/sections/modals/history.css:20-59 — base kicker/title/meta/error assume a dark background
- src/styles/sections/modals/leaderboard-profile-explore/shared-modal-skin.css:28-140 — the same cream panel/kicker/title/meta/error rules repeated for a 9-ID list
- src/styles/sections/modals/room-course.css:44-100 — the same skin copied again for 3 more IDs
- src/styles/sections/modals/room-insights.css:9-16 — Room Insights panel uses var(--panel) (#0b0b0b) and var(--text): still dark
- src/styles/sections/modals/room-templates.css:7 — Room Templates panel background #202428 (cards #252a2c at :38)
- src/styles/sections/modals/clear-check.css:52 — #fff3d9, a near-miss copy of --wamp-cream #fff3db
- src/styles/tokens.css:20-21 — disabled tokens #d2caba / #5f5a53
- src/styles/sections/modals/rating-welcome-goals.css:78-79 — per-dialog disabled colours #c2bbb6 / #6d6768 (also :743, :1310, wamp-o-gram.css:66)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The base `.history-modal-panel` and its kicker, title, meta and error rules are still dark. The cream skin is opt-in by dialog ID: title copied for 16 IDs, kicker 15, error 14, panel 9+3. About 168 rules and 1,300 lines repeat an earlier body, about 790 of those lines scoped to a dialog ID.
  
  Room Insights and Room Templates are the only dialogs still dark. Making the base cream will not fix them on its own, because their own rules override it:
  - Room Insights: room-insights.css:9-16 uses an ID selector.
  - Room Templates: room-templates.css:2-55 hard-codes #202428, #252a2c, #575c58, #e8e6d9 and #161c20, and loads after room-course.css.
  
  The cheapest fix: drop those dark backgrounds and recolour the template cards with the cream tokens. That part is small.
  
  The consolidation is a separate medium job:
  1. Make the base cream and add the --text, --text-muted and --border redefinitions to the base panel.
  2. Merge the per-ID lists, including src/bugReports/reporter.css, the hard-coded copy outside src/styles.
  3. Replace the 8 #c2bbb6/#6d6768 disabled rules (also in pvp.css, playlists.css and explore-queues.css) with --wamp-disabled-*.
  4. Replace #fff3d9/#181818 in clear-check.css with --wamp-cream/--wamp-ink.
  5. Add the check_shared_styles guard.
  
  Most dialogs have no screenshot smoke, so this needs a manual visual pass across about 34 of them.

### F271: Most user lookups still make two database trips because of fallback code for columns added in March-May

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F031
- **Also covers:** Bot and API-token requests make 4 trips including a write each time, and profile lookups read the same user row twice

**Summary.** Whenever the server looks up a player by email, wallet, ID, name or personal API token, it first reads the basic row with the profile fields blanked out, then makes a second trip for username, avatar and bio. That split exists only to survive a database missing columns added in March-May 2026. The sign-in check already reads those columns directly on every request, which proves they exist. Folding them back into one query removes a serial round trip from every profile view and personal-token request, and deletes about 130 lines.

**Technical detail.**

Pattern: SELECT ... NULL AS username, NULL AS avatar_url, NULL AS bio, NULL AS selected_avatar_id, then withUserProfileFields → loadOptionalUserProfileFields (a second SELECT). It appears in findUserByEmail (auth/store.ts:32-54), findUserByWallet (57-79), findUserById (82-104), findUserByDisplayName (107-129), findUserByUsername (131-161), loadMagicLinkByTokenHash (624-658), loadLiveEmailCodes (681-692, N+1 over up to 2 rows) and loadApiTokenAuth (908-944, every personal-token request). The fallback ladder is auth/store.ts:1116-1260: three regex predicates, two legacy loaders and 503 errors in updateUserProfile (482-498). Separately, hasUsernameColumn runs `SELECT username FROM users LIMIT 1` on every sign-up (262-272), and insertUserRecord retries without username (204-236).

Proof the columns exist: loadSessionFromToken selects u.username, u.avatar_url, u.bio, u.selected_avatar_id directly with no fallback (auth/store.ts:841-870). If they were missing, every signed-in request would fail. Migrations 0016 (2026-03-23), 0024 (04-15) and 0030 (05-09) added them, and deploy_prod.mjs:100-110 refuses to deploy with pending migrations. Hot callers: loadUserProfile and loadUserProfileSummary (profiles/store.ts:88, 144) await findUserById before anything else, so every profile view pays one extra serial D1 round trip. chat/store.ts:156/467 carries the same username fallback.

Fix: one shared USER_COLUMNS fragment plus a `selectUser(where)` helper, used by the 5 findUserBy* functions and the 3 joins. Delete withUserProfileFields, loadOptionalUserProfileFields*, loadLegacyOptionalUserProfileFields, the 3 predicates, hasUsernameColumn and the insert retry. While there, delete loadAllUserStatsRows (auth/store.ts:567, zero callers, an unbounded SELECT of user_stats), and move the profile-stat readers (loadUserStatsRow, loadPublishedRoomsByCreator, loadPublicUserProfileCourseCount, used only by profiles/store.ts) out of the 1,539-line auth store.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:40 — findUserByEmail selects NULL AS username/avatar_url/bio/selected_avatar_id
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:54 — then awaits withUserProfileFields (second query)
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:857 — session lookup already selects u.selected_avatar_id etc. directly, no fallback
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:944 — loadApiTokenAuth does the second query on every personal-token request
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:262 — hasUsernameColumn probe query on each sign-up
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:1187 — three 'no such column' predicates for 2026 migrations
- src/cloudflare/worker/profiles/store.ts:88 — every profile load starts with the two-query findUserById
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:567 — loadAllUserStatsRows has no callers
- scripts/deploy_prod.mjs:108 — deploy refuses to run with unapplied migrations
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:944 — API token auth re-reads profile fields
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:958-967 — awaited UPDATE last_used_at on every API-token request
- src/cloudflare/worker/agents/store.ts:355-360 — same awaited UPDATE for agent tokens
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/request.ts:84 — api-token lookup tried before the agent-token lookup
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:82-105 — findUserById selects NULL profile columns then re-reads them
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:1116-1290 — legacy missing-column fallback chain
- migrations/0016_user_profiles.sql:1-2 — avatar_url, bio exist; 0024:1 selected_avatar_id; 0030:1 username

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F272: Play.fun was removed in July, but about 60 queries and the client still filter its leftover accounts on every read

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Also covers:** Play.fun was removed in July, but its account filters still run inside 64 queries and add a database read to every run

**Summary.** When the Play.fun integration was removed on July 7, its auto-generated player accounts were kept and hidden instead. To hide them, about 60 database queries across 18 server files look up every row's player in two tables. Every ranked run start and finish runs an extra lookup, and the game then filters and re-ranks the same accounts a second time by name. A one-time cleanup that marks or removes those accounts would let all three layers go.

**Technical detail.**

generatedUsers/legacySource.ts:1-9 builds the table name 'playfun_user_links' from char codes. leaderboardIsolation.ts:74-105 emits correlated EXISTS(users ... AND EXISTS(playfun_user_links ...)) predicates, plus a LIKE 'playfun-%' display-name variant. sqlUserIdIsNotLegacyGeneratedOnly and sqlUserIdDoesNotHaveLegacyGeneratedDisplayNamePrefix are spliced into about 60 SQL sites in 18 files, including every ranked-leaderboard CTE (expandedRooms/leaderboards.ts:54, courses/leaderboards.ts:55), discovery (difficulty.ts, 8 uses), daily (9), dashboard (6), points (4) and admin. In a leaderboard CTE that means two extra index probes per candidate run row. isGeneratedLeaderboardExcludedUserId (leaderboardIsolation.ts:8-35) adds one query to every room/course/expanded run start and finish via assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed (e.g. runRoutes.ts:145, 279), and to every rename. The client repeats the filter: src/generatedUsers/ (153 lines) re-filters and re-ranks room, course and global boards by display-name prefix in runRepository.ts, courseRepository.ts:148 and expandedRooms/repository.ts. Commit 68588174 (2026-07-07) removed the integration itself.

Fix: one migration that sets users.leaderboard_excluded = 1 for generated-only accounts (no email or wallet, linked in playfun_user_links). Or, because those accounts can never sign in again, delete their run, rating and stat rows. Then replace the predicates with a single column check, or drop them, and delete src/generatedUsers/* and generatedUsers/legacySource.ts. That removes about 270 lines of helpers and simplifies about 60 SQL sites.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/legacySource.ts:1 — retired source name assembled from char codes to build table names
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:74 — nested EXISTS predicate spliced into leaderboard SQL
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:16 — extra query per run start/finish to check generated-only accounts
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/leaderboards.ts:54 — predicate evaluated per candidate run row in the ranked CTE
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts:145 — assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed on every expanded run start
- src/generatedUsers/leaderboards.ts:10 — client re-filters and re-ranks the same accounts by display-name prefix
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/legacySource.ts:1 — RETIRED_SOURCE_NAME built from char codes to spell 'playfun'
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:16-31 — D1 query run by isGeneratedLeaderboardExcludedUserId
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:37 — assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed, called at 11 run start/finish sites
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:103 — await assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed(env, auth, 'play')
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:31-32 — Daily Room (added 2026-10-05) re-adds both legacy guards
- migrations/0005_api_tokens.sql:1-11 — api_tokens has revoked_at but no expiry
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:25 — SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 30 days

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Split the work into two steps.
  
  (1) Now, with no migration: delete assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed (11 call sites), assertGeneratedOnlyDisplayNameChangeAllowed (2) and the finisher checks at points.ts:200/240. Generated-only accounts cannot authenticate any more, because every session path attaches an email or wallet and tokens require a session. So these always return false, and removing them saves one D1 round trip per run start, finish or claim (two on creator-reward finishes).
  
  (2) Later: a migration plus a policy decision. There are 42 predicate call sites in 18 files, not about 60. Read-path savings are negligible because these are PK probes, the email/wallet check short-circuits the second one, and room standings are cached. The real benefit is simplicity.
  
  The client filter in src/generatedUsers/leaderboards.ts is not a duplicate on room, course and expanded boards. It is the only enforcement of the 'playfun-' display-name rule there, and it is redundant only on the global board. Keep isHeuristicGeneratedCharacterDisplayName, which admin/suspiciousModel.ts uses. Only isAutoGeneratedLegacyDisplayName and the no-op isWampLeaderboardEligibleAuth are dead.
  
  The migration must reconcile three definitions: generated-only, any link (dashboard and mapScreenshot), and the name prefix. It must also either reserve the 'playfun-' prefix in the rename path or drop that rule, since any user can currently rename into invisibility.

### F282: Five client repositories keep private fetch-and-error copies and so miss the Safari page-leave fix in apiRequest

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F063
- **Also covers:** Three course and expanded-room API clients hand-roll the same request code, and five old course save methods are unused; The collection price and shelf loaders skip the shared request helper and lose its Safari page-exit fix

**Summary.** The game has one shared helper for talking to the server, but the room, course, Expanded Room, Expanded Room editor and Worlds code each carry their own 20-40 line copy. On October 20 the shared helper learned to cancel background reads when you leave a page, which fixes a Safari error. The copies didn't get that fix, so loading rooms and Expanded Rooms still does the old thing. Pointing the copies at the shared helper removes about 200 lines.

**Technical detail.**

src/api/request.ts:18-45 (apiRequest) routes through fetchWithPageReadLifetime (pageReadLifetime.ts:24-31; commit 254eea33, 2026-10-20). That aborts GET/HEAD reads at beforeunload/pagehide and restores them on pageshow, added for WebKit 'Context is stopped' failures. It also uses readApiErrorMessage. Private copies with raw fetch() and their own JSON-error parsing: persistence/roomRepository.ts:954-993 (every room load: loadRoom, loadRoomCurrent, summary), courses/courseRepository.ts:157-200, expandedRooms/repository.ts:128-162, expandedRooms/editorRepository.ts:125-162, ui/worlds/repository.ts:87-103, plus worlds/seedEditorAdapter.ts:133-148 and customSprites/catalogClient.ts:78-95. Each defines its own error class (RoomApiError, CourseApiError, ExpandedRoomApiError, ExpandedRoomEditorApiError, WorldsApiError) with the same (message, status) shape. getRoomStorageBackend is likewise copied in roomRepository.ts:627, worldRepository.ts:77 and auth/runtimeConfig.ts:10.

Fix: extend apiRequest with an optional `parse` hook for the record normalizers (cloneRoomRecord, normalizeCourseRecord) and 204 handling. Make each repo-specific error class a subclass of ApiError so existing isXApiError(error) && error.status checks keep working, and replace the seven request methods. About 230 → 40 lines, and room and Expanded Room loads gain the page-leave abort.

**Evidence.**

- src/api/request.ts:27 — shared apiRequest uses fetchWithPageReadLifetime
- src/api/pageReadLifetime.ts:24 — GET reads aborted on pagehide/beforeunload (WebKit fix)
- src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:961 — room repository calls raw fetch() with its own error parsing
- src/expandedRooms/repository.ts:135 — Expanded Room repository calls raw fetch()
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:161 — course repository calls raw fetch()
- src/ui/worlds/repository.ts:90 — Worlds repository calls raw fetch()
- src/auth/runtimeConfig.ts:10 — third copy of the VITE_ROOM_STORAGE_BACKEND reader
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:156-195 — hand-rolled request() with CourseApiError
- src/expandedRooms/editorRepository.ts:125-163 — same request() body with ExpandedRoomEditorApiError
- src/expandedRooms/repository.ts:128-162 — same request() body with ExpandedRoomApiError
- src/api/request.ts:18-45 — shared apiRequest using fetchWithPageReadLifetime and ApiError
- src/scenes/overworld/coursePlayback.ts:268 — `(isCourseApiError(error) || isExpandedRoomApiError(error))`
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:55-98 — createCourse/loadLatestDraftForRoom/saveDraft/publishCourse/unpublishCourse, no callers
- src/ui/setup/ownerCollectionReminder.ts:9 — raw fetch() for the price quote
- src/collections/repository.ts:6 — raw fetch() with credentials 'include' for public collection reads
- src/api/request.ts:27-31 — apiRequest uses fetchWithPageReadLifetime and ApiError

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** This is mainly a cleanup, not a missed Safari fix. Steps:
  1. Delete the five unused CourseRepository methods (createCourse, loadLatestDraftForRoom, saveDraft, publishCourse, unpublishCourse) and their interface entries.
  2. Replace the copies of getRoomStorageBackend in roomRepository.ts and worldRepository.ts with getStorageBackend from auth/runtimeConfig.
  3. Move the seven hand-rolled request functions (room, course, Expanded Room, Expanded Room editor, Worlds, seedEditorAdapter, custom-sprite catalog) onto apiRequest. First extend apiRequest with:
     - an error-factory option, or switch callers to `instanceof ApiError` (subclassing alone does not keep isXApiError working, because apiRequest throws a plain ApiError);
     - 204 handling;
     - a parse hook for cloneRoomRecord and the non-GET preview-cache invalidation, and for the course record normalization.
  
  Expected savings are about 150-200 lines.
  
  On the Safari side: the page-leave abort was deliberately limited to the shared helper and the run and guest-run reads that the WebKit test run caught. No reproduction ties room or Expanded Room loads to the error, and about 40 client files, including worldRepository.fetchWorldApi (the main overworld load path), still use raw fetch(). Any Safari benefit is incidental: it would only suppress errors during unload that the player never sees.

### F279: Expanded-room goal editing, goal flags and publishing are written out three times across three scenes

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** An expanded room's goal (type, time limit, markers) can be edited in three places: the Expanded Room setup screen, the Expanded Room editor, and the normal room editor when a cell is opened from setup. Each place has its own copy of the goal-setting code, the flag-and-label drawing, and in two places the whole publish sequence (build prompt, XP report, first-publish celebration). The 'daily claim limit' popup is also copied. Pulling these into a few shared helpers removes about 220 lines and means a publish fix only has to be made once.

**Technical detail.**

(1) Goal setters. CourseEditorScene.setCourseGoalType, TimeLimit, RequiredCount and SurvivalSeconds plus clearCourseGoalMarkers (CourseEditorScene.ts:1041-1089, 1110-1121) are character-identical to EditorCourseController (editor/courseController.ts:166-215, 227-238). EditorScene.ts:1798-1818 adds six more one-line forwarders to them. CourseComposerScene.ts:251-287 has a third variant built on mutateDraft.
(2) Marker drawing. The same flag sprite plus Courier New 12px label with stroke 4 and depth 130/131 appears in CourseEditorScene.ts:2343-2378, CourseComposerScene.ts:1206-1236 and courseController.ts:134-164.
(3) Publish. CourseComposerScene.publishCourseDraft (564-616) and CourseEditorScene.publishCourseDraft (1430-1490) run the same sequence: prepareBuildPromptEntry → capturePublishProgression → saveDraft → publishExpandedRoom → reportPublishProgression → completeBuildPromptEntry → announceFirstPublishedExpandedRoom. Each re-checks scene, course and user after every await, and they differ only in busy-overlay handling and the wake payload.
(4) Claim limit. DAILY_ROOM_CLAIM_LIMIT_* constants and showDailyRoomClaimLimitModal are duplicated in CourseEditorScene.ts:178-181 and 2082-2097 and in roomSession.ts:83, 110-112 and 1370-1385. shouldPersistGuestDraftLocally is duplicated at CourseEditorScene.ts:2078 and roomSession.ts:1191.
The product copy already says 'Expanded room goal is authored in Edit Expanded Room' (courses/goalAuthoring.ts:43-45), yet the single-room editor still offers live course-goal authoring (EditorScene.ts:988-993 → courseController).
Plan: add courses/editor/goalDraftCommands.ts (pure CourseSnapshot → CourseSnapshot functions used by all three), goals/expandedMarkerSprites.ts (draw(scene, markers, originOf, depth)), courses/editor/publishExpandedRoom.ts (one async function taking {record, repository, backup, isCurrent, onPlay}), and editor/claimLimitModal.ts. Optionally make the single-room editor's course-goal panel read-only with an 'Edit in Expanded Room' button, which would retire most of courseController.ts (331 lines). Low risk. Goal-authoring tests exist (courses/goalAuthoring.test.ts).

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1041-1089 — course goal setters identical to src/scenes/editor/courseController.ts:166-215
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1110-1121 — clearCourseGoalMarkers identical to src/scenes/editor/courseController.ts:227-238
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:2343-2378 — marker flag+label drawing; same at src/scenes/CourseComposerScene.ts:1206-1236 and src/scenes/editor/courseController.ts:134-164
- src/scenes/CourseComposerScene.ts:564-616 — publishCourseDraft sequence duplicated at src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1430-1490
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:178-181 — DAILY_ROOM_CLAIM_LIMIT_* duplicated from src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:83,110-112
- src/courses/goalAuthoring.ts:43-45 — 'Expanded room goal is authored in Edit Expanded Room' copy
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:988-993 — single-room editor still wires onSetCourseGoal*/marker placement

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Change the goal part from "share the setters across three surfaces" to "delete the dead copies". Only CourseEditorScene edits the expanded-room goal.
  
  1. Delete CourseComposerScene's goal setters, startMarkerPlacement, clearMarkers, the placement branch of handlePointerAction and createMarkerPointFromPointer (no UI, bridge or test callers since 8d6a6a3d).
  2. Delete courseController's setCourseGoal*/startCourseGoalMarkerPlacement/clearCourseGoalMarkers/placeGoalMarker and EditorScene's six forwarders (1797-1819). Their panel is always hidden (courseEditing.ts buildCourseEditorState visible:false). Keep redrawMarkers and removeGoalMarkerAt. Move EditorCourseGoalCapability from EditorCommonSceneBridge to CourseWorkspaceSceneBridge and the registry, and make the uiBridge course actions optional for EditorScene.
  3. Extract the two live publishCourseDraft sequences into one helper (busy-overlay and wake payload as parameters).
  4. Share the composer and course-editor marker drawing (origin lookup as a callback). The courseController variant uses depth 97/98 and descriptor colours, not 130/131.
  5. Move the claim-limit constants and modal into one module shared with roomSession.
  
  The read-only cell-editor panel idea is already built. Net removal is about 200-250 lines, mostly by deletion rather than new shared helpers.

### F276: 15 pop-up controllers still carry their own Escape and click-outside code the shared stack already does

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F073

**Summary.** The game now has one central piece that knows which pop-up is on top and closes it on Escape. But it only acts when two pop-ups are open, so each of 15 pop-ups still keeps its own copy of the Escape and click-outside code, and a 13-module helper keeps a third copy. Letting the central piece always close the top pop-up would remove about 280 lines and one source of 'Escape closed the wrong thing' bugs.

**Technical detail.**

modalState.ts:33-46 already finds the top open dialog and clicks its close button, but returns early when fewer than two are open (line 39: `if (open.length < 2) return;`). So each dialog keeps a private handleBackdropClick plus handleDocumentKeydown plus attach/detach. These are 31 declarations in 16 files: guestBuilderClaim, explore, guestbook, roomRush, profile, leaderboard, history, settings, signText, roomRushResult, chatModeration, runRating, playlist, welcome and wampOGram modals, plus chat/panel.ts. Examples: exploreModal.ts:96-108 with :187-188/:255-256, settingsModal.ts:53-64 with :191/:206, welcomeModal.ts:116-128 (Escape calls close(true), the same as its close button at :112). modalLifecycle.ts:12-36 holds a third copy of the same two handlers for its 13 adopters. Every copy checks only its own `hidden` class. Fix: (1) Drop the `< 2` early return so the capture-phase guard always closes the top dialog through its close button. (2) Add one capture-phase click listener: if event.target is the top .history-modal itself, click its close button, with an opt-out attribute for dialogs that must not close on backdrop. (3) Delete the per-controller handlers (~17 lines each × 15 ≈ 255 lines) and shrink createModalLifecycle to show/hide. profileModal.ts:164-177 special-cases the avatar picker, which is itself a .history-modal (#avatar-picker-modal), so the stack already handles it. Combine with the single dialog observer proposed for the Worlds finding. Vitest suites for these modals and smoke_keyboard_bindings.mjs cover the behaviour.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/modalState.ts:39 — shared Escape guard only acts when two or more dialogs are open
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:96-108 — private backdrop and Escape handlers
- src/ui/setup/settingsModal.ts:53-64 — identical private handlers
- src/ui/setup/welcomeModal.ts:122-128 — Escape handler calling close(true), same as the close button at :112
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:164-177 — Escape handler that special-cases the avatar picker (itself a .history-modal)
- src/ui/setup/modalLifecycle.ts:12-36 — a third copy of the same backdrop/Escape logic

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real duplication in 15 setup modals (not 16; chat/panel.ts handles Enter-to-open-chat for a non-modal panel and stays), worth roughly 230-260 net lines. Also fold in the extra Escape copies in dailyRoom/roomInsights/buildPrompts/firstPublishModal/activityInbox, clearCheckUi, roomTemplatePicker and bugReports/reporter, plus leaderboard's redundant Tab trap. The fix as written regresses, so change it as follows:
  (a) Do the single-dialog close in a bubble-phase document listener, or honour an opt-out. Otherwise the capture guard (registered at main.ts:206 before setupUI) pre-empts KeyboardBindingsEditor's "Escape cancels" (keyboardBindingsEditor.ts:69) and closes Controls, failing smoke_keyboard_bindings.mjs:147.
  (b) Skip hidden or disabled close buttons: the background-upload close button is hidden during upload (uiBridge.ts:1821).
  (c) Add a data-modal-close marker for dialogs with no matching close button (playlist-intro, performance-suggestion "Not now", build-prompt-publish "Cancel") rather than reducing createModalLifecycle to show/hide.
  (d) Make backdrop-close opt-in or audit each dialog.
  (e) Install the guard in guestRoomRecoveryModal.test.ts.
  This is cleanup only; no wrong-dialog Escape bug remains after F116.

### F298: Worker has two routers: a 34-entry table whose 'auth' labels are never enforced, and ~490 lines of hand-written if-chains

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** large
- **Related round-1 item:** F211

**Summary.** Requests reach their handler in two different ways. A tidy route table labels each route as public, signed-in or admin, but nothing checks those labels, and some are wrong. About 70 more routes are matched by hand-written if-statements below the table. Every handler therefore has to remember its own sign-in or admin check. Making the table enforce its labels and moving the remaining routes into it would make sign-in rules visible in one place and roughly halve the routing code.

**Technical detail.**

core/router.ts:1-40 defines RouteAuth and WorkerRoute.auth, but dispatchWorkerRoute never reads route.auth (router.ts:26-40), and router.test.ts tests only pattern matching. The table (worker.ts:155-340, 34 entries) carries wrong labels. /api/custom-sprites is 'public' (worker.ts:269-273), but its PUT and DELETE require a session (customSprites/routes.ts:66-67, 82-83). /api/school is 'authenticated' (worker.ts:212-216), but student-login is anonymous (school/routes.ts:126), as the F211 write-up already noted. Below the table, worker.ts:423-911 matches about 68 method/path pairs with regexes and if-statements, some doing their own auth inline (/api/world at worker.ts:497-501, music DELETE). Then rooms/routes.ts:93-616 uses a third style (segment arrays), and admin/routes.ts:49-200 a fourth (pathname if-chain) with about 40 per-handler requireAdminRequest calls. Across the Worker there are 161 calls to loadOptionalRequestAuth, requireAuthenticatedRequestAuth or requireAdminRequest. I spot-checked every admin handler, and each calls requireAdminRequest or the moderator check itself, so nothing is open today; safety depends on each new handler remembering.

Fix: (1) Have dispatchWorkerRoute resolve auth once from the label ('authenticated' → requireAuthenticatedRequestAuth, 'admin' → requireAdminRequest, 'optional' → loadOptionalRequestAuth) and pass it in context. Allow a per-method override for mixed prefixes such as custom-sprites. (2) Correct the labels and split mixed prefixes. (3) Move the 68 imperative blocks into the table: each becomes 3-4 lines, about 490 → 250. (4) Add a test that walks the table and asserts 401/403 without credentials for every 'authenticated' and 'admin' entry.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/core/router.ts:31 — dispatch loop matches method and pattern only; route.auth is never read
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:272 — /api/custom-sprites labelled 'public'
- src/cloudflare/worker/customSprites/routes.ts:67 — PUT on that prefix requires a session
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:214 — /api/school labelled 'authenticated' though student-login (school/routes.ts:126) is anonymous
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:423 — start of about 490 lines of hand-written regex/if routing after the table
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/routes.ts:55 — fourth routing style: pathname if-chain for admin

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: route.auth is never enforced, there are four routing styles, the if-chain is about 489 lines, and several labels are wrong. Corrections:
  
  1. More labels are wrong than the finding lists:
     - /api/background-images is 'authenticated', but GET list and GET/HEAD image are anonymous. HEAD also isn't in its methods list.
     - /api/admin/ is 'admin', but /api/admin/rooms/:id/restore is moderator-session only (admin/routes.ts:239). The labels need at least a 'moderator' value and per-method overrides before anything enforces them.
  2. Enforcing in the dispatcher is not a medium job:
     - 'authenticated' entries need a scope and a session-only vs token-allowed flag.
     - Auth isn't cached per request, so a pre-dispatch resolve must pass auth into roughly 150 handlers, or it doubles D1 lookups.
     - The full migration plus enforcement is large effort.
     - The /api/world inline auth is at worker.ts:459-463, not 497-501.
  3. A cheaper slice gets most of the safety:
     - (a) Fix the labels and add 'moderator' plus per-method overrides.
     - (b) Make the dispatcher fail closed only for 'admin', using the synchronous isAdminRequest header compare at no cost, and keep the handler checks as they are.
     - (c) Add a table-walk test asserting 401/403 for 'authenticated', 'admin' and 'moderator' entries with no credentials.
     - (d) Move the worker.ts if-blocks into the table mechanically, keeping their order.
     - Leave the rooms and admin sub-routers alone for now.
  4. The idea isn't new: docs/2026-06-10-repo-improvement-plan.md §3.3 already proposes it. What's new is the list of wrong labels.

### F296: The wallet-approval recovery logic is spread over six files, with five copies of 'who is signed in' and a two-tab gap

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: Collect & Lock: room collecting, wallet approvals and the crypto gate)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The safety logic for collecting a room is split across six files, written in quick succession. The same 'which account and wallet is active' check is written five times, the 'wallet switched' guard twice, and three nested layers each subscribe to the same cancel events. One gap remains: if the cost dialog is open in two tabs and the builder approves both, two mint requests reach the wallet, and the second fails on-chain and wastes gas. Merging the helpers removes about 50 lines and makes this kind of gap easier to see.

**Technical detail.**

Files: src/mint/roomWalletRecovery.ts (98), roomWalletRecoveryLifecycle.ts (63), roomWalletRecoveryRuntime.ts (26), src/main/roomWalletRecovery.ts (33), src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts (382), roomCollectionFlow.ts (153).

The identity reader 'authenticated ? user.id : null; walletAddress.toLowerCase()' appears in 5 places: roomWalletActions.ts:52-57, roomWalletRecoveryRuntime.ts:8-12, main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:11-14, scenes/editor/persistence.ts:64-68 (not lowercased) and persistence.ts:90-93. RoomWalletRecovery is built twice with identical wiring: roomWalletActions.ts:291-293 instead of the existing getRoomWalletRecovery() singleton (runtime.ts:15-25). The signer-seen guard is duplicated (roomWalletActions.ts:322-329 vs roomCollectionFlow.ts:74, 82-89). Sleep/shutdown/destroy plus auth-change subscriptions are registered by roomCollectionFlow (80-96), run() (338-342) and checkPending (285-288) for the same operation. hasCryptoWallet() exists (walletGate.ts:2-4), yet 14 inline dataset.wallet checks remain in 7 files. The drift shows: getPending()'s unfiltered branch (roomWalletActions.ts:72-76) causes the cross-account blocking described in the stale-approval finding.

Two-tab gap: intent() (191-197) and PendingRoomWalletStore.put (pendingRoomWallet.ts:70-76, which dedupes only by id) never refuse when another entry for the same room exists. The storage event (main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:18) does not cancel tab B's open consent, because roomSession.acceptWalletRecovery returns early while saveInFlight (roomSession.ts:377). The second mintRoom reverts with 'Room already minted.' (RoomOwnershipToken.sol:106).

Plan: export one currentWalletIdentity() next to hasCryptoWallet. Merge runtime + main installer + lifecycle into one module (−2 files, ~40 lines). Have RoomWalletActions use getRoomWalletRecovery(). Pass RoomCollectionFlow's isCurrent down instead of re-deriving the signer guard. In onBeforeSend, re-read the store and throw WalletRequestNotSubmittedError if another entry exists for the same room and kind.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:52-57 — first copy of the identity reader
- src/mint/roomWalletRecoveryRuntime.ts:8-12 — second copy
- src/main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:11-14 — third copy
- src/scenes/editor/persistence.ts:64-68 — fourth copy (wallet not lowercased)
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:291-293 — second RoomWalletRecovery built instead of using getRoomWalletRecovery()
- src/scenes/editor/roomCollectionFlow.ts:82-89 — duplicate of the signer guard at roomWalletActions.ts:322-329
- src/mint/pendingRoomWallet.ts:70-76 — put() dedupes only by id, so a second intent for the same room is accepted
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:377 — cross-tab recovery is ignored while this tab's own action is in flight

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The duplication is real but smaller than claimed, and the two-tab gap is real but low-impact.
  
  **Worth doing:**
  - **Two-tab guard.** In send()'s onBeforeSend, re-read the store and throw WalletRequestNotSubmittedError if another entry exists for the same room and kind (or have put() refuse it). This is about 3 lines and closes the gap. In practice the gap costs one reverted Base tx: the payment is refunded and gas is a fraction of a cent. It also needs both tabs' consent dialogs open before either approval is recorded.
  - **One identity helper.** Export a single currentWalletIdentity() (userId, lowercased wallet, signer) and use it in roomWalletActions, the runtime, main/roomWalletRecovery and persistence.
  - **Optional: drop the inner signer guard** in RoomWalletActions.run(), because every production caller already passes RoomCollectionFlow's isCurrent.
  
  **Not as proposed:**
  - **getRoomWalletRecovery() is not a straight swap.** RoomWalletActions builds its own RoomWalletRecovery on the session's injected RoomRepository, and the tests rely on that (roomSession.mint.test.ts:135). The singleton would need a repository parameter. Two instances cause no problem, because concurrent checks are already shared through the store-keyed WeakMap.
  - **Keep the lifecycle file.** RoomWalletRecoveryLifecycle is a pure class with its own tests. Merging it with the DOM installer saves little and makes it harder to test.
  - **Fix the numbers.** The realistic saving is about 15-25 lines, not about 50. There are 13 inline dataset.wallet checks in 6 files, not 14 in 7, and 10 of them use an injected document, so hasCryptoWallet() would need a document parameter.

### F278: Delete five unused /api/courses editor endpoints that duplicate /api/expanded-rooms with different rules

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** Leftovers from when Expanded Rooms were called 'courses': unused course create/publish calls and helpers (about 120 lines)

**Summary.** The server still has the old routes for creating, saving, publishing and unpublishing a course. They do the same job as the Expanded Room editor routes, but nothing calls them: not the game, the agent guide or any test. Two of them also apply different rules than their replacements. One enforces a daily publish limit the real publish skips, and one skips a world-access check the real lookup runs. Deleting them removes about 250 lines and a second way in with different rules.

**Technical detail.**

Routes: POST /api/courses (worker.ts:731-733 → courses/routes.ts:104-118), GET /api/courses/drafts/by-room/:id (worker.ts:740-747 → 152-178), PUT /api/courses/:id/draft (750-752 → 180-195), POST /api/courses/:id/publish (755-762 → 197-242), POST /api/courses/:id/unpublish (765-767 → 244-265). handleCourseCreate is line-for-line handleExpandedRoomCreate (editorRoutes.ts:46-60). The canonical publish passes enforceDailyPublishLimit:false (editorRoutes.ts:131-139); the course route keeps the limit on (courses/routes.ts:215-217). The expanded draft lookup runs assertPrimeOnlyAuthoringRooms before auth (editorRoutes.ts:66); the course one never does (courses/routes.ts:152-178).

No callers. CourseRepository.createCourse, loadLatestDraftForRoom, saveDraft, publishCourse and unpublishCourse (courseRepository.ts:56-97) have zero call sites: a repo-wide search for .createCourse(/.publishCourse(/.unpublishCourse( finds none, and every .saveDraft(/.loadLatestDraftForRoom( goes to the room or expandedRoomEditor repositories. public/skill.md:121-127 sends agents to /api/expanded-rooms/*, and openapi.json documents none of the five. No test references handleCourseCreate, DraftSave, DraftByRoomLookup, Publish or Unpublish outside the route files.

Fix: delete the five worker.ts blocks and the matching CourseRepository methods and interface members. Inline what editorRoutes.ts imports from courses/routes.ts (handleCoursePublish, handleCourseUnpublish) as expanded-room functions. Keep GET /api/courses/:id, which flow.ts:467 and runReplayLinks.ts:26 still call. Also drop '/api/courses' from requestMayQueueWorldTiles. About 175 worker lines, 37 router lines and 45 client lines go.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:732 — POST /api/courses still routed to handleCourseCreate
- src/cloudflare/worker/courses/routes.ts:104 — handleCourseCreate duplicates editorRoutes.ts:46 handleExpandedRoomCreate
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts:138 — canonical publish skips the daily publish limit (enforceDailyPublishLimit: false)
- src/cloudflare/worker/courses/routes.ts:215 — legacy publish enforces assertUserCanPublishContent
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts:66 — expanded draft lookup checks world access; courses/routes.ts:152 does not
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:56 — createCourse/saveDraft/publishCourse/unpublishCourse have no callers
- public/skill.md:124 — agent guide uses POST /api/expanded-rooms and PUT .../draft, not /api/courses
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:55-60 — createCourse (POST /api/courses), no callers
- src/courses/courseRepository.ts:86-91 — publishCourse, no callers
- src/scenes/overworld/coursePlayback.ts:551-571 — fallback to legacy course run start on 404/5xx
- migrations/0037_expanded_rooms.sql:139-181 — backfill of every course into expanded_rooms as legacy_course
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:731 — Worker still serves POST /api/courses

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The five legacy course mutation routes and the five CourseRepository methods really are unused and can be deleted. Corrections to the claim:
  - The rule differences are harmless. The legacy publish is stricter than the canonical one because it also enforces the daily limit. The legacy draft lookup returns only the caller's own drafts. Neither is a security gap.
  - Net deletion is about 140-150 lines, not 250:
    - worker.ts: about 38 lines (routes plus imports).
    - courses/routes.ts: about 60 lines (create, lookup, save and the enforce option).
    - courseRepository.ts: about 48 lines.
  - Publish and unpublish move into editorRoutes.ts rather than being deleted.
  - The fix also needs to:
    - update outboxDispatchGate.test.ts:6 when '/api/courses' is dropped from WORLD_TILE_OUTBOX_WRITE_PREFIXES;
    - reword public/skill.md:119, which mentions legacy course compatibility routes.
  - Keep these routes: GET /api/courses/:id, POST /api/courses/:id/runs/start, POST /api/courses/:id/ratings and POST /api/course-runs/:id/finish.

### F281: Feature flags that are always on, plus ~27 'table missing' guards for 5-month-old migrations, keep unreachable fallback paths alive

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Also covers:** Feature switches are read by 11 copy-pasted helpers with three different rules for what counts as 'on'

**Summary.** The server still checks several on/off switches that are set to on in every environment, or never set at all, so they default to on. The off branches can't run, yet each check is copy-pasted: one switch's helper exists in 7 files. On top of that, about 27 places catch "this table doesn't exist" errors for tables created in May-July and quietly fall back to old, slower code. That code can't run either, and it hides real errors. Removing both trims a few hundred lines and makes failures visible.

**Technical detail.**

Flags. wrangler.jsonc:38-43 and 96-100 set PLAYABLE_CONTENT_INDEX_READS, COMPACT_WORLD_READS, WORLDS_ENABLED and TILED_OVERWORLD_READS to "1" (rollout 100) in prod and safety. EXPANDED_ROOMS_ENABLED is set in neither and defaults on. The same 4-line isExpandedRoomsEnabled is copied into share/routes.ts:371, world/routes.ts:308, runs/roomRushLeaderboards.ts:463, runs/difficulty.ts:1272, profiles/store.ts:610, playlists/store.ts:860 and roomComments/store.ts:822. playableContentIndexReadsEnabled is copied into difficulty.ts:678, profiles/store.ts:339 and playableContentIndex/discovery.ts:42, about 23 branch sites in all. Builder discovery has three implementations (difficulty.ts:1029-1250): the index path is the one used; the by-area path runs only if the index table is missing, and the raw room_versions SQL only when expanded rooms are off. That is about 170 unreachable lines. profiles/store.ts:325-335 catches any error whose text mentions playable_content_index and falls back to loading every published room by the creator.

Schema guards. isExpandedRoomSchemaMissingError (expandedRooms/schemaErrors.ts:1-6) covers migration 0037 (2026-05-26) and is used at expandedRooms/store.ts:250, 314, 399, 474, writeStore.ts:40-67 (two wrappers), admin/suspicious.ts (3), suspiciousInvalidation.ts (2), launchStatsStore.ts (2), progressRows.ts:414, badgesTrophies.ts:258, difficulty.ts:1454 and discoveryViewerStates.ts:178. 'no such table' checks cover 0040 (2026-07-17) at playableContentIndex/discovery.ts:108 and runMetrics.ts:115, and 0042 at worldTiles/store.ts:537. deploy_prod.mjs:100-110 refuses to deploy with pending migrations (F193), so these can't trigger in production.

Fix: delete the flag readers and their off branches (keep the client's legacy /api/world/chunks fallback, which F030 deliberately retains), the builder-discovery fallbacks, the schema guards and schemaErrors.ts. Update scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts:290, which forces EXPANDED_ROOMS_ENABLED '0'. If a flag is still wanted, give it one shared reader in core/flags.ts.

**Evidence.**
