### F291: Share-link pages come from four copy-pasted code paths (~480 lines), and World links get no preview card

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When someone shares a room, profile, playlist or WAMP-o-gram link, a small server function adds the title and picture that chat apps show. It is written out four times, almost line for line, so any fix must be made four times. World links (wamp.land/w/3, which Worlds emails already send) get no preview at all. Folding it into one table makes the code about a third of its size, and adds World previews as one more row.

**Technical detail.**

src/pages/shareAppShell.ts (364 lines) holds four render*AppShell functions (:4-118, ~28 lines each) that differ only in the fallback and inject function they call. It also holds four fallback*HtmlResponse (:133-227, identical except meta builder and link label) and four inject*Metadata (:229-279, identical except meta builder). buildProfileMetaTags and buildPlaylistMetaTags (:311-355) differ only in og:type. shareMetadata.ts has three loaders (loadProfileMetadata :116-147, loadPlaylistMetadata :149-180, loadWampOGramMetadata :330-361) that are the same fetch-with-timeout-and-fallback with a different API path, User-Agent string and builder pair. shareRoutes.ts:26-65 repeats the parse, method check, load and render sequence four times. Fix: a ShareKind registry {parsePath, apiPath, buildFallback, buildPublished, metaTags, linkLabel} with one renderAppShell, one fallback, one inject and one loader. That takes shareAppShell.ts from 364 to ~110 lines and the loaders from ~95 to ~35. The existing shareAppShell/shareMetadata/shareRoutes tests stay as the regression net. Idea on the same blocks: World share paths already exist (worlds/geometry.ts:44-56 buildWorldSharePath/parseWorldSharePath; worker worlds/store.ts:158 returns sharePath). GET /api/worlds/number/:n exists (ui/worlds/repository.ts:23-25), and Worlds notification emails link to /w/N (worker/worlds/notifications.ts:47, 72). Yet pages/routes.ts:42-62 sends /w/* straight to env.ASSETS with no metadata. With the registry, a World preview (name, owner, room count) is one entry, and owners sharing their World get a proper card.

**Evidence.**

- src/pages/shareAppShell.ts:4-118 — four render*AppShell functions identical except the helpers they call
- src/pages/shareAppShell.ts:133-227 — four fallback*HtmlResponse bodies differing only in label and meta builder
- src/pages/shareAppShell.ts:229-279 — four identical inject*Metadata functions
- src/pages/shareAppShell.ts:311-355 — profile and playlist meta builders identical except og:type
- src/pages/shareMetadata.ts:116-180 — profile and playlist loaders are the same fetch/timeout/fallback code
- src/pages/routes.ts:42-62 — no handling for /w/ World share paths
- src/worlds/geometry.ts:44-56 — buildWorldSharePath/parseWorldSharePath already exist

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F288: Pull the shared room-drawing geometry into one small module; the same math is copied three or four times

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The rules for how a room is laid out in a picture are copied separately into the game, the NFT and map code, and the share-picture server: how an uploaded background is stretched, centered or tiled, how big an object is and where it sits, and which tile sheet a tile comes from. One copy was even written specifically to keep the others in step, but only one renderer uses it. Moving these rules into one module that every renderer imports removes about 250 lines and stops the copies drifting apart again.

**Technical detail.**

Copies found:
- **Custom-background fit math, three copies.**
  - getCustomBackgroundTileScale and getCustomBackgroundCenterRect: backgrounds/runtime.ts:59-80, mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:229-250, pages/roomImageAssets.ts:208-226.
  - The 128/96 constants: runtime.ts:14-15, roomMetadataRender.ts:48-49, roomImageAssets.ts:18-19.
  - Reason for the copies: runtime.ts imports Phaser (lines 1-2), so the NFT and Pages code could not import it.
- **The three-fit canvas draw, twice.** roomMetadataRender.ts:184-227 and roomSnapshotTexture.ts:261-307 are the same logic over CanvasImageSource; the Pages version is the RGBA equivalent.
- **The 'parity helpers' used by one renderer.** getRoomMetadataObjectDrawRect and getRoomMetadataBackgroundLayerLayout (mint/roomMetadataRenderLayout.ts:3-36) are used only by roomMetadataRender. roomSnapshotTexture re-derives the same formulas (230-239, 659-664) and the Pages renderer gets them wrong (finding above).
- **Tileset lookup, three copies.** config/tilesets.ts:1378, roomSnapshotTexture.ts:738-757, pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:831-839.
- **Tile decode, two copies.** config/editorState.ts:186 and roomImageRenderer.ts:845-864.
- **Custom-sprite lookup, two copies.** roomMetadataRender.ts:407-419 and roomImageRenderer.ts:502-527.

Plan: create src/rendering/roomDrawGeometry.ts, pure and importing only config, backgrounds/model and customTiles/model. It exports:
- resolveBackgroundDraw
- getBackgroundLayerLayout
- getCustomBackgroundFitRects(fit, srcSize, destSize), returning one rect or a tile grid
- a precomputed gid -> {tileset, localIndex} table
- getObjectDrawRect, getObjectFlipX and findCustomSprite

The canvas renderers share one drawCustomBackground(ctx, source, rects). The RGBA renderers keep only blit. Note: changing roomMetadataRender output requires bumping WORLD_TILE_RENDER_CONTRACT (world-tile-render.ts:10) and re-rendering leaves. Keep the refactor output-identical for the client renderers and verify with the parity test.

**Evidence.**

- src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:1-2 — imports Phaser, so its pure helpers (59-80) were copied elsewhere
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:229-250 — second copy of tile-scale and center-rect helpers
- src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts:208-226 — third copy
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:184-227 and src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:261-307 — same stretch/center/tile canvas draw
- src/mint/roomMetadataRenderLayout.ts:18-36 — parity helper used only by roomMetadataRender.ts:384
- src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:659-664 — re-derives the same object rect inline
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:831-864 — local getTilesetByGid and decodeTileValue duplicate config

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Scope it smaller and drop the new module.
  - Move the two fit helpers and the 128/96 constants into backgrounds/model.ts. That file is already pure and already imported by roomMetadataRender, roomSnapshotTexture and the Worker share renderer. Re-export them from backgrounds/runtime.ts, and delete the roomMetadataRender and roomImageAssets copies.
  - Move roomMetadataRenderLayout into a neutral shared location and use it in roomSnapshotTexture (background layer at 230-239, base object rect at 659-664). Keep the atlas-trim adjustment local.
  - Have pages/roomImageRenderer import getTilesetByGid, decodeTileDataValue and parseCustomSpriteObjectId from config and customSprites/model. Keep its unknown-input guard and sprite-shape checks as thin wrappers.
  - Optionally share one fit-rect function between the two canvas renderers and the RGBA renderer.
  - Skip the precomputed gid table.
  
  Expect a net saving of about 100-150 lines, not 250. Keep roomMetadataRender output byte-identical so WORLD_TILE_RENDER_CONTRACT does not need a bump. The existing tests pin the helper outputs (roomImageAssets.test.ts:271-300 and roomMetadataRender.test.ts).

### F299: World-map tile geometry and wire types are defined twice, once for the server and once for the game client

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The pre-drawn world-map tiles rely on the server and the game agreeing on tile size, zoom levels and the manifest format. Those rules and types are written out twice: once in the shared world-tiles model the server uses, and again in the game's own copy with different function names. They match today, but a server-side change won't cause any error in the game, and a mismatch is exactly how the map pyramid went dark in September (F003). Making the game import the shared model removes about 150 lines and makes such a mismatch a compile error.

**Technical detail.**

src/worldTiles/model.ts (server, renderer and contracts) and src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/geometry.ts plus types.ts (client) both define WORLD_TILE_MIN/MAX_LEVEL, CONTENT_WIDTH 640, CONTENT_HEIGHT 352, OVERLAP 1 and IMAGE_WIDTH/HEIGHT (model.ts:6-12 vs geometry.ts:10-17). They also both define assertWorldTileLevel, floorDivide, rooms-per-tile (getWorldTileRoomsPerAxis lookup table vs getRoomsPerWorldTile 2**(4-level)), pixels-per-tile, roomToWorldTileCoordinate, tile→room bounds (getWorldTileRoomBounds vs worldTileToRoomBounds), getWorldTileParent/Children (model.ts:161-186 vs geometry.ts:88-129) and worldTileCoordinateKey. Wire types are duplicated too: WorldTileLevel, Coordinate, Address, ManifestReady, ManifestEntry, RoomSummary, Manifest and Config (model.ts:3, 33-108 vs types.ts:1-64). The client copy has already loosened goalType from RoomGoalType to string. No client file imports src/worldTiles/model.ts. Its importers are cloudflare/worldTileRenderer/contracts.ts and worker/worldTiles/*. model.ts only imports a type from goals/roomGoals, so it is safe to bundle. Plan: re-export from model.ts in geometry.ts and types.ts, keep the client-only helpers (getWorldTileSpan, getWorldTileCorePlacement, worldRectToTileBounds, enumerateWorldTileBounds), and delete the duplicated bodies and types (about 150 lines). geometry.test.ts and coverage.test.ts keep it honest. The classic-script bootstrap (src/main/earlyWorldTileBootstrap.classic.ts:14) must keep its own literal, so assert it in its existing test.

**Evidence.**

- src/worldTiles/model.ts:6-12 — tile constants (640x352, overlap 1, levels 0-4)
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/geometry.ts:10-17 — the same constants redefined
- src/worldTiles/model.ts:161-186 — getWorldTileParent/getWorldTileChildren
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/geometry.ts:88-129 — second getWorldTileParent/getWorldTileChildren
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/types.ts:1-64 — client copies of WorldTileManifestReady/Entry/Config/RoomSummary/Manifest
- src/worldTiles/model.ts:57-108 — server versions of the same wire types (goalType: RoomGoalType)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real but smaller cleanup. Have the client re-export from src/worldTiles/model.ts: the constants, WorldTileLevel/Coordinate/Address/Bounds/RoomBounds, ManifestReady/Entry/Config/Manifest, assertWorldTileLevel, floorDivide, rooms/pixels per tile, room bounds and worldTileCoordinateKey. Also point src/world-tile-render.ts:5-9 at it. getWorldTileParent/getWorldTileChildren cannot simply be re-exported. First move the client's address-preserving overloads (geometry.ts:88-129) into model.ts, then simplify contracts.ts getParentAddress/getChildAddresses. Otherwise coverage.ts, displayPlan.ts and viewport.ts lose rendererVersion in their keys. Adapt roomToWorldTileCoordinate's argument order at controller.ts:598. Keep goalType as string on the client (for example Omit<WorldTileRoomSummary,'goalType'> & {goalType: string|null}) so an unknown goal type does not reject the manifest. Drop the F003 rationale (that was an asset-hash mismatch), and drop the "no error" claim, since the client manifest parser already rejects mismatched width/height/overlap at runtime. Net saving is about 100-130 lines. Drift risk is low because the constants equal ROOM_PX_WIDTH/HEIGHT.

### F285: Next cuts for OverworldPlayScene: a 379-line debug dump and PvP code that handles two opponent sources in five places

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Even after this week's refactors, the main play scene is still 5,600 lines. Two blocks are easy next moves. One is a 379-line function that only builds a debugging snapshot for test scripts. The other is about 580 lines of player-vs-player glue in which five different functions each ask 'is the opponent coming from the match connection, or from presence?'. Moving the debug snapshot to its own file and hiding the two opponent sources behind one small interface would cut roughly 900 lines from the scene without changing gameplay.

**Technical detail.**

(1) describeState (OverworldPlayScene.ts:5257-5636, 379 non-blank lines) only serializes state for main/debugState.ts:5-34, previewSmoke.ts:381/406 and debug/overworldLodStress.ts:50/57. It even fetches the presence snapshot twice (`presenceDebug` at 5263 and again at about 5631). Move it to overworld/debugSnapshot.ts as `describeOverworldState(view)`, reading through the same typed host as the composition modules. Together with getRuntimeTransitionProbe (5188, about 52 lines) and the debug* setters (4641-4720), that is about 480 lines.
(2) PvP, lines 3983-4640 (582 non-blank). attackPvpPeerInRect (4138), attackPvpPeerAtPoint (4163), maybeStompPvpPeer (4190), maybeApplyRemotePvpActionHit (4255) and resolvePvpPeerCollision (4324) each query pvpInstanceRenderer (the multiplayer-instance channel added in 82063fee) and then repeat the logic for the presence ghost (findPvpOpponentGhost 4368, getPvpGhostRect 4386). Introduce a PvpOpponentView with { userId, bodyRect, hitRect, center, remoteAction } that prefers the instance channel and falls back to presence. Each of the five methods then shrinks to a few lines. Move the lot, plus serializePvpOpponentGhost and getPvpOpponentIdentity, into a PvpCombatRuntime next to the existing pvpCombatCoordinator.ts and pvpCombatGeometry.ts. About 120 lines removed and about 450 moved. pvpCombatCoordinator.test.ts and pvpCombatGeometry.test.ts already pin the geometry. (3) 83 one-line forwarders remain, for example 648-662 and 4622-4628 for pvpArenaController getters. Callers inside the scene can use the controller directly.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:5257-5636 — describeState, 379 non-blank lines of debug serialization
- src/main/debugState.ts:5-34 — only consumer path (getGameDebugState)
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:4138-4161 — attackPvpPeerInRect: instance renderer first, then presence ghost
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:4190-4236 — maybeStompPvpPeer repeats the instance/presence split
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:4255-4311 — maybeApplyRemotePvpActionHit: 'instance' then 'presence' channel branches
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:648-662 — pvp getters that only forward to pvpArenaController

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Most of the numbers check out: describeState is 379 lines and builds the presence snapshot twice, the PvP block is 582 lines, five methods split instance/presence, and there are 83 forwarders. But describeState is also called in production, not just by test scripts: the guest-activity heartbeat, the replay recorder, WebGL and render-loop recovery, and capture_debug_info. Moving it to overworld/debugSnapshot.ts is only a file move and needs new getters in createCompositionPorts.
  
  For PvP, don't build a PvpOpponentView. The presence-ghost fallback can't be reached in practice: setPvpInstanceOpponentUserId (OverworldPlayScene.ts:4054, pvpArenaController.ts:426-430) hides the opponent's presence ghost (presence.ts:525-536), and findPvpOpponentGhost requires sprite.visible (4377). So delete the presence branches and the helpers only they use: findPvpTargetInRect, findPvpOpponentGhost, getPvpGhostRect/HitRect, getPvpRemoteActionDamageRect and serializePvpOpponentGhost. That removes about 150 lines and is small effort. Also switch getPvpOpponentIdentity off getDebugSnapshot().
  
  Most forwarders feed composition ports and the frame pipeline, so they can't simply be inlined. Only duplicates like isPvpPeerCollisionActive (== isPvpArenaActive) come out for free. The net deletion is about 150-200 lines plus about 450 moved, not about 900 cut.

### F287: OverworldPlayScene now carries a 478-line forwarding adapter, and 21 controllers still re-read the mode by hand

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F066

**Summary.** The F066 refactor moved controller set-up out of the scene's constructor, which was good. To make it work, it added a 478-line block that passes the scene's private values through to that code one by one: 145 relay functions, 156 getters and 24 setters. Fifty-six of those getters just expose fixed tuning numbers like jump speed. The shared 'runtime context' built for this is used by only 5 controllers, while 21 others each build their own 'what mode are we in' reader. Moving the tuning numbers to a settings file and handing controllers the context would delete most of this block.

**Technical detail.**

createCompositionPorts (OverworldPlayScene.ts:724-1201, 478 non-blank lines) declares 145 `const x: typeof owner.x = (...args) => owner.x(...args)` forwarders and lists each one again in the returned object, plus 156 `get X() { return owner.X; }` and 24 setters. composition/ports.ts:4 defines the port type as ReturnType of that function, so it is the only seam between the scene and the six composition modules. Three cuts, in order of safety:
(a) The scene declares 57 `private readonly` UPPERCASE tuning fields (e.g. 418-425: PLAYER_SPEED=150, JUMP_VELOCITY=-280, GRAVITY=700). The ports expose 56 of them through getters (e.g. 900-914, BIRD_WAVE_SPEED…JUMP_VELOCITY). Move them to exported constants in composition/settings.ts, which already holds MIN_ZOOM and similar. About 113 lines go, with no behaviour risk.
(b) `getMode: () => host.mode` appears 21 times across composition/world.ts (63, 230, 249, 274, 310, 397, 486, 556, 619, 720), ui.ts (45, 79, 108, 144, 192, 272), social.ts (22, 51, 87) and roomRush.ts (16, 52). The same holds for getPlayer ×10 and getPlayerBody ×11. Only 5 constructions take `runtime: host.runtimeContext` (player.ts:74, 93, 437; world.ts:80; social.ts:67). Migrating the rest to OverworldRuntimeContext finishes what F066 started and removes the matching port getters.
(c) For what remains, define an `OverworldCompositionHost` interface. The scene `implements` it, with the needed members marked `/** @internal */` instead of private, and passes `this`. Composition code calls `host.x(...)` as a member call (no bare method references were found), so `this` binding is preserved. Net effect is about 350-420 lines out of the largest file. composition.test.ts plus the frozen frame traces cover construction order. Risk: low for (a), medium for (b) and (c).

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:724-1201 — createCompositionPorts: 145 forwarders, 156 getters, 24 setters
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:729 — `const getSwordsmanTraversalPlannerMode: typeof owner.getSwordsmanTraversalPlannerMode = (...args) => owner.getSwordsmanTraversalPlannerMode(...args);`
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:418-425 — tuning constants stored as private readonly instance fields
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:900-914 — `get BIRD_WAVE_SPEED() { return owner.BIRD_WAVE_SPEED; }` … `get JUMP_VELOCITY()`
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/ports.ts:4 — port type = ReturnType<typeof OverworldPlayScene.createCompositionPorts>
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/world.ts:63 — one of 21 `getMode: () => host.mode` closures
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/player.ts:74 — one of only 5 `runtime: host.runtimeContext` consumers

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The boilerplate is real and 100% mechanical. The three proposed cuts should be corrected as follows.
  
  (a) Correct as proposed: about 113 scene lines and low risk, small effort. Move the 57 tuning fields to exported constants (composition/settings.ts or a playerTuning module) and drop the 56 port getters and their 28 Pick-list entries. The scene imports GRAVITY, JUMP_VELOCITY, PLAYER_HEIGHT, PLAYER_STANDING_HEIGHT and PLAYER_WIDTH. Net repo deletion is about 85 lines.
  
  (b) Migrating the 21 getMode, 10 getPlayer and 11 getPlayerBody closures to OverworldRuntimeContext removes no port getters, because createRuntimeContext still reads host.mode, host.player and host.playerBody (world.ts:49-75). It saves no composition lines either. It is optional consistency work that touches about 20 controller option types and about 24 tests (medium-to-large effort).
  
  (c) The adapter exists to keep scene members private, and composition.test.ts verifies it lazily. Replacing it means making about 325 members public, with @internal, and rewriting that test. The saving reaches about 400 lines only if the port type becomes the scene class itself. A hand-written host interface that re-lists every member would save little.

### F289: Room setup and teardown are written two or three times over in the streamer and presenter

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Since the presenter split, several pieces exist in duplicate:
- reset() and destroy() repeat the same 58 lines.
- The instant room builder and the step-by-step room builder create the same images and tile map separately.
- Room teardown exists in three versions: all at once, step by step, and a 'force' version.
- The 'release this room's textures' sequence is copied three times.

Every future change has to be made in each copy. Share these pieces.

**Technical detail.**

Duplicates, with line counts:
1. reset() (worldStreaming.ts:496-561) and destroy() (563-629) share 58 identical lines; a diff of the two bodies shows only 6 differing statements. Extract clearStreamState(reason).
2. Presenter createImmediate (fullRoomPresenter.ts:165-229) and createDormantShell (870-938) both build the image, foreground image, tilemap, TILESETS loop, custom tileset and blank layer, about 55 lines. Extract createRoomDisplayShell(identity, {dormant}).
3. Teardown: destroyLoadedRoomResources (354-393), the batched destroyLoadedRoomCollisionResources, destroyLoadedRoomInsetBodyBatch, destroyTerrain, destroyBackgroundSpriteBatch and destroyDisplay (821-849, 1046-1071), and forceDestroy* (786-819, 1073-1125) encode the same sequence three times. Drive both sync and force from the phase list.
4. 'Touch if cached, else release the texture keys' appears in destroyReplacedFullRoomAfterCommit (4436-4460), finalizePendingFullRoomTeardown (~4960-4995) and destroyFullRoom (5280-5312). The [textureKey, foregroundTextureKey, customRoomTileTextureKey].filter array is built 5 times.
5. The 5-line 'clear predicted intent' block appears 4 times (1702-1706, 3913-3920, 4557-4563, 4578-4585).
6. The byte-size formula appears 3 times (3434-3466 and roomTexturePreparation.ts:136).
7. The y-then-x coordinate comparator appears 3 times (2099-2112, 2755-2762).

Roughly 200 lines go away. In destroyLoadedRoomInsetBodyBatch, removing while iterating the live getChildren() array skips every other child (fullRoomPresenter.ts:835-843). It still terminates, but it takes about twice the intended jobs; iterate a copy.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:496-561 — reset() body
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:563-629 — destroy() body (58 identical lines)
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:165-229 — createImmediate image/tilemap setup
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:870-938 — createDormantShell repeats it
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:354-393 — all-at-once teardown
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:1073-1125 — force teardown variants
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:835-843 — removes from live children array while indexing it
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:5280-5312 — artifact release pattern (also 4436-4460)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real duplication worth sharing:
  - reset/destroy body (about 55 lines). A clearStreamState helper is safe because the call-order difference is a no-op.
  - The image/tilemap/tileset shell shared by createImmediate and createDormantShell (about 40 lines).
  - The artifact touch/release sequence (3 copies) and the [textureKey, foregroundTextureKey, customRoomTileTextureKey].filter array (4 copies).
  - The byte-size formulas and the y/x comparator.
  - cancelFullRoomPreparation 4557-4563 should call the existing detachPredictedPreparationIntent. The 4578-4585 block is not a copy (its increment is conditional).
  
  Drop or deprioritize unifying the three teardown variants. They differ on purpose in error policy (rethrow first error, throw to the force-complete wrapper, log and continue), in batching and in step order, and each step is only 2-6 lines.
  
  The inset-batch loop does skip alternate children of the live Phaser entries array. The cost is about log2(min(L,64)) extra 0.75 ms teardown jobs at the tail (e.g. 8 instead of 4 for 100 bodies), not about twice the jobs. Fix it by iterating a copy, as forceDestroyLoadedRoomInsetBodies already does.
  
  Realistic saving is about 120-170 lines.

### F293: The editor UI bridge is 3 lines from its limit: split out the 300-line background-photo panel and use the existing listener helpers

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The file that connects the editor's buttons to the game is one of the files at its size limit. Two easy wins free about 400 lines. The custom background photo upload and browse feature is a self-contained 300-line block living inside it. And the 900-line set-up function wires 55 buttons by hand, even though small helper functions for exactly that already exist next door.

**Technical detail.**

uiBridge.ts is 2,254 non-blank lines against a cap of 2,257 (eslint.config.js:13). bindListeners (uiBridge.ts:580-1479) is a single 900-line method. It mixes 51 calls to the existing helpers in uiBridge/bindings.ts:13-75 (bindDomEvent, bindButton, bindNumericInput, bindRangeInput, bindTextInput) with 55 hand-written addEventListener/removeEventListener pairs. Examples: 581-585 and 586-591 (button click loops), 608-616 (checkbox change), 617-631 (select change and camera input), 632-642 (title input+change, which is exactly bindTextInput). Converting the manual pairs saves about 110 lines. Separately, applyBackgroundSelection, openBackgroundUploadPicker, refreshBackgroundImages, the photos modal, renderBackgroundPhotoGrid, sorting and fit, renderBackgroundUploadStatus, handleBackgroundUploadFileSelected (98 lines) and the upload modal (uiBridge.ts:1481-1830) form one feature with its own state. Move it to uiBridge/backgroundPhotos.ts behind a small {render(viewModel), destroy()} class, removing about 300 lines. Splitting bindListeners into per-panel binders (goal, lighting/weather, smart brush, music, inspector) would be a natural follow-up. Low risk. The DOM contract test (F072) guards the IDs.

**Evidence.**

- eslint.config.js:13 — 'src/scenes/editor/uiBridge.ts': 2257 (file has 2,254 non-blank lines)
- src/scenes/editor/uiBridge.ts:580-1479 — bindListeners, one 900-line method
- src/scenes/editor/uiBridge.ts:632-642 — hand-rolled input/change listeners identical to bindTextInput
- src/scenes/editor/uiBridge/bindings.ts:13-75 — helper binders that already exist
- src/scenes/editor/uiBridge.ts:1481-1830 — background photo upload/browse feature (about 300 lines)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Mechanism: only the 18 'click' pairs fit an existing helper (bindButton) unchanged. The other ~37 are element 'change' or 'input' listeners. bindDomEvent is typed Document|Window, and bindTextInput/bindNumericInput attach both input and change, which double-fires on checkboxes. First widen bindDomEvent's target to EventTarget, or add a bindChange helper; with that, the ~110-line saving holds. Background block: the photo/upload methods (1522-1830) are 286 non-blank lines, plus about 45 lines of bindings (1096-1140) and about 30 lines of chrome sync (2290-2320). applyBackgroundSelection (1481-1520) is the general background picker, not photo-only. The extracted class needs callbacks for onSelectBackground, syncEditorChromeState and requestPhoneEditorAutoCollapse, beyond render() and destroy(). The title-input evidence is at 633-642, not 632-642.

### F297: Undo and Redo are the same 108 lines pasted twice in the edit runtime

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The editor's Undo and Redo functions are identical except for which history list they read from and write to. Any fix to how undo restores tiles, objects, spawn, music or goals has to be made twice, and the file is 6 lines from its size limit. Folding them into one shared function removes about 100 lines with almost no risk, and existing history tests cover it.

**Technical detail.**

editRuntime.undo (editRuntime.ts:3272-3379) and redo (3381-3488) differ in exactly 8 lines, per diff: takeUndo↔takeRedo, pushRedo↔pushUndo ×6, and the replay label 'undo'/'redo'. Both branch over layout, tiles (with smartBefore/smartAfter swap), objects, spawn, music and goal, and build the inverse entry the same way. Refactor: `private applyHistoryEntry(entry: HistoryEntry): HistoryEntry` performs the restore and returns the inverse. Then `undo() { const e = this.history.takeUndo(); if (e) { recordReplayEditorAction('undo'); this.history.pushRedo(this.applyHistoryEntry(e)); } }` and redo is the mirror. That saves about 104 lines and gives editRuntime (cap 3,287, 3,281 non-blank) real headroom. Coverage: history.test.ts, smartHistory.test.ts, historyControls.test.ts and editRuntime.characterization.test.ts.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/editRuntime.ts:3272-3379 — undo(): takeUndo, then six pushRedo branches
- src/scenes/editor/editRuntime.ts:3381-3488 — redo(): identical body with takeRedo/pushUndo
- eslint.config.js:10 — editRuntime cap 3287 vs 3,281 non-blank lines

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** Undo and redo differ in 9 lines, not 8, once the method signature is counted. The saving is also a bit smaller than claimed. redo has 100 non-blank lines, and two thin wrappers (guardEditable, take, replay label, push the inverse) cost about 12, so the net is about 85-90 non-blank lines, not 104. That still raises editRuntime's headroom from 6 lines to about 90. The ESLint cap in eslint.config.js should be lowered to match. smartHistory.test.ts does not exercise undo/redo. The coverage that matters is editRuntime.characterization.test.ts.

### F277: Admin pages hand-roll the same API request about ten ways, and several still show raw {"error":…} text

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F063

**Summary.** The admin tools have a shared helper that sends the admin key and turns server errors into readable sentences, but most of the launch control room doesn't use it. Seven requests there, plus the photo review, public dashboard and jam pages, each wrote their own version. Some show the raw server reply such as {"error":"Invalid admin key."}. Routing them all through the shared helpers removes about 150 lines and makes every error readable.

**Technical detail.**

adminApiClient.ts:12-24 (createAdminResponseClient) already sets x-admin-key. adminApiClient.ts:26-46 (createAdminApiClient) also unwraps errors through readApiErrorMessage, the F063 fix. Yet launch/app.ts uses the response client and then re-sends the same header and reads raw text in 7 places: :283-295 (launch stats), :322-330 (game jams), :517-529, :557-566 (progression caps), :639-654, :689-700 and :736-754 (comment review). Each throws `response.text()`, and the worker returns errors as {error} JSON (worker/ops/errors.ts:13), so admins see JSON (~85 duplicated lines). background-admin.ts:364-383 has its own adminRequest with the same raw-text error. dashboard.ts:103-111, a public page, does the same. jam.ts:410-429 re-implements apiRequest plus readApiErrorMessage. Helpers are copied too: escapeHtml in 5 versions (launch/viewModel.ts:55, suspicious/app.ts:987, background-admin.ts:465, dashboard.ts:394, school-admin.ts:599; the last omits the single quote) and formatTimestamp 4 times (launch/app.ts:1829, suspicious/app.ts:948, background-admin.ts:448, dashboard.ts:385). The key-storage name 'ep_launch_admin_api_key' is spelled out in 6 files (launch/app.ts:39, suspicious/app.ts:20, worlds/app.ts:5, featuredRoomsClient.ts:4, bugReports.ts:16, replays.ts:8). Some wrap sessionStorage in try/catch and some don't. Fix: a src/admin/adminSession.ts with get/set/clear key (try/catch once) plus re-exported escapeHtml/formatTimestamp. Switch the 7 launch blocks and background-admin to createAdminApiClient().request, and dashboard and jam to apiRequest. background-admin.ts and custom-sprite-admin.ts are now launch-admin modules (launch/app.ts:22-23) and can move under src/admin/launch/.

**Evidence.**

- src/admin/adminApiClient.ts:26-46 — shared client already sets the key and unwraps JSON errors
- src/admin/launch/app.ts:283-295 — re-sends x-admin-key and throws raw response.text() (same pattern at :322, :517, :557, :639, :689, :736)
- src/cloudflare/worker/ops/errors.ts:13 — server errors are {error: message} JSON
- src/background-admin.ts:364-383 — separate adminRequest with raw-text errors
- src/dashboard.ts:103-111 — public dashboard shows raw response text on failure
- src/jam.ts:410-429 — requestJson re-implements apiRequest/readApiErrorMessage
- src/school-admin.ts:599-605 — fifth escapeHtml copy, without the single-quote escape
- src/admin/worlds/app.ts:5 — one of six copies of the 'ep_launch_admin_api_key' storage name

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real and small, but the scope needs fixing.
  - Only launch-admin (7 blocks: game-jams, progression search/load/save, comments load/review; launch-stats already maps 403), background-admin adminRequest and the public dashboard show raw `{"error":…}` JSON.
  - jam.ts requestJson already unwraps `.error`, so it is duplication only.
  - An invalid key reads "Admin key is required to …", not "Invalid admin key.".
  - escapeHtml has 8 client copies, not 5. The school-admin variant is harmless because it is only used in element text.
  - formatTimestamp copies differ: dashboard uses a custom Intl formatter.
  - Expect roughly 100 lines removed, not 150.
  - Also delete createAdminResponseClient once launch/app.ts stops using it.

### F290: Seven standalone pages hold ~2,300 lines of inline CSS and seven palettes; Classroom Login doesn't look like WAMP

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The admin, dashboard and school pages each paste a large block of styles into the page, each with its own colours and a different look: cream, dark blue or sky. That's about 2,300 lines. The students' Classroom Login and the teachers' School Admin page look like a developer tool rather than WAMP. The admin and jam pages also load the old, roughly 6x larger font files the game itself dropped. One shared page stylesheet built on the game's colour tokens would shrink this a lot and make the school pages feel like part of the game.

**Technical detail.**

Inline <style> line counts: launch-admin.html 1,188 (own :root palette re-declaring cream/paper/blue/yellow/red/ink, lines 30-50), dashboard.html 379, suspicious-admin.html 342 (dark-blue palette, :8-20), school-admin.html 181, school-login.html 97, background-admin.html 66, worlds-admin.html 33 (all hex literals). That is 2,286 lines, with 7 separate :root blocks. The same primitives are redefined with different looks in 3-4 pages each: .panel, .status, .status.error, button.secondary, button.danger, button:disabled, table/th/td, .controls, .masthead, .shell. school-login.html:31 and school-admin.html ask for "IBM Plex Sans", which no page loads, so students get a system-font dark form. Fonts: jam.css:1-17, launch-admin.html:11-28, worlds-admin.html:8-9, background-admin.html:11-17 and dashboard.html:11-14 load the TTF files (HomeVideo Regular 93,580 B + Bold 105,572 B + Early GameBoy 10,616 B = 209,768 B). The game uses WOFF2 (base.css:28-50; 15,680 + 16,508 + 2,868 = 35,056 B). The pattern for sharing already exists: minted-room.ts:13 imports styles/tokens.css. Fix: src/styles/pages/standalone.css that imports tokens.css plus a fonts.css (the @font-face block split out of base.css) and ~150 lines of shared page primitives, imported from each entry TS. Then delete the inline blocks page by page, starting with school-login/school-admin (user-facing, smallest) and the jam.css font-face swap (a 3-line change saving ~175 KB on the public jam page).

**Evidence.**

- launch-admin.html:30-50 — sixth copy of the WAMP palette as page-local variables
- suspicious-admin.html:8-20 — separate dark-blue palette
- school-login.html:31 — student login uses "IBM Plex Sans", which is never loaded
- worlds-admin.html:7-37 — inline CSS with hard-coded palette hex and TTF @font-face
- src/jam.css:1-17 — public jam page loads .ttf fonts (~210 KB) instead of the game's WOFF2 (~35 KB)
- src/styles/sections/base.css:28-50 — game's WOFF2 @font-face set
- src/minted-room.ts:13 — a standalone page already reuses styles/tokens.css

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Six :root blocks, not seven: worlds-admin uses only hex literals, and background-admin's :root sets no palette. There are three looks: WAMP cream (launch-admin, worlds-admin, background-admin), sky (dashboard) and dark dev-tool (suspicious-admin, school-admin, school-login, near-copies of each other).
  
  background-admin.html is just a redirect to launch-admin#photo-review. Cut its 64 lines down to a bare redirect instead of porting them.
  
  Shared primitives would replace about 150-250 of the ~2,286 lines, not "a lot". Most of launch-admin is styling for its own sections.
  
  The TTF-to-WOFF2 swap saves about 175 KB raw but only about 6 KB on the wire with brotli (41.4 KB vs 35.1 KB), or about 19 KB with gzip. The jam ended in July 2026, so traffic is low. The TTF files must stay because capture.ts and mapCaptureRender.mjs use them.
  
  Recommended scope:
  - Restyle school-login and school-admin with tokens.css and fonts the page actually loads.
  - Swap the jam.css and admin @font-face rules to WOFF2.
  - Extend scripts/check_shared_styles.mjs (today it scans only src/styles/) to cover inline HTML styles and src/*.css.
  - Leave folding the admin-only pages into a shared sheet as optional.

### F280: Explore, Profile and Collection each carry their own lazy room-thumbnail loader (~260 lines)

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Room thumbnails in Explore, on profiles and in a collector's list load only when you scroll to them, which is good. But the code that does this is written out three times with small differences: different placeholder text, and one version never stops watching cards it threw away. One shared helper would cut about 190 lines and make all three behave the same.

**Technical detail.**

exploreModal.ts:159-180 builds an IntersectionObserver, and :1025-1124 hold attachRoomPreview, loadAndApplyRoomPreview, applyRoomPreview, loadRoomPreview and buildRoomPreviewKey (~120 lines). profileModal.ts:1532-1670 repeats the same steps as observeRoomPreview, getRoomPreviewObserver, getIntersectionObserverConstructor, resetRoomPreviewObserver, attachRoomPreview, applyRoomPreview, loadRoomPreview and buildRoomPreviewKey (~140 lines). The steps: cache check through getSharedRenderedRoomPreview, fallback text, observe with rootMargin, stale-guard on dataset.previewKey, then apply. profileCollection.ts:92-110 is a third, compact copy. The copies have drifted. Profile resets its observer on every render (profileModal.ts:1289), while Explore only disconnects in destroy (exploreModal.ts:258) and never unobserves cards discarded when the list re-renders with a new filter or tab. Fallback text differs between 'Preview', 'Loading preview...', coordinates and the room title. Fix: src/ui/roomPreviewLoader.ts exporting createLazyRoomPreviews({ load(room), key(room), fallbackText(room) }) with observe(previewEl, imageEl, fallbackEl, room) and reset(). That is about 60 lines, and the three call sites become ~10 lines each. It also takes ~130 lines off profileModal.ts, which is pinned at the max-lines ratchet (eslint.config.js:22, 1556).

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:159-180 — Explore's own IntersectionObserver setup
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:1025-1124 — Explore's attach/load/apply/key preview pipeline
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:1532-1670 — Profile's near-identical preview pipeline
- src/ui/setup/profileCollection.ts:92-110 — third copy for the collection tab
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:258 — Explore disconnects only on destroy; Profile resets per render (profileModal.ts:1289)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** There are four copies, not three: playlistModal.ts:258-307 repeats the same cache/stale-guard/apply/key pipeline without lazy loading. Explore's shared portion is about 95 lines; the 1025-1124 range includes the guest-draft renderer and title helpers, which stay. The Explore "never unobserves discarded cards" point is cosmetic, not a leak: targets are in a WeakMap, detached nodes never intersect, and browsers do not keep observed targets alive. Expect about 150-170 net lines saved (about 120 of them in profileModal.ts, which sits exactly at its 1556 max-lines ratchet). The helper needs key(room), fallbackText(room) and an optional shouldLoad() guard to keep the collection tab's wallet gate.

### F292: Small helpers are copied file to file: 8 array-chunkers, 5 HTML escapers, 3 minted-room queries, 7 ad-hoc page-size parsers

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** About 30 copy-pasted helpers in the Worker, including three copies of the minted-room protection lookup

**Summary.** Many small utility functions are copied into the file that needs them instead of being shared. Each copy is harmless alone, but some have already drifted: the copies that check whether a room is minted use two different tests, and page-size handling either rejects bad input or quietly fixes it depending on the route. Moving them into a few shared modules removes about 150 lines and keeps behavior consistent.

**Technical detail.**

chunkArray/chunkValues: 8 copies (rooms/store.ts:525, worldTiles/store.ts:1202, admin/suspicious.ts:1498, admin/suspiciousInvalidation.ts:880, runs/difficulty.ts:1498, profiles/store.ts:751, expandedRooms/store.ts:952, runs/discoveryViewerStates.ts:204). parseRowNumber is exported from progression/shared.ts:235 yet re-declared in difficulty.ts:1592, playlists/store.ts:894 and discoveryViewerStates.ts:212. roundQuality (shared.ts:247) is re-declared in difficulty.ts:1588 and profiles/store.ts:759. escapeHtml has 5 byte-identical copies (share/routes.ts:414, chat/mentions.ts:242, worlds/notifications.ts:135, admin/reviewNotifications.ts:131, auth/store.ts:1532). loadProtectedMintedRoomIds has 3 copies (expandedRooms/store.ts:850, editorRoutes.ts:391, writeStore.ts:251); one uses a local isMintedDatabaseRow, the other two use isRoomMinted from persistence/roomModel. normalizeDisplayName has 5 copies in two variants (auth/routes.ts:668, profiles/routes.ts:214, agents/routes.ts:210 vs guestRoomDrafts/routes.ts:201, guestActivity/routes.ts:157). There are 5 cursor codecs (rooms/store.ts:498, profiles/store.ts:344, music/store.ts:167, customSprites/catalogStore.ts:433, runs/difficultyModel.ts:39). core/http.ts:272 has parsePositiveIntegerQueryParam, but 7 routes parse limit themselves with different outcomes: collections/routes.ts:11-12 returns 400, admin/routes.ts:501-504 clamps, guestRoomDrafts/routes.ts:230 and customSprites/adminRoutes.ts:50 use local parseLimit, and profiles/routes.ts:73 uses parseBoundedInteger.

Fix: add core/collections.ts (chunk), core/sqlRows.ts (parseRowNumber, roundQuality), core/html.ts (escapeHtml), core/cursor.ts (base64 JSON codec) and expandedRooms/mintedCells.ts (one loader using isRoomMinted), and switch the 7 limit parsers to parsePositiveIntegerQueryParam. A lint rule (no-restricted-syntax on `function chunk|escapeHtml|parseRowNumber`) keeps new copies out.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:525 — one of 8 chunkArray/chunkValues copies
- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/shared.ts:235 — exported parseRowNumber, re-declared at runs/difficulty.ts:1592
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:1532 — one of 5 identical escapeHtml copies
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/store.ts:850 — minted-room loader with its own predicate; copies at editorRoutes.ts:391 and writeStore.ts:251
- src/cloudflare/worker/collections/routes.ts:12 — hand-rolled limit check returns 400, while admin/routes.ts:503 clamps
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/http.ts:272 — shared parsePositiveIntegerQueryParam already exists
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/writeStore.ts:251 — loadProtectedMintedRoomIds copy 1
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/store.ts:850 — loadProtectedMintedRoomIds copy 2 (same SQL, same isRoomMinted predicate)
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts:391 — loadProtectedMintedRoomIds copy 3
- src/cloudflare/worker/jam/routes.ts:326-331 — getRequestIp falls back to X-Forwarded-For
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/rateLimit.ts:13-16 — shared getClientIp uses CF-Connecting-IP only
- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/shared.ts:235 — exported parseRowNumber that 3 other files re-implement

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The duplication is real: 8 chunk helpers, 5 identical Worker escapeHtml copies, 2 roundQuality copies, 3 minted-room loaders and 5 normalizeDisplayName copies in 2 deliberate variants. There is no drift in the minted check: all three loaders call isRoomMinted, one through a wrapper. The parseRowNumber local copies (and profiles/store.ts parseRatingRowNumber) are NaN-safe, but the exported shared.ts one is not. The fix is to harden shared.ts parseRowNumber to return 0 for non-finite values and then delete the copies, not to switch the copies to the current shared version. The cursor helpers use 4 wire formats, so only the 2-3 JSON ones can share a codec. There are 8 hand-rolled limit parsers, not 7, and 7 of them already return 400; only an admin-only route clamps. Replace guestRoomDrafts parseLimit, profiles parseBoundedInteger, collections, publishedGoalIssues and parseRoomVersionLimit with parsePositiveIntegerQueryParam. The customSprites parsers need their store default and maximum first. Leave the two normalizeDisplayName variants separate, or share them as two named helpers. Drop the jam XFF item; it is unreachable behind Cloudflare.

### F294: The July jam's sign-up and submit endpoints have returned 'closed' since July 28, and carry a second Turnstile check with a different secret name

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: Worker and data layer)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F216

**Summary.** The one-off July game jam's registration and submission code (about 520 server lines and part of the jam page) can only answer "closed" now. Its copy of the bot check reads a differently named secret from the guestbook's copy of the same check. The setup docs mention only the jam's name, so a server set up from the docs would make the guestbook reject every signature. Retiring the jam's write paths, or making them reusable under the open jam item, and keeping one bot-check helper fixes both.

**Technical detail.**

jam/routes.ts:69-71 and 164-169: registration throws 410 after JAM_SUBMISSIONS_CLOSE_AT (wrangler.jsonc:34, 2026-07-28). jam/routes.ts:109 and 171-180: submissions also 410. The write paths account for about 290 of jam/routes.ts's 346 lines, and all of jam/store.ts (227 lines; only upsertJamRegistration and upsertJamSubmission, both called only from those routes), plus the form logic in src/jam.ts:87-160. Weekly Build Prompts (F128) replaced the event.

Duplicated helpers: verifyTurnstileToken exists in jam/routes.ts:292-324, reading env.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, and in guestbook/routes.ts:245-290, reading env.TURNSTILE_SECRET. Both share TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY. docs/development/environment.md:64-65 documents only TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY. With the site key set and TURNSTILE_SECRET unset, the guestbook throws 503 'Turnstile verification is unavailable' on every signature (guestbook/routes.ts:252-255). getRequestIp, normalizeHeaderValue and a salted hash*Ip are copied in jam (326-346), guestbook (297-317) and roomComments (448-472). core/rateLimit.ts:13-16 and 51-55 already provide getClientIp and hashRateLimitKey. The copies fall back to X-Forwarded-For, which rateLimit.ts deliberately avoids.

Fix: move one verifyTurnstile(env, token, ip) into core/ that reads TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, falls back to TURNSTILE_SECRET during transition, and is documented. Use core getClientIp/hash in all three modules. Then either delete the jam write routes, jam/store.ts and the jam page form (keeping GET /api/jam and admin/gameJams.ts reads for the archive), or fold them into the generic jam work tracked by F216.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/jam/routes.ts:167 — registration returns 410 after July 28
- wrangler.jsonc:35 — JAM_SUBMISSIONS_CLOSE_AT 2026-07-28T12:00:00Z
- src/cloudflare/worker/jam/routes.ts:298 — jam Turnstile reads env.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestbook/routes.ts:251 — guestbook Turnstile reads env.TURNSTILE_SECRET
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestbook/routes.ts:254 — guestbook returns 503 when site key is set but TURNSTILE_SECRET is not
- docs/development/environment.md:65 — docs list only TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/rateLimit.ts:13 — shared getClientIp already exists; three modules copy their own

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The dead jam write paths (jam/routes.ts write half plus jam/store.ts, about 520 lines, and more of src/jam.ts than 87-160) and the Turnstile secret mismatch are both real. Scope it as follows:
  - **Docs:** only docs/development/environment.md lists TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY alone. .env.example:73-74 lists both names with no explanation. The guestbook 503 happens only when someone sets the site key without TURNSTILE_SECRET.
  - **Evidence line:** wrangler.jsonc:34, not :35.
  - **X-Forwarded-For:** unreachable in production (CF-Connecting-IP is always set), so this is consistency, not security.
  - **Verifier:** keep the guestbook's version (it has the 503 guard, try/catch and 403s), moved into core/, reading TURNSTILE_SECRET with TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY as a fallback. Fix environment.md, .env.example and core/types.ts, and remove the dead Turnstile fields from GET /api/jam.
  - **Hashes:** switching to hashRateLimitKey changes the salts and stored ip_hash values, which resets the guestbook's per-IP count once. That's acceptable.
  - **Jam page:** jam.html still renders a disabled form and a live 'Create account' button, so it needs an archive rewrite. Keep GET /api/jam for scripts/smoke_mint_network.mjs.

### F286: Old-name pass-through files (music/model.ts and pvp/model.ts) re-export about 100 names nobody imports from them

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Dead code: game client)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Two renames were never finished. 'PvP' became 'Multiplayer', and music code moved into separate pattern, phrase and key files. Both times a pass-through file was left behind that re-exports everything under the old names. 16 files still import the old PvP names, and most of the music pass-through list is never used. Pointing imports at the real files and deleting the pass-throughs removes about 180 lines and the confusion of having two names for the same thing.

**Technical detail.**

src/pvp/model.ts (57 lines) is nothing but `export { MULTIPLAYER_* as PVP_* }` and `export type { Multiplayer* as Pvp* }` from ../multiplayer/model. knip flags 26 of its names as unused, including PVP_ARENA_HEARTS, PVP_COUNTDOWN_MS, PvpMatchHitMessage and PvpInviteOfferMessage. 16 files import it, among them partykit/presenceServer.ts, src/partykit/presenceProtocol.ts, src/presence/worldPresence.ts, src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts and src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts. Rewrite those imports to the Multiplayer* names and delete the file.

src/music/model.ts:21-131 is about 110 lines of `export { ... } from './key' / './pattern' / './phraseArrangement'`. knip flags 70 exports in this file. Most re-exported names (ROOM_PATTERN_*, clone*/createEmpty* helpers, ROOM_PHRASE_ARRANGEMENT_*) are imported straight from pattern.ts or phraseArrangement.ts by every consumer. Keep only the re-exports that the 17 importers of music/model actually use, or point those imports at the source modules.

src/scenes/courseEditor/inspectorUi.ts (11 lines) re-exports editor/inspectorViewModel.ts with one rename. 4 of its names are unused, including getPressurePlateTargetLabel, whose 28-line implementation at inspectorViewModel.ts:122-149 has no caller at all. CourseEditorScene.ts:168 and courseEditor/objectInspector.ts:41 can import inspectorViewModel directly.

This is purely mechanical; tsc confirms each step.

**Evidence.**

- src/pvp/model.ts:1-57 — whole file is renamed re-exports of ../multiplayer/model
- src/music/model.ts:21-131 — re-export blocks from key/pattern/phraseArrangement
- src/scenes/courseEditor/inspectorUi.ts:1-11 — re-export shim with one rename
- src/scenes/editor/inspectorViewModel.ts:122 — getPressurePlateTargetLabel, reachable only via the unused re-export

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Keep src/music/model.ts. It is a real 475-line module, and 42 of its 102 same-name re-exports are used by about 15 importers. Delete only the 60 unused re-export lines, or point those importers at pattern.ts/phraseArrangement.ts/key.ts if a fully explicit layout is wanted. pvp/model.ts is 55 lines with 17 importers (src/pvp/repository.ts is the 17th) using 24 of its 51 names. Rewrite them to the Multiplayer* names and delete the file. For inspectorUi.ts, point its 2 importers at inspectorViewModel, delete the shim and the dead getPressurePlateTargetLabel, and un-export getContainerLabel, which is used internally. ### F295: The object palette's five filter-tab rows are five copies of the same code (~140 lines)

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** In the editor's object picker, the sub-filter rows (custom objects, decoration groups, vines, tree types, tree families) each have their own copy of the code that handles clicks, highlights the active tab and validates the choice. One small reusable 'tab row' piece would replace about 140 lines with about 40, and make the next filter row a one-liner.

**Technical detail.**

paletteController.ts (1,782 lines, pinned at the max-lines ratchet: eslint.config.js:21, 1590 non-blank) has five bind*Tabs methods (:780-850). Each loops its tab array, normalizes a dataset value, resets dependent filters, then calls resetObjectGridScroll, renderObjectSubcategoryTabs and renderObjectGrid. renderObjectSubcategoryTabs (:852-908) has five identical loops toggling .active and aria-pressed. There are five normalize* methods (:1631-1660) that are the same `list.includes(value) ? value : 'all'` check. Fix: a FilterTabGroup<T> helper ({ tabs, datasetKey, values, get, set, resets, visible }) with bind() and render() (~40 lines). The controller then declares five groups and ~100 lines go away. Lowering the ratchet entry for this file afterwards locks in the gain.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:780-850 — five near-identical bind*Tabs methods
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:878-907 — five identical active/aria-pressed loops
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:1631-1660 — five identical normalize* guards
- eslint.config.js:21 — file is grandfathered at 1590 lines by the max-lines ratchet

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F300: Worlds Worker carries about 70 lines of dead or copy-pasted code, and seed saves parse every grant's 2.5 MB draft twice

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Gap review: Classroom accounts and Worlds: routes added since the F209 fix)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Some World helpers are never used. The new-World defaults are typed out by hand in two places while an unused constant holds the same values. The entitlement query is copied four times. Looking up one World grant loads and parses every grant's saved seed room, so each seed-editor autosave parses up to 2.5 MB of JSON at least twice. All of these are small, safe deletions or merges.

**Technical detail.**

Dead code:
- requireWorldForMutation (worlds/access.ts:191-207, 17 lines): no callers; it duplicates resolveWorldMutationAccess's Prime and frozen checks.
- DEFAULT_WORLD_SETTINGS (worlds/store.ts:550-555): unused, while activation hardcodes 'request_to_join', 'approval_required', 5, 10 at worlds/activation.ts:112 and repeats 5, 10 at 172.
- D1WorldEntitlementProvider.activate (worlds/entitlements.ts:12-14): never called. adminRoutes uses only reactivate and freeze, so the whole 23-line wrapper could become direct setWorldEntitlementStatus calls.

Duplication:
- The 10-line entitlement SELECT appears 4 times (store.ts:249, 348, 365, 518) and can become one constant.
- listEntitlementsForUser(...).find(id) is used as a by-id lookup at store.ts:338, 407 and 417. mapEntitlement JSON-parses and clones every row's seed_draft_json (263-270), and seed drafts can be up to 2.5 MB (routes.ts:270). saveWorldSeedDraft parses all of a user's drafts twice per autosave, via requireOwnedUnactivatedEntitlement (411-420) and again at 407. Use loadWorldEntitlementById plus an owner check.
- The claim block in saveDraft and publishRoom is identical (rooms/store.ts:903-912 and 1048-1057), and so are the prepareRoomMutationGuards arguments (932-935, 1089-1092). Extract `assertClaimAllowed(world, …)`.
- saveDraft and publishRoom each check the World policy and then existing.permissions, which for World rooms is the same policy (store.ts:881-890, 1006-1020). For WAMP 0 rooms the two checks come from different permission systems, which is the root of the World-id finding.

Total: roughly 60-70 lines removed, and no seed-JSON parsing on lookups.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/access.ts:191-207 — requireWorldForMutation has no callers
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/store.ts:550-555 — DEFAULT_WORLD_SETTINGS unused
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/activation.ts:112 — defaults hardcoded in SQL
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/activation.ts:172 — limits hardcoded again
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/entitlements.ts:12-14 — activate() never called
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/store.ts:407-420 — by-id lookups that parse every grant's seed draft
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:903-912 — claim block duplicated at 1048-1057

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The dead code and duplication are real. Delete requireWorldForMutation. Either use DEFAULT_WORLD_SETTINGS (bound values, or DEFAULT_WORLD_CLAIM_LIMIT and DEFAULT_WORLD_PUBLISH_LIMIT) in activation.ts:112/172 or delete it. Share the entitlement SELECT prefix. Extract the World/WAMP 0 claim block used by saveDraft and publishRoom. Keep D1WorldEntitlementProvider and its activate(): the interface requires it, and it is the documented boundary for billing. The seed-draft cost is small, not 2.5 MB per grant: usually one grant with a normal room, parsed twice per autosave. loadWorldEntitlementById would not remove that parsing because it uses the same mapEntitlement. The real fix is a lookup without the seed column for the owner and not-yet-activated check, plus building the save response from the snapshot already in memory. Expect about 40-55 lines removed, not 60-70.

### F284: Map-screenshot video export uses untested copies of its date/frame logic while the tested versions are never called

- **Area:** Superfluous and duplicated code (reviewer: Dead code: game client)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The admin map-screenshot gallery has a 'make a video' tool. Its date-range, frame-rate and duration logic was written twice: once as tested TypeScript helpers and once inside the gallery page's own script. The page uses only its own copy, which has no tests, and the tested helpers are never used. Pick one copy, preferably by bundling the tested helpers into the page, so the tests cover what actually runs.

**Technical detail.**

src/mapScreenshot/video.ts has selectVideoFrames (8-26), videoDurationSeconds (28-33), formatVideoDuration (35-41), clampVideoFps (43-49) and htmlDateToEasternDate (63-68). All are exercised by video.test.ts, and none has a production caller: galleryHtml.ts imports only DEFAULT/MIN/MAX_VIDEO_FPS, earliestAndLatestDates and easternDateToHtmlDate (galleryHtml.ts:7-13).

The gallery's inline script reimplements them as plain JS strings: framesInRange (galleryHtml.ts:225-231), formatDuration (233-239) and fps validation (247), which rejects out-of-range values where the TS version clamps. A fix to one copy will not reach the other.

Other test-only or unused pieces in the same worker:
- naming.ts:32-51 dailyScreenshotFileName, manualScreenshotFileName and parseManualIndex (test-only).
- infoOverlay.ts:61-64 and 84-100 CORNER_MARK_* and buildFontFaceCss.
- bounds.ts:64-70 and 101-102.
- config.ts:31 and 36.
- testBucket.ts, a test fixture living in src.
About 100 lines in total.

Fix: serve video.ts to the gallery as a small module, either by building it with the worker or by inlining the esbuild output of video.ts into the page. Then delete the inline copies, or delete the unused TS versions and their tests if you'd rather keep the inline script.

**Evidence.**

- src/mapScreenshot/video.ts:8-49 — selectVideoFrames/videoDurationSeconds/formatVideoDuration/clampVideoFps, test-only
- src/mapScreenshot/galleryHtml.ts:7-13 — gallery imports only constants and two date helpers from video.ts
- src/mapScreenshot/galleryHtml.ts:225-247 — inline framesInRange, formatDuration and fps validation duplicate the TS helpers

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real but smaller than stated: about 80 lines of dead or test-only code in src/mapScreenshot:
  - video.ts: selectVideoFrames, videoDurationSeconds, formatVideoDuration, clampVideoFps, htmlDateToEasternDate.
  - naming.ts: dailyScreenshotFileName, manualScreenshotFileName, parseManualIndex.
  - infoOverlay.ts: CORNER_MARK_*, buildFontFaceCss.
  - bounds.ts:64-70 and 101-102.
  - config.ts:36 GAME_TILE_PX.
  
  The gallery's inline script (galleryHtml.ts:217-247) duplicates the video helpers without tests, but the two copies currently behave the same: clampVideoFps throws on bad values rather than clamping, just as the inline check rejects them. Leave testBucket.ts alone; it is a used vitest fixture.
  
  Do not delete MAX_MANUAL_SHOTS_PER_DAY. Instead, make lease.ts:21-24 use it and the naming helpers in place of the hardcoded [1..9] and its own regex, so the documented tunable actually works.
  
  Preferred fix: delete the unused TS helpers and their tests, rather than adding a client build for the Worker-served gallery. If tests matter, cover the inline script through http.test.ts or inject the helpers with toString(). Also, the gallery is public, not admin.

### F301: Rooms with custom tiles re-check the whole custom tile list on every tile lookup, costing milliseconds per frame

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** high · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a room uses custom tiles, the game re-validates every custom tile, pixel by pixel, each time it asks what a single tile is. That happens on every frame the player runs across a custom-tile floor, while building the room's picture and collision, and when sword enemies plan their moves. On this desktop one lookup takes 0.6 ms with 32 custom tiles and 2.5 ms with 128, and phones are several times slower, so these rooms stutter while you run and hitch when you enter them. Cleaning the tile list once per room and reusing it fixes every caller at once.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: getCustomRoomTileDefinitionForGid (src/customTiles/model.ts:57-66) calls normalizeCustomRoomTileDefinitions(room.customTiles) on every call. That walks up to 128 tiles (model.ts:83-100). For each tile, normalizeCustomRoomTileDefinition (:104-130) rebuilds the object, calls new Date().toISOString(), and runs normalizeTilePixels (:183-199): an Array.from of 256 entries, each tested with a regex and lower-cased. getCustomRoomTileCollisionProfile (:69-79) goes through the same path. Non-custom gids return early, so only custom-tile cells pay.

Hot callers:
- Every running frame: movementController.ts:610-611 → tryApplySingleTileGapAssist (:1362-1406) → isSolidTerrainTileAtFoot (:1437-1453) → OverworldPlayScene.isSolidTerrainAtWorldPoint (:3426-3442) → terrainTileCollidesAtLocalPixel → getTerrainTileCollisionProfile (terrainCollision.ts:76-88) → :139. That is 1-2 probes per grounded frame.
- Also per projectile hit (OverworldPlayScene.ts:3389) and the swordsman probes (swordsmanController.ts:747/2688/2714/2836; swordsmanTraversal.ts has 12 call sites).
- Room build: fullRoomPresenter.ts:329 and :440-445 make about 3 lookups per custom cell.
- Room snapshot rows: roomSnapshotTexture.ts:450 makes 1 lookup per cell per layer, in 2-row jobs budgeted at 0.5 ms (worldStreaming.ts:135, :3926-3931). Chunk previews use the same path (chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:1090).
- Editor: edgeGuides.ts:35 and clearCheck.
- Worker share image: roomPreviewImage.ts:278 and :287 make 2 lookups per custom terrain cell, so this costs Worker CPU too.

Measured with tsx against the real module on an Apple-silicon desktop (scratch bench-collide.ts / bench-customtiles.ts), cost per terrain probe on a custom cell:
- 8 tiles: 0.157 ms
- 32 tiles: 0.617 ms
- 128 tiles: 2.524 ms

One snapshot pass of lookups alone:
- 16 tiles / 200 cells: 85 ms
- 32 tiles / 400 cells: 241 ms
- 128 tiles / 880 cells: 2,173 ms

At a 3-5x phone slowdown, running on a 32-tile floor costs about 2-6 ms per frame, and each 2-row texture job in such a room takes 100-250 ms instead of 0.5 ms.

Fix (small):
1. Memoize the normalized list in a WeakMap keyed by the customTiles array. To be safe against in-place editor mutation (the runtime.ts:51-53 comment says the editor may mutate the source array), validate the cache with length plus each tile's updatedAt, or normalize once when the snapshot is ingested.
2. Also build a gid→profile array (128 entries) per room.
Expected cost per lookup drops to well under 1 µs. Add a unit test that calls getCustomRoomTileCollisionProfile 10k times on a 128-tile room under a time bound, or that asserts normalize is called once.

**Evidence.**

- src/customTiles/model.ts:57-66 — getCustomRoomTileDefinitionForGid calls normalizeCustomRoomTileDefinitions(room.customTiles) on every lookup
- src/customTiles/model.ts:183-199 — each tile's 256 pixels are re-created and regex-tested per normalization
- src/customTiles/model.ts:69-79 — collision profile lookups take the same path
- src/scenes/overworld/terrainCollision.ts:76-88,139 — getTerrainTileCollisionProfile → getCustomRoomTileCollisionProfile per probe
- src/scenes/overworld/movementController.ts:610-611,1345-1359,1437-1453 — gap-assist foot probes run every grounded frame while moving
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:3426-3442 — isSolidTerrainAtWorldPoint → terrainTileCollidesAtLocalPixel
- src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:450 — per-cell lookup while drawing room snapshot rows
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:135 — PREPARED_TEXTURE_ROWS_PER_JOB = 2 (jobs budgeted at 0.5 ms, :3926-3931)
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:278,287 — the Worker share image makes two lookups per custom terrain cell
- scratch bench (tsx, real module): 0.157 / 0.617 / 2.524 ms per probe at 8 / 32 / 128 custom tiles

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** The defect is real, and the cost grows linearly at about 18 µs (desktop) per custom tile in the room's list, for every lookup on a custom-tile cell. The headline "milliseconds per frame while running" holds only for rooms with many custom tiles. Gap assist plus the other movement probes make 1-3 lookups per frame. With 1-4 tiles that is about 0.02-0.2 ms on desktop and well under 1 ms on a phone. It reaches 2-6 ms on a phone only at about 16-32 tiles.
  
  The bigger and more common cost is the hitch when a room is built or previewed. The collision passes alone make about 3-6 lookups per custom cell. With only 4 tiles and 200 custom cells, that is about 84 ms of collision work plus 16 ms of snapshot drawing on desktop, roughly 3-5x that on a phone. A single 2-row texture job takes about 6 ms against its 0.5 ms estimate. Overworld chunk previews pay the same cost per visible custom-tile room.
  
  Overstated or cached paths:
  - Swordsman surface scans are cached per room version, not per frame.
  - Weather surfaces are cached.
  - The Worker share image is edge-cached for 24 h, so its CPU cost is per cache miss only.
  
  Fix:
  - Memoize normalizeCustomRoomTileDefinitions with a WeakMap keyed by the customTiles array. This is safe because editRuntime replaces the array rather than mutating it.
  - Optionally keep a gid→profile array per room.
- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F305: Sword Hunters and police re-search every possible route on every frame while chasing you

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a Sword Hunter or police enemy chases the player onto a different platform, it works out its route from scratch on every single frame by listing every possible 1-, 2- and 3-jump path through the room. In a room with lots of ledges that is about 1,000 paths and several thousand throwaway objects per enemy per frame. Three chasing enemies can use most of a phone's frame budget, which shows up as stutter exactly during fights. The enemies should reuse their route for a fraction of a second (the newer planner already does) and the search should stop copying lists for every path.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: updateSwordsmanDuelObjective -> runSwordsmanTraversalObjective (swordsmanController.ts:362) calls getSwordsmanTraversalDecision up to three times per enemy per frame (:855, :863, :872). In the default 'classic' mode (OverworldPlayScene.ts:5021-5024; only collect-mode uses 'robust') this always reaches decideSwordsmanTraversal (:1083), which calls findBestTraversalPath (swordsmanTraversal.ts:274). That function (:1074-1144) is a breadth-first enumeration of every simple path up to MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH = 3 (:153) with no cross-path pruning; every queued path allocates an object, a copied edges array, a spread temp array and a new Set (:1135-1139). There is no replan interval, unlike the robust planner's 900 ms commit / 420 ms replan (swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:92-93). Chase only starts inside 240x176 px (swordsmanController.ts:86-87) and far enemies sleep, so the cost is concentrated in active combat.

Measured (scratch vitest bench, Node 22 on an M-series Mac; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jonathanmann-SongADAO-Dropbox-Jonathan-Mann-projects-games-everybodys-platformer/cfd92898-41f7-4501-8041-0f41609c86da/scratchpad/audit-tmp/perf/planner.bench.test.ts): a room with 5 rows of 3-tile ledges (39 surfaces) builds a graph of 117 nodes / 570 edges (avg out-degree 4.9). One decision enumerates 328 paths from the ground (0.14-0.19 ms) and 1,053 paths from a mid ledge (0.54-1.03 ms), i.e. roughly 1,300-4,200 short-lived objects per call. A sparse 14-ledge room costs 0.009-0.014 ms and ~13 KB per call. At 60 fps one chasing enemy on a mid ledge produces ~250,000 allocations/s; three such enemies are ~1.5-3 ms/frame on desktop and, at a typical 4-5x phone slowdown (estimate), most of a 16.7 ms frame.

Fix plan: (1) memoize the classic decision per enemy keyed on graph.cacheKey + currentNodeId + targetNodeId + blocked-edge set, refreshed at most every ~200 ms or on node change (same policy the robust planner uses); (2) make the enumeration allocation-free: depth <= 3 means visited fits in a 4-slot array and edges can be tracked by parent index instead of copying; (3) reuse one Set in getSwordsmanBlockedTraversalEdgeIds (:2307-2315), which currently filters and builds a new Set per call. Keep the exact enumeration order so existing swordsman traversal tests stay equivalent. Expected: <0.02 ms and near-zero garbage per enemy per frame.

**Evidence.**

- src/enemies/swordsmanTraversal.ts:1074-1144 — findBestTraversalPath enumerates every simple path, no pruning across paths
- src/enemies/swordsmanTraversal.ts:1135-1139 — each queued path allocates an object, [...current.edges, edge] and new Set([...current.visited, edge.toId])
- src/enemies/swordsmanTraversal.ts:153 — MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH = 3
- src/enemies/swordsmanTraversal.ts:274 — decideSwordsmanTraversal runs the full search on every call
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:1083 — classic decision always calls decideSwordsmanTraversal (no cache or replan interval)
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:855-877 — up to three traversal decisions per enemy per frame
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:5021-5024 — classic planner is the default unless ?swordHunterPlanner=robust
- src/enemies/swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:92-93 — the robust planner already has 900 ms commit / 420 ms replan intervals
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:2307-2315 — blocked-edge Set rebuilt with filter+map on each decision

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Real, but narrower and smaller than stated. Normally there is 1 classic decision per enemy per frame; the 2nd and 3rd calls happen only after a fallback block or a route-loop event. The search runs only when the enemy and player are on different surfaces inside the 240x176 chase box, and not during windup, attack or cooldown. The cost depends heavily on how many ledges the room has:
  - Typical sparse rooms: about 0.005-0.015 ms per call.
  - Dense ledge grids (about 39 surfaces): 0.15-0.4 ms per call on desktop.
  - Three hunters chasing in a dense room: about 1.2 ms per frame on desktop, an estimated 5-6 ms on phones. That is about a third of the frame budget, not most of it, plus GC churn.
  
  Fix order: first make findBestTraversalPath allocation-free, which keeps behavior exactly the same. That means parent-index paths, a small fixed visited array, an index cursor instead of queue.shift(), and the same strict-< tie order. Any memoization should cache only the chosen path or first edge for a short window, invalidated when the enemy's or target's node changes or the blocked set changes. The decision itself must be rebuilt from live positions each frame, because scoreTraversalPathEntry and buildSwordsmanTraversalDecisionFromEdge depend on the exact enemy and target X positions. Reusing the blocked-edge Set is a minor extra.
- **partially confirmed.** Real, but scope it as follows.
  
  Severity: one search per chasing enemy per frame. The 2nd and 3rd calls only happen on fallback-block or route-loop events. It is skipped on the same surface, outside the 240x176 chase box, during windup/attack/cooldown, and in collect mode (which uses the robust planner).
  
  Cost by room type:
  - Dense ledge-grid rooms (about 40 surfaces): about 1,000 paths and 0.5-0.85 ms per enemy per frame on desktop, so stutter is plausible with 2-3 chasers on phones.
  - Typical rooms (about 15-20 surfaces): 50-160 paths, 0.02-0.06 ms per call. The main cost there is 45-145 KB of garbage per call, so GC churn rather than frame time.
  
  Impact is medium, not high.
  
  Fix priority: make the change that keeps behavior identical first. Make findBestTraversalPath allocation-free: parent-index edges, a fixed 4-slot visited array, an index-based queue instead of shift(), and the same enumeration order. Also stop rebuilding the blocked-edge Set every call.
  
  Treat memoization as optional. scoreTraversalPathEntry and buildSwordsmanTraversalDecisionFromEdge depend on the enemy's x position, so any cache should store the path but rebuild the decision from its first edge each frame, and invalidate on node change or blocked-set change.
- **partially confirmed.** The per-frame, allocation-heavy depth-3 path enumeration in the classic planner is real and is the default for duel and police enemies. But it costs about 1 ms per call only in very dense rooms (about 40 ledges, about 1,000 paths from a mid ledge). In a typical room it costs 0.006-0.02 ms. It only runs while enemy and player stand on different surfaces inside the 240x176 chase range, and usually once per frame, not three times. Impact is medium (worst-case stutter in dense multi-enemy rooms), not high.
  
  Fix plan:
  - Do step (2) first. Rewrite findBestTraversalPath as a level-ordered nested loop (e1; e1,e2; e1,e2,e3) with no per-path arrays or Sets, a per-call node base-score memo and entry scores hoisted per first edge. The score is endScore(node) + 72*depth + entryScore(firstEdge), so results are identical. A prototype matched the old function on 1,482 of 1,482 cases and ran 4-11x faster.
  - Add a new equivalence test that uses the old implementation as the oracle. There are no existing tests for decideSwordsmanTraversal.
  - Treat memoization as optional. Never cache the whole decision, because its direction, targetX and jump velocities depend on live positions. Cache at most the chosen first edge and rebuild the decision each frame, accepting a behaviour change that needs playtesting.
  - Reusing the blocked-edge Set is a trivial extra.
