### F302: Coin-collecting Sword Hunters can freeze the game for a moment when they first plan, and re-plan every frame when coins are out of reach

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Builders can set a Sword Hunter to collect coins. The first time one plans a route in a room, it test-simulates every jump in the room on the spot, which took 160-190 ms on a fast Mac in a busy test room, so likely most of a second on a phone. If the coins it has left are unreachable, it gives up without remembering that and tries again on the next frame, for every coin ledge. It also re-checks every coin in the room every frame. Spreading the jump tests over several frames and remembering 'no route' for a second would remove both problems.

**Technical detail.**

Collect mode always uses the robust planner (swordsmanController.ts:1019-1022). Every frame getSwordsmanCollectObjectiveTarget (:437-466) runs gatherSwordsmanCollectCandidates (:469-638), which walks every collectible in the room and allocates bounds rectangles, objective-target objects (often 2-3 spreads), traversal snapshots, a Map entry and closures per coin. When no route is committed, selectSwordsmanCollectTarget clears and calls selectBestCollectRoute (swordsmanCollectSelection.ts:220-222), which runs planSwordsmanRobustTraversal for every candidate node (:343-356). Candidates with no exact or useful partial route are skipped with continue (:358-371), so if all fail nothing is committed and the next frame plans all of them again. Each plan sorts the whole frontier on every expansion (swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:174) and copies the visited Set for every pushed state (:223), up to 160 states (:91). On first use every edge is physically simulated in 1/60 s steps for up to 2.2 s of game time (:377-436, :102-103); the cache is keyed by room version and cleared wholesale at 4,096 entries (:793-802).

Measured (scratch planner.bench.test.ts, M-series Mac, Node 22) in a 39-ledge room: first plan 157-190 ms with 280 edge simulations; warm plan 1.0-1.2 ms with 147 expanded states. An unreachable candidate exhausts the 160-state budget, so N unreachable coin ledges cost about N ms per frame on desktop.

Fix plan: (1) precompute edge simulations as a budgeted frame-work job (frameWorkCoordinator already exists) when a room containing a collect-mode swordsman loads, or cap simulations per frame and treat pending edges as unknown; (2) after selectBestCollectRoute returns nothing, store a no-route backoff (e.g. 1 s or until the coin count/current node changes); (3) build the room's collectible inventory once per frame (or at 10 Hz) and share it across swordsmen; (4) use parent pointers and a binary heap in the planner instead of copying edges/visited and sorting the frontier.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:1019-1022 — collect objective always uses the robust planner
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:437-466 — collect target recomputed every frame
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts:529-637 — every collectible in the room scanned with several allocations per coin per frame
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanCollectSelection.ts:220-222 — clearRoute then selectBestCollectRoute when nothing is committed
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/swordsmanCollectSelection.ts:343-371 — one robust plan per candidate; failures continue without any backoff
- src/enemies/swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:174 — whole frontier re-sorted on each expansion
- src/enemies/swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:223 — visited Set copied for every pushed state
- src/enemies/swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:377-436 — edge simulated step by step on cache miss
- src/enemies/swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts:793-802 — simulation cache cleared entirely at 4,096 entries

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect is real, but its size depends on how many ledges the Sword Hunter can reach.
  
  First route plan in a room (measured as CPU time on an M-series Mac):
  
  | Room | First-plan freeze |
  |---|---|
  | Dense, 40 connected ledges | about 160-245 ms |
  | 22 connected ledges | about 100 ms |
  | 12-ledge staircase | about 20 ms |
  | Rows 4 or more tiles apart (the swordsman jumps about 50 px) | 6 ms or less |
  
  The per-frame re-planning only happens when no remaining non-current coin ledge gives a committable route: either an exact route, or a partial route that ends on a node with coins. While a route is committed (7.2 s), it doesn't happen.
  
  Per-frame cost per unreachable coin ledge:
  
  | Room | Cost per ledge per frame |
  |---|---|
  | Dense, 40 ledges | about 0.7-0.9 ms |
  | 22 ledges | about 0.36 ms |
  | 12 ledges | about 0.07 ms |
  
  So "N ms per frame" holds only in dense rooms.
  
  Other corrections:
  - The first plan simulates only the edges the search reaches, not every jump in the room.
  - simulatedEdges counts successful expansions, including cache hits.
  - The per-coin scan each frame is microsecond-scale, so fix item (3) is low value.
  
  Priority order:
  1. A no-route backoff (small effort).
  2. A per-frame cap or budget on cold edge simulations (medium effort).
  3. A heap and parent pointers in the planner (optional).

### F306: World-map tile system still re-plans its whole display every frame, while you play and while the map sits still

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F010

**Summary.** The pre-drawn world map tiles are on for everyone, and their code still rebuilds its full 'which tiles should be on screen' plan on every frame, even when the camera has not moved and even during play. It is no longer scanning its whole history (that part of F010 was fixed), but it still recomputes about a dozen lists and lookups per frame for the same answer. That is roughly 0.1-0.45 ms per frame on a fast Mac and likely 0.5-2 ms on a phone, all the time. The plan should be reused until something actually changes, and play mode should refresh it a few times a second at most.

**Technical detail.**

framePipeline.ts:79-84 runs worldStreamingController.updateWorldTiles() every frame; worldStreaming.ts:1126-1147 calls worldTileController.update(camera) in both browse and play (the only skip is urgent destination work), and in browse also calls isTargetLodReady (:1163). WorldTileClientController.update (controller.ts:419-513) has no unchanged short-circuit. Per frame with a still camera it: rebuilds refreshAvailability's default Set (:956-958); builds a candidate object per coverage key, ranks them (scheduler.ts:139-164: Map + spread copies + sort) and reconciles queues with new Maps/Sets/arrays (:1062-1092); in syncCoverage resolves 3 display plans plus one more per visible target just to count ready targets (:1406-1445), each plan allocating 2 Sets, 2 arrays, key strings and 2 sorted copies (displayPlan.ts:39-81); builds displayKeys via spread+Set and a staleRoomIds Set; then phaserLayer.syncDisplay filters, maps and joins a signature string and builds a new Set (phaserLayer.ts:136-143); metrics.update spreads objects and metrics.recordFrame returns an unused snapshot copy (metrics.ts:84-100). isCameraTargetLodReady re-enumerates bounds and resolves yet another plan (:1766-1785). F010's delivery note itself says 'Timed LOD/fallback transitions remain active every frame'.

Measured (scratch bench worldtiles.bench.test.ts reusing controller.bootstrap.test.ts helpers, ready-empty manifests, Phaser layer stubbed so real syncDisplay cost is excluded): 0.06-0.45 ms per update with a still camera across 3 runs (2-6 visible, 6-8 guard tiles), 65-75% of it in syncCoverage. Rollout is 100% (feature-ledger.md:825).

Fix plan: keep a frame signature (tile bounds + level + zoom bucket + an availability revision bumped in refreshAvailability/installs + queue lengths + fallback state + whether a timed LOD commit is pending) and skip queueCoverageImages/syncCoverage when unchanged, still running the timed parts when a commit window or fallback timer is due (the F010 fact-check caveat). Count ready targets from the single desired plan instead of V extra plans. Make recordFrame return void. In play mode refresh at <= 4 Hz unless the tile bounds change. Expect ~0 ms on idle frames.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/framePipeline.ts:79-84 — streaming stage runs updateWorldTiles every frame
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1126-1147 — world tile update runs in play and browse; only urgent destination work skips it
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/controller.ts:419-513 — full coverage pipeline every frame with no unchanged short-circuit
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/controller.ts:1439-1445 — one resolveWorldTileDisplayPlan per visible target every frame just to count ready targets
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/displayPlan.ts:39-81 — each plan allocates Sets, arrays, key strings and sorted copies
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/controller.ts:956-958 — refreshAvailability default argument builds a new Set every call
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/metrics.ts:84-100 — recordFrame returns a fresh snapshot copy every frame
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/phaserLayer.ts:136-143 — filter + map + join signature + new Set every frame
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/controller.ts:1766-1785 — isCameraTargetLodReady re-enumerates bounds and resolves another plan

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim stands: after F010, world-tile update() still rebuilds its full coverage plan every frame, still camera included, in browse and play, for 100% of users. Three corrections:
  
  1. **Plan count.** It is usually the desired plan plus the guard plan, plus one per visible target, plus one in isCameraTargetLodReady, plus one more in browse via worldStreaming.ts:1163 (only when a published room is selected). The third display plan exists only during LOD transitions.
  
  2. **Real cost is higher than the bench, not lower.** The bench stubbed phaserLayer and used ready-empty tiles. The real syncDisplay also runs syncPinnedTextures twice, syncStaleMasks and repairStableDisplay every frame. With image tiles, queueCoverageImages also ranks every ready key.
  
  3. **The fix plan must preserve repairStableDisplay.** It is an intentional per-frame self-heal from 38e6a9a3. Run it at about 4 Hz or keep it outside the skip. The unchanged-frame signature must also include:
     - immediateMaskedRoomIds and optimistic room versions;
     - the selected room key;
     - previousRendererVersion;
     - the deferTargetRefinement and gesture time windows;
     - the timers for pending target-LOD waiters, level commits and fallback.
  
  A safer first step, small effort: count ready targets from the desired plan, make recordFrame and metrics.update return void, drop the default-argument Set, compute isCameraTargetLodReady once per frame, and limit play mode to 4 Hz or less unless tile bounds change.

### F304: Every game canvas texture does a blocking pixel read-back and keeps a second full-size copy that nothing uses

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Whenever the game turns a drawn canvas into a texture (room pictures, map chunk previews, custom backgrounds, custom tiles and sprites), Phaser's canvas-texture class reads every pixel back into a hidden copy and keeps it for the texture's whole life. Nothing in WAMP ever uses that copy. It roughly adds a third copy of every such image (0.9 MB per room layer, 3.6 MB per map chunk, 3.9 MB per photo background), and the read-back itself can stall a phone for several milliseconds at the moments the game is trying hardest to stay smooth. Registering these canvases as plain textures avoids both.

**Technical detail.**

CanvasTexture's constructor calls getContext('2d', {willReadFrequently:true}) and getImageData(0,0,w,h) (CanvasTexture.js:86,118), keeping imageData/data/pixels for the texture's lifetime. On an accelerated canvas, getImageData forces a GPU flush and synchronous readback. rg finds no reader of texture pixel data in src (no getPixel/getPixels/putData/imageData use).

Sites that pay it:
- room terrain/foreground per prepared room: roomTexturePreparation.ts:93,101 (640x352 → 0.9 MB each);
- buildRoomSnapshotTexture: roomSnapshotTexture.ts:105;
- chunk previews: chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:595-599 and :1266 (8x8 rooms at 4 px/tile = 1280x704 → 3.6 MB hidden copy each, plus its readback, while panning the map);
- custom backgrounds: backgrounds/runtime.ts:308 (1280x768 → 3.9 MB);
- custom tile atlases: customTiles/runtime.ts:102, :184;
- custom sprites: customSprites/registry.ts:564, :582;
- starfield, fog and lighting textures;
- every TileSprite's private canvas (previous finding).

The room-artifact cache budgets 640x352x4x2 bytes per room (worldStreaming.ts:3434-3444), but each room actually holds canvas + ImageData + GPU, about 3x that. So the 8 MB 'reduced' budget (worldStreaming.ts:133) really holds about 24 MB. The readbacks happen inside 'gpu-upload' frame-coordinator jobs that are costed at 1 unit (e.g. worldStreaming.ts:4049-4061), so the coordinator underestimates them.

Fix (small): for canvases that are never redrawn, replace textures.addCanvas(key, canvas) with textures.addImage(key, canvas as unknown as HTMLImageElement). TextureManager.addImage → create → a plain Texture whose TextureSource detects the canvas (TextureSource.js:143) and uploads it via createCanvasTexture (:231) with no getImageData. For canvases that are redrawn (the animated background), call texture.source[0].update() instead of refresh(); it re-uploads via updateCanvasTexture (TextureSource.js:333). For stills decoded as ImageBitmap, pass the bitmap directly and skip the staging canvas as well. Saves about 0.9 MB per room texture, 3.6 MB per chunk preview and about 7.8 MB per 1280x768 background (staging canvas plus ImageData), and removes one synchronous readback per texture.

**Evidence.**

- node_modules/phaser/src/textures/CanvasTexture.js:86,118 — getImageData of the whole canvas retained as this.imageData
- src/scenes/overworld/roomTexturePreparation.ts:93,101 — room terrain/foreground registered with addCanvas
- src/scenes/overworld/chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:595-599,1266 — chunk previews via createCanvas/addCanvas (up to 1280x704)
- src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:299-308 — custom background staged into a canvas then addCanvas
- src/customTiles/runtime.ts:102,184 — custom tile atlas via addCanvas/createCanvas
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3434-3444 — cache counts one 640x352x4 copy per texture
- node_modules/phaser/src/textures/TextureManager.js:471 — addImage → create(key, source) builds a plain Texture
- node_modules/phaser/src/textures/TextureSource.js:143,231,333 — plain textures accept canvas sources and can be re-uploaded with update()

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real, but narrower in mechanism and different in size.
  - A real readback of drawn content happens only at the addCanvas sites: room terrain/foreground (roomTexturePreparation.ts:93,101), play-mode scheduled chunk uploads (chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:1266), custom backgrounds (runtime.ts:308), and custom tile atlas and sprite commits.
  - The createCanvas sites read back a blank canvas at construction, so only their memory cost counts: browse-mode chunk previews (:595), buildRoomSnapshotTexture, starfield, fog and lighting. The claim of a readback "while panning the map" is wrong.
  - The memory cost is larger than claimed for chunk previews. The preview cache holds up to 32M pixels (chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:120), so there can be up to about 128 MB of unused ImageData.
  - The background saving is about 3.9 MB, not 7.8 MB. Handing Phaser the ImageBitmap only swaps which object is kept alive.
  - Limit the change to the large textures that are never redrawn: room layers, both chunk paths, room snapshot textures and still backgrounds. Switch them to textures.addImage(key, canvas), creating a detached canvas where createCanvas is used today.
  - Leave these as CanvasTexture: custom sprites (refreshCustomSpriteTexture would silently stop updating), the custom tile atlas (ensureCustomRoomTileTexture calls refresh() with no guard and would throw on a plain Texture), animated backgrounds (they use texture.context), and the tiny starfield, fog and lighting textures.
  - Update the six test files that mock addCanvas.
  - Stall times are unmeasured. Profile a 640x352 and a 1280x704 readback on a phone before claiming several milliseconds.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** [PR #297](https://github.com/songadaymann/wamp/pull/297). Room layers, snapshots, previews and still backgrounds are registered as plain images, dropping the hidden full-size copy. Reviewed adversarially before merging; `npm run check` and the muted phone smokes passed. [Receipt](wamp-round2-phone-play-2026-10-22.md).

### F303: Custom tiles are painted one pixel at a time into room and map pictures (256 draw calls per tile, even for 4-pixel thumbnails)

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When the game draws a room or map preview containing custom tiles, it paints each custom tile cell pixel by pixel: up to 256 separate colour changes and rectangle draws per cell, even when the cell is only 4 pixels wide on the map. A room covered in custom tiles needs over 200,000 draw calls just for its picture, which slows room loading and map panning on phones. The game already builds a ready-made sheet of each room's custom tiles, so each cell could be copied from it in a single draw.

**Technical detail.**

drawRoomTileLayerRowsToContext (roomSnapshotTexture.ts:429-486) calls drawCustomTileFrame for each custom cell (:450-461). That does save/translate/scale/restore and drawCustomRoomTileToContext (customTiles/draw.ts:4-27): for every non-null pixel, set fillStyle (a string parse) and fillRect.

Scale:
- Full-room snapshot at 16 px/tile: up to 256 fillRects per cell, about 225k for an 880-cell room (each 2-row job, worldStreaming.ts:135, does up to 80 cells, about 20k fillRects).
- Chunk previews at 4 px/tile (chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:1090): cellSize = 0.25 but each rect is ceil'd to 1 px (draw.ts:20-25), so 256 overlapping 1-px rects produce a 4x4 output.
- createCustomSpriteCanvas (customSprites/registry.ts:447-469) and the atlas builder (customTiles/runtime.ts:217-238, 4 tiles per job, worldStreaming.ts:136) use the same pixel loop: up to 32 jobs and about 32k fillRects for a 128-tile atlas.
This is on top of the lookup cost in the custom-tile normalization finding.

Fix (small):
1. Build each room's tile pixels once into an ImageData: map hex to RGBA through a small Map cache and putImageData once. That also makes the atlas a single job instead of 32.
2. Draw snapshot and preview cells with one drawImage per cell from that atlas canvas (or a per-tiles-array cached canvas), keeping the existing flip transform.
3. Use the same approach for custom sprite canvases.
Expected: about 225k canvas calls → about 880 drawImage calls for a fully custom room.

**Evidence.**

- src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:450-461,488-500 — per custom cell: save/translate/scale + pixel loop
- src/customTiles/draw.ts:12-25 — fillStyle + fillRect per pixel, rect size ceil'd to ≥1 px
- src/scenes/overworld/chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:1090 — map previews draw tile rows through the same function
- src/customTiles/runtime.ts:217-238 — atlas drawn via the same per-pixel routine
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:136 — PREPARED_CUSTOM_TILES_PER_JOB = 4
- src/customSprites/registry.ts:447-469 — custom sprite canvases painted per pixel

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The real cost is play-mode room streaming for rooms that use custom tiles. RoomTexturePreparation draws 2 rows per job across 3 layers, and play-mode chunk previews draw 1 row per job. A row band dense with custom tiles turns a job estimated at 0.5 ms into about 8 ms (headless Chromium, desktop) or 29 ms (headless WebKit), and more on phones. Map panning in Browse is mostly unaffected: published rooms use server world tiles once the cutover is active, and chunk previews are cached by content signature. The existing atlas is built after the room textures and never for chunk previews. The fix should therefore build a per-room (or per-tiles-array) 256x128 canvas once via ImageData/putImageData, ahead of texture preparation, and drawImage each cell from it, keeping the flip transform. The atlas job can reuse that canvas. Drop the custom-sprite change: sprites are at most 32x32 and cached, so it is negligible.

### F307: Each loaded room uses about twice the memory the budget thinks, and always builds an empty foreground layer

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Every room in play is drawn into two full-size images, a main layer and a foreground layer. Each is kept both as a page canvas and as a graphics-card texture, but the memory budget counts only one copy. The foreground image is built and drawn on top of every room even when the builder never placed a foreground tile, which costs memory and extra drawing on phones. Skip empty foreground layers and count the real memory.

**Technical detail.**

Memory:
- Room textures are committed with textures.addCanvas (roomTexturePreparation.ts:93,101). Phaser 3.90 TextureSource keeps the canvas as its image (node_modules/phaser/src/textures/TextureSource.js:51), so each 640x352 layer holds a 0.9 MB canvas backing store plus a 0.9 MB GPU texture. The immediate path does the same through createCanvas (visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:105).
- The artifact budget counts 640*352*4*2 = 1.8 MB per room (worldStreaming.ts:3434-3445) against budgets of 24 MB / 8 MB (132-133). Real residency is about 3.6 MB per room, so the reduced 8 MB budget actually allows about 16 MB.
- When a texture is released, its canvas is not shrunk. cancel() zeroes only uncommitted canvases (roomTexturePreparation.ts:110-122), and releaseTextureIfPresent just calls textures.remove (fullRoomPresenter.ts:112-116). iOS Safari counts canvases toward its fixed canvas-memory cap until garbage collection.

Empty foreground: PREPARED_LAYERS always includes 'foreground' (roomTexturePreparation.ts:13). Both builders always create a full-room foreground image at depth 27.25 (fullRoomPresenter.ts:176-182 and 881-889). Even when the layer has no tiles that adds 0.9 MB canvas + 0.9 MB GPU, a texture bind, and a full-room transparent quad of overdraw for every visible loaded room.

Fix:
1. Skip the foreground texture and image when tileData.foreground has no tiles. Keep foregroundImage nullable; the type already allows it.
2. Count both copies in getFullRoomArtifactByteSize, or halve the budgets.
3. Set width = height = 1 on the source canvas when a room texture is released.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/roomTexturePreparation.ts:13 — PREPARED_LAYERS always includes foreground
- src/scenes/overworld/roomTexturePreparation.ts:93 — textures.addCanvas(terrainTextureKey, terrain.canvas)
- src/scenes/overworld/roomTexturePreparation.ts:101 — textures.addCanvas(foregroundTextureKey, foreground.canvas)
- src/scenes/overworld/roomTexturePreparation.ts:110-122 — only uncommitted canvases are zeroed on cancel
- node_modules/phaser/src/textures/TextureSource.js:51 — this.image = source (canvas retained)
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3434-3445 — artifact size = ROOM_PX_WIDTH*ROOM_PX_HEIGHT*4*2
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:132-133 — 24 MB normal / 8 MB reduced budgets
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:176-182 — immediate path always creates foreground image
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:881-889 — dormant shell always creates foreground image
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:112-116 — release is textures.remove only

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Each committed room layer is held three times, not twice:
  - the canvas
  - a retained ImageData copy, because Phaser's CanvasTexture constructor calls getImageData (CanvasTexture.js:118)
  - the GPU texture
  
  Real residency is about 5.4 MB per room against the 1.8 MB counted. The budget only limits LRU-cached rooms that are not protected; loaded rooms are always kept, and reduced play loads one full room. The resulting totals (about 20-25 MB reduced, about 70 MB normal) are an uncalibrated knob, not a demonstrated memory problem.
  
  The canvas-shrink-on-release step applies only to the prepared path's detached canvases. Immediate-path canvases come from CanvasPool, and Phaser already shrinks them to 1x1 on textures.remove.
  
  The overdraw cost of empty foreground quads is negligible because the canvas is CSS-pixel sized. The worthwhile saving from skipping empty foregrounds is per room load: a canvas, a readback, a texture upload and about 2.7 MB held. That saving depends on how many rooms really have no foreground tiles, which is unmeasured.
  
  Recommended fix:
  - Skip the empty foreground layer, updating texturesReady (worldStreaming.ts:3726), commitNext, both builders and the resource keys and sizes together.
  - Use textures.create instead of addCanvas for prepared canvases, which drops the ImageData copy and the readback.
  - Fix the byte accounting.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** [PR #297](https://github.com/songadaymann/wamp/pull/297). Rooms with no foreground tiles build no foreground layer. Reviewed adversarially before merging; `npm run check` and the muted phone smokes passed. [Receipt](wamp-round2-phone-play-2026-10-22.md).

### F312: Room building is throttled by fixed cost guesses, so a room needs at least ~0.6 s to get ready on phones

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Building a neighbouring room is split into about 50 small jobs spread across frames so play stays smooth. Each job is charged a fixed guessed cost of 0.5–1 ms whether or not it actually takes that long. On phones the game therefore runs only one or two jobs per frame, and every room needs at least about 36 frames before it is ready. The game already records how long each job really takes. Using those measurements instead of fixed guesses could let faster phones finish rooms much sooner, which also shortens the waits at room edges described above.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism:
- FrameWorkCoordinator charges max(estimate, actual) for every job (frameWorkCoordinator.ts:317).
- CPU caps are 2 ms per frame for normal and 1 ms for reduced (130-131).

Preparation pipeline estimates, per room:
- 33 texture-row jobs at 0.5 ms each (3 layers x 22 rows / PREPARED_TEXTURE_ROWS_PER_JOB=2; worldStreaming.ts:135, queuePreparedTextureBatch ~3925-3945)
- runtime shell, 1 ms
- background, 0.75 ms
- 6 terrain-row jobs (22 / 4) at 0.75 ms
- collision, 0.75 ms
- 6 inset jobs at 0.75 ms
- lighting, 0.75 ms
- ceil(objects / 4) object jobs at 0.75 ms
- finalisation, 0.75 ms
- commit, 1 ms
- 2 GPU uploads at 1 ms each

That is about 30.5 + 0.75*ceil(n/4) ms of charged CPU. With the 1 ms reduced cap only one 0.75 ms job fits per frame, so a room takes at least about 36 + ceil(n/4) frames: about 0.6 s, or 0.77 s with 40 objects. With the 2 ms cap the floor is about 20 frames (0.33 s). These floors hold regardless of how fast each job really runs.

The real durations are already recorded per job (FrameWorkExecutionRecord.actualDurationMs, frameWorkCoordinator.ts:66-75, and maxActualJobDurationMs) but never fed back.

Fix:
1. Keep a per-label running average (EWMA) of actual cost in the coordinator and admit jobs on max(EWMA, a small floor), keeping the existing caps.
2. Alternatively, make rows-per-job adaptive.
3. Measure first with the mobile profiler, which already exposes frameWork diagnostics through getDebugMetrics.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/frameWorkCoordinator.ts:317 — chargedDurationMs = Math.max(nextJob.estimatedCostMs, actualDurationMs)
- src/scenes/overworld/frameWorkCoordinator.ts:130-131 — normal 4/2 ms, reduced 2/1 ms budgets
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:135-138 — 2 texture rows, 4 terrain rows, 4 objects per job
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4087-4100 — background job estimated 0.75 ms
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4103-4128 — terrain-row jobs estimated 0.75 ms
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4249-4259 — commit job estimated 1 ms
- src/scenes/overworld/frameWorkCoordinator.ts:66-75 — actualDurationMs already recorded per execution

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** On phones, background preparation of a neighbouring room has a floor of about 35 frames (0.58 s), plus about 1 frame for every 4 objects (44 frames, 0.73 s, with 40 objects). This applies only to rooms whose textures are not cached; with cached textures it is 18 frames. Real job speed does not change these floors, because each job is charged at least its fixed estimate.
  
  The floor does not apply at room edges. Within 72 px of a seam, or once activation is requested, the policy becomes seam-critical and the work runs on the normal 2 ms budget. That floor is about 18-22 frames minus work already done, and the commit job always runs there. The repo's throttled mobile-emulated trace measured 0 ms seam hold, so there is no evidence of waits a player can see. The likely benefit is faster speculative preparation on fast touch devices, and less partial work lost when the predicted direction changes.
  
  Measure real per-label job durations on phones before changing anything. If the gap is real, admit jobs on min(cpuSubCap, max(EWMA, floor)): the clamp is required to avoid starvation. Also allow for coarse performance.now() precision, since the site is not cross-origin isolated. World-tile work shares the same 1 ms CPU sub-cap, which can block 0.75 ms jobs entirely in frames where it runs.

### F313: Room data is deep-copied two or three times every time it is downloaded or read from a cache

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Every downloaded room is copied into the streaming cache, copied again into a shared cache, and copied a third time whenever the shared cache is read. Live building previews are copied twice. About 25 places still use an old accessor that copies a whole room just to read one field. Each copy re-checks the whole room and costs about 0.2 ms on a fast laptop and several times that on a phone. When dozens of rooms arrive at once, those copies add up to visible stalls. Keep one read-only copy and share it.

**Technical detail.**

Measured in Node 22 on an M-series laptop: cloneRoomSnapshot takes 0.19 ms for a typical room (11 KB JSON, 60 objects), against 0.044 ms for JSON.parse of the same room. cloneRoomSnapshot does full normalisation: migrations, music, lighting, smart terrain, custom sprites and tiles (roomModel.ts:761-797).

Copies per path:
1. Batch download: clone (previewCache.ts:227), then setSharedRoomSnapshot clones again (sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:25 via previewCache.ts:237). Same pattern at 141+143 for chunk hydration and 282+292 for portal destinations.
2. Shared-cache hit: getSharedRoomSnapshot clones on every read (sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:20). The module also keeps up to 256 extra full-room copies resident (:3).
3. Presence previews: ownRoomPreview already clones the wire snapshot (presence/roomPreviewCache.ts:22), then worldStreaming.ownChangedPresencePreview clones it again (worldStreaming.ts:2716-2729). That repeats every 1.2 s per active builder in view.
4. The deprecated getRoomSnapshotForCoordinates still clones (worldStreaming.ts:1253-1262). It is wired into the selection, course, respawn, session-reset, PvP and Room Rush hosts (composition/world.ts:595), about 25 call sites in total. For example, coursePlayback.ts:191-192 clones every course room just to look for pressure plates.

In play mode, distant previews load at 'full' detail in batches of 48 with 3 workers (worldStreaming.ts:2845-2894). One 48-room batch therefore costs 96 clones: about 18 ms on desktop and roughly 100 ms on a phone, in one promise continuation.

Fix:
1. Normalise once on receipt and store the same object (treated as RoomSnapshotView, optionally frozen in dev) in both caches.
2. Make getSharedRoomSnapshot return the view.
3. Drop the second clone in ownChangedPresencePreview.
4. Point the composition wiring at getRoomSnapshotViewForCoordinates and delete the deprecated getters. Keep cloneRoomSnapshotForCoordinates for the one caller that mutates (OverworldPlayScene.ts:3929).
5. Watch getRoomSnapshotCloneCountSinceReset in the profiler to confirm the drop.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:227 — cloneRoomSnapshot(entry.snapshot) for each downloaded snapshot
- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:237 — setSharedRoomSnapshot(..., entry.snapshot)
- src/persistence/sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:25 — set clones again
- src/persistence/sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:20 — get clones on every hit
- src/persistence/sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:3 — MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 256 resident copies
- src/presence/roomPreviewCache.ts:22 — presence preview already cloned once
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:2716-2729 — streaming clones the owned preview again
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1253-1262 — deprecated accessor returns a deep clone
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/world.ts:595 — selection host wired to the cloning accessor
- src/scenes/overworld/coursePlayback.ts:191-192 — clones each course room to read placedObjects

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real but smaller than claimed, and not a frame-rate or stall issue. The steady-state paths (movement, transitions, HUD) already use RoomSnapshotView, and the perf trace enforces zero steady-state clones. The redundant work is one extra deep clone per room on 'full' downloads (`setSharedRoomSnapshot` at `previewCache.ts:143/237/292`, plus `sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:35`, which clones twice), and up to 256 duplicate rooms kept in memory. Measured clone cost is 0.002-0.45 ms per room depending on placed-object count. That saves roughly 1-10 ms on desktop per new 48-room batch, not 18 ms of unavoidable stall.
  
  A shared-cache read replaces a download (1 clone), so it is not a third copy. The presence double clone happens only on revision change, at most every 1.2 s per editing builder, which is negligible. Overview-detail downloads clone once.
  
  The roughly 25 deprecated-accessor call sites are all event-driven single-room reads (selection, course start, respawn, PvP spawn, leaderboard refresh). Converting them to views is type-safety and cleanup work, not a performance fix.
  
  Recommended scope:
  1. Make the shared cache store the already-normalised object and return a RoomSnapshotView.
  2. Drop the extra clone in `sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:35`.
  3. Optionally fold coursePlayback's pinned cache into the shared cache.
  4. Migrate the deprecated getter as cleanup, typing callers as RoomSnapshotView so TypeScript flags any mutation.

### F311: In-game room pictures copy a 12-field tileset object for every tile they draw

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When the game builds the small room pictures used on the map and for neighboring rooms, it makes a fresh copy of a tile sheet's settings for every single tile, just to read one number. For a full screen of map previews that is about 97,000 throwaway objects and roughly 37 ms of extra work on a fast laptop, more on phones. A lookup table cuts that to about 3 ms.

**Technical detail.**

drawRoomTileLayerRowsToContext (src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:429-486) calls resolveTilesetForGid (738-757) for every non-empty tile. That function scans TILESETS (25 entries) backwards and returns `{ ...tileset, localIndex }`, a fresh copy of a 12-key config object per tile.

This path is used by chunk previews (scenes/overworld/chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:638-652, 1090), neighbour rooms in play and editor (fullRoomPresenter.ts:134-149, scenes/editor/backgrounds.ts:287) and special tiles.

Measured in Node 22: 97,200 lookups (300 tiles x 324 rooms, the phone browse budget) took 36.6 ms with the spread versus 2.65 ms with a precomputed gid-indexed array (scratch benchmark using the real TILESETS). The spread also creates about 97k short-lived objects (roughly 10 MB) per full fill. Phones are typically 3-5x slower.

It also duplicates config.getTilesetByGid (config/tilesets.ts:1378-1391), which is allocation-free but also a linear scan.

Fix: build one `TILESET_BY_GID` array once in config (max gid known from TILESETS) and use it from roomSnapshotTexture, roomMetadataRender (284), the Pages renderer (831) and getTilesetByGid itself. Compute localIndex inline. About 25 lines changed, and output is identical.

**Evidence.**

- src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:464-471 — resolveTilesetForGid(gid) called per tile, then .localIndex/.columns/.key read
- src/visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts:738-757 — returns `{ ...tileset, localIndex }` (new object per call)
- src/config/tilesets.ts:1378-1391 — existing allocation-free getTilesetByGid duplicates the lookup
- src/scenes/overworld/chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:1090 — chunk previews draw rows through this path

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism and the fix are right. The cost is smaller and more spread out than claimed. In play mode, chunk previews run one row per scheduler job under the frame budget, so there is no frame-rate impact. In browse mode, each 8x8 chunk is drawn synchronously on a 24 ms timer, and the lookup overhead is about 3-5 ms per chunk on a laptop. That is a minor part of a build cost dominated by drawImage, not one 37 ms hit. About half the overhead is the 25-entry linear scan rather than the object spread, and a gid-indexed table removes both. Garbage is about 6 MB per full fill, not 10 MB. Treat this as a small speedup for browse-mode chunk fills and a cleanup of the three duplicate gid-to-tileset lookups (roomSnapshotTexture.ts:738, config getTilesetByGid at tilesets.ts:1378, pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:831).

### F314: Tapping a room on the map rebuilds every Expanded Room label, re-drawing long titles one letter at a time

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** On the world map, every tap on a room throws away and recreates all the Expanded Room badges in view, each with three text images. For long titles, the code shortens the title one character at a time and fully redraws and re-uploads the text after each try until it fits, which can be about 17 redraws for one 40-character title. With several expanded rooms on screen, a single tap can trigger around a hundred text redraws, which shows up as a hitch on phones. Badges should only be rebuilt when their content changes, and titles should be measured once.

**Technical detail.**

selectRoomCoordinates (selection.ts:52-64) calls host.redrawWorld(); redrawWorld (OverworldPlayScene.ts:2894-2906) calls browseOverlayController.redrawBrowseOverlays(), which destroys every activity and expanded-room badge (browseOverlays.ts:240-242) and recreates them for every cell in the world window (:250-259). Each expanded-room badge (:335-357) builds all three tiers regardless of zoom (:740-750): the compact tier creates a Text (:629-635) and the text tier creates two more (:649-666). fitTextBadgeTitle (:558-580) loops maxLength from the full title down and calls titleText.setText(candidate) each time until it fits; each setText re-renders the canvas and re-uploads the texture. ROOM_BADGE_TEXT_MAX_WIDTH is round(640*0.5*0.88/1.45) = 194 px (:23, :30-33), which fits about 23 characters of 12 px Courier New plus stroke and padding, while expanded/course titles can be 40 characters (courses/model.ts:109), so a 40-character title costs ~17 extra renders. Per badge: 3 Text creations (each with a MeasureText pixel readback and a new GPU texture) + up to ~17 re-renders, on every selection change and every redrawWorld (window refresh, room activity changes via social.ts:29).

Fix plan: key each badge by room id + title + goal type and only create/destroy badges whose key changed (move the rest); find the fitting title length by measuring with one canvas measureText (or binary search on setText) instead of a linear setText loop; create the text tier lazily when zoom first reaches it.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/selection.ts:52-64 — every room selection calls redrawWorld
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:2894-2906 — redrawWorld always calls redrawBrowseOverlays
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:240-262 — destroys all badges and recreates them for every window cell
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:740-750 — dot, compact and text tiers all built for each badge
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:629-635 — compact tier creates a Text
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:649-666 — text tier creates two Texts
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:558-580 — fitTextBadgeTitle calls setText once per shorter candidate until it fits
- src/scenes/overworld/browseOverlays.ts:30-33 — max badge text width ~194 px
- src/courses/model.ts:109 — titles may be 40 characters

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism is right, but scope and size need correcting. Badges are rebuilt for every expanded-room anchor in the whole loaded world window (browse chunk radius 3-4 x 8 cells, so up to about 72x72 cells), not only those on screen. The one-character-at-a-time setText loop (about 17 renders for a 40-character title) only runs for titles longer than about 23 characters; the default 'EXPANDED ROOM' never runs it. So the always-paid cost is 3 Text creations per badge, each with a MeasureText getImageData readback and a GPU texture, on every selection, window refresh and room-activity change. "About a hundred redraws per tap" holds only if several long-titled expanded rooms are loaded. The same tap also refills the full room grid in roomCells.redraw, so the badge churn is only part of the tap cost. Fix as proposed: reuse badges by key (the pattern of roomCells frontier labels), measure the title once or binary-search it, and build the text tier lazily.

### F310: Every coin pickup creates a brand-new text image for its '+10' popup, then throws it away

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Each time you grab a coin, the game makes a new '+10' text from scratch: it draws the text to a hidden canvas, reads pixels back to measure it, sends it to the graphics chip as a new texture, then deletes it half a second later. Running through a line of coins does this several times a second, plus two short-lived effect sprites per coin. On phones this kind of create-and-delete churn causes small hitches at exactly the moments that should feel best. Reusing a handful of popups (or a pixel font) avoids all of it.

**Technical detail.**

Collection (liveObjects/collection.ts:73-79) calls playCollectFx (fx/controller.ts:25-47): two playAnimatedFx sprites created and destroyed on ANIMATION_COMPLETE (:221-256) and spawnScorePopup (:259-282), which does scene.add.text(...) with a style that has no `metrics`, tweens it for 460 ms and destroys it. In Phaser 3.90 each Text takes a canvas from CanvasPool and registers its own texture (Text.js:139, :276); a style without metrics runs MeasureText (TextStyle.js:438-440), which draws the string on a pooled canvas and calls getImageData (MeasureText.js:21, :66); updateText then uploads the canvas with canvasToTexture (Text.js:1455), and destroy deletes the GL texture. So each coin costs one 2D draw + pixel readback for metrics, one draw + GPU texture create/upload and one texture delete, plus 2 sprites, 2 'once' listeners and a tween. Jump dust, landing dust, sword slash, muzzle flash and bullet impact also create and destroy a Sprite per event (same playAnimatedFx path), and flashes/rings create an Arc that is triangulated on creation. Battery Saver skips only the popup (:260-261).

Fix plan: keep a small pool (6-8) of score-popup Texts created once with precomputed `metrics` and reuse them via setText (text values are a few fixed strings like '+10'/'+50', so cache their rendered frames, or switch popups to BitmapText with the existing pixel font). Pool the FX sprites per animation key (setActive/setVisible + play) instead of create/destroy.

**Evidence.**

- src/fx/controller.ts:25-47 — playCollectFx spawns two FX sprites and a score popup per pickup
- src/fx/controller.ts:259-282 — scene.add.text per popup, destroyed after a 460 ms tween
- src/fx/controller.ts:221-256 — every FX sprite is created and destroyed per event (no pooling)
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/Text.js:139 — each Text takes its own canvas from CanvasPool
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/Text.js:276 — each Text registers a new canvas texture
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/TextStyle.js:438-440 — without style.metrics, MeasureText runs
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/MeasureText.js:66 — MeasureText reads pixels back with getImageData
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/Text.js:1455 — updateText uploads the canvas to a GPU texture

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Each coin pickup does create and destroy one Phaser Text, with its own small GL texture uploaded about twice and then deleted, plus two FX sprites and a tween. It does NOT read pixels back: Phaser 3.90's MeasureText returns early via actualBoundingBoxAscent on all modern browsers. CanvasPool reuses the canvas elements. The labels are short ('+1', '+3', '+5') and the cost is likely well under 1 ms per pickup, so the claim of phone hitches is unmeasured. If done, pool about 6 score-popup Texts per SceneFxController and reuse them with setText; identical strings then skip re-rendering entirely. Pooling the FX sprites is optional and worth very little. BitmapText would need a new bitmap font asset because none is loaded today. Measure before prioritizing.

### F309: Editor 'layer guides' overlay is rebuilt from scratch every frame while it is switched on

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a builder turns on layer guides in the editor, the little coloured corner markers are recalculated and redrawn on every frame, even when nothing in the room has changed. For a well-filled room that means checking all 2,640 tile spots, building about a thousand text keys and drawing about 2,800 triangles every frame, which wastes battery and can make editing feel heavier on tablets. Redrawing only after an edit or a visibility change would make it free.

**Technical detail.**

EditorScene.update calls overlayController.updateLayerGuideOverlay() every frame (EditorScene.ts:1083). With editorState.showLayerGuides on (default off, toggled at uiBridge.ts:881), updateLayerGuideOverlay (overlays.ts:113-132) clears the Graphics and, per layer, collectLayerGuideCells (:178-228) calls layer.getTileAt for all 40x22 cells (2,640 calls across 3 layers), builds an `${x}:${y}` string key per occupied cell plus each placed object's footprint, then splits and parseInts every key (:124-129) and drawLayerGuideCorner (:231-248) issues 3 fillStyle+fillTriangle pairs and allocates two 6-element arrays per cell. A room with ~950 occupied cells costs ~950 strings, ~950 split arrays, ~1,900 point arrays and ~2,850 triangle commands per frame, and Phaser replays the whole command buffer at render.

Fix plan: cache the guide drawing behind a key of editRuntime.documentRevision + layer visibility + showLayerGuides (the pattern gridOverlay.ts:59-68 already uses), redraw only when it changes, and use numeric cell indices (y*ROOM_WIDTH+x) instead of string keys.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1083 — updateLayerGuideOverlay called from update() every frame
- src/scenes/editor/overlays.ts:113-132 — clears and rebuilds all guides each call, then split/parseInt per key
- src/scenes/editor/overlays.ts:178-228 — getTileAt over every cell and string keys per occupied cell and object footprint
- src/scenes/editor/overlays.ts:231-248 — three fillTriangle calls and two point arrays per cell
- src/scenes/overworld/gridOverlay.ts:59-68 — existing keyed-redraw pattern to copy

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The overlay is rebuilt every frame while it is on, but a cache will not make it free. Phaser replays the Graphics command buffer every frame, so about 2,850 triangles are still drawn. Caching removes only the JS rebuild and its garbage.
  
  The cache key needs:
  - documentRevision
  - isPlaying
  - showLayerGuides
  - a signal for an edit in progress, such as currentBatch length or the identity of the placedObjects array. Without it, tiles painted mid-stroke and objects in a live-preview drag will not show guides until pointer-up, because the revision only goes up on commit. Rebuilding every frame only while a gesture is active is a simpler alternative.
  
  Layer visibility is irrelevant and should not be in the key.
  
  Two cheap additions:
  - Replace the first fillTriangle (the colour at 0.92, which the black at 0.75 then covers) with one pre-blended colour. That cuts the triangles drawn each frame by a third.
  - Use numeric y*ROOM_WIDTH+x keys instead of strings.
  
  Copy the documentRevision cache pattern already in EditorScene (weatherPreviewCache, edgeGuides.sync), not the overworld gridOverlay.

### F308: Each NPC name tag is drawn and sent to the graphics chip about five times when a room loads

- **Area:** Performance: frame rate and smoothness (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** NPC name tags are set up in several steps (create, sharpen, set resolution, apply text preferences, wait for the font) and each step redraws the label completely, reads its pixels back and re-uploads it. That is about five full redraws per NPC every time a room with named NPCs loads, right when the game is busy streaming the next room. Setting the final style once and redrawing once after the font is ready would cut this to one or two.

**Technical detail.**

attachNpcNameLabel (npcNameLabel.ts:135-150): scene.add.text with a style lacking metrics runs MeasureText (pixel readback) and render #1; installNpcNameLabelSharpness (:68-82) wraps updateText so every later render also runs sharpenNpcNameLabelCanvas (:94-121: getImageData, quantize loop, putImageData and a second canvasToTexture upload at :118); syncNpcNameLabelResolution either calls setResolution, which re-renders (TextStyle.js:778-783 -> update -> updateText), or the caller runs label.updateText() (:145): render #2; bindCanvasTextPreferences (settings/textPreferences.ts:27-43) calls setStyle({fontFamily, fontSize}), which recalculates metrics (MeasureText readback) and renders (#3), then document.fonts.load(...).then(updateText) (#4); refreshNpcNameLabelWhenFontReady (:122-133) adds another fonts.load(...).then(updateText) (#5). Per label: ~5 canvas renders, ~9 GPU uploads, 4 sharpen readbacks and 2 MeasureText readbacks; a room with 10 named NPCs does ~50 renders/~90 uploads during load.

Fix plan: compute the final font family/size/resolution before creating the Text and pass them (with precomputed metrics) to scene.add.text; drop the duplicate fonts.load path (keep one promise per font, not per label); have bindCanvasTextPreferences skip setStyle when the computed key equals the initial style; only call updateText once after fonts are ready.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/npcNameLabel.ts:135-150 — label creation runs add.text, sharpness install, resolution sync/updateText, preferences binding and font refresh
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/npcNameLabel.ts:68-82 — every updateText also sharpens the canvas
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/npcNameLabel.ts:104-118 — sharpen does getImageData, putImageData and a second texture upload
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects/npcNameLabel.ts:122-133 — extra fonts.load then updateText
- src/settings/textPreferences.ts:27-43 — setStyle on bind, then fonts.load then updateText
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/TextStyle.js:778-783 — setResolution re-renders the text
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/text/TextStyle.js:525-535 — update(true) re-runs MeasureText then updateText

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Five renders and nine uploads per NPC label is accurate (pixel text mode), and every NPC gets a label, not only named ones. But the cost is small:
  - MeasureText uses measureText bounding boxes, not pixel readback.
  - The sharpen getImageData runs on a willReadFrequently CPU canvas, so there is no GPU stall.
  - Canvases are about 250x40 px or smaller (resolution at most 3).
  - Two of the five renders run later, after the font promises resolve.
  
  Expect well under 1 ms per label, so this is negligible frame-rate impact unless a room has many NPCs.
  
  Do the cheap cleanup, not the full redesign (precomputed metrics are not needed):
  1. Delete refreshNpcNameLabelWhenFontReady. It duplicates the font wait in bindCanvasTextPreferences.
  2. In bindCanvasTextPreferences, on the first apply, skip setStyle when the computed fontFamily and fontSize already match label.style. This also helps the roomCells frontier labels.
  3. Optionally, create the label with its final resolution and sharpen the existing canvas instead of calling updateText again.
  
  That gets each label to about 2-3 renders.

### F317: The default player sprite sheet uses 26 MB of graphics memory but is 98% empty, and every other avatar on screen adds another 21 MB

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F013

**Summary.** The player character's animation sheet is a huge mostly-transparent image: 1344×4032 pixels, of which only 1.9% are drawn. Phones must decode it and hold all of it in graphics memory before the first frame. It is 82% of all startup texture memory, and each other player with a different avatar adds another copy. Packing the frames tightly, as the tree atlases already do, would cut this by about 94%.

**Technical detail.**

Measured with pngjs on public/assets/player/default: PlayerSheet.png is 1344×4032 RGBA = 20.7 MB decoded. It holds 290 untrimmed 96×84 frames (PlayerSheet.json meta, `"trimmed":false`), 1.9% opaque pixels, and the trimmed frame boxes cover 3.7% of the sheet (0.8 MB). FXSheet.png is 864×1344 = 4.4 MB with 0.2% opaque (0.1 MB trimmed). WeaponsSheet is 1.5 MB at 0.8% opaque. All four default atlases load before the first frame (src/player/defaultPlayer.ts:26-42 via BootScene.ts:192). Boot also loads the viewer's own avatar when it differs from the default (BootScene.ts:444-450), which can double this. The boot art set as a whole is 176 files, 415 KB and 33.2 MB decoded, so the default avatar alone is 27.1 MB of it (82%). Online players' ghosts load their own packs (presence.ts:929 ensureGhostAvatarPackLoaded). All 22 colors/*, the gamejew-* packs and generated punks use the same 1344×4032 layout (colors/091321 measured identical), so five visible players with distinct avatars add about 105 MB of GPU memory, a classic iOS context-loss trigger. Decoding and uploading 21 MB per sheet costs tens of milliseconds on the main thread on phones, at boot and whenever a new player appears.

Fix: reuse scripts/build_tree_atlases.mjs:22-37. It already trims each sprite and shelf-packs it, writing `trimmed/spriteSourceSize/sourceSize`, which Phaser's JSON atlas parser honours so sprite origins stay put. Run it over PlayerSheet/FXSheet/WeaponsSheet for default, colors/* and gamejew-*, and make the cryptopunk generator (src/cloudflare/cryptopunk-avatar-queue-worker.ts:8-10,139-140) pack after compositing. Check that physics bodies use explicit sizes rather than frame sizes. Use the tree atlas screenshot-parity approach as the gate. Expected result: about 26.6 MB to about 1.5 MB GPU for the default player, boot decoded total 33 MB to about 8 MB, and each remote avatar about 21 MB to about 1 MB. PNG bytes change little because transparent area compresses well.

**Evidence.**

- public/assets/player/default/PlayerSheet.json — meta size 1344×4032, 290 frames of 96×84 with "trimmed": false
- src/player/defaultPlayer.ts:26-42 — the default avatar loads PlayerSheet, PlayerCombatActionsSheet, WeaponsSheet and FXSheet atlases
- src/scenes/BootScene.ts:192 — this.load.atlas(...) for every boot avatar atlas in preload()
- src/scenes/BootScene.ts:444-450 — boot avatars = default plus the selected avatar
- src/scenes/overworld/presence.ts:929 — ghosts of online players load their avatar pack
- scripts/build_tree_atlases.mjs:22-37 — existing trim + shelf-pack writing sourceSize/spriteSourceSize

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The memory figures and load paths in the claim are correct. The fix plan needs these corrections:
  (a) build_tree_atlases.mjs is tree-specific and has to be generalized into a packer that reads an existing atlas, slices its frames, then trims and packs them.
  (b) The punk compositing happens in gen-avatar/cryptopunk/build-avatar-pack-for-punk-id.py. That script reads public/assets/player/default/PlayerSheet.{png,json} as an untrimmed 96x84 template and errors on any frame-size mismatch (:331-368, :454-465). So keep an untrimmed template outside the runtime sheet, or trim and pack after pasting. Existing punk packs in R2 need regenerating or stay large.
  (c) src/player/avatar/previews.ts:73-99 must honour spriteSourceSize and sourceSize, or the picker previews will be cropped.
  (d) The physics check is unnecessary: the body is a separate rectangle (playerLifecycle.ts:63-77).
  (e) Bigger, easier wins: only 72 of the 290 base frames and about 50 of the 112 FX frames are used by animations. The WeaponsSheet atlas is loaded at boot but none of its frames are ever used, so drop it.
  A used-frames-only repack, the same pattern as scripts/build-player-combat-actions-atlas.mjs, cuts about 90% on its own and keeps the generator and previews working unchanged. Trimming on top of that reaches about 95%. The default pack is 27.1 MiB, not 26.
- **partially confirmed.** The measurements and mechanism hold.
  
  Corrected impact: every session uploads about 27 MiB of default-avatar textures, and returning players with a level-unlocked color avatar about 48 MiB. Each distinct avatar seen adds about 21 MiB and is never evicted. Expect memory headroom and a one-time frame hitch per new avatar mid-play. Do not expect a demonstrated iOS context-loss trigger: no telemetry or report supports that, and the multi-avatar case depends on how many players are online at once.
  
  Cheaper, lower-risk first step (small effort):
  - Repack PlayerSheet to only the 72 frames the animations reference, keeping frame names and 96x84 untrimmed frames. For example an 8x9 grid, 768x756 px, about 2.2 MiB, a 89% cut.
  - Repack FXSheet to its 47 used frames, about 1.45 MiB.
  - Stop loading WeaponsSheet, which nothing references.
  
  This works as-is with the punk generator, which reads frame boxes from the template JSON and only replaces those 72 frames, and with previews.ts. Apply it to default, colors/*, gamejew-* and punk-465.
  
  Full trim and shelf-pack (about 0.17 MiB for the used base frames) is a medium-effort follow-up. It must:
  - keep an untrimmed template for gen-avatar/cryptopunk/build-avatar-pack-for-punk-id.py, or move packing after compositing;
  - update previews.ts to draw at the spriteSourceSize offset inside a sourceSize canvas;
  - regenerate existing R2 punk packs.
  
  Minor: the sourceSize/spriteSourceSize write in build_tree_atlases.mjs is at line 47, not 22-37.
- **partially confirmed.** The memory numbers hold, but the fix should change.
  
  **Step 1 (small effort)**
  - Remove the unused WeaponsSheet atlas from boot (defaultPlayer.ts:34-38). No animation or sprite references it, and it costs 1.55 MB decoded.
  - Copy only the frames animations actually use (72 of 290 PlayerSheet frames, 47 of 112 FX frames) into compact untrimmed 96x84 grids. scripts/build-player-combat-actions-atlas.mjs already does exactly this.
  - Result: default avatar about 28.4 MB → about 4.5 MB GPU, and about 22 MB → about 2.9 MB per remote avatar.
  - This needs no changes to previews.ts or the punk generator.
  
  **Step 2 (optional, for about 3 MB more)**
  - Trim the frames as well. That requires:
    - updating src/player/avatar/previews.ts:73-98 to honour spriteSourceSize;
    - changing gen-avatar/cryptopunk/build-avatar-pack-for-punk-id.py:337-368 to composite on an untrimmed layout and pack afterwards. It errors when a frame box isn't 96x84. The cited cryptopunk-avatar-queue-worker.ts lines only upload files;
    - adapting the tree packer (build_tree_atlases.mjs only handles trees);
    - regenerating all in-repo packs together, because registry.test.ts checks frame-key parity.
  
  **Notes**
  - Avatar textures are never evicted, so the cost accumulates per session. That makes the case stronger.
  - F021 content versioning makes swapping the files in place safe.

### F316: Startup art (176 files, 415 KB) can't start downloading until the map cover and game code finish; it could download while players wait

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F015

**Summary.** On a first visit the game waits up to 1.4 seconds for the map preview, then runs its 2.7 MB of code, and only then begins fetching its 176 art files. The network sits mostly idle while the phone parses the code. Telling the browser to fetch that art quietly during the wait, as was already done for the code itself, should shave a noticeable part of a second off first visits on phones.

**Technical detail.**

src/main/coarseFirstStartup.ts:1-3 sets the gate: 750 ms coarse wait, 650 ms refinement and a 1,400 ms ceiling before importMain(). F015 added low-priority modulepreload hints, so JavaScript now downloads during the gate. But BootScene.preload (src/scenes/BootScene.ts:136-192) only queues art after main.ts has evaluated (1.65 MB main chunk + 1.1 MB Phaser) and created the Phaser game. Measured boot art (bundled registries + file sizes): 176 files, 415 KB, made up of the default avatar 8 files / 204 KB, tilesets 25 / 70 KB, gameplay objects 107 / 65 KB, police enemy sheets 12 / 60 KB, and the rest under 10 KB. dist/index.html preloads only one image (flag-checkered.png). The art uses content-versioned ?v= URLs served immutable (staticAssets.ts:71-77), so a warmed response is reused from the HTTP cache. Plan: have the build plugin that writes the module preloads (src/build/bootModulePreload) also emit the versioned boot-art URL list, about 176 short paths and roughly 2 KB br, into the entry chunk. In coarseFirstEntry, after the coarse cover settles so tiles keep first claim on the network, issue `fetch(url, { priority: 'low' })` for that list; Phaser's loader then hits the cache. This helps first visits and the first visit after an art change, and repeat visits are already cached. Expect the gain to be bounded by main-script parse/eval plus Phaser/WebGL init, and confirm it with the existing F015 startup probes (held-config and phone cases) rather than assuming it. The atlas trimming finding reduces the decode side of the same path.

**Evidence.**

- src/main/coarseFirstStartup.ts:1-3 — 750 / 650 / 1,400 ms waits before importMain()
- src/scenes/BootScene.ts:136 — tilesets, objects, enemy sheets, avatar atlases and FX are queued in preload(), which runs only after main.ts creates the game
- src/scenes/BootScene.ts:192 — avatar atlases (204 KB of the 415 KB) are queued last
- dist/index.html — only one image preload (flag-checkered.png) next to 15 low-priority module preloads
- src/pages/staticAssets.ts:71-77 — ?v=-versioned public assets are served 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Boot art is about 179 unique files and 416 KB, of which 204 KB is the default avatar. All of it is queued only in BootScene.preload, after main.ts has evaluated, so it can safely be warmed earlier through ?v= URLs cached as immutable. Three corrections to the plan:
  
  - **What overlaps:** the art would overlap module evaluation and Phaser boot, not parsing. modulepreload already compiles the runtime during the gate.
  - **When to start it:** at the importMain() call, or once the runtime modulepreload links have loaded. Starting right after the coarse cover would compete with sharp-tile refinement and low-priority runtime JS on bandwidth-limited phones.
  - **How to build the list:** extract a shared boot-art list from BootScene and use it in both BootScene and the build plugin, with a test, so they can't drift.
  
  The saving is limited by the arrival world fetch, which main.ts starts at the same time as the art (F018). Expect roughly 0.2-0.6 s on cold phone visits and nothing on repeat visits. Measure it with the F015 phone and held-config probes. Two smaller points: avatar atlases aren't queued last, and the prefetch must read each response body (WebKit may still download a few files twice).

### F328: Wallet-only code (room approval recovery, collection prices, wallet signing) is downloaded by every visitor, including those with no wallet

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** This week's wallet work added about 8 KB to the startup download that every player gets, although the features only switch on when a crypto wallet is detected. That is the largest single source of this week's growth. Loading these pieces only after the wallet check says yes would keep players without a wallet from downloading crypto code, which matches the 'crypto parts only for wallet holders' rule.

**Technical detail.**

Scratch builds of each merge show boot JS going 652.4 → 657.7 KB at 254eea33 (#267, wallet approval recovery, +5.3 KB, which added roomNetwork, walletGate, wallet-gate, roomWalletRecovery, walletReceiptWait, pendingRoomWallet, roomWalletRecoveryLifecycle, roomWalletReceipt, roomWalletRecoveryRuntime and main/roomWalletRecovery to boot). Further steps were +0.8 at fc43bc1e (#270, walletSendGuard), +0.4 at #271-#272, and +1.5 at 2d540764 (#277, roomWalletCost + ownerCollectionReminder): about 8 KB in all. The code is runtime-gated but statically imported. src/main.ts:5 and :232 install recovery for everyone, and the lifecycle only runs when `dataset.wallet === 'yes'` (src/main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:10). src/scenes/overworld/hud.ts:1 and :461 construct OwnerCollectionReminder for everyone, and it is only visible with a wallet (ownerCollectionReminder.ts:43). src/auth/client.ts:1, :35, :36 and :39 statically import walletSendGuard, walletTransaction, walletReceiptWait and walletAuthentication. In-bundle cost of those 13 modules is about 18.7 KB minified, 4.7 KB brotli, plus the wallet branches inside auth/client.

Fix: add src/mint/walletFeatures.ts exporting `installWalletFeatures(game, hud)`. Load it with `import()` from a listener on the existing 'wallet-gate' event (or immediately when document.documentElement.dataset.wallet === 'yes'). Move recovery install, OwnerCollectionReminder construction and the wallet sign-in/transaction paths of auth/client behind it, and keep only wallet-detect/wallet-gate (864 B) in boot. Add these modules to a boot-forbidden list in check_bundle_budget.mjs. Test with ?crypto=0 and ?crypto=1 as the crypto-wallet-gate skill prescribes.

**Evidence.**

- src/main.ts:5 — static import of installPendingRoomWalletRecovery; installed for every visitor at :232
- src/main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:10 — recovery only enabled when document.documentElement.dataset.wallet === 'yes'
- src/scenes/overworld/hud.ts:461 — OwnerCollectionReminder constructed for every player (imported at :1)
- src/ui/setup/ownerCollectionReminder.ts:43 — reminder only visible when dataset.wallet === 'yes'
- src/auth/client.ts:1 — walletSendGuard is statically imported into the always-loaded auth client, with walletTransaction (:35), walletReceiptWait (:36) and walletAuthentication (:39)
- Scratch builds: 3ad1f213 652.4 KB → 254eea33 657.7 KB (+10 wallet modules into boot); a9dabba8 659.2 → 2d540764 660.7 (+roomWalletCost, ownerCollectionReminder)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real, but the fix saves about 4.5–5 KB brotli (about 16.5 KB minified, about 0.7% of the 660.7 KB boot), not the 8 KB in the summary. The wallet detector and gate (about 1 KB), the wallet branches left in auth/client, and the unrelated code in #267 stay. The fix must also make walletReceiptWait lazy in auth/client, because it pulls in mint/roomWalletRecovery and pendingRoomWallet. Moving main/roomWalletRecovery alone leaves most of the recovery code in boot. The crypto-gate rule only covers what is displayed and what data is fetched, so this is budget headroom and hygiene, not a rule violation. The noticeable load-time gain is tiny. The main benefit is getting back about half of the 9.3 KB left under the 670 KB budget and adding a boot-forbidden guard.

### F315: A music-theory library adds ~10 KB gzip to the startup download just for two scale tables and a sharp/flat map

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** A catch-all music-theory import ships every chord and scale dictionary at startup (about 5 KB)

**Summary.** Every page load downloads the 'tonal' music-theory library (about 28 KB raw, 10 KB compressed) inside the startup room-data file. WAMP only uses it to list the notes of a major or minor scale and to turn flats into sharps, which takes about 25 lines of plain code. Three functions that used it are not called anywhere. Replacing it trims the boot download and removes two dependencies.

**Technical detail.**

key.ts imports majorKey/minorKey from @tonaljs/key and Interval/Note from tonal (key.ts:1-2). Live uses: Note.pitchClass/Note.enharmonic in normalizeEnharmonicPitchClass (key.ts:31-39, used by normalizeRoomMusicKeyTonic on every room load) and majorKey(t).scale / minorKey(t).natural.scale in getCandidateScaleSemitones (key.ts:104-117, editor key detection, which builds full key objects with chord tables 24 times per detection). transposeRoomMusicKeyTonic, getRoomMusicKeyDeltaSemitones and getRelativeRoomMusicKey (key.ts:57-95) have zero callers in src (grep, non-test). The module lands in dist/assets/cache-v2/room-data-*.js (215,766 B raw / 54,863 B gzip), which index.html modulepreloads at boot; that chunk contains tonal's key extras (substituteDominants, secondaryDominants, chordScales). Bundling exactly the used imports with esbuild (minify, tree-shake) measured 27,862 B raw / 9,843 B gzip; @tonaljs/note pitchClass+enharmonic alone is 2,382 / 1,295 B. Fix: replace with MAJOR=[0,2,4,5,7,9,11], MINOR=[0,2,3,5,7,8,10] offsets from the tonic semitone and a 7-entry flat→sharp map (Db→C#, Eb→D#, Gb→F#, Ab→G#, Bb→A#, plus Cb/Fb/E#/B# edge cases), delete the three dead functions, drop tonal and @tonaljs/key from package.json (161,166). The Worker bundle (music/store.ts imports key.ts) shrinks too. Existing key.ts tests cover detection results.

**Evidence.**

- src/music/key.ts:1-2 — imports @tonaljs/key and the full tonal package
- src/music/key.ts:57-95 — three exported helpers with no callers
- src/music/key.ts:104-117 — scale membership derived from majorKey()/minorKey() objects
- dist/index.html — modulepreload of assets/cache-v2/room-data-0Co79BW2.js at boot
- dist/assets/cache-v2/room-data-0Co79BW2.js — 215,766 B raw, 54,863 B gzip; contains substituteDominants/secondaryDominants
- package.json:161,166 — @tonaljs/key and tonal dependencies
- src/music/key.ts:2 — import { Interval, Note } from 'tonal' (the umbrella package)
- src/music/key.ts:32 — Note.pitchClass; :37 Note.enharmonic; :61 Interval.fromSemitones; :62 Note.transpose are the only uses
- dist/assets/cache-v2/room-data-0Co79BW2.js — contains the full scale/chord dictionaries ('kumoijoshi', 'bebop', 'messiaen')
- package.json:166 — "tonal": "^6.4.3" alongside @tonaljs/key at :161

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Reframe this as "fix key normalization and detection, and drop tonal along the way":
  - Replace key.ts's tonal use with plain semitone arithmetic: a letter-to-semitone table, plus #/b/x accidentals, an optional octave, mod 12, then ROOM_MUSIC_KEY_TONICS[n]. For scale membership, take tonic + the MAJOR/MINOR offsets. pattern.ts:169-170 already defines MAJOR_SCALE_INTERVALS/MINOR_SCALE_INTERVALS, so move them into key.ts and import them back.
  - Delete the three dead helpers and remove tonal and @tonaljs/key from package.json.
  - Add key.ts tests: all 12 tonics plus flats, lowercase, octave and double-accidental inputs normalize correctly, and all 24 ascending scales detect correctly. Today 10 of 24 are misdetected and all five sharp tonics normalize to C.
  - Before shipping, check production phrases and rooms for a stored sharp keyTonic. Those currently load as C and will change pitch after the fix.
  - The bundle saving is about 9.5 KB gzip on the first visit, about 1% of boot JS. That is low on its own; the real value is the correctness fix.
  - Do not take the cheaper route of swapping only the 'tonal' umbrella import for '@tonaljs/note'. It saves about 6.5 KB gzip but keeps the bug.

### F325: Swordsman AI, PvP arena, Room Rush and ghost-race code (about 30 KB) download for every player before the first frame

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Four gameplay systems that only matter in particular rooms or modes load at startup for everyone. They are the swordsman enemy's path-planning AI, the PvP arena, Room Rush and ghost races. Together they are about 133 KB of code (about 30 KB compressed), roughly 5% of all startup code. Loading the swordsman AI when a room containing one appears, and the modes when a player enters them, would trim startup without changing gameplay.

**Technical detail.**

In-bundle brotli cost, measured by removing each group from the concatenated minified boot modules: swordsman AI 72 KB minified / 16.7 KB br (liveObjects/swordsmanController.ts 2,853 lines, enemies/swordsmanTraversal.ts 1,430, swordsmanRobustPlanner.ts 816, swordsmanCollectSelection.ts 505, swordsmanRuntimeStateController). PvP is 32 KB / 7.4 KB br (pvpArenaController, pvpSpawn, pvpCombatCoordinator, pvpLocalPresentationController, pvpCombatGeometry, composition/pvp, ui/setup/pvpModal). Room Rush is 17 KB / 3.2 KB br, and ghost race is 12 KB / 3.0 KB br. The swordsman AI is reached only through src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects.ts:69, a static import constructed at :377 and used per enemy at :930-931 (`case 'swordsman'`). OverworldPlayScene.ts:36-38 imports only a type. The swordsman catalog stays in room-data (enemies/swordsmanAi.ts), so the editor palette is unaffected. Plan: (1) keep a thin facade in liveObjects with the same method surface, and `import('./liveObjects/swordsmanController')` when a hydrated room snapshot contains swordsman_ai or a swordsman objective. Rooms already hydrate asynchronously, so spawn those enemies dormant until the module resolves, then reset them through the existing resetFacingMemory/applyFacing path (liveObjects.ts:1833-1834). (2) Build the PvP and Room Rush composition owners on the first entry into those modes. Add each to the boot-forbidden list. The combined saving is about 30 KB brotli and about 133 KB less JavaScript to parse on phones.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects.ts:69 — static import of LiveObjectSwordsmanController into the boot chunk
- src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects.ts:930 — the controller is only exercised for live objects of kind 'swordsman'
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:36-38 — only a type import from swordsmanRobustPlanner
- output/build/chunk-graph.json — main-CZ-WS5lm.js contains swordsmanController, swordsmanTraversal, swordsmanRobustPlanner, pvpArenaController, pvpSpawn, roomRushMode, ghostRace and their helpers

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Lazy-load the Sword Hunter controller group (liveObjects/swordsmanController and runtime-state controller, swordsmanCollectSelection, enemies/swordsmanTraversal, swordsmanTraversalSkills, swordsmanRobustPlanner). This saves about 16.7 KB br / 71 KB minified.
  - Trigger the import for swordsman_ai **and police enemies**: POLICE_ENEMY_OBJECT_IDS map to kind 'swordsman' (behaviorRegistry.ts:77).
  - Prefetch when the room snapshot is fetched, and hold a goal run's start until the module is ready.
  - The facade must return default objective and defeat modes, because enemyLifecycle.ts:169/173 queries them for every enemy.
  
  Secondary:
  - Move the PvP arena controller, spawn and modal behind a facade, loaded on invite or launcher open, for about 5-7 KB br. pvpCombatCoordinator, pvpCombatGeometry, pvpHeartDisplay and pvpInvulnerabilityFx stay in boot, since they are used per frame or by shared renderers.
  - Move roomRushMode, roomRushResults and the weekly repository out, for about 2-3 KB br. roomRushRuns' HUD formatters stay.
  - Drop ghost race. It runs on every goal run and in the goal-intro modal.
  
  Realistic total is about 23-27 KB br (about 4% of boot), not 30 KB.

### F320: Half of the startup page is level-editor markup and phone-editor styles that players never see unless they build

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F025
- **Also covers:** Phone-editor styles (225 rules, 49 KB) still load in every player's render-blocking stylesheet

**Summary.** The first page every visitor downloads still contains the whole level editor's sidebar, toolbars, music and sprite editors: 1,193 hidden elements, half the page.
