The always-loaded stylesheet still includes 42 KB of phone-editor styles. The editor's code and desktop styles already load only when someone builds. Moving this markup and these styles along with them would make the first page about a third smaller and quicker to process on phones.

**Technical detail.**

I parsed dist/index.html (270,609 B / 37,244 B br), which has 2,421 live elements. These builder-only roots are still in the initial document: #sidebar (index.html:251, 718 elements, 69 KB), #editor-shell-top (:1349, 123), #editor-music-overlay (:1649, 86), #editor-sprite-overlay (69), #editor-inspector (89), #course-editor-shell (:1860, 61), #editor-shell-dock (35) and #mobile-editor-nav (12). That totals 1,193 elements and 115,206 B. Removing them brings the HTML from 37,244 B to 25,220 B br (12.0 KB less). Every module that queries these ids is already in lazy chunks (sidebarSections → usage-*.js; editorPhoneDock, editorDockShell, customSpriteEditor, paletteController and courseComposerPanel → editorUi-*.js; musicWorkflow → keyboardShortcuts-*.js). The one exception is keyboardPassthrough.ts, which only needs #sidebar to exist. CSS: src/styles/sections/responsive.css:1 still imports phone-editor-shell/tools/music/actions/dock into the render-blocking main.css (:7). That is 50,867 B of source, 41,949 B minified and 5,179 B br. F025 moved editor.css and course-editor.css into the lazy editor-bundle.css but left these. Plan: (1) wrap the eight roots in `<template id="deferred-…">` and swap them in from ensureEditorUiReady, the same mechanism LazyModal.ensure uses (lazyModal.ts:64-68, index.html:2367). This removes 49% of the startup DOM, though not the bytes. (2) For the 12 KB br, move the markup into the editor chunk as an HTML string or an imported .html asset, which also moves it into immutable cache instead of the per-release HTML. (3) Move the phone-editor-* imports into editor-bundle.css after the existing ordering checks (smoke:editor-phone, smoke:editor-dock), keeping the display:none defaults in the always-loaded editor-placeholders.css.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:251 — <div id="sidebar"> (718 builder-only elements) in the initial document
- index.html:1349 — #editor-shell-top (123 elements); :1649 #editor-music-overlay (86); :1860 #course-editor-shell (61)
- index.html:2367 — existing <template id="deferred-room-history-modal"> pattern from F025
- src/ui/setup/lazyModal.ts:68 — template.replaceWith(template.content) on first open
- src/styles/sections/responsive.css:1 — phone-editor-shell/tools/music/actions/dock imported into the always-loaded sheet
- src/styles/main.css:7 — responsive.css is part of the render-blocking main.css (dist main-BL_6D6kV.css 317,803 B / 35,029 B br)
- src/styles/main.css:7 — @import './sections/responsive.css' in the render-blocking sheet
- src/styles/sections/responsive.css:1 — imports phone-editor-shell/tools/music/actions/dock into it
- src/styles/editor-bundle.css:1-4 — lazy editor sheet with the same layer order exists
- src/ui/setup/editorStyles.ts:1 — editor bundle is loaded only by the editor
- dist/assets/cache-v2/main-BL_6D6kV.css — 317,803 B; 225 editor-only phone rules = 48,843 B / 5,204 B br

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Keep the numbers: 1,193 elements and 115,206 B (49% of the live DOM), HTML 37,244 to 25,220 B br, and 41,949 B min / about 5.2 KB br of phone-editor CSS. Correct the mechanism. keyboardPassthrough is not the only boot dependency. MobileUiController (src/ui/mobile/controller.ts:51-52, :157, :182), setupLazyModalTriggers (src/ui/setup/controllers.ts:243, #btn-wamp-o-gram) and the scene commands (src/ui/setup/sceneCommands.ts:45-46, :352, :364, Expanded Room Save/Publish) also bind at boot to elements inside #sidebar and #mobile-editor-nav. Because of optional chaining, deferring the roots would silently drop those listeners. The plan has to move them into setupEditorUi or use delegation. For the CSS move, note that the lazy sheet is inserted before main.css (editorStyles.ts:30-31). That flips equal-specificity order between phone-editor rules and the other files in the responsive layer, so the F025 computed-style parity matrix has to be rerun. The display:none defaults at phone-editor-dock.css:2-5 also need to stay always-loaded. Total gain is about 17 KB br on first or post-release loads, plus parse and DOM-creation time for subtrees that are already display:none. That is low impact, about the same as F025.

### F323: Returning players re-download the whole 327 KB game chunk after every release, even when its code did not change

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** large

**Summary.** The main game file gets a new name on every release, because it contains the names of about 60 other files and those change whenever any of them changes. In 8 of the last 23 releases none of its own code changed, but every returning player still re-downloaded and re-compiled it. Letting the page map stable names to versioned files would let the browser keep it.

**Technical detail.**

I built 23 consecutive main commits (45d3b6f4 → 2d540764) in scratch. main-*.js (334,676 B br, 1.65 MB raw, 410 modules) got a new name in 23 of 23 builds. phaser-vendor changed in 0 of 22, room-data in 8 of 22 and rewardStings in 15 of 22. git diff shows 8 of those builds changed no source file in the main chunk (adcd47f2, ac2b8c89, 3ad1f213, adb31c8d, 4ca2f98c, c25b1f7b, 4596b928, a9dabba8). I diffed main between 254eea33 and adb31c8d with hashed names normalised. The only differences are 86 embedded chunk file names (EditorScene-*, aboutModal-*, room-data-* and so on) and re-mangled cross-chunk import aliases (`cp as TC` → `cO as TC` from room-data). This is Rollup's hash propagation: [name]-[hash] at vite.config.ts:91-92, with the main chunk statically importing 15 chunks and dynamically importing 25. Each release (about 8 a day this week) therefore costs a returning player about 327 KB br of download plus a cold compile of 1.65 MB, because V8's code cache is keyed by URL. Fix options: (a) import map. Have cross-chunk specifiers name stable bare ids, write `<script type="importmap">` into index.html (already revalidated on every visit), and hash chunks on their own content only. That needs a post-build plugin that also rewrites Vite's __vite__mapDeps preload lists, so treat it as a spike. (b) Combine it with `output.minifyInternalExports: false` so export aliases stop reshuffling. (c) Split main by churn: engine modules are about 70% of its bytes and were touched in 14 of 23 builds, UI 14% (7 builds), data/network 17% (7 builds). The expected cut is at least 35% of main-chunk re-downloads from (a) alone, more with (c).

**Evidence.**

- vite.config.ts:91-92 — entry and chunk names are [name]-[hash].js
- vite.config.ts:95 — manualChunks only separates phaser-vendor and room-data (:101); everything else lands in one 410-module main chunk
- output/build/chunk-graph.json — main-CZ-WS5lm.js has 15 static and 25 dynamic chunk imports
- Scratch builds 45d3b6f4…a9dabba8 — 23 distinct main-*.js names; phaser-vendor-D2-AkG0J.js identical in all
- Normalized diff of main chunk between 254eea33 and adb31c8d builds — only embedded chunk hashes and import aliases differ

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Rollup's hash propagation does rename main-*.js (334,676 B br, 1.65 MB raw) on every release. Main's own content also changes every commit, because vite.config.ts:35-37 and :60 put the git revision into VITE_APP_BUILD_ID, which src/main/clientErrorReporter.ts:35 and src/bugReports/reporter.ts:62 compile into the main chunk. An import map alone would therefore save nothing. Any spike must first move the build ID out of main (into the small entry chunk, the HTML or a window global), then add the import map with stable chunk ids, rewrite __vite__mapDeps and the modulepreload links, and set minifyInternalExports:false. The saving is about 35% only for players who return after a single release, and roughly 0.35^k after k releases. At this week's ~12-14 main deploys a day, daily returning players gain almost nothing. Worth revisiting once the release pace slows. Dropping the build SHA from main is the cheap first step.

### F326: The NFT image renderer (6.8 KB) loads at startup because of a single cache-clearing import

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Every first visit downloads the code that draws room pictures for NFT metadata and share images, even though nothing on the first screen uses it. It is pulled in only because the room-saving code imports one small 'clear this cache' function from a file that also imports the renderer. Changing that file to load the renderer on demand removes 6.8 KB and one request from startup.

**Technical detail.**

src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:26 imports invalidateSharedRoomPreviewCache and uses it only at :990 and :998 after saves. That module (src/persistence/sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:1) statically imports renderRoomSnapshotToPngDataUrl from src/mint/roomMetadataRender, but calls it only inside the async loader at :36. The renderer chunk roomMetadataRender-CRbYqm51.js (23,220 B raw / 6,838 B brotli) holds mint/roomMetadata.ts (16.6 KB minified), roomMetadataRender.ts, roomMetadataRenderLayout, roomTokenLinks, customTiles/draw and starfieldCanvas. Because of this edge it is a boot file with its own modulepreload hint in dist/index.html. The edge dates from a889dc39 (2026-07-18), and F019's deferral work did not catch it. Every real caller of the renderer is already lazy: exploreModal, firstPublishModal, guestRoomRecoveryModal, profileModal, wampOGram/render and playlistModal. Fix (2 lines): `const { renderRoomSnapshotToPngDataUrl } = await import('../mint/roomMetadataRender');` inside the IIFE at sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:29-39, or move the invalidation maps into their own tiny module. Then add 'src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts' to the boot-forbidden list in scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs. Saves 6.8 KB brotli, 23 KB of parse work and 1 of 18 boot requests.

**Evidence.**

- src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:26 — import { invalidateSharedRoomPreviewCache } from './sharedRoomPreviewCache'
- src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:990 — the only uses are cache invalidation after writes (also :998)
- src/persistence/sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:1 — static import of renderRoomSnapshotToPngDataUrl from '../mint/roomMetadataRender'
- src/persistence/sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:36 — the renderer is only awaited inside the async preview loader
- output/build/boot-bundle.json — roomMetadataRender-CRbYqm51.js is one of the 18 boot files (6,838 B br)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Making the renderer import lazy in sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts does take the NFT and share-image renderer out of startup, but it saves about 6.0 KB brotli (6,155 B; about 21.9 KB raw parse), not 6.8 KB. It does not save a request: startup still needs starfieldCanvas and customTiles/draw (through visuals/starfield.ts and roomSnapshotTexture.ts), so Rollup puts them in a new ~0.6 KB brotli startup chunk, starfieldCanvas-*.js, and the count stays at 18. There is no general list of modules banned from startup in check_bundle_budget.mjs; adding the guard means a new check like `bootModules.has('src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts')`. This is a cheap tidy-up worth doing, but its effect on load time is small.

### F319: Developer-only debugging tools (about 8 KB) ship in every player's startup download

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** Load the opt-in phone profiler and resource logger only when asked for: about 5 KB of the 9 KB boot-budget headroom

**Summary.** Several diagnostic tools are switched on only by special web addresses or by the bug-report button, yet everyone downloads them at startup: a resource logger, a phone performance profiler, a capture debugger and the bug-report form. Loading them only when their switch is on would save about 8 KB for every visitor.

**Technical detail.**

In-bundle cost of 9 modules is 27 KB minified / 7.6 KB br: src/main/resourceDebug.ts (7.3 KB minified), src/debug/mobilePerformanceProfiler.ts (6.9 KB), src/bugReports/reporter.ts (6.0 KB) + reporter.css (1.8 KB), src/main/captureDebug.ts (2.5 KB), main/debugState, main/runtimeTransitionProbe, main/worldReplacementCoverage and avatars/debug. Gating: installRuntimeResourceDebugLogger returns null unless query options are present (resourceDebug.ts:241-244). createMobilePerformanceProfiler returns null unless a query flag is set (mobilePerformanceProfiler.ts:100-107). The bug report dialog is wired at boot through bugReports/runtime.ts:9 but only opens on a button click (reporter.ts:86). Plan: dynamic-import the logger and profiler when their query flags are present. Keep window.get_wamp_resource_debug as a thin stub that lazy-loads, so smoke scripts keep working. Import reporter.ts and reporter.css on the first Report click, keeping the recording buffer (recentReplay, recorder) in boot. Add src/debug/* and main/resourceDebug to the boot-forbidden list.

**Evidence.**

- src/main.ts:42-45 — static import of getRuntimeResourceDebugState/installRuntimeResourceDebugLogger
- src/main/resourceDebug.ts:241-244 — the logger returns null unless query options are present
- src/debug/mobilePerformanceProfiler.ts:100 — the profiler is null unless isMobilePerformanceProfilerEnabled() (query flag)
- src/bugReports/runtime.ts:9 — the bug report dialog module is statically imported at boot
- src/bugReports/reporter.ts:86 — the dialog opens only from button clicks
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:31-35 — static import of createMobilePerformanceProfiler into the boot scene
- src/debug/mobilePerformanceProfiler.ts:97-113 — profiler returns null unless ?mobilePerf or ?perf is set
- src/main/resourceDebug.ts:237-244 — logger returns null unless explicitly enabled
- src/main.ts:202-205 — existing lazy-import pattern for the audio debug overlay
- scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs:14 — boot budget 670 KB; current build reports 660.7 KB

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Only resourceDebug.ts, mobilePerformanceProfiler.ts and the bug-report dialog (reporter.ts + reporter.css + sender.ts + analytics/replay/player.ts) can realistically be deferred. Together that is about 6-7 KB brotli (about 1% of the 660.7 KB boot JS), not the full 9-module total.
  
  The other modules are needed at runtime or synchronously:
  - worldReplacementCoverage: production world-tile events.
  - avatars/debug: header on every profile and avatar request.
  - debugState: main.ts:163 browse check and guest replay.
  - captureDebug: sync window.capture_debug_info used by smoke scripts.
  - runtimeTransitionProbe: also wired into main.ts:302; only 0.1 KB.
  
  The bug-report form is a player-facing feature, not a developer tool. Lazy-load it on the first "Report a bug" click, but:
  - keep an isOpen() stub for the postrender recorder;
  - freeze the replay synchronously before awaiting the import;
  - guard the scene-shutdown race for the async profiler;
  - move the query-flag check into a tiny module that stays in boot.

### F318: After the first tap, every player downloads all 29 sound effects (469 KB), including editor, PvP and bounce-pad sounds the room may never play

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F023

**Summary.** Seconds after a player first touches the game, WAMP fetches every sound effect one after another, about 469 KB on Android and Chrome. Most rooms use only a few of them, and the files are high-quality stereo even for tiny clicks. Preloading only the core sounds plus those the current room needs, and encoding short effects in mono, would roughly halve this background data use on phones.

**Technical detail.**

src/audio/sfx.ts:452-454: on first interaction it warms HOT_GAMEPLAY_CUES (:88: jump, land, footstep, collect, player-hurt), then after BACKGROUND_WARM_DELAY_MS = 1,500 (:90) calls warmRemainingCues. That function (:479-484) chains a download plus decode for every non-MP3 cue path, 29 files. Format choice (:384-386) is .ogg where Vorbis plays, otherwise .m4a. Sizes from public/assets/sfx: 468,570 B as OGG and 398,701 B as M4A. The largest are bounce-pad 75,839 B, ladder-climb 35,619, game-fail 29,818, gun-shot 23,397 and fruit-collect 23,231, and ui-click/ui-hover are 19 KB each. `file` reports every OGG as 'Vorbis audio, stereo, 44100 Hz, ~160000 bps'. That is about 23 s of stereo audio, kept decoded in this.buffers (sfx.ts:620) as about 9 MB of float PCM. The list includes music-editor cues (clear-slot, place-phrase) that only builders hear. Plan: warm hot cues plus cues mapped from object ids in the loaded room snapshots (placed bounce pads, guns, ladders); load editor and music-editor cues when the editor opens; load the rest on first play, where the 120 ms on-time window already exists. Separately, re-encode short effects as mono 80-96 kbps Vorbis/AAC with the existing scripts/build_audio_assets.mjs pipeline and an ear check. That should be about 50-60% smaller and halve decoded memory.

**Evidence.**

- src/audio/sfx.ts:88 — HOT_GAMEPLAY_CUES = jump, land, footstep, collect, player-hurt
- src/audio/sfx.ts:454 — warmRemainingCues() 1.5 s after the first interaction
- src/audio/sfx.ts:479 — warmRemainingCues loads every non-MP3 cue path one after another
- src/audio/sfx.ts:620 — decoded buffers are kept in this.buffers
- public/assets/sfx/movement/bounce-pad.ogg — 75,839 B, Vorbis stereo 44.1 kHz ~160 kbps (all cue OGGs total 468,570 B)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Narrow this to a low-impact asset trim. Keep the background warm-up, because it is the deliberate fix for feedback cues being dropped as 'late' on first play. Then:
  (a) Cut bounce-pad.ogg/.m4a to about 1.3 s, since playback stops at 1.0 s plus a 220 ms fade.
  (b) Re-encode the 20 stereo 160 kbps effects as mono at about 80-96 kbps, which first needs scripts/build_audio_assets.mjs extended to output SFX OGG/M4A, plus an ear check. Expected saving is about 40-50% of the 469 KB and about half the decoded memory; the shortest files shrink less because of Vorbis header overhead.
  (c) Optionally skip the background warm-up when navigator.connection.saveData is set.
  Corrections to the finding: 9 of the 29 OGGs are already mono. Assets are cached for 1 day, so this is roughly a once-a-day cost. Room-aware warming is medium effort because bounce and ladder sounds come from tiles, stomps and bullets, not just placed objects. It should only be done if first-play drops are measured and found acceptable.

### F322: Players who turn sound effects off still download every effect (~400-470 KB) and start the audio engine

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F078

**Summary.** F078 made the game skip effects while the effects volume is zero, but the background preloading that runs after the first tap was not included. A player with effects off still downloads all 29 effect files and starts the audio engine. That is wasted data on phones, and classroom players who mute everything still pay for it.

**Technical detail.**

onFirstInteraction schedules warmCues(HOT_GAMEPLAY_CUES) and warmRemainingCues() (sfx.ts:452-455), which call loadBuffer for every non-MP3 cue path (sfx.ts:471-485) with no volume check; loadBuffer calls engine.getContext(), which creates the AudioContext (sfx.ts:618-629), and the gesture listeners then resume it. play() itself blocks at volume 0 (sfx.ts:553-556), and room music skips loading while muted (controller.ts:225-231), so the warm-up is the only path that ignores the setting. Measured on dist: the 29 warmed paths total 468,570 B as .ogg (Chrome/Firefox) and 398,701 B as .m4a (Safari). Fix: in warmCues/warmRemainingCues return when this.volume <= 0; in setVolume, when going from 0 to >0 after the first gesture, run the warm-up then. Optionally suspend the shared context while both music and effects are 0.

**Evidence.**

- src/audio/sfx.ts:452-455 — warm-up scheduled after first gesture regardless of volume
- src/audio/sfx.ts:471-485 — warm loops load every non-MP3 cue
- src/audio/sfx.ts:618-629 — loadBuffer creates the AudioContext via engine.getContext()
- src/audio/sfx.ts:553-556 — play() already skips when volume is 0 (F078)
- src/music/controller.ts:225-231 — music skips work while muted
- src/main.ts:208-211 — stored volumes applied at startup

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F321: Neighbouring rooms can be downloaded twice when you start moving right after entering a room

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** On phones, entering a room immediately asks the server for all four neighbouring rooms in one request. When you start running toward one of them a moment later, the game asks for that room again in a second request. It only recognises a duplicate request when the whole list of rooms matches. That doubles the download and the server work for the room you are heading into, and the room-loading code also uses two different server endpoints for the same data. Track in-flight downloads one room at a time.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism:
- In the reduced runtime profile, every computePreviewSelection calls prefetchExactCardinalRoomSnapshots (worldStreaming.ts:2665-2671, 2676-2711). That issues one batch of up to 4 rooms.
- On the next frame, a moving player triggers prefetchPlayableRoomForTransition, because the prefetch distance is the full 640 px room width (roomTransition.ts:85, 359-372). That calls ensureRoomSnapshotsBatch for a single room (worldStreaming.ts:1396-1400).
- previewCache dedupes only by the exact canonical set of references (buildRoomSnapshotBatchKey + queryRoomSnapshotBatch, previewCache.ts:304-327). A request for [E] while [E,W,N,S] is in flight sends a second POST. The nearest-9 startup batch overlaps the same way.
- A separate transport, ensurePublishedRoomSnapshot (GET /api/rooms/:id/published, previewCache.ts:482-529), has its own per-room in-flight map and doesn't know about the batch path.
- The snapshot route answers 'private, no-store' (rooms/routes.ts:128), so every duplicate is a Worker call plus a D1 read.

Scale: up to one extra POST of the full room (about 10–50 KB) per room crossing on phones whenever the player moves before the cardinal batch returns, which typically takes 100–300 ms.

Fix:
1. Keep a Map<roomId:detail, Promise> of in-flight snapshot loads in previewCache.
2. Subtract in-flight rooms before building a batch and await their promises.
3. Route ensurePublishedRoomSnapshot through the same index, or retire it in favour of the batch path.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:2665-2671 — reduced play profile calls prefetchExactCardinalRoomSnapshots on every selection
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:2676-2711 — one 4-room 'full' batch
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1396-1400 — transition prefetch issues a 1-room batch
- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:304-327 — dedupe keyed by the whole reference set
- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:482-529 — second transport (GET published) with its own in-flight map
- src/scenes/overworld/roomTransition.ts:85 — prefetch distance = whole room
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:128 — snapshot query response is private, no-store

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F324: Room pictures in menus download their art one file at a time, and fetch tree art the game already has

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The small room pictures in Explore, profiles, playlists, the end-of-run rating screen, the first-publish celebration and the postcard maker load each picture file only after the previous one finishes. A forest room needs about 15 files, so on a phone this is a chain of 15 waits instead of one batch. Trees are also downloaded as 221 separate files even though the game already loads them as 11 combined sheets. The server copy of this code already loads everything at once, and the same fix takes about 30 lines here.

**Technical detail.**

src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts awaits each asset inside its draw loops:
- background layers in sequence (170-181; themes have 3-8 layers: forest 8, dark_forest 7, spooky_mountain 7)
- each tileset at its first tile (293)
- each object type (376)

There is no prefetch, so N distinct assets cost N sequential round trips on a cold cache. Example: forest with 2 tilesets and 5 object types is 15 serial fetches, about 1.5 s at a 100 ms mobile RTT versus roughly one RTT plus transfer if run in parallel. The Pages copy already solves this with primeRoomAssetCache (src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:309-349), which collects every path and runs Promise.allSettled before drawing.

Callers: Explore, profile and playlist cards via sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:36 (tilePixelSize 4); firstPublishModal.ts:163; guestRoomRecoveryModal.ts:266; runRatingModal.ts:649; wampOGram/render.ts:35; minted-room.ts:95; and world-tile leaf rendering (world-tile-render.ts:58), where serial loads also lengthen Browser Rendering time.

Trees: in-game, trees come from 11 family atlases (assets/sceneArt.ts:16-18, 67; dist/assets/objects/trees/atlases). roomMetadataRender loads objectConfig.path, the individual PNGs (221 files under dist/assets/objects/trees/devkidd), so the same art is downloaded a second time. imageCache (46) also never evicts.

Fix:
1. Add a prime step mirroring primeRoomAssetCache: collect background layer paths, tileset paths for every gid present, and object paths, then Promise.all(loadAssetImage). About 30 lines.
2. Optionally resolve tree ids to their atlas image plus frame rect from the atlas JSON, like roomSnapshotTexture.ts:672-681.

**Evidence.**

- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:170-181 — `await loadAssetImage(layer.path)` per background layer, sequential
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:293 — `await loadAssetImage(tileset.path)` inside the per-tile loop
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:376 — `await loadAssetImage(objectConfig.path)` per placed object
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:309-349 — the server copy prefetches all assets in parallel first
- src/persistence/sharedRoomPreviewCache.ts:36 — Explore/profile/playlist cards use this renderer
- src/assets/sceneArt.ts:16-18 — the game draws trees from atlas frames, not the individual PNGs

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Keep fix 1, with the benefit stated smaller. Add a per-snapshot prime step that mirrors primeRoomAssetCache (Promise.allSettled over background layers, the tilesets of gids actually present, and object paths) before drawing. It can be adapted from the unused warmRoomMetadataRenderAssetCache at roomMetadataRender.ts:488-504. The saving applies mainly to:
  - Explore, profile and playlist cards whose background theme is not cached yet (a chain of 3-8 layer fetches becomes one parallel round)
  - tree and decoration PNGs that have not been seen yet
  - the cold standalone pages (minted-room.html, room-preview-render.html, the first leaf of each world-tile browser session)
  
  It is not "15 serial waits" for in-game menus. BootScene already preloads every tileset and boot object under the same immutable versioned URLs, and the run-rating, first-publish, guest-recovery and postcard previews draw rooms whose art the game has already loaded. A realistic saving is a few hundred ms on first view per theme on mobile, and nothing on later views.
  
  Drop fix 2 (atlas reuse for trees). The renderer fetches only the trees placed in the room, never all 221. A single tree PNG is about 5 KB against 20-132 KB per family atlas, and the editor palette already uses the individual PNGs, so switching to atlases would often download more bytes.

### F327: The world-map tile cache rereads its whole index from disk after almost every tile it loads from disk

- **Area:** Load time and downloads (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The browser-side cache for world-map tiles keeps one small record per tile on disk. Every time it serves a tile from disk or saves a new one, it reopens the database and reads every record to decide whether to delete old tiles. It also re-checks each tile's fingerprint even though it checked it when saving. For returning visitors this repeats many times while the map loads, on the phone's main thread. Load the index once, keep a running total, and only clean up when over budget.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism:
1. Every persistent hit re-hashes the whole blob with SHA-256 (byteCache.ts:218) and schedules a metadata touch (223).
2. Touches and writes drain through setTimeout(0) (258-264) into persistBatch (288-348).
3. Each drain opens IndexedDB in saveMetadata (434-447), then prunePersistent runs loadAllMetadata (363-364, 465-478). That opens IndexedDB again, getAll()s every record and sorts it (367) just to compare the total against the budget.
4. Drains serialise, so a page load with warm tiles runs one full-table read per burst.

Scale: the budget is 128 MB normal and 48 MB reduced (scheduler.ts:101,111), which is thousands of records for 642x354 tile PNGs.

The in-memory LRU also copies and sorts all entries on every insert once it is over 16 MB (byteCache.ts:350-361).

Fix:
1. Load metadata once on the first openCache into an in-memory index with a running byte total.
2. Update the index on write, touch and delete, and prune only when the total exceeds byteBudget.
3. Keep one IDB connection.
4. Skip re-hashing persistent hits: the cache key already embeds contentHash, and bytes were verified before they were written (byteCache.ts:139).
5. Use Map insertion order (delete and re-set on access) for the memory LRU.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:218 — SHA-256 re-check on every persistent hit
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:223 — each hit schedules a metadata touch
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:258-264 — drain on setTimeout(0)
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:347 — every drain ends with prunePersistent
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:363-367 — prune loads all metadata and sorts
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:436 — saveMetadata opens its own IDB connection
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:466 — loadAllMetadata opens another IDB connection
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:356 — memory eviction sorts every entry per insert
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/scheduler.ts:101 — 128 MB persistent budget (48 MB reduced at :111)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The tile cache re-reads its whole metadata store from IndexedDB once per persistence drain, not once per tile, because hits arriving during a drain are batched together (tested at byteCache.test.ts:268). The store is about 1,000 small records, not thousands: production has 994 tiles of about 84 KB each, and the whole world fits under the 128 MB budget. The waste is real for warm returning visitors, because touch-only batches cannot add bytes yet still trigger prunePersistent's getAll. Fix: in persistBatch (byteCache.ts:347), prune only when the batch saved at least one new write; optionally reuse one IndexedDB connection. Keep the SHA-256 check on persistent hits; it is a deliberate, tested integrity guard (byteCache.test.ts:336), costs under 1 ms and runs asynchronously. Do not add a load-once in-memory index with a running total, because it would go stale across tabs and miss the early bootstrap's cache entries, which have no metadata. Skip the memory-LRU change, which saves microseconds on about 200 entries.

### F329: Ghost race lookup still loads and parses every saved version of a room, on every goal-room intro and restart

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** high · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F026

**Summary.** When a player opens a timed challenge room, the game asks the server for the #1 and personal-best ghosts. That server call still reads every version the builder ever published (each 9-38 KB) and parses them all, which is the slow pattern fixed for leaderboards in F026. The ghost route was added four days before that fix and never got it. Switching it to the same lightweight loader the run-finish path already uses is a small change and makes every timed room open faster.

**Technical detail.**

handleRoomGhosts (src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghosts.ts:83-103) calls loadRoomRecord, which batches prepareLoadRoomVersionsStatement (rooms/store.ts:806-826: `SELECT version, snapshot_json, ... FROM room_versions WHERE room_id = ? ORDER BY version`, no LIMIT) and runs mapStoredRoomVersions over every row (JSON.parse + cloneRoomSnapshot per version, store.ts:828+). It only needs one version: resolveAggregatedRoomLeaderboardSelection(record, version) plus the family version list. The F026 fix (loadRoomRankingRecord with compact room_version_facts and `snapshotVersions: [v]`) is already used by run finish at runs/routes.ts:217-221 and by the lineage routes at :608 and :654. Callers: ghostRaceIntro.ts:33-48 fetches on every goal intro for a published time-ranked room (supportsGhostRace = any time-ranked goal), and ghostRace.ts:113-130 via OverworldPlayScene.ts:4735 refetches after each restart while racing; ghostRepository.ts:35-36 sends cache:'no-store' and the response is private, no-store, so nothing caches it. Size: the 7 production rooms in test/fixtures/smart-autotiling/references are at versions 3-13 with snapshots of 9.2-37.6 KB, so a v12 room means about 190 KB read from D1 and 12 parses per request instead of one row. git log shows the route arrived in bf4718da (2026-10-06); F026 completed 2026-10-10 without touching it. Fix: replace loadRoomRecord with loadRoomRankingRecord(env, roomId, coords, { viewerUserId, viewerWalletAddress, snapshotVersions: [requestedVersion] }) and add a statement-count test like auth/sessionLookup.test.ts. Optional follow-up: the `top` half is public and could share the 20 s room-standings cache.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghosts.ts:86 — handleRoomGhosts calls loadRoomRecord (all versions) before selecting one version
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:806-826 — versions statement selects snapshot_json for every version of the room, no LIMIT
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:78-91 — loadRoomRecord maps every row through mapStoredRoomVersions (parse each)
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:217-221 — run finish already uses loadRoomRankingRecord with snapshotVersions: [existing.roomVersion]
- src/ui/setup/ghostRaceIntro.ts:48 — loadRoomGhosts on every goal intro for time-ranked published rooms
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:4735 — refreshAfterRestart refetches ghosts after each restart
- src/runs/ghostRepository.ts:35-36 — fetch with cache: 'no-store'; server replies private, no-store (ghosts.ts:103)
- test/fixtures/smart-autotiling/references/*.room.json — real rooms at versions 3-13, snapshots 9.2-37.6 KB

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** Small corrections:
  
  1. runs/routes.ts:608 and :654 are the difficulty-vote and rating-submit routes, not "lineage routes". The closest model for the fix is handleRoomLeaderboard at :566-571, which passes snapshotVersions: [version], the requested version. Doing the same here is enough, because the selection only moves to the current published version, whose snapshot is always loaded.
  2. The finding understates the cost in two ways. First, the full-record path also recomputes every version's fingerprint facts on every request (roomVersionLineage.ts:100-107). Second, the cost has no upper bound as a room's history grows. For a time-ranked room with a long history (the spawn room 0,0 has about 176 versions and 10.5 MB, per F026), every goal intro and every racing restart would bring back the 1-4 s room_record time and Worker CPU risk that F026 removed. I did not check whether 0,0's goal is time-ranked; that needs production data.
  3. For typical rooms of 3-13 versions, the saving is modest: about 100-200 KB of D1 reads and around 10 parses per request.
- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism, the missed call site and the fix all hold. The fix is to swap loadRoomRecord for `loadRoomRankingRecord(env, roomId, coords, { viewerUserId, viewerWalletAddress, snapshotVersions: [requestedVersion] })`, as handleRoomLeaderboard already does, and to change the ghosts.test.ts mock to rooms/rankingRecord.
  
  Correct the benefit statement on two points:
  1. Typical rooms (v3-13) save only about 100-200 KB of D1 reads and a few milliseconds. The high-impact case is heavily republished, time-ranked rooms such as 0,0 (176 versions, about 10.5 MB) and 2,1 (215 versions). There, every ghost intro and every racing restart repeats the full pre-F026 cost of 0.2-3.7 s and risks the CPU limit. Whether 0,0 is time-ranked is likely but not verified from code.
  2. The ghost fetch does not block Start, so the gain is mainly server cost, D1 contention and how soon the ghost option appears, not "rooms open faster".

### F332: Every link-preview image is a 3 MB uncompressed PNG, and most of the render time goes to a slow checksum

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** Share preview images are 3 MB uncompressed PNGs, redrawn from scratch on every link unfurl (146 ms each)

**Summary.** When someone shares a WAMP room or a Wamp-O-Gram, the preview picture that Discord, X, iMessage or WhatsApp downloads is about 3 MB, because the server writes the PNG without compressing it. The same picture compressed is 12 to 70 KB. About 150 of the 150 to 250 ms it takes to make each picture is spent on a checksum written one bit at a time. Turning on the compression that is built into Cloudflare makes the images about 40 to 200 times smaller and roughly 5 to 10 times faster to make.

**Technical detail.**

Both server rasterizers emit zlib 'stored' (uncompressed) blocks: src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:722-784 (createZlibUncompressedBlockStream writes BTYPE=00 blocks of 65,535 bytes) and the copy in src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.ts:641-698. A 1200x630 RGBA card is therefore (1200*4+1)*630 = 3,024,630 bytes of IDAT, and the PNG is 3,024,928 bytes. The CRC is computed bit by bit (roomPreviewImage.ts:819-828, roomImagePrimitives.ts:752-760) over the whole 3 MB IDAT, and Adler-32 uses a modulo per byte (838 / 763).

Measured in Node 22 (scratch benchmarks importing the real modules, Pages renderer fed a fake ASSETS binding reading dist/):
- API card (renderRoomSharePreviewPng): 149 ms per render; 8-cell Expanded Room card: 140 ms.
- Pages real-art card: 304-341 ms cold, 195-250 ms warm.
- Of that, bitwise CRC32 over 3,024,630 bytes = 123 ms and Adler-32 = 28 ms.
- CompressionStream('deflate') (zlib format, exactly what IDAT needs) over the same bytes: 16 ms, output 12-15 KB for the abstract API card and 68,748 bytes for a real-art forest card with filter type 0.

Caching makes this worse. Pages /r/x/y/image.png (src/pages/routes.ts:56-59 -> roomImageRenderer.ts:94-111) never calls the Cache API, and Worker output is not edge-cached by default, so every crawler fetch renders again despite 's-maxage=3600'. The Wamp-O-Gram preview has no cache at all (separate finding). Only the API share image is colo-cached (share/routes.ts:75 via core/publicCache.ts:30-38), so each new datacenter renders it again. WhatsApp is widely reported to skip og:images over about 300 KB. iMessage builds the preview on the sender's phone, so it downloads 3 MB over cellular for each share.

Fix (one shared encoder):
1. Make encodePng async and pipe the filtered scanlines through new CompressionStream('deflate'). The zlib stream already contains Adler-32, so delete adler32 and createZlibUncompressedBlockStream.
2. Use a 256-entry table CRC, now run over about 15-70 KB.
3. Await the encoder in share/routes.ts:202-204 and wampOGram/routes.ts:101. roomImageRenderer.ts:157 is already async.
4. Rewrite the test that pins the legacy byte stream (src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.test.ts:202-237).
5. On the Pages image route, wrap the response in caches.default keyed by the versioned URL (?v=&renderer= already make it immutable, shareMetadata.ts:363-369), and bump ROOM_IMAGE_RENDERER_VERSION (shareMetadata.ts:10).

Payoff: images about 44x smaller (real art) to about 200x smaller (abstract cards), and roughly 130 ms less CPU per render.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:722-737 — encodePng wraps scanlines in createZlibUncompressedBlockStream
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:761-784 — stored deflate blocks (header byte 0x00/0x01, raw copy), no compression
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:819-838 — bit-at-a-time CRC32 loop and per-byte modulo Adler-32 over the full 3 MB
- src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.ts:641-698 — identical uncompressed encoder in the Pages renderer
- src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.ts:752-771 — identical bitwise CRC and Adler
- src/pages/roomImagePrimitives.test.ts:202 — test 'emits the exact legacy uncompressed PNG byte stream' pins the format
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:94-111 — image route sets s-maxage but never uses the Cache API; renders on every GET
- src/pages/routes.ts:56-59 — /r/x/y/image.png goes straight to handleRoomImageRequest
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:722-737 — encodePng emits raw scanlines
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts:761-784 — 'uncompressed block stream' (stored deflate blocks)
- src/cloudflare/worker/wampOGram/routes.ts:82-111 — preview re-rendered on every GET; Cache-Control only
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/routes.ts:190-211 — room share images use the same encoder, uncached
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/publicCache.ts:20-39 — existing Cache API helper not used here

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** Every room, Expanded Room and Wamp-O-Gram link preview really is a 3,024,928-byte uncompressed PNG. About 130 of the 145-243 ms render goes to the stored-block encoder and the bit-by-bit CRC and per-byte Adler checksums. With zlib compression the images are 10-111 KB. Scope corrections:
  - Only unfurl crawlers and iMessage on the sender's phone fetch these images. Platforms cache them per URL, so renders are infrequent and the CPU cost is negligible.
  - The user-visible harm is likely missing thumbnails on WhatsApp (about 300 KB reported cap), 3 MB sender downloads on iMessage, and slower unfurls elsewhere. Impact is medium, not high.
  - The API room and Expanded Room image IS cached per datacenter (share/routes.ts:75). Only the Pages /r/x/y/image.png route and the Wamp-O-Gram preview are uncached.
  - When adding the Pages Cache API wrap, do not cache fallback-snapshot renders (roomImageRenderer.ts:102-104), or an API timeout will pin a blank grassland card to the versioned URL.
- **partially confirmed.** The images really are 3,024,928-byte uncompressed PNGs, and the bitwise CRC plus Adler-32 really do take about 145 of the roughly 150-180 ms render. That is measured and confirmed for both encoders.
  
  What's overstated is the benefit. The cost savings are negligible: renders happen only on unfurl fetches, and CPU and egress are nearly free on Cloudflare. The real gain is preview size and speed (about 20 KB abstract, about 62 KB real-art) and likely WhatsApp compatibility, which is not verified from code.
  
  Corrections to the fix:
  - A synchronous table CRC alone saves about 110 ms with no async ripple. Compression is what fixes the size.
  - When adding caches.default to the Pages /r/x/y/image.png route, do not cache the 200 fallback image that is rendered when the snapshot load fails or times out (roomImageRenderer.ts:107-109). Also note that createPagesWorker's fetch has no ctx for waitUntil (routes.ts:44).
  - Beyond the two pinned PNG tests, the fix must also update:
    - roomImageAssets.test.ts:20-28 (synchronous encodePng fixture helper)
    - workerRoutes.test.ts, which pins renderer=assets-v5, if the renderer version is bumped

### F331: Every guest death, every first clear and every tab return reloads the uncached daily-challenge endpoint (4-6 database trips each)

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The Room of the Day panel reloads its data from the server after every guest run ends (including deaths and quits, twice per run) and every time the browser tab regains focus, even when the run had nothing to do with today's room. Each reload makes 4 to 6 database trips in a row to the main database with no caching. Around midnight UTC, every one of these reloads can also run the expensive 'pick today's room' search until one finishes. Reloading only when the run was today's room, caching the shared part for 30 seconds, and picking tomorrow's room before midnight removes almost all of this traffic.

**Technical detail.**

Client triggers: dailyRoom.ts:60 subscribes onClear to POST_RUN_RATING_REQUEST, POST_RUN_GUEST_CLAIM_REQUEST and GUEST_RUN_PROGRESS_CHANGED; onClear (:98) resets lastLoaded and refreshes regardless of which room was played. GuestRunService.finish notifies twice per guest attempt, 'queued' (runService.ts:80) and after delivery (:100), and guest finishes include failed and abandoned results (goalRuns.ts:534, :551, :869-874). onAuth (:97) runs on every AUTH_STATE_CHANGED and resets busy=false. renderAuthUi dispatches AUTH_STATE_CHANGED unconditionally (auth/client.ts:1128), and refreshSession runs on both window focus and visibilitychange (:523-532), so a tab return gives two /api/daily calls. The repository sends cache:'no-store' (daily/repository.ts:5). Server: handleDaily (daily/routes.ts:6-10) forces a first-primary session and replies private, no-store. loadDailyResponse (daily/store.ts:174-200) runs sequentially: loadDailyRow, the 7-day history, the viewer's completions (signed in), dailyPickAvailable (a 4-way join), then a window-function leaderboard over room_runs, expanded_room_runs and course_runs. That is 4 trips for guests and 6 for signed-in players including the session lookup. Midnight herd: if today's row is missing, ensureDailyPick (:116-121) runs loadCandidates (:47-100), which scans all of playable_content_index with EXISTS subqueries over four run tables, for every concurrent request until one INSERT lands. The first cron tick of the day is 00:07 (wrangler.jsonc:10), and only if earlier steps in scheduled() don't throw. Fix: (1) In onClear, refresh only when event.detail's contentId/version matches response.pick, and in onAuth only when the user id changed (buildPrompts.ts:104-108 already does this). (2) Serve pick, top 10 and recentPicks from loadAnonymousPublicCache keyed by date with a 30 s TTL. Read only the viewer's completed and rank fresh, as F036 did for leaderboards. (3) Have the 23:52 tick call ensureDailyPick for tomorrow's date; INSERT OR IGNORE keeps it idempotent. Result: a guest who dies 20 times makes 0 extra daily calls instead of about 20-40.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/dailyRoom.ts:60 — onClear bound to rating, guest-claim and guest-progress events
- src/ui/setup/dailyRoom.ts:98 — onClear refreshes unconditionally
- src/ui/setup/dailyRoom.ts:97 — onAuth resets busy and refreshes on every auth-state event
- src/auth/client.ts:1128 — renderAuthUi always dispatches AUTH_STATE_CHANGED_EVENT
- src/auth/client.ts:523-532 — session refresh on both focus and visibilitychange
- src/guestRooms/runService.ts:80 — notify on queue; :100 notify again after delivery
- src/scenes/overworld/goalRuns.ts:534 — failed runs set pendingResult and go through guest finish
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/routes.ts:6-10 — first-primary session, private no-store, no edge cache
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:174-200 — sequential row, history, completions, availability, leaderboard queries
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:116-121 — missing row triggers loadCandidates per request
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:47-100 — candidate query scans playable_content_index with EXISTS over 4 run tables

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The finding should say the trigger is every qualified guest run end, not every guest death. Deaths end a run only in survival rooms (goalSafety.ts:25). Other ends are a clear, time-up, NPC loss, or leaving or restarting the room mid-run, and each causes 1-2 calls because the busy guard drops overlaps. Add the larger trigger the reviewer missed: every page load fires about 4-5 parallel /api/daily calls, from the init refresh plus repeated onAuth from wallet-gate, refreshSession, the extra renderAuthUi and AUTH_SESSION_REFRESHED, because onAuth resets busy each time. Every tab return fires 2.
  
  Corrected fix:
  (1) For guest-claim and guest-progress events, call render() only, with no fetch. Guest daily progress is computed client-side from recentPicks plus local records, and guest runs never change the server response. Refresh on POST_RUN_RATING_REQUEST only when detail.contentId and version match response.pick; GuestRunSaveResult has no content fields. In onAuth, skip when the user id is unchanged, as buildPrompts.ts:104-108 does.
  (2) Optionally, cache pick, top 10 and recentPicks with a DiscoveryPublicCache-style keyed data cache (pass ctx into handleDaily), and keep the viewer's completions and rank fresh.
  (3) If pre-picking tomorrow's room, pass `${tomorrow}T00:00:00.000Z` as `now`, or change runBindings to use row.date. Otherwise dailyWindow(row.picked_at) points the daily board at the previous day. Note that featureStatements would switch the featured room about 8 minutes early.

### F330: Every guest attempt copies the whole room (9-38 KB) into the database, and abandoned attempts keep the copy for 14 days

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Each time a guest starts a try at a room, including every retry after dying, the server copies the full published room into a new database row so it can check the run later. The room version it copies never changes and is already stored, so the copy is pure overhead. Finished runs delete the copy, but runs left open when someone closes the tab keep it for two weeks. Checking against the stored version at finish time instead would remove most guest write volume and storage growth.

**Technical detail.**

startGuestRun (guestRuns/attempts.ts:73-104) runs existingStart, then loadGuestRunSnapshot (snapshots.ts:20-40, reading immutable room_versions / expanded_room_versions by id+version), then INSERTs snapshot_json, the full JSON up to 1.5 MB (:20). For Expanded Rooms it also inserts one guest_run_snapshot_rooms row per cell (:95-97). It then calls existingStart again: 3-4 sequential trips plus the rate-limit trips. Finish (:127-133) parses that copy, and the final batch (:172-178) rewrites the row with snapshot_json = NULL and deletes the cell rows. pruneGuestRuns (:189-195) removes unclaimed rows only once expires_at passes (set to now+14 days at start, :18, :89) or the result is failed/abandoned, so 'active' rows from closed tabs keep their copy for 14 days. Every guest attempt starts a run (goalRuns.ts:966-969), so a guest who dies 20 times in a median 16 KB room writes about 320 KB of duplicate JSON, and a 4-cell Expanded Room attempt copies about 64 KB. Real room sizes: 9.2-37.6 KB across the 7 production fixtures. D1 has a hard per-database size cap, and these large TEXT rows spill into overflow pages on every write. Fix: store only content_type, id, version and snapshot_hash (already stored and bound into the trace nonce). At finish, call loadGuestRunSnapshot again and reject if computeRoomSnapshotVerificationHash differs from row.snapshot_hash. Retire guest_run_snapshot_rooms. Replace the second existingStart with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING. A taken-down version then fails verification, which is the right outcome.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:84-97 — INSERT copies snapshot_json, plus one guest_run_snapshot_rooms row per course cell
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:74,99 — existingStart read before and again after the insert
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:18 — 14-day retention for unfinished attempts
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:172-178 — finish rewrites the row with snapshot_json = NULL and deletes cell copies
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:189-195 — prune keeps active rows until expires_at
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/snapshots.ts:31-40 — the source is an immutable versioned row that can be re-read
- src/scenes/overworld/goalRuns.ts:966-969 — each guest attempt calls guestRuns.begin

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The fix stands: store only the identifiers and hash, reload the immutable version at finish the way signed-in ranked runs already do, and retire guest_run_snapshot_rooms. Correct the scope as follows:
  - Deaths do not start new runs except in survival and practice. Attempts are per restart or room entry.
  - The median room snapshot is about 12 KB (range 9-38 KB).
  - D1 bills per row, so single-room attempts save bytes and storage but not billed writes. Expanded Rooms save 2N billed row writes per attempt.
  - Steady-state storage comes only from orphaned 'active' rows. Sources are tab close or crash, plus the clearCurrentRun and restartRunForRoom paths that drop a run without abandoning it.
  - Latency stays about the same: one fewer read at start (through RETURNING), one more at finish.
  - The bigger win is closing an amplification vector. Self-minted guest identities at up to 120 starts/min per network can each park a full room (or about 600 KB Expanded Room) copy for 14 days.
  - Recomputing the hash at finish is optional; the signed-in path does not do it.

### F333: Finishing a run still waits on about 14 database trips in a row, half of which can be skipped or run together

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F029

**Summary.** F029 moved the reward bookkeeping off the critical path, but the player still waits on roughly 14 sequential database trips before 'Submitting run…' clears. Several are duplicates or don't depend on each other: a check whether the account is a retired generated account (impossible if the player has an email or wallet), three independent leaderboard reads done one at a time, and a re-read of the run that was just written. Removing those roughly halves the wait on every signed-in finish. Run start drops a trip too.

**Technical detail.**

handleRunFinish (runs/routes.ts:195-546) before reply: session (1); assertWampLeaderboardWriteAllowed (:201, 1); loadRoomRunByAttemptId (:203, 1); loadRoomRankingRecord (:217, about 2); previous best (:264, 1); top-10 (:312, 1); viewer row (:322, 1); loadEffectiveTrustTier (:369, 2: progress row then a 4-way read); UPDATE batch (:409, 1); recordRunVerificationAudit (:449, 1 when audited); reload of the finalized run (:474, 1); exact-version previous best (:489, 1); awardRunDailyClear (:517, 1+). Avoidable: (a) isGeneratedLeaderboardExcludedUserId (generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:8-35) can only return true when email and wallet_address are both NULL. auth.user already carries both (auth/model.ts:5-15), so return early when either is set. Same gate on run start (:103), course start/finish (courses/routes.ts:291,378), Expanded Room start/finish (expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts:145,279), guest claim and Room Rush. (b) previous best, top-10, viewer row and trust tier depend only on roomRecord: one Promise.all or one D1 batch (-3). (c) put the audit insert in the :409 batch (-1). (d) build finalizedRun from existing + finalBody instead of re-reading (-1). (e) when rewardScope.versions is [roomVersion], provisionalPreviousBest is the same query run before this run was finalized, so reuse it (-1). Net about 14 → 7 sequential trips on every signed-in finish, and run start 4 → 3. Add a statement-count test as sessionLookup.test.ts does.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:201 — generated-account gate awaited on every finish (and :103 on start)
- src/cloudflare/worker/generatedUsers/leaderboardIsolation.ts:16-31 — query can only match when email and wallet_address are NULL
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:264,312,322,369 — independent reads awaited one after another
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:449 — verification audit insert outside the UPDATE batch
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:474 — re-reads the run it just updated
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:489-495 — previous best queried again after the provisional one
- src/auth/model.ts:5-9 — AuthUser already includes email and walletAddress

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F335: A failing world-map alert email is retried forever, blocks newer alerts, and stops the daily pick and activity emails from running on that cron tick

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** One failing timer step skips the rest: a stuck alert email delays Room of the Day, #1 alerts and prompt results

**Summary.** The quarter-hour cron job first checks the fast world map and sends any alert email. If that email fails, for example because the address is rejected, it is retried every 15 minutes forever with no limit. It stays at the front of the queue, so newer alerts never go out. It also crashes the whole cron run, so the activity emails, build-prompt results and Room of the Day steps after it are skipped until the hourly run. The activity-email code already does this correctly, with retry limits and growing delays, and the same pattern applies here.

**Technical detail.**

scheduled() (worker.ts:343-365) awaits checkAndAlertWorldMap (:346), or runHourlyMaintenance (:355) on the hourly cron, with no try/catch. A throw skips runActivityEmails, settleExpiredBuildPrompts, ensureDailyPick and sendDailyFeatureEmail (:357-364). sendPendingAlerts (worldTiles/health.ts:114-139) leases the oldest unsent alert (`WHERE sent_at IS NULL AND (lease_until IS NULL OR lease_until <= ?) ORDER BY created_at`). On a provider error it sets lease_until = NULL and rethrows. attempts is incremented but never checked; migrations/0051 has no cap either. The cleanup at :140-141 deletes only sent alerts. A permanently undeliverable alert (Resend 4xx) is therefore retried 96 times a day indefinitely, stays oldest, so no later outage or recovery alert is ever sent, and aborts the rest of every :07/:22/:37/:52 tick. checkAndAlertWorldMap also throws on every tick if alerts are enabled but RESEND_API_KEY or the recipient is missing (:146). runHourlyMaintenance (maintenance/hourly.ts:9-16) chains six prunes, and any D1/R2 error in one skips the rest plus all jobs after it. Fix: (1) wrap each scheduled step in its own try/catch that logs a named event, or run independent steps with Promise.allSettled. (2) Give alerts the activity-email policy (activity/emails.ts:77-110): `attempts < 8` in the lease query, exponential lease_until on failure, and break instead of throw. (3) Treat 'enabled but misconfigured' as a logged no-op.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:345-364 — scheduled steps awaited in sequence with no per-step error handling
- src/cloudflare/worker/worldTiles/health.ts:117-119 — lease query has no attempts cap, ordered by created_at
- src/cloudflare/worker/worldTiles/health.ts:134-137 — failure clears lease_until (no backoff) and rethrows
- src/cloudflare/worker/worldTiles/health.ts:146 — throws every tick when enabled but unconfigured
- migrations/0051_world_map_health_alerts.sql:13-25 — attempts column with no limit
- src/cloudflare/worker/activity/emails.ts:80-82,103-108 — correct pattern: attempts < 8, exponential lease, break
- src/cloudflare/worker/maintenance/hourly.ts:9-16 — six prune steps chained without isolation
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:343-365 — sequential awaits with no per-step isolation
- src/cloudflare/worker/worldTiles/health.ts:117-119 — the alert lease has no attempts cap
- src/cloudflare/worker/worldTiles/health.ts:133-137 — a send failure rethrows
- src/cloudflare/worker/maintenance/hourly.ts:9-16 — six chained prune steps

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect is real but narrower than claimed. scheduled() has no per-step isolation, and the alert outbox has no backoff and no head-of-line escape. Corrected scope:
  (a) A stuck alert, or a failing hourly prune, only lowers how often the later steps run, from every 15 minutes to hourly. The :17 hourly tick does not call checkAndAlertWorldMap. ensureDailyPick and settleExpiredBuildPrompts also run lazily on user reads, and dethrone emails send immediately per run. Expect delays under an hour, not a stop.
  (b) Head-of-line blocking only matters for failures specific to one message. The realistic case: the recipient or sender is fixed in env after rows were queued with the old address baked into message_json. Those stale rows then 422 forever and block every newer outage or recovery email.
  (c) Retrying until sent and throwing when misconfigured are documented, tested 'fail visibly' behavior, so drop fix (3) and don't silently give up after 8 attempts.
  Fix:
  1. Wrap each scheduled step, and each hourly prune, in try/catch with a named console.error event. Let all steps run, then rethrow an aggregate error at the end so the cron still fails visibly.
  2. In sendPendingAlerts, apply exponential lease_until on failure. On a non-429 4xx, mark the row failed (dead-letter with last_error) so newer alerts can go. Optionally rebuild to/from from the current env at send time.

### F349: details withheld

Security, safety or anti-cheat item; details withheld from this public repo until it is fixed (see the private review page, or ask Claude to read it from the review artifact).

### F346: Streaming rooms onto the map reads each room's draft as well as its published copy, and no response can be cached

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** As players move, the game downloads the rooms coming into view in batches of up to 48. For published rooms, the server also reads each builder's private draft copy, roughly doubling the data pulled from the database, and then throws it away. The request is also a POST, so neither Cloudflare nor the browser can reuse it, even though a given room version never changes. Reading only the needed copy is a quick fix. Serving published versions over a cacheable address would let every player share one database read per room.

**Technical detail.**

loadRoomSnapshotsByReferences (rooms/store.ts:393-453) loads current_preview references with `SELECT id, x, y, draft_json, published_json FROM rooms WHERE id IN (...)` (:411-413) and then uses only one column per reference (:434-436). The client sends current_preview with state, version and updatedAt from the compact summary (previewCache.ts:150-190), in batches of 48 awaited one after another (:192-197). For a batch of published rooms at the 16 KB fixture median, about 770 KB of draft_json crosses from D1 to the Worker unused. The route is POST /api/rooms/snapshots/query (rooms/routes.ts:106-128, private no-store, X-WAMP-Cache bypass; client worldRepository.ts:305-316), so every new session re-downloads every room it sees from D1. Yet the reference (roomId, version, updatedAt) pins the content: the server already drops snapshots whose updatedAt differs (store.ts:441). Fix 1 (small): split current refs by state. Published refs select `id, x, y, published_json`; claimed refs select `id, x, y, draft_json, published_json IS NOT NULL AS has_published`. Fix 2 (medium): add GET /api/rooms/:id/snapshot?v=&u=&detail= for published refs, served through loadAnonymousPublicCache with a long max-age so browsers and the colo cache share it. Keep the POST for drafts. Because of takedowns (see F189), use a day-scale edge TTL or purge on unpublish rather than 'immutable'.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:411-413 — selects both draft_json and published_json for every current reference
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:434-436 — only one of the two columns is used
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:441 — updatedAt mismatch rejected, so refs are content-pinned
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:106-128 — POST route, private no-store, cache bypass
- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:192-197 — batches of 48 awaited sequentially
- src/persistence/worldRepository.ts:305-316 — client POST for snapshots

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** This only affects play mode, room transitions and the tile fallback. Browse mode is tile-served at 100% rollout, and the probe gate forbids published references there. Fix 1 is still a cheap win: select only published_json for published references, and draft_json plus a has_published flag for claimed ones. The benefit is less D1-to-Worker transfer and Worker memory, about one extra room copy per published row. D1 rows-read billing and SQLite page reads stay the same, because draft_json comes before published_json in the row. Fix 2 should not use one GET per room on the Worker plus the colo cache. That multiplies Worker invocations, and the edge cache is per colo. If response caching is pursued, it should mainly target browser caching for returning players. Use a batched, chunk-keyed GET, or reuse the existing immutable GET /api/rooms/:id/versions/:n route. Account for F189 takedowns either way.

### F344: Signed-in session check makes 6 database trips in a row and fires twice every time the tab regains focus

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Whenever a signed-in player comes back to the WAMP tab, the game asks the server 'who am I?' twice, once for the focus event and once for the tab-visible event. Each answer takes six database trips one after another, including duplicate lookups of the same ban and account facts. Asking once, skipping repeats within 30 seconds, and running the server lookups in parallel would make returning to the game feel quicker and cut this traffic by about 80 percent.

**Technical detail.**

Client: bindSessionRefreshListeners (auth/client.ts:517-533) calls refreshSession on both window focus and visibilitychange→visible, with no single-flight or throttle. Switching tabs fires both. refreshSession (:368-371) then renderAuthUi (:1128) dispatches AUTH_STATE_CHANGED unconditionally to about 28 listeners, which also drives the /api/daily reloads in the daily-challenge finding. Server, /api/auth/session for a session (auth/routes.ts:77-97): loadOptionalRequestAuth (1); resolveChatModerationViewer → isChatAdminUser then isChatBannedUser (chat/moderation.ts:14-43, 2 sequential); getRoomClaimQuota (rooms/store.ts:1448-1461) → resolveRoomCapabilities → loadOrBackfillUserProgress (1) → loadEffectiveTrustState 4-way Promise.all (progression/trustCaps.ts:63-99, 1 trip, 4 statements) → countRoomClaimsSince (1). That is 6 sequential trips and 9 statements. Duplicates: the trust state re-reads chat_bans (already answered by isChatBannedUser) and users.created_at (already in the session row). Fix: client single-flight plus a 30 s minimum interval, and dispatch AUTH_STATE_CHANGED only when the user id or flags actually changed. Server: run chat moderation and claim quota concurrently, or put all statements in one env.DB.batch, and pass session.user.createdAt and the ban result into the trust computation. About 12 trips per tab return → about 2.

**Evidence.**

- src/auth/client.ts:523-532 — refreshSession on focus and on visibilitychange, no dedupe
- src/auth/client.ts:1128 — AUTH_STATE_CHANGED dispatched on every render
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/routes.ts:85-94 — chat moderation then claim quota, awaited in sequence
- src/cloudflare/worker/chat/moderation.ts:22-26 — admin check then ban check, sequential
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:1454-1455 — capability lookup then claim count, sequential
- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/trustCaps.ts:63-97 — re-reads chat_bans and users.created_at

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real but narrower than claimed. The double focus+visibilitychange refresh (client.ts:517-533) has no dedupe, and /api/auth/session runs 6 sequential D1 waves (9 statements) with duplicate chat_bans and users.created_at reads. However, the tab-return refresh is fire-and-forget, so it does not slow returning to the game. The latency win is on the awaited refreshAuthSession calls after claim and publish, and on the initial load (no Smart Placement).
  
  Recommended fix:
  - Client: single-flight or a ~1-2 s debounce to merge the two events. Do NOT use a 30 s throttle: focus refresh is the only cross-tab sign-in/out sync, so a throttle would leave a tab signed out after a magic-link sign-in in another tab.
  - Client: dispatch AUTH_STATE_CHANGED only when the full auth snapshot changes (status, loading, chatModeration and claim quota fields included), not just the user id and flags. That also halves the dailyRoom and editor background-image refetches.
  - Server: after the session lookup, run moderation and quota together (Promise.all or one DB.batch), select chat_bans.created_at once, and pass session.user.createdAt in.
  
  Expected result: about 18 → 7 statements per tab return (~60%, not 80%), and 6 → 2 sequential waves.

### F345: Spam limits for guest saves are stored in the main database, adding about 12 writes and 4 extra trips to every guest attempt

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** To stop spam, the server logs every guest run start and finish in a database table and counts recent entries. Each attempt adds four log rows (plus their index entries), costs four extra trips to the database before any real work, and needs another cleanup pass later. Cloudflare has a built-in, free rate limiter that fits these one-minute limits exactly. Moving the high-volume guest, Lost Songs and Room Rush limits to it would remove all of this, while the email and sign-in limits stay in the database where exact counts matter.

**Technical detail.**

takeRateLimitSlot (core/rateLimit.ts:59-80) runs one INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit per rule, and takeRateLimitSlots (:88-101) awaits the rules one by one. rate_limit_events (migrations/0049:2-13) has an AUTOINCREMENT key plus two secondary indexes, so each slot writes about 3 rows (row + 2 index entries) plus sqlite_sequence. limitGuestRunRequest (guestRuns/identity.ts:18-26) applies two rules (identity + /64 network) on start, finish and by-client lookup (guestRuns/routes.ts:20-31). Per guest attempt that is 4 slots, about 12+ rows written, and 4 sequential D1 trips. pruneRateLimitEvents (:117-122) later deletes them with an unbounded DELETE each hour, about the same again, unlike pruneExpiredRecords' 5,000-row cap. The same pattern covers lost songs (lostSongs/routes.ts:30-37), weekly Room Rush starts (runs/roomRushLeaderboards.ts:80-83) and client error reports (ops/errors.ts:62). All of these use 60-second windows, which matches the Workers Rate Limiting binding (`ratelimits` in wrangler.jsonc, period 60). That binding is free, needs no D1, and adds no measurable latency; it counts per location, which is fine for flood control. Keep D1 slots for the email/code and mention buckets, where exact multi-hour or day windows matter. Smaller interim fix: send both rules in one env.DB.batch (one trip) and add a LIMIT to the prune.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/core/rateLimit.ts:66-79 — INSERT...SELECT with COUNT per rule
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/rateLimit.ts:94-100 — rules awaited one at a time
- migrations/0049_rate_limit_events.sql:2-13 — AUTOINCREMENT plus two indexes per event row
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/identity.ts:21-25 — two 60 s rules per guest start/finish/claim
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/routes.ts:21,25,30 — limit applied to lookup, start and finish
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/rateLimit.ts:117-122 — hourly unbounded DELETE
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:31-36 — 60 s windows
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/roomRushLeaderboards.ts:80-83 — 60 s windows

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real but smaller than stated.
  - Guest start/finish/lookup, Lost Songs and weekly Room Rush starts each make 2 sequential D1 write trips per request. Each slot writes about 3 rows (table plus 2 indexes, plus sqlite_sequence), and the hourly prune deletes about the same again 2 days later.
  - The client error limit uses a 1-hour window (ops/errors.ts:30), so it does not fit the 10/60 s Rate Limiting binding. Drop it from the move.
  - The latency is hidden from players because guest start and finish are async/queued on the client. The dollar cost is negligible within D1's included rows, so the benefit is mainly less load on the single D1 primary and better flood resilience.
  - Recommended order: (a) batch the two INSERTs in one env.DB.batch and release on a partial limit, which is small, and cap the prune; (b) optionally move the 60 s guest, Lost Songs and Rush buckets to about 5 ratelimits namespaces (top level and env.safety), with a D1 fallback when the binding is absent and rewritten tests (progress.test.ts:340-356, lostSongs/routes.test.ts).
  - Keep the email/code, mention, guest-draft-daily and client-error buckets in D1.

### F339: Guest activity ping reads then writes the database every 15 seconds per tab, updates an index nothing uses, and is never cleaned up

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Backend speed, cost and reliability)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Every open guest tab reports activity every 15 seconds. Each report first reads the visit row and then writes it back, which is two database trips where one would do. The table keeps five extra indexes, one of which no query ever uses, and old visits are never deleted. Merging the read into the write, dropping the unused index and adding a retention window would roughly halve the cost of the most frequent request in the game.

**Technical detail.**

handleGuestActivityHeartbeat (guestActivity/routes.ts:36-46) SELECTs last_seen_at and mode, computes the credited delta in JS, then upserts (:55-90). The delta (min(now - last_seen_at, 60 s), credited to the previous mode) can be computed inside ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE from guest_visits.last_seen_at and guest_visits.mode, using MIN(60, (julianday(excluded.last_seen_at) - julianday(guest_visits.last_seen_at)) * 86400) in a CASE on guest_visits.mode, so one statement does the job. Indexes: guest_user_id, last_seen_at, mode (migrations/0027:20-27), last_play_at and last_edit_at (0028:4-8). Every heartbeat moves last_seen_at, and while playing last_play_at, so about 3 rows are written per ping. The only reader of guest_visits is admin/launchStats.ts (:144-145, :236-280, :676-702), which filters on last_seen_at, last_play_at and last_edit_at, never mode, so idx_guest_visits_mode is write-only overhead. Cadence: HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 15 s (analytics/guestActivity.ts:17,58-60), guests only (:80). Per playing guest tab per hour that is 240 pings = 480 D1 statements and about 720 rows written. No code deletes from guest_visits, so the table (which also stores user_agent and referrer) grows by one row per session forever. Fix: single upsert, a migration dropping idx_guest_visits_mode, and a bounded 90-day delete in runHourlyMaintenance. Optionally raise the cadence to 30 s; the 60 s delta cap keeps the attribution the same.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/guestActivity/routes.ts:36-46 — SELECT before every heartbeat upsert
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestActivity/routes.ts:55-90 — upsert; deltas could use guest_visits.* in DO UPDATE
- migrations/0027_guest_visits.sql:26 — idx_guest_visits_mode
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/launchStats.ts:241-280 — only readers, filtering by last_seen_at/last_play_at/last_edit_at
- src/analytics/guestActivity.ts:17 — 15 s heartbeat interval
- src/analytics/guestActivity.ts:80 — guests only

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Merge the SELECT into the upsert: one statement instead of two, and the double-credit race goes away. Concurrent close-time pings (visibilitychange plus pagehide) currently both credit the same delta. Do not claim it halves cost. The SELECT is one near-free primary-key row read. Writes dominate D1 billing, and each ping rewrites the row plus all five secondary indexes (about 6 rows written, not 3). Dropping the unused `idx_guest_visits_mode` saves about 1 in 6 writes. Bigger write savings: stop setting `guest_user_id` and `guest_display_name` on every update, or move to a 30 s cadence. Pings are only sent from visible tabs. Retention was already raised in F038 and deferred as optional analytics. Pruning would change the admin all-time guest totals and work against open F127, so roll the counts up first or leave it to a product decision.

### F334: Use the pre-drawn world-map tiles as share pictures instead of drawing rooms again on the server

- **Area:** Backend speed, cost and reliability (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F003

**Summary.** Every published room already has a full-size, real-art picture stored for the world map, drawn by the same code as the map itself. Share links could point straight at that stored picture, so there is no drawing per share, the preview always matches the map, and the file is already compressed and served from Cloudflare's edge. The current drawing would remain only as a fallback for the minute after a room is published.

**Technical detail.**

Building blocks already in the repo:
