- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/tilesprite/TileSpriteWebGLRenderer.js:41 — WebGL draws src.fillPattern, not sprite.texture
- node_modules/phaser/src/renderer/webgl/WebGLRenderer.js:3067-3086 — fill pattern filter is NEAREST unless antialias
- src/main.ts:95 — pixelArt: true
- src/cloudflare/worker/backgroundImages/validateUpload.ts:22-25 — stills allowed up to 1280x768

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Per tile-fit TileSprite, the pattern copy costs 8.4-16.8 MB (canvas plus GPU), depending on aspect ratio: 16:9 or 3:2 photos become 2048x1024, while 4:3 and portrait photos become 1024x1024. On phones, play mode keeps only 1 full room plus at most 1 predicted room ('reduced' profile, fullRoomBudget=1), so a phone pays this 1-2 times. Desktop pays it up to 9 times, and the editor adds one more. A pre-scaled `${key}@tile` texture cuts the per-sprite copy to about 128 KB. It does not remove the ~12 MB shared original, which room snapshots and chunk previews still read. The fix also has to remove the derived texture alongside the source and either skip animated sources or re-derive them per frame. The visual bug holds as stated: setFilter(LINEAR) hits the TileSprite's private texture, and the fillPattern is NEAREST with no mipmaps at about 13-16x minification.
- **partially confirmed.** The per-sprite fill-pattern mechanism is right and the setFilter(LINEAR) call has no effect on it. Scale and impact need restating:
  - **Phones:** the reduced full-room budget is 1 (previewStreaming.ts:49, and every touch device is 'reduced' per deviceLayout.ts:55-56). A phone holds about 8-17 MB extra only while it is in a tiled-photo room (plus about 1.5 s of transition retention). It does not hold that per room in view.
  - **Desktop:** with a budget of 9, it can reach roughly 9x.
  - **Size:** 17 MB per sprite applies only to 16:9 images at about 1280x720-768 (2048x1024 POT). Typical 4:3 or portrait phone photos (1024x768 or 576x768) produce a 1024x1024 pattern, about 8.4 MB.
  - **Missed cost:** the pattern is rebuilt and uploaded again on every entry into such a room, which probably causes a hitch on phones.
  - **Most visible effect:** tiled photos are point-sampled at 10-16x minification with no mipmaps, so they look grainy or aliased on every device.
  - **Fix:** only still images need the derived `${key}@tile` texture. It must be removed together with the source texture.
- **partially confirmed.** Per tile-fit TileSprite, the waste is a POT copy of the full source: 8.4 MB (1024x768 phone photos -> 1024x1024) to 16.7 MB (1280x720/768 -> 2048x1024), as canvas plus GPU texture. On phones the reduced profile loads 1 full room in play (previewStreaming.ts:49), plus predicted/transition rooms, so about 1-3 sprites. Desktop loads up to 9.
  
  The fix must:
  - **Keep the full source texture.** roomSnapshotTexture.ts:216 and chunkPreviewRenderer.ts:531 draw tile-fit previews from it, so the ~12 MB shared copy is not saved.
  - **Size the pre-smoothed derived tile for camera zoom**, not at 128 px. The fill pattern is always NEAREST under pixelArt, and fixed-room zoom reaches about 3x on desktop (cameraController.ts:92).
  - **Leave animated backgrounds (at most 240 px) on the current path**, or regenerate the derived texture each frame.
  
  Expected saving is about 7-15 MB per sprite, and the LINEAR intent at runtime.ts:115 gets fixed.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** [PR #297](https://github.com/songadaymann/wamp/pull/297). Tiled still photos draw from one shared downscaled copy per background, about 2 MB per room instead of about 17 MB. Reviewed adversarially before merging; `npm run check` and the muted phone smokes passed. [Receipt](wamp-round2-phone-play-2026-10-22.md).

### F353: Each starfield or parallax background layer costs 3-7 MB of hidden memory per room; a Forest room is about 50 MB

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The repeating background layers (the default starfield, and built-in sets like Forest) use a Phaser object that secretly makes room-sized and power-of-two copies of its image for every room. A plain starfield room carries about 6 MB of these copies, a Forest room about 50 MB, and a Dark Forest room about 45 MB, even though all rooms share the same source art. On a phone that holds 1-3 rooms at once this is a big, avoidable share of memory. A small custom layer class that shares one pattern per image and skips the unused canvas would remove almost all of it.

**Technical detail.**

Phaser 3.90 TileSprite, per instance:
- (a) `this.canvas` sized to the sprite (640x352 for room backgrounds; TileSprite.js:181), with a CanvasTexture of its own (:240). The CanvasTexture constructor reads it back with getImageData and keeps the ImageData (CanvasTexture.js:86,118) and uploads a GPU texture (TextureSource.js:231). In WebGL this canvas is never drawn (updateCanvas returns early, TileSprite.js:500-511; the renderer binds fillPattern, TileSpriteWebGLRenderer.js:41). That is 3 x 0.9 MB = 2.7 MB of dead weight per room layer.
- (b) A POT fillCanvas (:277) plus a fillPattern GPU texture (:470) of the source art: identical for every sprite using the same key, but never shared.

Per room:
- 'none' rooms (the default) get a color rect plus 2 starfield TileSprites (fullRoomPresenter.ts:486-512). 2 x (2.7 + 2x0.26) ≈ 6.4 MB.
- Built-in groups create one TileSprite per layer (fullRoomPresenter.ts:608 → runtime.ts:140-142). Forest is 8 layers of 576x324 (POT 1024x512 = 2.1 MB each, x2): about 8 x 6.9 ≈ 55 MB (≈48 MB if the browser defers the unused canvas backing).
- Other groups, by script over config/backgrounds.ts: dark_forest 46 MB, meadow 33 MB, grassland/mountains 26 MB, spooky_mountain 25 MB, jungle_vines 22 MB, aurora/cave 20 MB, spooky_moon 18 MB.
Phones keep REDUCED_PLAY_FULL_ROOM_BUDGET = 1 plus seam-prepared and retained neighbors (previewStreaming.ts:49), so 1-3 rooms. The backdrop's two screen-size starfield sprites add about 9 MB once (backdropController.ts:60-70).

Also, in 'none' rooms the depth-8 colorRect (fullRoomPresenter.ts:487-495) is fully covered by starfield layer 0, which is opaque because drawStarfieldToContext fills #050505 first (starfieldCanvas.ts:38-39). That is one wasted full-room fill per room.

Fix (medium): add a `RoomTileSprite extends Phaser.GameObjects.TileSprite` used by createStarfieldTileSprite and createBuiltInBackgroundObject. In WebGL it should:
1. construct with a 1x1 internal canvas and override updateCanvas to only update frame size and origin;
2. override updateTileTexture to take a refcounted shared fillPattern per source key (built once) instead of its own fillCanvas.
In Canvas renderer mode (?renderer=canvas) it keeps Phaser's behaviour. Expected: Forest room ≈ 55 → under 1 MB of per-room overhead, 'none' room ≈ 6.4 MB → about 0. Drop the redundant colorRect for 'none'. Longer term, Phaser 4's TileSprite drops these canvases entirely.

**Evidence.**

- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/tilesprite/TileSprite.js:181,240 — per-sprite room-size canvas registered as its own CanvasTexture
- node_modules/phaser/src/textures/CanvasTexture.js:86,118 — constructor getImageData copy retained as this.imageData
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/tilesprite/TileSprite.js:277,470 — per-sprite POT fill canvas + fillPattern GPU texture
- node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/tilesprite/TileSpriteWebGLRenderer.js:25,41 — WebGL binds only fillPattern
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:486-512 — 'none' rooms create a color rect + 2 starfield TileSprites
- src/scenes/overworld/fullRoomPresenter.ts:608 / src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:140-142 — one TileSprite per built-in layer
- src/visuals/starfieldCanvas.ts:38-39 — starfield tile is opaque, hiding the color rect
- src/scenes/overworld/previewStreaming.ts:49 — REDUCED_PLAY_FULL_ROOM_BUDGET = 1

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** 1. The memory figures need one correction. At construction, getImageData forces the room-size canvas backing into memory. setFrame then sets canvas.width = 0 (TileSprite.js:348), which frees it. updateCanvas (:500-501) sets the size back, but nothing ever draws to the canvas in WebGL, so browsers that allocate lazily never rebuild the backing. The certain dead weight per layer is therefore the ImageData plus the GPU texture, about 1.8 MB, not 2.7 MB. Per-room totals should be quoted as ranges: 'none' room about 4.7-6.5 MB, Forest about 48-55 MB, Dark Forest about 42-48 MB.
  
  2. The scope is wider than phones. Desktop play keeps up to 9 full rooms (previewStreaming.ts:48), so a neighborhood of Forest rooms there can carry several hundred MB.
  
  3. Two details for the fix:
     - WebGLTextureWrapper keeps `pixels` so it can re-upload after a WebGL context loss (wrappers/WebGLTextureWrapper.js:139, :267). Each shared fillPattern must therefore keep one shared POT canvas per key; that canvas cannot be shrunk.
     - preDestroy (TileSprite.js:552-556) deletes the fillPattern, so it must be overridden to decrement a refcount instead.
  
  4. The app's `sprite.texture.setFilter(...)` calls (starfield.ts:81, runtime.ts:115/146/154) only change the dead per-sprite texture. The fillPattern gets NEAREST from pixelArt:true (main.ts:95) through canvasToTexture. A rewrite must not rely on those setFilter calls.
  
  5. A cheaper first step would recover part of the waste: shrink the per-sprite room canvas to 1x1 in WebGL. Sharing the fillPattern is where most of the saving comes from.
- **partially confirmed.** Per room layer, Phaser 3.90 TileSprite keeps two room-sized copies, not three:
  - a 640x352 ImageData (about 0.9 MB of JS heap)
  - a never-drawn 640x352 GL texture (about 0.9 MB)
  
  The room-size canvas backing is probably not kept, because setFrame resets its width and WebGL never draws to it.
  
  On top of that, each sprite keeps its own unshared POT fillCanvas plus a matching fillPattern GL texture.
  
  Realistic avoidable cost per room:
  - default starfield ('none') room: about 4.6 MB
  - Forest: about 48 MB
  - Dark Forest: about 42 MB
  - other groups: 14-30 MB
  
  Phones ('reduced' profile) hold 1-3 full rooms, so the saving is about 5-15 MB in typical starfield areas and about 50-150 MB in Forest areas. Desktop holds 9 full rooms, which is about 430 MB in a Forest area.
  
  The memory is freed when a room unloads, so this is a working-set cost, not a leak. The same work, including about 23 MB of texture uploads for a Forest room, happens in a single prepare-room-background job, so it also causes a hitch at room transitions.
  
  Custom backgrounds with fit 'tile' use the same path. Uploads have no dimension cap, so a large photo pays the power-of-two copy twice.
  
  How common built-in groups are on live rooms is unverified. The redundant 'none' colorRect is real but negligible. Fix as proposed:
  - a TileSprite subclass that constructs at 1x1, then calls setSize
  - a no-op updateCanvas under WebGL
  - a refcounted shared fillPattern per texture key
  - handling for the __DEFAULT→setTexture swap; keep stock behaviour in the Canvas renderer.
- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism and the per-room totals are right: Forest about 48-55 MB, Dark Forest about 42-48 MB, a starfield ('none') room about 4.6-6.4 MB. Four things need correcting.
  
  1. The dead copy the size of the room is about 1.8 MB per layer: the retained ImageData plus a GPU texture. The canvas backing is most likely never allocated, because the canvas is never drawn in WebGL.
  2. Sharing patterns only removes duplicates between rooms with the same background. The first room of each built-in group still needs one shared power-of-two pattern per layer, and its canvas must be kept or rebuilt because the app relies on Phaser's in-place context restore (webglRecovery.ts). So Forest's first room drops to about 17-34 MB, not under 1 MB. A phone in a single Forest room saves about 20-38 MB.
  3. 'none' rooms, and later rooms in the same group, do drop to almost zero, as claimed.
  4. Desktop holds 9 full rooms (FULL_ROOM_BUDGET), so the absolute cost and saving are larger there than on phones.
  
  Cheaper first step (small effort): build the room and starfield TileSprites at 1x1 and call setSize afterwards, or override updateCanvas. This removes the dead copy and most of the 'none'-room cost. The refcounted shared fillPattern subclass is a medium-effort follow-up. Dropping the colorRect in 'none' rooms is a trivial extra with negligible benefit.

### F356: Phones redraw the game at full speed behind full-screen menus, while paused and when idle, and Battery Saver doesn't slow it

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Mobile play on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F011

**Summary.** On phones every menu (Explore, Leaderboards, Settings, Activity) covers the whole screen, yet the game keeps redrawing the hidden map 60 to 90 times a second. It also keeps redrawing while a run is paused and while the map just sits there. Battery Saver barely changes anything on phones, because phones are already on the reduced setting in Auto. Still, the 'Gameplay running slowly?' popup recommends it. Slowing or stopping the redraw in these cases would cut heat and battery drain a lot.

**Technical detail.**

Frame-rate modes are only 'auto', '60' and 'uncapped' (frameRateMode.ts:1). In auto, FrameCadenceGate caps only near 120/240 Hz (frameCadence.ts:40,46). 60 and 90 Hz phones render every vsync, and nothing in the gate knows about covered, paused or idle states (:76-79).

Covered: phone modal panels are 100vw wide and at least the full visible height (phone-modals-touch.css:30-38). Paused: gameplayPause uses scene.pause() (gameplayPause.ts:25), but Phaser still renders PAUSED scenes (node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js:593 renders status < SLEEPING; PAUSED=6, SLEEPING=7).

Battery Saver on phones: deviceLayout.ts:55-57 makes every touch device 'reduced' in Auto. performancePolicy.ts:44-52 gives Battery Saver the same visual and runtime profiles. The only differences are half the weather particles (weather/controller.ts:252) and no score popups (fx/controller.ts:261). worldStreaming.ts:5199-5200 even keeps recently left rooms longer under Battery Saver than under Auto on phones. Meanwhile performanceSuggestionModal.ts:72 switches players to Battery Saver, and index.html:3214 promises it 'reduces background and visual work'.

Fix, reusing FrameCadenceGate:
- Add a throttle input: about 5 fps while hasBlockingModalOpen() on a phone, or while gameplay is paused. 5 fps stays inside renderLoopRecovery's 750 ms stall threshold, which is gated to browse mode and !isPaused.
- Cap at 30 fps under Battery Saver. Physics stays a fixed 60 Hz step (F138), so gameplay is unchanged.
- Cap browse mode at 30 fps after about 20 s without input. main.ts:183-186 already receives every pointer, touch and key event for renderLoopRecoveryMonitor.

Expected savings: about 92% fewer frames behind menus and 50% fewer in Battery Saver or idle browsing.

**Evidence.**

- src/performance/frameRateMode.ts:1 — only auto/60/uncapped
- src/main/frameCadence.ts:40 — auto caps only near 120/240 Hz
- src/main/frameCadence.ts:46 — otherwise every vsync renders
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-modals-touch.css:32-35 — phone modals are full-screen
- src/ui/gameplayPause.ts:25 — pause uses scene.pause()
- node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js:593 — paused scenes still render
- src/ui/deviceLayout.ts:55-57 — all touch devices are already 'reduced' in Auto
- src/performance/performancePolicy.ts:44-52 — Battery Saver resolves to the same profiles
- src/weather/controller.ts:252 — weather density is the main Battery Saver difference
- src/fx/controller.ts:261 — score popups skipped
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:5199-5200 — Battery Saver retains rooms longer than Auto-reduced
- src/ui/setup/performanceSuggestionModal.ts:72 — the slowness popup switches to Battery Saver

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real gap: nothing slows the frame rate behind full-screen phone modals, while paused, or when idle, and Battery Saver on phones only halves weather and drops score popups. Fix that scope:
  (a) Throttle to about 5-10 fps only when the scene is paused, or in browse mode with a modal or menu open. Never throttle while liveReason (multiplayer or Weekly Rush) keeps the run going: Phaser's smoothStep clamps deltas at 200 ms, which would slow the simulation, and the advisor stays eligible there. Drive this from a cached modal-open signal, not a per-frame querySelectorAll.
  (b) Cap Battery Saver at 30 fps. This was suggested before in F002 and F081 but not built. Physics stays per-step (F138), and the advisor is off outside Auto.
  (c) The idle 30 fps browse cap is optional and must also stay off during camera motion.
  Drop the worldStreaming retain-grace argument; the grace is only 300 ms.

### F354: iPads and Android tablets switch to the phone layout whenever the on-screen keyboard opens in landscape

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Mobile play on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F076

**Summary.** On a tablet held sideways, the game measures the space left above the keyboard and decides the device is a phone. Typing in chat or the sign-in box makes the layout jump to the phone design mid-typing. In the editor it is worse: the phone layout moves the 'Room Name' box into a hidden menu while you are typing in it, so the keyboard closes and the layout flips back. The phone fix in F076 corrected portrait/landscape detection but left this half unchanged.

**Technical detail.**

deviceLayout.ts:75-77 sizes the screen from window.visualViewport, which shrinks when the keyboard opens. classifyDeviceClass (:42-49) calls anything whose shortest edge is 540px or less a 'phone'. Since F076, orientation uses the layout viewport (:83-85), but deviceClass still uses the visual viewport (:86).

I ran the real module under tsx with stubbed viewports:
- 1180x770 layout with a 1180x400 visual viewport (iPad 11" landscape, keyboard open) -> 'phone landscape'
- 1080x760 with a 1080x380 visual viewport -> 'phone'
- 1180x770 with no keyboard -> 'tablet'
- 820x1180 portrait with a keyboard -> 'tablet'
The existing test (deviceLayout.test.ts:40) only covers a phone in portrait.

Consequences:
1. Every body[data-device-class='phone'] rule applies while the keyboard is up. That includes the 44px :is(button) minimums (phone-touch-targets.css:35-38), phone modals at full width and full visible height (phone-modals-touch.css:30-38), and fixed-position chat.
2. editorDockShell.ts:428-436 watches data-device-class. Its syncProxyActions calls editorPhoneDock.sync, which activates when deviceClass==='phone' (editorPhoneDock.ts:60-61). activate() then moves #room-title-section, which contains #room-title-input (index.html:1512-1514), into the hidden #editor-phone-menu (editorPhoneDock.ts:98, index.html:1353). Moving a focused input out of the document removes focus, so the keyboard closes. The viewport then grows, the class returns to 'tablet', and restore() moves the section back.
3. MobileUiController.render shows #mobile-editor-nav for isPhone && editor (controller.ts:477-481).

The same thing happens when a tablet user pinch-zooms the HTML UI (scale > 1 shrinks the visual viewport), as the F076 fact-check noted.

Fix: classify deviceClass from the layout viewport (innerWidth/innerHeight) or screen.width/height, as F076's fix item (2) originally proposed. Alternatively, freeze deviceClass while an editable element has focus; updateKeyboardInset at :102-114 already detects that. Add a tsx/vitest case for tablet landscape with the keyboard open. One function changes, about 5 lines.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/deviceLayout.ts:75-77 — width/height come from visualViewport
- src/ui/deviceLayout.ts:83-86 — orientation uses the layout viewport, deviceClass still uses the visual one
- src/ui/deviceLayout.ts:42-49 — shortest edge <= 540 means 'phone'
- src/ui/setup/editorDockShell.ts:428-436 — data-device-class changes re-sync the dock
- src/ui/setup/editorPhoneDock.ts:60-61 — phone dock activates when deviceClass is phone
- src/ui/setup/editorPhoneDock.ts:98 — moves #room-title-section into the phone menu
- index.html:1512-1514 — the room name input lives in #room-title-section
- index.html:1353 — #editor-phone-menu starts hidden
- src/ui/deviceLayout.test.ts:40 — only a portrait phone keyboard case is tested

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim and editor focus loop are confirmed. Three corrections:
  
  1. Consequence 3 is wrong. #mobile-editor-nav stays hidden while the phone dock is active (controller.ts:478-481).
  2. The room-title move is at editorPhoneDock.ts:99.
  3. Don't switch deviceClass to plain innerWidth/innerHeight. That breaks the existing "mobile browser fits overflowing tablet content" test (deviceLayout.test.ts:49-53): 738x1598 at scale 0.53 must stay 'phone'.
     - Don't use screen.* either, because it would call iPad Slide Over and Split View windows 'tablet'.
     - Classify from the layout viewport times the existing fitScale: round(innerWidth*min(1,scale)) by round(innerHeight*min(1,scale)).
     - Optionally, keep the previous deviceClass while a text field has focus.
     - Leave --app-viewport-* on visualViewport.
     - Add vitest cases for a 1180x760 tablet with a 1180x360 visual viewport, which should give 'tablet', and for pinch scale 1.5. Optionally add a tablet keyboard scenario to mobile_smoke.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** [PR #295](https://github.com/songadaymann/wamp/pull/295). Phone vs tablet is judged from the screen's real width, so opening the keyboard or zooming never flips a tablet to the phone layout; the layout is also held while a text field has focus. Reviewed adversarially before merging; `npm run check` and the muted phone smokes passed. [Receipt](wamp-round2-phone-play-2026-10-22.md).

### F362: Rotating the phone mid-run drops your held stick and jump while the run keeps going

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Mobile play on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** If a phone rotates during a run, for example when a player shifts in bed or on a couch, the touch controls jump from the bottom panel to the corners. The game deliberately lets go of the stick and the jump button, so the hero stops or falls short, but the timer and enemies keep moving. The game already pauses runs for menus and hidden tabs, so it should also pause briefly while the screen rotates.

**Technical detail.**

MobileUiController builds the layout key from the touch layout and orientation (controller.ts:426, :495). PortraitPlayControlsController.render releases every move and jump press when the key changes (portraitPlayControls.ts:77-83). OverworldPlayScene.handleResize then re-fits the zoom and re-applies the camera (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1714-1716).

gameplayPause only pauses for an open menu, a blocking modal, a pending dialog or a hidden page (gameplayPause.ts:63). Rotation is not on that list, so physics, enemies and the run clock keep going through the rotation animation and the release.

Fix: when the touch layout key changes during play-world, give installGameplayPause a transient 'rotating' blocked reason for about 800 ms. readUi can take another flag, and the existing 'Paused' status shows. The existing 'Ranking time includes breaks' message already covers ranked runs. About 15 lines.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/mobile/controller.ts:426 — touch layout chosen per orientation
- src/ui/mobile/controller.ts:495 — layout key includes orientation
- src/ui/mobile/portraitPlayControls.ts:77-83 — all presses released when the layout key changes
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:1714-1716 — camera re-fit on resize during play
- src/ui/gameplayPause.ts:63 — rotation is not a pause reason

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The release on a layout-key change is intended and correct (commit 14c8c5df), and the OS probably cancels touches on rotation anyway. Only the pause is missing. The fix must:
  1. Fire only when the key changes between two non-none layouts during play-world. Entering or leaving play changes the key from or to 'none:*', and that must not pause.
  2. Pass the flag from MobileUiController to installGameplayPause through a dataset value or a custom event. That is about 20-30 lines plus a test, not 15.
  3. Hold the pause until the layout settles and the first touch lands on the moved controls, capped at about 1.5-2 s. A fixed 800 ms can end with inputs still released. The pause also starts only after resize fires, so some of the release has already happened by then.
  
  Ranked runs gain nothing on time, because ranking time includes breaks. The benefit is limited to freezing physics and enemies.

### F360: Battery Saver doesn't pause or simplify animated backgrounds

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F011

**Summary.** Battery Saver halves the weather and skips score pop-ups, but animated room backgrounds, which shipped after that work, ignore it. They keep animating at full speed, re-uploading textures many times a second, and still unpack every frame. Holding the first frame in Battery Saver (exactly what the reduced-motion setting already does) is a one-line change, and unpacking only that first frame would also save the memory.

**Technical detail.**

Battery Saver levers: weatherDetailScale (weather/controller.ts:250-253) and spawnScorePopup (fx/controller.ts:260-261), both gated on getDevicePerformanceMode() === 'battery-saver'. The policy marks Battery Saver as visualDataProfile/activeRuntimeProfile 'reduced' (performancePolicy.ts:44-54).

The animation tick (animation.ts:165-168) only checks prefersReducedMotion() and document.hidden. So in Battery Saver an animated tile background still:
- redraws and re-uploads its texture and every TileSprite pattern at the animation's rate (about 10 changes/s for the chosen loop);
- keeps all frames decoded (7.6 MB for the chosen loop, up to 69 MB).

Fix (small):
1. In the update closure, treat battery-saver like reduced motion: `const still = prefersReducedMotion() || getDevicePerformanceMode() === 'battery-saver'`, holding frame 0 (the existing branch).
2. Better: give decodeBackground an option to decode only the first ANMF when Battery Saver is on at load time, and subscribe to DEVICE_PERFORMANCE_MODE_CHANGED_EVENT (devicePerformanceMode.ts:3,139-142) to re-decode lazily if the player switches back.
3. Extend controller.batterySaver.test.ts-style coverage to animation.test.ts.
Optionally halve the animation rate under the automatic 'reduced' profile, mirroring the F011 decision to keep strong cuts behind the explicit choice.

**Evidence.**

- src/backgrounds/animation.ts:165-168 — only prefersReducedMotion() freezes frames
- src/weather/controller.ts:250-253 — weather halves under battery-saver
- src/fx/controller.ts:260-261 — score popups skipped under battery-saver
- src/performance/performancePolicy.ts:44-54 — battery-saver resolves to reduced visual/runtime profiles
- src/performance/devicePerformanceMode.ts:3,139-142 — mode-change event already dispatched

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F359: details withheld

Security, safety or anti-cheat item; details withheld from this public repo until it is fixed (see the private review page, or ask Claude to read it from the review artifact).

### F361: Idea: invite repeat phone players to add WAMP to their home screen, and fix the Android icon

- **Area:** Mobile play (reviewer: Mobile play on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** WAMP can already be installed as an app, but nothing ever suggests it. Installed, it runs without the browser's address bar, which gives back about 50-60px of height in landscape play, roughly 15% of a phone screen. The Android icon also isn't marked as 'maskable', so Android shows it shrunk on a white plate. A one-time 'Add WAMP to your home screen' tip for returning phone players, plus a proper icon, is a cheap win.

**Technical detail.**

public/app.webmanifest:12-23 lists icon-192 and icon-512 with no "purpose". icon-192.png has transparent rounded corners and a yellow border, so Chrome's adaptive-icon handling places it inside a white shape. The manifest also has no screenshots, so Android shows the plain mini install prompt. index.html:9-12 sets the mobile-web-app tags. No code handles beforeinstallprompt or checks display-mode: standalone; a grep of src finds neither.

Build:
(1) Add a full-bleed maskable 512px icon (W inside the central 80% safe zone on #050505) with purpose 'maskable', and keep the current icons as 'any'.
(2) After a player's second session or first clear on a coarse-pointer phone, show a one-time tip. On Android, capture beforeinstallprompt and call prompt() from the button. On iOS, show 'Share, then Add to Home Screen' steps. Reuse the existing one-time modal pattern (postRunReminder.ts and welcomeModal.ts already handle once-only and visibility).
(3) Hide the tip when matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)') matches.

Caveat for the iOS copy: home-screen apps on iOS have separate storage, so guests start fresh and signed-in players must sign in again. Say so in the tip.

**Evidence.**

- public/app.webmanifest:12-23 — icons have no 'purpose', no screenshots
- public/icons/icon-192.png — transparent rounded corners (not maskable)
- index.html:9-12 — mobile-web-app meta tags present
- index.html:23 — manifest linked; no install handling in src

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The maskable-icon half was already proposed in F077's write-up (details.md:2731) and was never done, because the F077 fix only changed orientation; treat it as a leftover from F077. The new part is the install tip. "Nothing ever suggests it" is true on iOS only: the manifest meets Chrome's install criteria (no service worker needed), so Android Chrome can already show its own mini-infobar. The custom tip mainly helps iOS players and Android players who dismissed Chrome's prompt. The ~15% height gain applies only to landscape overlay play. Portrait, the default phone play mode, gains about 7-8%, and iOS keeps its status bar with style "default". On iOS, show the tip to signed-in players, or warn guests clearly, because guest clears in localStorage stay behind in Safari. Players can sign in again in the home-screen app with the email code (emailCodeDialog.ts), which is on main.

### F365: Expanded Room setup on phones: the panel covers the whole map, and the map can't be dragged by touch

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** On a phone, the Expanded Room setup panel covers everything except a thin strip at the top of the screen. The map behind it can only be moved with the right mouse button, Space or Alt, none of which a phone has. That leaves a phone builder unable to see or pick the neighbouring rooms they want to add, so they're stuck with the room they started in. The fix is to make the panel a bottom sheet that can be hidden on phones, and to let fingers drag and pinch the map.

**Technical detail.**

course-editor.css:306-313: on phones .course-editor-panel is top calc(96px+safe-top), left/right 8px, bottom 8px with width:auto. Its parent #course-editor-shell is inset:0 inside #game-container (index.html:1503, 1860), so the canvas shows only through a ~96px band. Cells are chosen only by tapping the map: pointerup → handlePointerAction (CourseComposerScene.ts:1280-1289, 1311-1347), using pointer.worldX/Y. Panning needs pointerRequestsPan (1361-1367): right button, Space or Alt. There is no pinch; zoom is wheel (137, 188) or the +/- buttons. centerCameraOnCoordinates (1412-1418) centres the selected cell in the middle of the full canvas. On a 390x844 phone that is y≈422, behind the panel. At the initial 0.18x zoom each cell is about 115x63px, so the visible band holds roughly 1.5 rows of cells, and the selected cell isn't one of them. Tablets: the panel is 380px wide (course-editor.css:37-44), so on a 768px iPad in portrait the centred cell straddles the panel edge, and touch panning doesn't work there either. Phones can reach the composer: phone-world-chat.css:154 shows 'Expanded Room Builder' in the HUD details. The phone smoke never visits it, because smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:39-40 opens openSyntheticCourseEditor directly. Fix (medium): (1) on phones, make the panel a ~45dvh bottom sheet with a Hide toggle, using the editor sheet pattern in phone-editor-dock.css:8-17 and 83-105. (2) Add touch pan and pinch with EditorTouchGesture (touchGesture.ts:48-103), as CourseTouchController.pinch already does (courseTouch.ts:59-67; CourseEditorScene.ts:659-668), and select a cell only when up() returns 'tap'. (3) Offset centerCameraOnCoordinates by the area the panel covers. Optionally add ←↑→↓ 'select neighbour' buttons beside Add Cell. Add a phone composer step to smoke_editor_phone_dock.

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/course-editor.css:306-313 — phone panel covers the canvas except a 96px top band
- src/scenes/CourseComposerScene.ts:1247-1289 — pan only when pointerRequestsPan; every other pointerup selects a cell
- src/scenes/CourseComposerScene.ts:1361-1367 — pan requires rightButtonDown, Space or Alt
- src/scenes/CourseComposerScene.ts:1412-1418 — selected cell centred in the full canvas (behind the panel on phones)
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-world-chat.css:154 — Expanded Room Builder button shown on phones
- scripts/smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:39-40 — phone smoke skips the composer and opens the course editor directly

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The core defect is right: on phones the panel covers everything but the top ~96px (which also holds the account controls), there is no touch pan or pinch, and every touch release selects a cell. Three corrections:
  (1) Phone builders aren't completely stuck. With + zoom at 0.8x or more, the top strip shows the cell directly above the centred one (and cells above to the side at lower zoom), so those can be picked. The same-row neighbours and the cell below can never be picked.
  (2) Landscape phones count as phones too (short edge 540px or less), so the strip is 96px out of a 390px-tall screen.
  (3) A phone smoke does visit the composer: smoke_first_publish.mjs runs on phone, narrow-phone and landscape, enters it, and taps Publish with touch. What no smoke covers is picking a cell on the map or panning by touch. Add that step to smoke_first_publish or to smoke_editor_phone_dock.
  Also, Fit and Center both centre the camera on the full canvas, so the offset fix in step (3) of the proposal must cover fitCourseToView too, not only centerCameraOnCoordinates.
- **partially confirmed.** On phones, the panel covers everything except a 96px band at the top and 8px strips at the sides and bottom. The map can't be panned or pinched by touch, and Center/Fit put the selected cell behind the panel. So a phone builder can't see neighbouring cells, and can't realistically pick one. That is how they get stuck at one cell. Strictly, the 8px side strips at fit zoom, and the bottom of the top band after one '+' press, do land on adjacent cells, but nothing tells the player this.
  
  The 0.18x zoom applies only to a new empty draft. Drafts that already have cells open at fit zoom, about 0.53x on a 390px-wide phone.
  
  Tablets are only degraded. Neighbours are partly visible to the right of the 380px panel, and tap, Center and '-' zoom work, so tablet builders aren't blocked.
  
  Real-world reach is narrow. A cell can only be added if it is a published room the same builder authored, next to the existing cells. On phones the Expand Room button sits behind More. Impact is medium rather than high.
  
  The fix stays as proposed: a hideable bottom sheet on phones, EditorTouchGesture pan/pinch with tap-to-select, and centring offset by the area the panel covers. Optionally add buttons to select the neighbour in each direction, and a phone composer step in the smoke test.
- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F368: On phones, most of the WampOS 95 and Backrooms tilesets can't be reached because the tile picker won't scroll by touch

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** On phones the classic tileset picker sits in a box 166 pixels tall. The tileset image fills the box's width and treats every touch as a 'select tiles' drag, so a swipe can't scroll it. For WampOS 95, 21 of its 27 rows are out of reach, Backrooms loses about 4 rows and the Cybercity sets lose 1–2. The fix is to let vertical swipes scroll and to select a block of tiles with tap-and-hold.

**Technical detail.**

phone-editor-tools.css:76-80 caps #palette-container at max-height:166px with overflow:auto. paletteController.ts:395-401 and paletteLayout.ts:5-13 scale the canvas to the container width (phone maximum 2x). A 192px-wide sheet therefore draws about 354px wide in a ~358px container, leaving a 2px gutter. paletteController.ts:414 sets canvas touchAction='none'. pointerdown (462-487) starts a rectangle selection with setPointerCapture, and pointermove (489-511) extends it. Nothing in the file auto-scrolls the container, and iOS/Android overlay scrollbars can't be dragged. Computed with the real tileset sizes for a 390px phone: wampos95 192x432 → a 354x796 canvas with 630px (21.4 rows of 29.5px) hidden. backrooms 192x160 → 295px tall, 129px (4.4 rows) hidden. cybercity yellow and pink 192x112 → 40px (1.4 rows) hidden. snow → 26px hidden. forest, desert, cave, water and gothic → 11px (part of the last row) hidden. micromono and micromonobold (256x672 on screen) hide 15.8 rows, but have 51px gutters a user could scroll from if they knew to. Fix (small): for coarse pointers set touch-action:pan-y on the canvas so vertical swipes scroll natively. Make a tap select one tile, and start a block selection only after a ~250ms hold, reusing updateSelection (paletteController.ts:483, 509). Remove the 166px cap inside the phone dock sheet, which already scrolls. Add a smoke check that taps the last row of wampos95 on a 390px viewport.

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-tools.css:76-80 — #palette-container max-height 166px, overflow auto
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:395-401 — canvas scaled to container width, phone max 2x
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:414 — paletteCanvas.style.touchAction = 'none'
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:462-511 — any touch on the canvas becomes a rectangle selection with pointer capture
- src/config/tilesets.ts:1022-1026 — wampos95 is 192x432
- src/config/tilesets.ts:1001-1005 — backrooms is 192x160

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **confirmed.** Minor refinements, no change to the verdict:
  1. **Numbers.** Container clientWidth is ≈355 (the #editor-sidebar-scroll padding-right of 3px was missed), so WampOS 95 hides ≈627px rather than 630. The row counts stand.
  2. **The fix must also move selection off pointerdown.** pointerdown calls updateSelection immediately. If only touch-action is changed to pan-y, every scroll swipe would still change the selected tile before the browser sends pointercancel. Selection needs to commit on a tap (pointerup without movement), with block-select started by a hold. The special-tile shortcut and the auto-collapse should also stay on tap.
  3. **Removing the cap needs the touch-action change too.** Otherwise the canvas fills the outer sheet's width and blocks that sheet's scrolling as well.
  4. **More affected sets.** Special, Boygame, Jungle Vines and the text sets are also only reachable through the side gutters, so the smoke check should cover one of them too.
  5. **Possibly tablets.** Tablets probably have the same problem at a milder level: no cap, but a full-width touch-action:none canvas in the drawer. I did not verify this.
- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F363: Editor rebuilds the publish checklist (full room copy, sort, JSON and hash) on every UI refresh, including each pinch-zoom step

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Runtime performance: frame rate, GC and memory)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F159

**Summary.** The editor's Ready-to-Publish checklist is recalculated every time the editor panel refreshes, and for any room with a goal that means copying the whole room, sorting it, turning it into text and hashing it, even when there is no saved clear check to compare against. Zooming with the mouse wheel or pinching on a phone refreshes the panel on every step, so pinch-zoom does this dozens of times a second. That costs about 2 ms per step on a fast Mac and likely 8-10 ms on a phone, making zoom feel sticky. A one-line fix skips the hash when there is nothing to compare, and zoom should only update the zoom label.

**Technical detail.**

Path: interaction.ts:970 (wheel handleZoom) and :1530 (each pinch move above a 2% change) call host.updateZoomUI(); EditorScene.ts:1659-1661 maps that to renderEditorUi(); renderEditorUi (:1900-1906) runs chromeController.render(), which builds buildReadyToPublishChecklist(this.editRuntime.exportRoomSnapshot(), ...) on every call (chrome.ts:65), then uiBridge.render, inspector refresh and renderMusicUi. Inside, hasEditorDraftClear (clearCheck.ts:54-58) evaluates `receipt?.fingerprint === getEditorDraftFingerprint(snapshot)`: the optional chain only guards the left side, so the fingerprint is computed for every goal room even when no receipt exists. getEditorDraftFingerprint (:29-35) does cloneRoomSnapshot, a recursive Object.entries/sort/fromEntries copy of the whole room (2,640 tile cells, smart-terrain cell map, objects, music, custom tile pixels), JSON.stringify and a per-character double hash. The checklist rows are then rebuilt with replaceChildren (clearCheckUi.ts:6-14), forcing DOM/style work. Every document revision also calls renderEditorUi via the edge-guide sync (EditorScene.ts:1328-1331). Added by the F159 Clear Check feature (blame e1b73df1 / 66c2b33a, 2026-10-09).

Measured (scratch bench clearcheck.bench.test.ts, M-series Mac, Node 22) on a 35 KB room (60% terrain, 400 smart cells, 60 objects, reach_exit goal): fingerprint 1.12 ms, full checklist with goal and no receipt 1.64 ms, checklist without goal 0.49 ms, cloneRoomSnapshot 0.38 ms; exportRoomSnapshot comes on top. Pinch moves arrive at 60-120 Hz.

Fix plan: (1) in hasEditorDraftClear return false when no receipt matches the room before fingerprinting (one line; removes ~1.1 ms from every render of every goal room); (2) cache the checklist keyed on editRuntime.documentRevision + title + edge summary, and cache the fingerprint per revision; (3) make updateZoomUI update only the zoom text (renderEditorUiViewModel field) instead of the full renderEditorUi; (4) only replaceChildren when the rows changed.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/chrome.ts:65 — every chrome render builds buildReadyToPublishChecklist(this.editRuntime.exportRoomSnapshot(), ...)
- src/scenes/editor/clearCheck.ts:54-58 — getEditorDraftFingerprint is evaluated even when readReceipts finds no receipt
- src/scenes/editor/clearCheck.ts:29-35 — fingerprint = cloneRoomSnapshot + recursive sorted copy + JSON.stringify + per-char hash
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:970 — wheel zoom calls updateZoomUI on every event
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:1530 — pinch move calls updateZoomUI on every >2% step
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1659-1661 — updateZoomUI() just calls renderEditorUi()
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1900-1906 — renderEditorUi runs chrome render, practice button and music UI
- src/scenes/editor/clearCheckUi.ts:6-14 — checklist rows recreated with replaceChildren on each render
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1328-1331 — every edit revision also triggers renderEditorUi

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F369: Phone builders have to reopen the library just to switch between Draw and Erase

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** On phones the row of drawing tools (Draw, Erase, Fill, Move, shapes) lives inside the library sheet, and that sheet hides itself after every tile or object pick. Switching tools takes three taps: open a library tab (which more than halves the room view), tap the tool, then tap Hide. That's for the most common action in building. A compact tool strip, or at least a Draw/Erase toggle, should stay on screen while the sheet is hidden.

**Technical detail.**

index.html:251-255: #editor-phone-tools is a child of #sidebar. editorPhoneDock.ts:100-104 moves .editor-shell-tools and the four tool pickers into it. phone-editor-dock.css:107-109 hides #sidebar entirely when data-mobile-editor-collapsed='true'. The sheet collapses itself after every tile pick (paletteController.ts:513-518) and every object pick (693-705, which also forces activeTool='pencil' at 699). The phone bar holds only Undo, Redo, Test, Publish, More and Show/Hide (editorPhoneDock.ts:96-99; phone-editor-dock.css:40-46). The repo's own smoke taps Terrain before every tool tap (smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:183-195). Cost per switch on a 390x664 Safari viewport: the stage shrinks from 562px (664−48−54) to 257px when the sheet opens (minus min(46dvh,344)=305), then grows back, and the camera re-centres each time. Draw→Erase→Draw takes 6 taps, against 2 clicks or keypresses on desktop. Fix (medium): while the sheet is collapsed, keep #editor-phone-tools visible as a ~52px strip above the dock. That means moving it out of #sidebar into a sibling row; it already scrolls sideways (phone-editor-dock.css:129-140). Alternatively, add a current-tool chip to the phone bar that toggles Draw/Erase on tap and opens the full list on long-press. Also, when picking an object, keep Erase if the builder is erasing objects instead of forcing pencil.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:251-255 — #editor-phone-tools sits inside #sidebar
- src/ui/setup/editorPhoneDock.ts:100-104 — tools and pickers moved into #editor-phone-tools
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-dock.css:107-109 — collapsed sheet hides #sidebar (and the tools)
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:513-518 — tile pick auto-collapses the sheet
- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:693-705 — object pick forces pencil and auto-collapses
- scripts/smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:183-195 — every tool switch preceded by reopening Terrain

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Only Tilesets palette picks (paletteController.ts:513-518) and object picks (:693-705) auto-collapse the sheet. Auto-Tile (smart) theme and brush picks in editorDockShell.ts:877-908 leave it open. Tapping a tool never collapses the sheet, and the bar's Show button reopens it without picking a library tab. The real cost is Show → tool → Hide: 3 taps per switch with the full stage kept, or 1 tap if the builder draws in the 257px view with the sheet open. On resize the camera keeps its world midpoint rather than re-centring, though the 305px change in stage height still shifts the view. Drop the suggestion to keep Erase on object pick: forcing pencil there is intentional. Recommended fix: add a current-tool Draw/Erase chip to the phone bar (small), or move #editor-phone-tools into its own always-visible row outside #sidebar (medium; costs about 52px of stage).
- **partially confirmed.** Phone tools are reachable only through the open library sheet (index.html:252-256, editorPhoneDock.ts:100-103, phone-editor-dock.css:107-109). Phones have no right-click, shortcut or gesture fallback for Erase. Picking an object always collapses the sheet and forces pencil. Picking a raw tile collapses it only in Advanced mode; Beginner/Auto-Tile smart-brush picks (the default) leave the sheet open, so those builders draw on a ~257px stage or tap Hide themselves. A switch costs 2 taps (Show/tab + tool), or 3 with Hide. Draw→Erase→Draw is 4-6 taps against 2 on desktop. The camera keeps its world midpoint (interaction.ts:347-361) rather than re-centring. The smoke's repeated Terrain taps are mostly redundant, so they are not evidence. Undo in the bar already handles erasing a fresh mistake. Drop the 'keep Erase on object pick' sub-suggestion. This is the unbuilt part of F110's 'floating tool rail' idea (merged into F161, closed when the tools went into the sheet). Fix: keep a ~52px tool strip visible while collapsed, either by showing only #editor-phone-tools in collapsed mode and adjusting --phone-editor-stage-height and aria-hidden, or with a Draw/Erase chip in the phone bar.
- **partially confirmed.** Tool taps do not collapse the sheet: builders can keep it open and switch with one tap, at the cost of a stage about 257px tall. The extra taps (Show, tool, optional Hide) apply when the sheet is collapsed, which is where it ends up after every tile or object pick. The camera keeps its world midpoint and does not re-centre on the room; a pending Move selection is cancelled on each open or close (objectMoveController.ts:67). Drop "keep Erase on object pick": object erase ignores the selection (editRuntime.ts:2207-2209), so pencil is the right default. Recommend the small fix first: a Draw/Erase chip in the phone bar that clicks the existing [data-tool] buttons and opens the full tool list on long-press. Keep the persistent strip, which is medium effort and costs about 52px of stage, as a follow-up. Impact is medium rather than high, because Undo is already on the bar.

### F367: On a 390px phone, Markers (Spawn and Goal) and Room Setup start off-screen in the dock, with no hint to scroll

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F161

**Summary.** The phone dock has seven buttons but only about five fit on a typical phone. Markers, where Place Spawn and Goal now live, and Room Setup (music, background, templates) start past the right edge. The tool row has the same problem: Rectangle, Circle and Line are off-screen. Nothing shows that either row scrolls, and the automated phone test scrolls each button into view before tapping it, so it can't catch this.

**Technical detail.**

phone-editor-dock.css:159-183: the dock row is a flex row of buttons at flex:1 0 74px, Room Setup at 108px, 4px gaps and 0 4px padding, inside an overflow-x:auto dock (149-157). The seven buttons (index.html:1476-1482) need 6×74+108+6×4+8 = 584px. On a 390px screen, Markers starts at about x=398 and Room Setup at about x=476. The tool row (129-140) holds nine tools at 60px plus 4px gaps, 576px in total, so Scramble, Rectangle, Circle and Line start at x≥392. No phone-editor stylesheet adds a fade or scroll indicator. smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:50-54 calls scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() before every tap, and its bounds checks (56-58, 66-67) test only the containers and the phone bar. F161's plan put 'Markers (Spawn/Goal)' in the phone tab bar specifically so it would be one tap away, and on the most common phone width it now isn't visible. Fix (small): make the dock fit the width, either as seven equal ~52px columns with the existing icons shown (phone-editor-dock.css:185-187 hides them) and short labels, or by moving Room Setup into More. Add an edge-fade mask to the tool row. Change the smoke to assert that every dock button's box is inside the viewport without scrolling.

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-dock.css:170-183 — dock buttons flex-basis 74px, Room Setup 108px
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-dock.css:137-140 — tool buttons 60px each in a scrolling row
- index.html:1476-1482 — seven dock buttons; Markers is 6th, Room Setup 7th
- scripts/smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:50-54 — tap helper scrolls each target into view first

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** On a 390px phone, Markers starts at x=394 and Room Setup at x=472; the dock's left padding is safe-left (0) plus the grid's 4px. Deco ends exactly at 390, so no part of Markers shows. The tool row has 9 tools at 572px, starting at x=8 inside the sidebar. Scramble (328-388) is mostly visible, and only Rectangle, Circle and Line are fully off-screen. The fix needs to work at 320px, which the smoke tests: seven equal columns come to about 41px there. Prefer moving Room Setup into the ☰ menu, which gives six buttons of at least 48px, or go icon-only on narrow phones. Add edge fades, and make the smoke assert that every dock button's box is in the viewport without scrolling.

### F371: With the Move tool picked, touch builders can't zoom or pan, and phones have no Fit button

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F162

**Summary.** On a phone, a two-finger pinch is the only way to zoom or move around the room. With the Move tool selected, the second finger just cancels the move and the pinch never starts, so a builder who has zoomed in can't reach the far side of the room without switching tools. Phones also hide the Fit and +/- zoom buttons that desktop has. Pinch should win over Move, and a 'Fit room' button belongs in the More menu.

**Technical detail.**

interaction.ts:708-712: objectMove.down(pointer) runs before handleTouchPointerDown and returns true for every touch while Move is active. objectMoveController.ts:82 and 87: a second pointer during a drag or marquee calls cancel() and returns true, so touchGesture.down never sees either finger. Later moves of finger 2 reach touchGesture.move, which returns 'ignore' (touchGesture.ts:71). CourseEditorScene.ts:2387-2389 has the same order, so Expanded Rooms are affected too. objectMoveController.test.ts:117 asserts only the cancel. Neither editor has a one-finger pan. The zoom fallback is gone on phones as well: the dock shell hides .mobile-editor-actions-panel (dock-shell.css:967-973), which holds #btn-mobile-editor-zoom-out, zoom-in and fit (index.html:1320-1325, still bound at uiBridge.ts:1468-1478), and phone-chrome.css:106-111 hides #btn-fit-screen. Fix (small): in both pointerdown handlers, pass touch pointers to the touch gesture first. If it reports 'pinch', call objectMove.stopGesture() (the selection is kept) and start the pinch. Add a 'Fit room' button to #editor-phone-menu wired to actions.onFitToScreen (append it to elements.fitBtns, uiBridge/elements.ts:254-256).

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:708-712 — objectMove.down consumes touch before the touch gesture runs
- src/scenes/editor/objectMoveController.ts:82 — second pointer during a drag: cancel() and return true
- src/scenes/editor/objectMoveController.ts:87 — second pointer during a marquee: cancel() and return true
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:2387-2389 — same order in the Expanded Room editor
- src/styles/sections/editor/dock-shell.css:967-973 — mobile zoom/Fit panel hidden under the dock shell
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-chrome.css:106-111 — #btn-fit-screen hidden on phones
- src/scenes/editor/uiBridge.ts:1468-1478 — zoom/fit handlers exist but their phone buttons are hidden

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F366: Landscape phones get a 109px-tall room view, and tablets lose 366px of height to toolbars

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Turning a phone sideways keeps the portrait stack: top bar, bottom dock and bottom library sheet. On an 844x390 phone that leaves the room 109px tall while the library is open (about 88px on iPhones with a home bar), drawn at 4 pixels per tile. iPads under 1680px wide get the desktop layout with 366px of fixed bars, about half the screen in landscape. A side-panel layout in landscape would fix the phone case.

**Technical detail.**

deviceLayout.ts:42-49 classifies a device by its shortest edge (≤540 → phone), so phones in landscape keep the phone layout. phone-editor-dock.css:8-13: bar 48+safe-top, dock 54+safe-bottom, sheet min(46dvh,344px), and the stage is 100dvh − bar − dock − sheet (game-container height at 73-82). For 844x390 that is 390−48−54−179 = 109px; with the iPhone landscape safe-bottom of 21px it is 88px. Collapsed, it is 288px (267px). No phone-editor stylesheet has a landscape rule; only phone-editor-music.css:399 has an orientation:landscape query. fitToScreen (interaction.ts:417-440) uses 32px padding outside phone portrait and rounds to quarter steps: min((844−32)/640, (109−32)/352) = 0.22 → clamped to 0.25, so the room is 160x88px with 4px tiles. #editor-shell-top uses padding: var(--safe-top) 4px 0 (line 34), with no safe-left/right. In landscape, Undo (the first 44px column) therefore sits inside the 47px rounded-corner inset, while the sheet and dock do respect safe-left/right (lines 90 and 152). Tablets: dock-shell.css:14-18 with 1329-1332 sets, at ≤1680px wide, a 210px top shell, a 120px dock and a 36px bottom bar, 366px fixed in total. iPad Air in landscape Safari (~1180x750) leaves ~384px of canvas, and iPad mini (~1133x690) ~324px, which fits the room at 0.75 zoom (12px tiles). Fix (medium): add a phone-landscape block that puts the sheet in a side column (min(340px,42vw) wide, full stage height), merges the phone bar and dock into one row, and adds safe-left/right to #editor-shell-top. smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs already runs 844x390 (line 13); add an assertion that #game-container is at least 50% of the viewport height. For tablets, collapse the ≤1680 top shell into one row and move the title into More.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/deviceLayout.ts:42-49 — phone = shortest edge ≤540, so landscape phones keep the phone layout
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-dock.css:11 — sheet height min(46dvh, 344px) in every orientation
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-dock.css:34 — phone top bar padding ignores safe-left/right
- src/styles/sections/responsive/phone-editor-music.css:399 — only the music editor has a landscape media query
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:423-434 — non-portrait fit uses 32px padding and quarter-step rounding
- src/styles/sections/editor/dock-shell.css:1329-1332 — ≤1680px: top shell 210px (plus dock 120px and bottom bar 36px at lines 14-18)
- scripts/smoke_editor_phone_dock.mjs:13 — smoke already runs 844x390 but never checks canvas size

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Phone landscape is confirmed: with the library open the stage is 109px (88px with the home bar), the room fits at the 0.25 floor (160x88px, 4px tiles), and collapsed it is 288px (267px). It is worse in one case: with the Community or Mine filter in Stuff, phone-editor-shell.css:11-13 (min(66vh,540px), specificity 0,4,1) overrides the dock's sheet height. The landscape stage then drops to about 31px (about 10px with the home bar), while the sidebar's max-height clamps the visible sheet to 208px, leaving a dead band of about 49px. The fix must clamp or scope that rule as well. Minor corrections: text-preferences.css:108-125 does have a phone-landscape editor rule, but only bar columns for readable or large text. The missing safe-left only puts Undo under the rounded corner, not the notch. The tablet half is not a defect: the 366px chrome is the desktop ≤1680px dock layout already verified at 1024x768, and iPads still fit the room at 0.75–1.0 zoom (12–16px tiles). Treat it as optional low-impact polish or split it out.

### F370: Placing objects, pastes and markers by touch is blind: the preview is hidden under your finger, and sliding cancels

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** At the zoom a phone opens the room with, a tile is about 9 pixels wide, so a fingertip covers roughly a 5x5 block of tiles. The placement preview is drawn exactly under the finger, and if the finger slides more than 10 pixels the placement is silently dropped. A better model is the phone's text loupe: show the ghost a little above the finger, let the builder slide to adjust, and place on lift.

**Technical detail.**

interaction.ts:1188-1195 classifies single-object placement, paste, goal/spawn markers and fill as touchAction 'tap'. handleTouchPointerUp places only when gesture.up returns 'tap' (1276-1278). touchGesture.ts:76 and 85 turn any movement over 10px into 'drag', after which nothing is placed and no status is shown. updateCursorHighlight (452-628) draws the object or paste preview at activePointer's tile, which is under the contact point. Phone fit (interaction.ts:425-434, 12px padding) gives zoom min((390−12)/640, …) = 0.59, so a 16px tile is 9.4px on screen and a 44px fingertip spans about 4.7 tiles. Fix (medium): for 'tap' actions on touch, follow the finger and draw the existing preview (getObjectPreviewRectForTile, drawClipboardPastePreview) at the tile ~56px above the contact point. On up, place at that tile whatever the movement; cancel only on pinch, touchcancel, or a lift outside the room. Apply the same change in CourseTouchController.tap (courseTouch.ts:91-94). This also solves aiming at room edges, where the finger hangs off the canvas.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:1188-1195 — object, paste, goal and fill touches classified as 'tap'
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:1276-1278 — placement only when the gesture result is 'tap'
- src/scenes/editor/touchGesture.ts:76 — any movement over 10px marks the touch as a drag
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:486-512 — object preview drawn at the pointer's own tile
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:425-434 — phone portrait fit zoom (≈0.59 on a 390px phone)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real gap on phone portrait only. At fit zoom (about 0.59, 9.4px tiles) the object and paste preview is drawn under the finger. A slide over 10px silently drops these tap placements: non-repeatable objects, paste, goal and spawn markers, fill and practice-test placement. Repeatable decorations and collectibles are not affected, because a slide drag-paints them. Pinch-zoom is the existing workaround, so 'blind' is overstated. The fix must (a) exclude pen pointers, which isTouchPointer treats as touch, (b) keep the existing-object inspector and link tap (handleObjectModePrimaryAction) working sensibly, for example by applying the offset only once the finger is held or moves, (c) cancel when the offset target is outside the room, not when the finger lifts outside it, and (d) pass a tile instead of the pointer through handleObjectPlace and handleToolDown in both EditorScene and CourseEditorScene (classification at CourseEditorScene.ts:607-611, up at courseTouch.ts:91-93). A cheap first step is to show a status message or toast when a tap-placement is dropped because the finger slid.

### F364: Erasing a rectangle, line, connected area or stamp shape needs a right-click, so touch builders can't do it

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** On desktop, right-dragging with the Rectangle, Circle or Line tool erases that shape. Right-clicking with Fill erases a whole connected area, and right-dragging a multi-tile stamp erases exactly that stamp's tiles. None of this is possible on phones or tablets, where the eraser only offers 1x1, 3x3 and 5x5 brushes. The code already exists, so the fix is an 'erase' switch in those tools' option pickers.

**Technical detail.**

interaction.ts:737-768, right button: floodErase for 'fill' (749-752), shapeEraseActive for drag-stamp tools (753-762), and eraseWithActiveBrush → eraseStampAt for pencil (763-767, 1367-1373). The touch path (1188-1214) never sets shapeEraseActive or calls floodErase or eraseStampAt, and finishCurrentTouchDraw always passes erase:false (1357-1358). The Expanded Room editor works the same way: shape erase (CourseEditorScene.ts:2606-2611) and flood/stamp erase (2728-2733) are right-button only. The eraser picker offers just 1x1/3x3/5x5 and Nuke Terrain/Objects (index.html:1404-1426). Fix (small): add an 'Erase' toggle to the rect/ellipse/line, fill and pencil pickers for coarse pointers, backed by a sticky editorState flag. In the touch path, pass erase:true to stampShape, call floodErase in applyTouchTap, and use eraseStampAt in the 'tiles' branch. Add the flag to editorTouchToolKey (touchGesture.ts:106-120) so flipping it cancels a held edit, and mirror the change in CourseTouchController's host callbacks.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:749-767 — flood erase, shape erase and stamp erase only inside the rightButtonDown branch
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:1196-1213 — touch tile path never selects an erase variant
- src/scenes/editor/interaction.ts:1357-1358 — touch shape commit hard-codes erase:false
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:2606-2611 — Expanded editor shape erase requires right button
- index.html:1404-1426 — eraser picker: sizes and Nuke only

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The gap is real in both the Room and Expanded editors, and touch Curve erase is also unreachable (interaction.ts:1351 passes erase=false to beginPathBend). The proposed fix is mis-specified. The dock has no Rectangle/Circle/Line pickers (those tools switch Filled/Outlined by being tapped again), and the phone dock does not move the Fill picker into phone tools (editorPhoneDock.ts:102). An 'Erase' toggle therefore needs a new control. It has to show for rect/ellipse/line/fill/pencil in tiles mode and be wired into the phone dock. It also needs a sticky editorState flag that is included in editorTouchToolKey. On the touch side, the flag has to be read in five places: the touch shape commit and the curve bend, applyTouchTap (to call floodErase), the 'tiles' pencil branch (to call eraseStampAt), and CourseEditorScene's handlePrimaryPointerDown, tap and beginBrush host callbacks. The DOM-contract and smoke tests need updating too. Effort is roughly small-to-medium, not small.

### F373: Uploading an animated background holds every full-size frame at once (up to 128 MB) and wastes a PNG encode per frame on Safari

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Gap review: Phone cost of visual effects: animated backgrounds, weather, starfield, custom textures)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** To prepare an upload, the game first unpacks every frame of the animation at its original size and keeps them all, then shrinks and re-encodes them one by one. For a big animation that can be over 100 MB of images plus several copies of the 8 MB file at the same moment, enough to crash Safari on many iPhones or fail with a confusing error. On Safari, which can't save WebP natively, it also makes and throws away a PNG for every frame before using the backup encoder. Processing one frame at a time, and checking the encoder once, keeps memory to a couple of frames and saves seconds.

**Technical detail.**

prepareBackgroundFile (upload.ts:32-127):
- accepts files up to 8 MB (:15);
- reads file.arrayBuffer() (:35) and wraps it in a new Blob (:41);
- decodeBackground then calls blob.arrayBuffer() again (animation.ts:45-47);
- webpChunks slices every chunk (webp.ts:121) and parseWebpAnimation slices every frame again (:150).
That is about 4-5 copies of the input, roughly 32-40 MB for an 8 MB file.

decodeBackground then keeps one full-input-size canvas per frame (animation.ts:79-86), and the encode loop runs only afterwards (upload.ts:71-109). Peak decoded memory is frames x w x h x 4, bounded only by MAX_BACKGROUND_DECODE_PIXELS = 32M (webp.ts:20), so up to 128 MB of 2D canvases. Example: a 480x270, 240-frame input is 31M px, about 124 MB. iOS Safari caps total canvas memory; when the cap is hit, getContext returns null and the user sees 'Could not prepare animated background frame.' (:83-84).

Stills: createImageBitmap(blob) decodes up to 16M px (64 MB) at full size before drawing into the ≤1280x768 canvas (upload.ts:49-57,112).

Safari: encode() (upload.ts:18-29) calls canvas.toBlob(..., 'image/webp') for every frame. Browsers without WebP encoding return a PNG, which is discarded before the jSquash fallback. That is one wasted PNG encode per frame (estimated 3-8 ms at 240x240 on a phone, so roughly 1-2.4 s for 300 frames) plus a getImageData readback on a context created without willReadFrequently.

Fix (small):
1. Stream the frames: composite frame i into one full-size canvas, immediately drawImage it into the ≤240 output canvas, encode, append the ANMF, and keep no snapshots (factor the compositor out of decodeBackground so runtime and upload share it). Peak becomes 1 full canvas plus 1 small one.
2. Probe native WebP support once (module-level flag) and go straight to the fallback afterwards.
3. Create the output canvas with {willReadFrequently: true} when the fallback is active.
4. For stills, use createImageBitmap(blob, {resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality: 'high'}) using the already-known dimensions (upload.ts:38).
5. Pass subarray views instead of slice copies in webpChunks/parseWebpAnimation; they are read-only here.

**Evidence.**

- src/backgrounds/upload.ts:15,35,41 — 8 MB input read and re-wrapped
- src/backgrounds/animation.ts:45-47,79-86 — re-reads bytes; one full-size canvas per frame kept until the end
- src/backgrounds/upload.ts:71-109 — encode loop runs only after all frames are decoded
- src/backgrounds/webp.ts:20,121,150 — 32M-pixel decode ceiling; chunk and frame slice copies
- src/backgrounds/upload.ts:18-29 — native WebP toBlob attempted on every call before the fallback
- src/backgrounds/upload.ts:49-57,112 — stills decoded at full size then scaled
- src/backgrounds/webpEncoder.ts:6-13 — lazy jSquash fallback (webp_enc_simd 346 KB in dist)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism is real. prepareBackgroundFile decodes every animated-WebP frame into its own full-input-size canvas (animation.ts:79-86) before the encode loop (upload.ts:71-109) runs, so peak use reaches up to 128 MB at the 32M-pixel cap. On browsers without native WebP encoding, encode() (upload.ts:18-29) also wastes a PNG toBlob on every frame.
  
  The scope needs narrowing:
  - Only animated WebP takes this path, since GIF and APNG are rejected. It is a rare, one-time, builder-only upload that only affects the uploader's device.
  - Typical inputs are far below the ceiling.
  - "Crash Safari on many iPhones" is not supported. Failure is plausible only on low-RAM devices or when the editor already uses a lot of canvas memory. It may show up as blank frames rather than the 'Could not prepare animated background frame.' error.
  - About 2-3 byte copies (16-24 MB) are live at once, not 4-5. The rest is short-lived garbage.
  
  Do fixes 1 and 2:
  - Stream composite → downscale → encode one frame at a time through a compositor shared with runtime.
  - Cache the native-WebP probe.
  
  Drop fixes 3-5 (willReadFrequently, subarray views, createImageBitmap resize). Their gains are negligible or uncertain on Safari.

### F372: Picking an irregular group of tiles (Ctrl+click in the tileset) has no touch equivalent

- **Area:** Mobile building (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** On desktop, holding Control while clicking or dragging in the tileset adds or removes single tiles from the selection, so builders can grab an L-shape or a tree without its empty corners. On touch devices that hint is simply hidden, and there's no other way to do it. A small 'Add/Remove tiles' toggle next to the tileset would cover it.

**Technical detail.**

paletteController.ts:479-481 enters mask-paint mode only when event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey. beginPaletteMaskPaint and applyPaletteMaskPaint (300-330) then toggle occupied cells, which also drive stamp shape and pattern order (drawSelectionPatternOrderOverlay at 459). index.html:758 wraps the instruction in .fine-pointer-hint, which base.css:1198 hides for coarse pointers, so touch users never learn the feature exists. Fix (small): add a 'Pick tiles' toggle button (coarse pointers only) beside the tileset palette. While it's on, pointerdown calls beginPaletteMaskPaint instead of updateSelection. Include it in the touch fix for the tileset picker so scrolling and mask painting don't fight.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/paletteController.ts:479-481 — mask paint only with Ctrl/Cmd held
- index.html:758 — Control+Click hint inside .fine-pointer-hint
- src/styles/sections/base.css:1198 — .fine-pointer-hint hidden for coarse pointers

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The gap is real, but it is narrower than described. A plain drag in the tileset already leaves out transparent cells (buildSelectionOccupiedMask uses the per-tile pixel occupancy, paletteController.ts:1275-1298), so grabbing a tree without its empty corners already works on touch. What touch users can't do is drop non-empty tiles from a rectangle, combine tiles that aren't next to each other, or set their own Pattern order. Any "Pick tiles" toggle must also skip the phone auto-collapse that palette pointerup triggers (paletteController.ts:517 → editorPhoneDock.ts:47). Otherwise the phone sheet closes after every tap.

### F374: After each release, anyone with WAMP already open can't open the editor or menus until they reload the page

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** high · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** If an on-demand dialog fails to download, nothing happens, and a finished Room Rush can lose its score

**Summary.** WAMP downloads the editor and about 20 menus only when someone first opens them. Each release deletes the old copies of those files, and there were 32 releases between Oct 18 and Oct 21. If a tab was opened before a release, clicking Build or opening a menu fails with a 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' error, and Retry fails the same way. A small handler can catch this and offer a one-click reload, or reload automatically when no draft is unsaved.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: the main boot chunk makes 25 dynamic imports, and 18 lazy controllers plus the editor UI and editor CSS load on first use. Every Pages release replaces all /assets/cache-v2/*-[hash].js names (vite.config.ts:91-92). An old tab then asks for file names that are no longer deployed. The Pages worker turns the SPA HTML fallback into a 404 'Asset Not Found' (src/pages/staticAssets.ts:81-88). The comment at vite.config.ts:16-18 records that previously issued asset URLs did get the HTML fallback once. Vite's preload helper already dispatches a cancelable 'vite:preloadError' event on every failed dynamic import (dist/assets/cache-v2/preload-helper-Dp1pzeXC.js: `a().catch(m)`, where m dispatches the event and rethrows unless it is prevented), but nothing in src listens for it (rg finds no 'preloadError' anywhere in the repo). The loaders then reset and invite a retry that hits the same missing URL: editorSceneLoader.ts:10-24, lazyModal.ts:75-78 and editorUiLoader.ts:25. flow.ts:571-575 shows the raw error in the busy overlay. Exposure: there were 32 first-parent merges to main from Oct 18 to Oct 21, and each is an automatic Pages release (about 8 a day), so almost every tab kept open for a few hours crosses a release. Builders keep long sessions open, so they are hit hardest.

Fix (about 30 lines): in src/main/coarseFirstEntry.ts add `window.addEventListener('vite:preloadError', e => { e.preventDefault(); ... })`. It should show a small 'WAMP was updated. Reload' card using the existing busy-overlay retry button. When no editor draft is dirty, it should reload automatically once, guarded by a sessionStorage key that includes VITE_APP_BUILD_ID so it cannot loop. Treat a failed editor stylesheet (editorStyles.ts) the same way. Optionally emit a tiny no-store /version.json at build time and check it on visibilitychange, so the reload offer appears before the user clicks. To size the problem today, count client error reports (clientErrorReporter.ts:35 already attaches the build id) whose message contains 'dynamically imported module'.

**Evidence.**

- dist/assets/cache-v2/preload-helper-Dp1pzeXC.js:1 — a failed import() dispatches a cancelable 'vite:preloadError' event and rethrows when not prevented; the repo has no listener
- src/scenes/editorSceneLoader.ts:10-24 — Build imports EditorScene/CourseComposerScene/CourseEditorScene lazily; on failure it resets and rethrows, so a retry requests the same deleted URL
- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:571-575 — a load failure only shows showBusyError(error.message)
- src/ui/setup/lazyModal.ts:75-78 — a failed menu download clears `loading` for a retry; nothing reloads the page
- src/pages/staticAssets.ts:81-88 — an /assets/ request that falls back to HTML is answered with 404 'Asset Not Found'
- vite.config.ts:16-18 — comment: previously issued asset URLs were once served the Pages HTML fallback
- src/ui/setup/lazyModal.ts:32-49 — open() has try/finally but no catch or user feedback
- src/ui/setup/lazyModal.ts:75-78 — ensure() rethrows the load error
- src/ui/setup/remainingModalTriggers.ts:43-46 — Rush result opened via `void controllers.roomRushResultModal.open(detail.run)`
- src/ui/setup/remainingModalTriggers.ts:47-55 — app-mode change closes (cancels) not-yet-loaded modals
- src/ui/setup/roomRushResultModal.ts:370-389 — leaderboard submission lives inside the lazily loaded dialog
- src/scenes/overworld/roomRushResults.ts:99-109 — result request dispatched once after the overview hydrates
- vite.config.ts:16-19 — Pages fallback served HTML at previously issued asset URLs
- src/ui/setup/lazyFirstPublish.ts:47 — sibling lazy controller does catch its load failure

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect and its mechanism hold as stated. Four corrections:
  
  1. The proposed fix as written would cause a new bug. In Vite's helper, calling preventDefault() makes the failed import resolve to undefined. Callers would then throw a TypeError, for example `new (undefined).LeaderboardModalController` or reading `editor.EditorScene` from undefined. Only call e.preventDefault() on the branch that actually reloads, after setting a once-per-build sessionStorage guard keyed by VITE_APP_BUILD_ID. When a reload is unsafe (an unsaved course or guest draft, or a Room Rush result still pending), leave the event alone so the loaders reset. Then show a 'WAMP was updated — Reload' card using the existing showBusyError({ retryLabel: 'Reload', retryHandler: () => location.reload() }) pattern, which main.ts:314-320 already uses for WebGL recovery.
