  2. Reloading for a Room Rush result loses that result. Before reloading, save the pending submission body (buildRoomRushSubmissionBody) or submit it without the modal.
  
  3. Sizing with client error reports only counts menu and Rush failures. clientErrorReporter receives only uncaught errors and unhandled rejections, and flow.ts catches editor-load failures and never reports them. Add an explicit report in the new handler.
  
  4. Who is affected: a lazy part of the UI fails only if this tab first opens it after a release. A builder who already opened the editor before the release keeps a working editor, but still hits menus they have not opened yet. Also, the editor stylesheet fails only when the editor CSS itself changed, because a CSS file's hash depends only on its own content.
- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism and the user-facing symptoms are confirmed, and exposure is wider than stated. The git SHA is compiled into the main chunk, so every commit, including docs-only ones, gives 24 of the 25 lazy chunks new names. Three parts of the finding need fixing:
  
  1. Do not call `e.preventDefault()` unless the page reloads in that same tick. In Vite's helper, preventing the event makes `import()` resolve to `undefined` instead of rejecting. Callers would then throw TypeErrors such as `new (await import(...)).X` or `editor.EditorScene` of undefined, which would compete with the reload card and skip the loaders' reset paths. Instead, let the rejection propagate and have the listener only show the update card. Copy the webglRecovery pattern: reload automatically only in browse mode with no active run, editor or dirty draft; otherwise show showBusyError with title 'WAMP was updated' and retryHandler set to location.reload. Guard against reload loops with a sessionStorage key that includes the build id. Also map the editorStyles.ts link failure to the same card.
  
  2. A reload does not save the Room Rush score: the result exists only in memory and inside the lazy dialog. That needs its own small fix. Either load the roomRushResultModal chunk when the Rush start dialog loads or the run starts, while the tab's build is still live, or move submitRoomRushRun out of the lazy dialog.
  
  3. Line references: the error display is at src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:384-386, 421-423 and 574-579, not 571-575. There is no Retry button; the user just clicks Build again.
  
  Optional, lower priority: read the build id at runtime (for example from a meta tag in index.html) instead of compiling it into the shared chunk, so lazy chunk names survive releases that do not touch them. Overall effort is still small, about 40-60 lines plus a unit test.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** PR #288, `src/main/staleBuildRecovery.ts`. Never calls preventDefault, so callers reset as before. A review showed "browsing with nothing open" doesn't prove nothing is unsaved, so auto-reload was dropped in favour of the offer. A Playwright run against a local build with one lazy chunk and the entry script returning 404 showed the card and no reload. [Receipt](wamp-round2-security-and-step1-2026-10-22.md).

### F379: Expanded-room cell saves skip the 'edited somewhere else' check, so two tabs or devices still overwrite each other

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F058

**Summary.** The fix for two open editors overwriting each other (F058) only went into the single-room editor. The Expanded Room editor saves and publishes its cells without telling the server which version it started from, so a stale laptop tab or phone can still silently wipe newer work on any cell of an expanded room. The editor already remembers that version for its local backups. Sending it with the save is a one-line change per call, plus showing the same 'changed elsewhere' prompt the room editor uses.

**Technical detail.**

The room editor sends `baseUpdatedAt` on every write (roomSession.ts:655-657 saveDraft, 757-759 publish). On a 409 it runs handleEditConflict (roomSession.ts:678-681, 1280). RoomWriteOptions documents 'Omit to overwrite' (roomRepository.ts:94-105). CourseEditorScene writes each dirty slice with `this.roomRepository.saveDraft(sent)` (CourseEditorScene.ts:1288) and `this.roomRepository.publish(sent)` (CourseEditorScene.ts:1361), with no options and no 409 branch. The base it needs is already tracked per slice in `roomBackupBases` (set at 1947 on load and 2058 after each save) for the local-backup recovery path. Failure scenario: cell 3,-2 is open in Edit Expanded Room on a laptop. The builder then edits the same cell on a phone through the single-room editor ('Open Selected Room' in the composer, or Edit on a draft cell, flow.ts:358-363) and saves. Back on the laptop, Save Room or Publish uploads the old full snapshot, and the phone's edit is gone with no warning. Fix: pass `{ baseUpdatedAt: this.roomBackupBases.get(slice.roomId)?.updatedAt }` at both call sites. Catch `isRoomEditConflict`, keep the local backup (draftBackup.writeRoom already exists), and show the room editor's conflict choice. If the expanded-room input code is unified (next finding), this save path should move to a shared per-slice session at the same time. About 30 lines. Add one test next to roomSession's conflict tests.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1288 — `const record = await this.roomRepository.saveDraft(sent);` with no baseUpdatedAt
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1361 — `const record = await this.roomRepository.publish(sent);` with no baseUpdatedAt
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:655-657 — room editor passes `baseUpdatedAt: this.serverDraftUpdatedAt`
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:757-759 — publish also passes baseUpdatedAt
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:678-681 — 409 conflict handled via handleEditConflict
- src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:94-105 — RoomWriteOptions: 'Omit to overwrite'
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1947 — roomBackupBases already stores {id, updatedAt, version} per slice on load
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:2058 — roomBackupBases refreshed after every save

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** Minor corrections only:
  - The refresh after save is at CourseEditorScene.ts:2059, not 2058.
  - Only cells this session has edited, or that carry a session override, can be overwritten, and only when the user presses Save or Publish. It is not any cell of the expanded room.
  - A conflict on one cell aborts the multi-cell save loop, so the fix must handle each cell separately (Keep Mine retries that cell without a base; Load Latest reloads that cell).
  - I rate impact medium, not high. F058 itself was medium, and expanded-room cells being edited on two devices at once is a narrower case.
  - The setup record has the same gap (expandedRoomEditorRepository.saveDraft at 1417 and 1458 sends no base) and could be fixed at the same time.
- **partially confirmed.** The bug is real, with two corrections.
  
  **1. Use the right base version.** Do not send roomBackupBases as the base for a slice restored from a session override. That map is reset to the current server version at CourseEditorScene.ts:1947, even when the content comes from an older override. Carry the base with the override instead: use the override snapshot's own updatedAt, or store the base next to the override. Then send that base on both writes:
  - saveDraft(sent, { baseUpdatedAt }) at :1288
  - publish(sent, { baseUpdatedAt }) at :1361
  
  **2. Scope is wider than the edited cells.** After a composer round trip, Publish targets every slice that has an override (:2189-2200). That includes cells the builder never edited in this session.
  
  **Minimal fix:**
  - On a 409, stop the slice loop and flush backupDebouncer, so the local backup keeps the old base.
  - Show "Cell x,y was changed on another device." The existing draftBackup.recoverRoom flow then offers restore-or-load on reopen.
  - A full Load Latest / Keep Mine dialog is optional on top of that.
  
  Note that the course editor was deliberately left out of F058's commit 0ae59b67, so treat this as a follow-up to F058, not a regression. Impact is medium, not high.
- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: Expanded Room cell saves and publishes (CourseEditorScene.ts:1288 and 1361) send no baseUpdatedAt. The server (store.ts:844-851, mutationGuards.ts:15-16) therefore skips the conflict check. F058's commit 0ae59b67 left the course editor out on purpose.
  
  Corrections:
  - Effort is medium, not "one line per call, about 30 lines". The work includes:
    - moving isRoomEditConflict out of roomSession.ts into persistence/roomEditConflict.ts;
    - keeping the conflicting slice in scope inside both per-slice loops, and deciding what happens to the remaining slices (partial save or partial publish);
    - for Load Latest: reloading only that slice while skipping the session override (accountRoomChoices) and discarding the local backup;
    - for Keep Mine: one save without a base;
    - testing through a smoke script such as scripts/smoke_draft_recovery.mjs, because CourseEditorScene has no unit-test harness.
  - Passing the base without a resolve choice would make every later Save on that cell fail. The cheap fallback is to tell the user to reopen the editor, which already reaches draftBackupController.recoverRoom's conflict chooser.
  - Impact is medium (a subset of F058), not high.
  - The evidence line for the refresh after save is :2059, not :2058.
  - The course goal and setup save (expandedRoomEditorRepository.saveDraft at :1417 and :1457) has the same gap.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** PR #292 (four commits, after four review rounds). New `src/scenes/courseEditor/sliceEditConflict.ts`, which compares contents normalized with `cloneRoomSnapshot`, as the server does. `draftSession.ts` records each session copy's server base, and the room editor refreshes that copy after every accepted save. Other cells keep saving past a conflict. Cmd+S key-repeat is ignored and only one save runs at a time. Remaining: the Expanded Room goal/setup save (`expandedRoomEditorRepository.saveDraft`) sends no base, publish has no timeout, and pressing Play twice during an upload could start two play tests. `npm run check`: 629 files, 5,384 tests. [Receipt](wamp-round2-security-and-step1-2026-10-22.md).

### F378: Escape or P during a Room Rush throws the run away with no score, while the Stop button, phone Stop and gamepad save it

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F151

**Summary.** There are four ways to stop playing during a Room Rush, and they disagree. The on-screen Stop button, the phone Stop button and the controller's Select button end the Rush, show the result screen and save the score to the leaderboard, including the Weekly Rush. The keyboard's Escape and P keys quietly abandon the Rush, so the player gets no result screen and nothing is saved. Route all of them through the same 'end the Rush' command.

**Technical detail.**

Keyboard 'stop' (default P) is wired to `getActiveOverworldScene(game)?.returnToWorld()` (sceneCommands.ts:149-150). Escape calls host.returnToWorld() (inspectInput.ts:117-122). OverworldPlayScene.returnToWorld → flow.returnToWorld → resetPlaySession (flow.ts:271) → abandonRoomRushRun (sessionReset.ts:146-147) → roomRushMode.abandonActiveRun, which only marks the run 'abandoned' (roomRushMode.ts:93-95; roomRushRuns.ts:225-236) and never calls showResult.

The other inputs go through endRoomRushRun:
- Touch stop and gamepad Select: framePipeline.ts:249-252
- HUD Play/Stop button: playSelectedRoom → endRoomRushRun (OverworldPlayScene.ts:3951-3958)

end() completes the run and calls showResult (roomRushMode.ts:209-218), which opens the result dialog that alone submits the leaderboard entry. That submission rejects anything but 'completed'/'failed' (roomRushResultModal.ts:370-389). A signed-in player who presses Escape to finish a 5-minute Weekly Rush (startRule 'weekly', roomRushRuns.ts:132) loses the result. The bug predates this window, but the Oct 16 gamepad work (db01f9c8) made the mismatch obvious by routing the pad correctly.

Fix: add a single scene command, e.g. stopCurrentPlay(), that does `activeRoomRushRun ? endRoomRushRun() : returnToWorld()`, and call it from installGameplayShortcuts, inspectInput's Escape handler, framePipeline.dispatchCommands and playSelectedRoom. About 15 lines. Add a unit test that presses P/Escape with an active rush and asserts the result request fires.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/sceneCommands.ts:149-150 — keyboard stop shortcut calls returnToWorld()
- src/scenes/overworld/inspectInput.ts:117-122 — Escape calls returnToWorld()
- src/scenes/overworld/framePipeline.ts:249-252 — touch/gamepad stop calls endRoomRushRun() when a rush is active
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:3951-3958 — HUD playSelectedRoom ends the rush via endRoomRushRun()
- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:271 — returnToWorld runs resetPlaySession
- src/scenes/overworld/sessionReset.ts:146-147 — resetPlaySession abandons the rush
- src/scenes/overworld/roomRushMode.ts:93-95 — abandonActiveRun shows no result; end() at 209-218 does
- src/ui/setup/roomRushResultModal.ts:370-372 — leaderboard save only for completed/failed runs

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **confirmed.** The core claim holds. I'd lower the impact to medium, because a lost run can be replayed and the visible Stop, touch and gamepad paths all work. The fix should also cover a fifth stop path the reviewer missed: the HUD Room Rush button (sceneCommands.ts:233-234), which already ends the Rush correctly. The InspectInput host interface needs a new stopCurrentPlay method. The Controls label for P ('Return to browse', keyBindings.ts:6) could change to 'Stop' to match.

### F385: Pressing Escape to close the room-chat or comment box also kicks you out of the room and ends your run

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F168

**Summary.** If you open the in-room chat (T) or comment box (C) during a run, click back on the game to keep playing, and then press Escape to close the box, the game closes the box and also leaves the room. You lose the attempt, and a duel is cancelled. Since 19 October, clicking the game no longer closes the box, so this now happens in a common sequence. The fix is a single Escape handler that stops once the chat or comment box has used the key.

**Technical detail.**

OverworldPlayScene.setupGameplayKeys registers keyboard.on('keydown-ESC') (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1657-1664). It closes the comment or chat composer and `return`s. OverworldInspectInputController.initialize (called right after, OverworldPlayScene.ts:1391-1392) registers a second 'keydown-ESC' listener, handleReturnToWorldKeydown (inspectInput.ts:117-122). That listener calls host.returnToWorld() whenever mode === 'play' and no `.history-modal` is open. Phaser's KeyboardPlugin emits KEY_DOWN+'ESC' to every listener (node_modules/phaser/src/input/keyboard/KeyboardPlugin.js:797-801), and a `return` in the first listener does not stop the second. The composers are not `.history-modal` elements (roomChat.ts:368 'room-chat-composer', roomCommentsComposerController.ts:206 'room-comment-composer'), so hasBlockingModalOpen() is false.

While the input has focus this was safe: the input's own handler calls preventDefault (roomChat.ts:310-316; roomCommentsComposerController.ts:146-148), and KeyboardManager ignores defaultPrevented events. Commit 82defd8d (19 Oct) added a capture-phase canvas pointerdown that blurs whatever has focus (keyboardPassthrough.ts:19-23). Neither composer closes on blur: the only blur in roomChat.ts is inside closeComposer (line 261). Repro: in play mode press T, click the game canvas, move around, press Escape. The chat closes and returnToWorld → resetPlaySession abandons the goal, Expanded Room or Rush run and clears PvP (OverworldPlayScene.ts:4739-4750; flow.ts:271). This is the same class of bug F168 fixed for dialogs, and its fix did not cover the composers.

Fix (about 10 lines): merge the two ESC listeners into one ordered handler (comment composer → chat composer → modal check → returnToWorld), or have handleReturnToWorldKeydown return early when roomChatController.isComposerOpen() or the comments composer is open. Add a vitest that opens the composer, blurs it, emits ESC, and asserts returnToWorld is not called.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:1657-1664 — first ESC listener closes the comment/chat composer and returns
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:1391-1392 — setupGameplayKeys then inspectInputController.initialize register two ESC listeners on the same keyboard
- src/scenes/overworld/inspectInput.ts:117-122 — second ESC listener calls returnToWorld when mode==='play' and no .history-modal is open
- node_modules/phaser/src/input/keyboard/KeyboardPlugin.js:797-801 — KEY_DOWN+code is emitted to all listeners
- src/ui/setup/keyboardPassthrough.ts:19-23 — canvas pointerdown now blurs the focused element (added 82defd8d, Oct 19)
- src/scenes/overworld/roomChat.ts:252-262 — composer only blurs inside closeComposer; no blur→close path
- src/scenes/overworld/roomChat.ts:368 — composer root is 'room-chat-composer', not a .history-modal

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect holds as described. Two corrections:
  1. Clicking the game never closed the box. Before 82defd8d, Phaser's preventDefault on canvas mousedown left the box focused and the game keys off. Since 82defd8d, a canvas click takes focus from the box and hands the keys back to the game while the box stays open. That is why the open-composer-plus-Escape state is now easy to reach.
  2. The fix must be a single ordered ESC handler: comment composer, then chat composer, then the .history-modal check, then returnToWorld. Alternatively, the first listener can record that it handled the event and the second can check that record. An isComposerOpen() early return inside handleReturnToWorldKeydown would not work: the earlier-registered listener (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1391 runs before 1392) has already closed the composer when it runs.
  The test should emit ESC through the scene keyboard with both listeners registered. Impact is medium: desktop keyboard players only, and only with a composer open.
- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** Real and still open on main. The only working fix is one ordered Escape handler: comment composer, then chat composer, then modal check, then returnToWorld. For example, remove the scene's keydown-ESC listener and have handleReturnToWorldKeydown call a host hook that closes the composers first and returns true if it closed one. Adding an isComposerOpen() check to handleReturnToWorldKeydown would not help: the scene listener runs first and has already closed the composer. Impact is medium, not high. It only affects signed-in desktop keyboard players who click the canvas while a composer is open, and the path existed before 82defd8d through HUD-button clicks. F168's fact-check, note (3), already flagged this gap, but F168's fix left it out.

### F383: Opening a room from Profile, My Rooms, Explore or a playlist mid-run leaves the old run half-alive

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F170

**Summary.** Players can now open the menu during a run (that is what the new pause is for). If they open My Rooms, a profile, a playlist or Explore and click a room, the game jumps to that room without properly ending the run they were in. After leaving an Expanded Room this way, the map still shows the run's timer and a 'Stop Expanded Room' button. The next click on Play for any Expanded Room only shuts down the stale run, so nothing starts. The jump should end the current run first, exactly like pressing Stop.

**Technical detail.**

selection.jumpToCoordinates (selection.ts:67-82) sets mode='browse', camera, coordinates and URL, then calls refreshAround. It never calls resetPlaySession or clearActivePvpMatch. Compare flow.returnToWorld (flow.ts:262-275), which resets the play session before setMode('browse'). The later browse branch of runtimeController.syncModeRuntime (runtimeController.ts:110-126) only destroys the player and calls clearCurrentGoalRun (goalRunController.clearCurrentRun, not abandon). activeCourseRun is cleared only by sessionReset.ts:160/184, OverworldPlayScene.ts:1632 and :4034, so it survives.

Results:
- The HUD keeps the Expanded Room goal panel and 'Stop Expanded Room' (hudViewModel.ts:494-496, 520, 572).
- The course's transient room overrides stay applied in browse.
- A ranked single-room attempt is dropped without an abandon event.
- An active PvP match is not cleared.
- The next Play on any Expanded Room goes playSelectedRoom → playSelectedCourse, which hits `if (getActiveCourseRun()) { returnToWorld(); return; }` (flow.ts:441-445), so the first click does nothing visible.

Reachable mid-run because the menu works in any scene (gameMenu.ts:4, 38-39: My Rooms/Profile). Profile room cards call close()+jumpToCoordinates (profileModal.ts:1299-1302), and the new collection shelf (Oct 21) does jump then playSelectedRoom (profileCollection.ts:133-141). Explore cards (exploreModal.ts:663-666, 671-673) and playlist items (playlistModal.ts:213) do the same.

Fix: in OverworldPlayScene.jumpToCoordinates, `if (this.mode === 'play') this.returnToWorld()` (or call resetPlaySession + clearActivePvpMatch) before delegating. Pass a flag to skip the editor-playtest wake. About 5 lines plus a test that starts a course run, jumps, and asserts activeCourseRun === null.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/selection.ts:67-82 — jumpToCoordinates flips mode to browse without resetPlaySession
- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:262-275 — returnToWorld resets the session before switching mode
- src/scenes/overworld/runtimeController.ts:110-126 — browse sync only destroys the player and clears the goal run
- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:441-445 — playSelectedCourse just calls returnToWorld when a stale course run exists
- src/scenes/overworld/hudViewModel.ts:494-496 — Play button still reads 'Stop Expanded Room' while activeCourseRun is set
- src/ui/setup/gameMenu.ts:38-39 — My Rooms/Profile open from the menu in any scene
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:1299-1302 — room card closes profile and jumps
- src/ui/setup/profileCollection.ts:133-141 — new collection 'Play Room' jumps then playSelectedRoom
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:663-666 — Explore card closes and jumps

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real bug, but the symptoms need rewriting. Jumping mid-run (Profile, My Rooms, the collection shelf, Explore, a playlist card, or "Next" in a Play All / playlist sequence) does not end the run. activeCourseRun stays set (it also stays set after a completed run), and so do the course room overrides, any PvP match and the editor-playtest return targets. A ranked single-room run is dropped without its abandon submission or challenge reset.
  
  The map does NOT show the old timer or 'Stop Expanded Room', because hudState.ts:264-267 hides runs outside play mode. Instead, the next 'Play Expanded Room' click, or the collection shelf's auto-play of an expanded-room member, snaps the camera back to the stale run's start room and starts nothing. If a playtest return target was left over, it can wake the editor. Consecutive expanded rooms in a room sequence break the same way.
  
  Fix: in OverworldPlayScene.jumpToCoordinates, when mode === 'play', clear the PvP match and both return targets, then call resetPlaySession and clearTouchGestureState before delegating. Calling returnToWorld directly would trigger the editor wake. Add tests for a stale course run after jump and for sequence Next across two expanded rooms.

### F375: After a test run, Stop/Escape returns to the room editor with the room's music still playing, and a later test can start silent

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a builder tests their room and presses Stop (or Escape) to go back to the editor, the room's music keeps looping inside the editor while the editor's music button still shows ▶ (stopped). If the builder then stops it from the editor, the next test of the same room can start with no music, because the game still thinks it is playing. The Expanded Room editor already handles this correctly; the ordinary room editor does not. Builders test constantly, so this is one of the most-heard audio bugs.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: OverworldFlowController.returnToWorld sets mode 'browse' and then queues wake('EditorScene') + sleep() (flow.ts:261-317). Room music is only ever stopped from the per-frame pipeline (framePipeline.ts:105-109 → OverworldRoomMusicPlaybackController.sync, roomMusicPlaybackController.ts:86-98). Phaser's ScenePlugin.sleep only queues the op (ScenePlugin.js:589-596) and SceneManager.update runs processQueue() before stepping any scene (SceneManager.js:555-568), so when Stop comes from a DOM handler (sceneCommands.ts:149-150 gameplay shortcut, 155-159 HUD play/stop button) the overworld never runs another update in 'browse' mode and never stops the music. The overworld's SLEEP listener only touches the performance advisor (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1417-1421). EditorScene.handleWake (EditorScene.ts:204-212) does not stop music either, whereas CourseEditorScene's wake goes through openFromData → musicWorkflow.resetForSceneOpen() (CourseEditorScene.ts:304-306, 1673-1678), which stops it. EditorScene.startPlayMode only stops the editor's own preview (EditorScene.ts:1878-1884). Second symptom: the overworld controller keeps lastMode='play' and lastPlayback (only cleared by reset() in create, OverworldPlayScene.ts:1357/1586), so on the next test of a room whose music key is unchanged, sync() returns early (roomMusicPlaybackController.ts:113-121) and never calls playArrangement — silent if the builder stopped the music in the meantime (e.g. ▶ then ⏹, which hits the 'already-playing' path and then stopArrangement). Fix (small): in the overworld SLEEP handler call roomMusicPlaybackController.reset() (stops with 0.08 s fade and clears lastPlayback); optionally mirror the course editor by stopping preview playback in EditorScene.handleWake. Add a unit test: sync(play) → simulate sleep → expect stopArrangement and a fresh playArrangement on the next play sync. Hands-on check: Test a music room, press Stop, listen in the editor.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:261-317 — returnToWorld sets mode 'browse' then wakes EditorScene and sleeps the overworld in the same call
- src/scenes/overworld/framePipeline.ts:105-109 — music sync only happens inside the overworld frame update
- src/scenes/overworld/roomMusicPlaybackController.ts:86-98 — non-play mode stops music only when sync() runs
- src/scenes/overworld/roomMusicPlaybackController.ts:113-121 — early return when identity/sourceRoom/musicKey match lastPlayback
- node_modules/phaser/src/scene/ScenePlugin.js:589-596 — sleep() queues the op for the next Scene Manager update
- node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js:555-568 — processQueue() runs before any scene steps
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:1417-1421 — SLEEP handler only resets performance-advisor state
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:204-212 — handleWake has no music stop
- src/scenes/CourseEditorScene.ts:1673-1678 — course editor wake path calls musicWorkflow.resetForSceneOpen()
- src/ui/setup/sceneCommands.ts:149-159 — Stop shortcut and HUD play/stop are DOM handlers

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** Two refinements, but the core claim stands. (1) The leak is unconditional. It is not limited to DOM-triggered Stop: touch and gamepad Stop run in the frame 'commands' phase after the music stage, so they also never get a 'browse' sync before the queued sleep. (2) The silent second test has a more common trigger than ▶ then ⏹. Pressing ▶ in the editor and then Test also causes it, because startPlayMode stops the preview while the overworld controller still believes the same key is playing.

### F380: Five dialogs moved into on-demand templates lost the keyboard-focus, stacked-dimming and game-key fixes (F175/F116 regressed)

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F175
- **Also covers:** Explore, Profile, Room History and Avatar menus lost their keyboard focus, dimming and key handling when they became load-on-demand

**Summary.** On 17 October, the Explore, Profile, Leaderboard, Room History and Choose Avatar dialogs became templates that are only added to the page on first use, to speed up startup. The code that moves keyboard focus into dialogs and back, dims stacked dialogs only once, and hands game keys to dialogs only watches dialogs that existed at startup, so it never sees these five. Keyboard users get no focus move or return in Explore, Profile, Room History and the avatar picker. A profile opened from the Leaderboard or Explore darkens the screen twice, which is the near-black stack F116 fixed.

**Technical detail.**

Commit eda0dcf9 (17 Oct) wrapped #room-history-modal, #leaderboard-modal, #explore-modal, #profile-modal and #avatar-picker-modal in `<template id="deferred-…">` (index.html:2367, 2478, 2803, 2844, 2969). LazyModal.ensure swaps them in on first open (lazyModal.ts:64-69). Three global installers call `doc.querySelectorAll('.history-modal')` once and observe only those elements: installModalStackBackdrops (modalState.ts:61-70, installed at main.ts:207), installDialogKeyboardSync (keyboardFocus.ts:131-135, main.ts:236) and installModalFocusManagement (modalState.ts:187-190, main.ts:237). Template content is not in the document then, so these modals' class/aria-hidden changes never trigger:
- The focus-into-dialog and return/blur-on-close logic (modalState.ts:131-150). Explore, Profile and History have no focus code of their own (no .focus( in exploreModal.ts/profileModal.ts/historyModal.ts; they use createModalLifecycle, which only toggles classes, modalLifecycle.ts:37-55). Only Leaderboard focuses itself (leaderboardModal.ts:310-314).
- data-modal-covered (modalState.ts:52-60). Profile over Leaderboard/Explore, or the avatar picker over Profile, stack two 80% backdrops.
- syncGameKeyboardFocus on open. In browse mode, '0' still refits the map behind Explore. In unpaused live modes (Weekly Rush, co-op, PvP) the gamepad still drives the player behind a Profile dialog, because canPlay reads the stale keyboard.enabled (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1407-1408).

The Tab trap still works because it queries live. gameplayPause.ts:75-88 already handles this correctly with a body childList observer. mannCool.ts:29-31 has the same static pattern but self-heals per message.

Fix: extract gameplayPause's addition watcher into one `watchModals(doc, onChange)` util and use it in the four installers (net about −10 lines). Add a vitest that installs the managers, then swaps in a deferred template and asserts focus moves in and data-modal-covered updates.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:2844 — <template id="deferred-profile-modal"> (also 2367, 2478, 2803, 2969)
- src/ui/setup/lazyModal.ts:64-69 — templates are swapped into the page only on first open
- src/ui/modalState.ts:187-190 — focus manager observes only .history-modal elements present at install
- src/ui/modalState.ts:66-70 — stack backdrop observer, same static list
- src/ui/keyboardFocus.ts:131-135 — dialog keyboard sync, same static list
- src/main.ts:207 — installModalStackBackdrops at boot; main.ts:236-237 keyboard sync and focus manager at boot
- src/ui/gameplayPause.ts:75-88 — pause code already watches body for inserted .history-modal (correct pattern)
- src/ui/setup/modalLifecycle.ts:37-55 — Explore/Profile/History show() only toggles classes, no focus
- src/ui/modalState.ts:61-69 — backdrop observer observes only .history-modal nodes present at install
- src/ui/modalState.ts:187-189 — focus-management observer, same one-time querySelectorAll
- src/ui/keyboardFocus.ts:132-134 — dialog keyboard sync, same one-time querySelectorAll
- src/main.ts:206-207 — escape guard/backdrops installed before setupUI; :236-237 keyboard sync and focus management installed at boot

### F388: Server logs are now sampled at 1%, so 99 of 100 error references and phone crash reports are thrown away

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and data integrity: API, storage and realtime)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F185

**Summary.** On Oct 18, to save money on the new multiplayer server, logging was turned down to 1% for the whole Worker, which also covers the game's API. When something breaks, players see 'Something went wrong. Reference: …', but 99 times out of 100 there is no log line for that reference. The same goes for the automatic crash reports from phones, which are only ever logged. This quietly undoes most of the error-visibility fix from the first checkup.

**Technical detail.**

wrangler.jsonc:20-22 sets observability.logs.head_sampling_rate to 0.01. Commit 5d138368 changed it from 1 (git show). The release note says this was deliberate and Worker-wide: docs/review/wamp-cloudflare-presence-2026-10-18.md:10, 'including the API because sampling is Worker-wide'. Head sampling drops every console line of an unsampled invocation. Affected: (a) the `api_error` line, the only record behind the 'Reference: <cf-ray>' players see (src/cloudflare/worker/ops/errors.ts:11-27); (b) the client crash beacon, which is never stored ('Logged as … for Workers Logs; nothing is stored', ops/errors.ts:44-45, 66-80); (c) failures of after-response work such as `run-rewards-failed` (runs/deferredRewards.ts:20-26) and cron outcomes (src/cloudflare/worker.ts:343-365). With crons firing 5 times an hour, about one cron run every 20 hours is logged. Fix options, cheapest first: (1) Move PresenceDurableObject into its own Worker script (a wrangler.presence.jsonc with a `script_name` DO binding). Keep 1% there and put the API back at 1.0, its pre-Oct-18 setting. (2) If the cost needs one script, send api_error and client_error to an unsampled sink: a Workers Analytics Engine dataset, or a bounded D1 `server_errors` ring that the hourly prune trims. The F185 reference id then always resolves. Add a test asserting apiErrorResponse writes to the sink.

**Evidence.**

- wrangler.jsonc:20-22 — logs.head_sampling_rate: 0.01
- docs/review/wamp-cloudflare-presence-2026-10-18.md:10 — sampling at 1% 'including the API because sampling is Worker-wide'
- src/cloudflare/worker/ops/errors.ts:17-25 — 500s are only a console.error line; players are given a Reference id
- src/cloudflare/worker/ops/errors.ts:44-45 — client error beacons: 'nothing is stored'
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/deferredRewards.ts:20-26 — reward failures are only logged

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect is real exactly as described: 1% Worker-wide log sampling since 5d138368 means api_error references, client_error beacons, run-rewards-failed lines and cron result lines are recorded only about 1% of the time. Correct the fix and effort. The cheapest fix is a config change, not a script split. In wrangler.jsonc, set observability.logs.invocation_logs: false (supported by the installed wrangler schema) and put logs.head_sampling_rate back to 1. The Worker emits only about 9 console.log calls, and the presence DO logs only on failure, so the volume the 1% was meant to cut is almost all automatic invocation logs from per-message DO invocations. Check the cost against the post-Dec-1 log pricing. Moving PresenceDurableObject to its own script (needs a DO delete/transfer migration) or adding an Analytics Engine/D1 error sink are fallbacks only if that is not enough. Scope: frequent client errors still surface statistically at 1%, and uncaught cron exceptions still show in the dashboard's cron event history. The real loss is rare errors, lookups by player reference ID (about 1% resolvable), cron result details and reward-failure lines.
- **confirmed.** The core claim stands. Two corrections:
  
  1. **Cheapest fix.** It is a config change, not splitting out the Durable Object or adding a new sink. Set `observability.logs.invocation_logs: false` in wrangler.jsonc, which the installed wrangler schema supports, and restore `head_sampling_rate: 1`. The cost came from automatic per-invocation logs on presence WebSocket messages and alarms, and the presence code itself writes almost nothing to the console. The API only writes error lines and about 7 cron or prune lines. Then measure real log ingestion, which the Oct 18 note says was never done. Splitting the DO into its own script, or adding an Analytics Engine or D1 sink, is the fallback if that is not enough.
  
  2. **Cron outcomes.** They are not fully invisible. The world-map-health and ghost-cost crons still send alert emails, and Cloudflare's unsampled invocation metrics still count errors. What is lost is the content: route, message, stack, the client reports, and the line behind each Reference id.
  
  Impact is on operator visibility, not on what players see.
- **partially confirmed.** The regression is real and the evidence and numbers are correct. What needs correcting is the scope and the fix.
  
  Scope:
  - What is lost is after-the-fact lookup of an individual player's Reference, and rare client errors and after-response failures.
  - Widespread crashes still appear at 1%, live `wrangler tail` should still work, and cron email alerts are unaffected.
  - The beacon covers every browser, not just phones.
  
  Fix: the DO-split option is the most expensive one, not the cheapest. It is medium effort: a DO class migration in production and safety, duplicated secrets for the identity core and PARTYKIT_INTERNAL_TOKEN, and a new deploy step. Cheapest first:
  1. Write api_error and client_error to an unsampled Workers Analytics Engine dataset (or a bounded D1 ring trimmed by the hourly prune), with a test that apiErrorResponse writes to it. Small effort.
  2. Config only: set observability.logs.invocation_logs=false and restore head_sampling_rate to 1. The presence DO emits almost no console lines, so its log volume is per-invocation records. All explicit console lines (api_error, client_error, cron, run-rewards-failed) would come back at 100%. Per-request invocation records are lost, and 5% tracing stays. Re-run the cost projection first.
  3. Split the DO into its own script only if both of the above are rejected.
  
  Impact: medium. Effort: small.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** PR #290: `observability.logs.head_sampling_rate: 1`, `invocation_logs: false`. Log ingestion should be checked in the dashboard after a few days. [Receipt](wamp-round2-security-and-step1-2026-10-22.md).

### F376: An interrupted wallet approval never expires, so Collect & Lock or Add artwork can stay stuck for that room forever

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Collect & Lock: room collecting, wallet approvals and the crypto gate)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F239

**Summary.** When a builder starts Collect & Lock or Add artwork, the game saves a note on the device just before the wallet opens. If the wallet disconnects, times out or the phone closes the tab before a transaction ID comes back, nothing ever clears that note. From then on the button only says 'not confirmed yet, check again' and never opens the wallet again. The app also re-checks the chain three times every time the tab regains focus, with no end date. The server already knows when an approval has expired (it signs each one for 30 minutes), so the fix is to use that deadline to clear dead approvals and offer 'start over'.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: roomWalletActions.send() calls onBeforeSend → remember() (roomWalletActions.ts:213) which stores the PendingRoomWallet with txHash=null before the wallet request. The only removals are a 4001 rejection, WalletRequestNotSubmittedError, or a matching revert (215-219), plus completion in RoomWalletRecovery. A provider disconnect, a WalletConnect expiry that does not use code 4001, or the OS killing the tab all leave the entry. roomSession.mint.test.ts:224-231 locks in 'Provider disconnected before returning a hash' → entry kept. Recovery: with no hash, receipt is null, so the status is 'pending' (roomWalletRecovery.ts:83-91). mintRoom and refreshMintMetadata always resume any pending entry (roomWalletActions.ts:100-101, 147-148) → checkPending → 'Check again before starting another approval' (297-302). That is a permanent loop. createdAt is written (196) and validated (pendingRoomWallet.ts:39) but never read, so nothing expires. A hash that the wallet replaced through 'speed up/cancel' and that never mines behaves the same way. The artwork case is worse: the room is minted, but the stored hash never matches, so it stays 'pending' even after artwork is added from another device.

Two side effects. (a) getPending() without a kind ignores account and wallet (72-76). On a device where another account, or the same account before a wallet change, left an entry, recoverPending (92-96) runs on every editor open. RoomWalletRecovery throws AbortError on the identity mismatch (roomWalletRecovery.ts:56-58), and checkPending's catch then shows the 'Could not check the room approval' modal each time (303-307). (b) RoomWalletRecoveryLifecycle re-arms every 30 s on focus, visibilitychange and storage (roomWalletRecoveryLifecycle.ts:25-29; main/roomWalletRecovery.ts:20-23) and runs 3 attempts (45-48). Each attempt is a POST /ownership/refresh doing 3-5 Base RPC calls (service.ts:260-284). That is up to 15 RPC calls per tab focus per dead entry, forever.

The safe exit already exists. Prepare signs with deadline = now + 30 min (mint/routes.ts:56), and the contract rejects after it (RoomOwnershipToken.sol:102). An unhashed mint intent older than deadline + a few minutes, whose room the chain still shows as unminted, can never succeed. The same deadline also fixes a related hole: the cost dialog has no expiry (roomWalletConsent.ts:25-37), so a user who comes back after 30 min sends a transaction that reverts ('Mint authorization expired') and pays gas.

Fix plan (~60 lines + tests): (1) add deadline to RoomMintPrepareResponse (roomOwnership.ts:167-175) and PendingRoomWallet. (2) In RoomWalletRecovery.run, for kind=mint with no hash, or a hash with no receipt, past deadline+5 min and the summary unminted → remove the entry and return a new 'expired' status that re-enables Collect & Lock. (3) For artwork, which has no deadline, show 'Start a new artwork approval' after createdAt + 15 min without a hash. A late old request is harmless because require-fresh refresh re-reads tokenURI. (4) Filter getPending() by account in mintRoom/refreshMintMetadata/recoverPending. (5) Re-prepare if consent was accepted after deadline − 2 min. (6) Stop lifecycle auto-checks for expired entries.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:213 — onBeforeSend stores the intent with txHash null before the wallet popup
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:215-219 — only a 4001 rejection, WalletRequestNotSubmittedError or matching revert removes an entry
- src/mint/pendingRoomWallet.ts:39 — createdAt is validated; grep shows no reader anywhere, so entries never expire
- src/mint/roomWalletRecovery.ts:83-91 — no hash means receipt null → status 'pending' indefinitely
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:100-101 — Collect & Lock always resumes any pending entry instead of preparing a new approval
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:297-302 — the only outcome is 'not confirmed yet. Check again before starting another approval'
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:72-76 — getPending() without kind ignores userId/wallet, so another identity's entry blocks this room
- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:303-307 — identity-mismatch AbortError surfaces as a 'Could not check the room approval' modal on editor open
- src/mint/roomWalletRecoveryLifecycle.ts:25-29 — re-arms every 30 s on focus with 3 attempts (line 45) per entry, no end date
- src/cloudflare/worker/mint/routes.ts:56 — server authorization deadline is 30 minutes
- contracts/src/RoomOwnershipToken.sol:102 — mintRoom reverts after the deadline, so old unhashed mint intents are provably dead
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.mint.test.ts:224-231 — test asserts a disconnected, unhashed approval is kept and blocks a new send

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** Real regression from the F239 fix. On a device where a wallet request ended without a hash and without a definite 4001 or not-submitted error, the pending note is never cleared. Collect & Lock / Add artwork then stay blocked for that room in that browser until site data is cleared. Typical causes are a WalletConnect expiry (code 6), a WC offline error, or a reload or tab kill before the user decides. Each time that builder opens the room's editor, a "Room approval" modal appears (roomWalletActions.ts:301).
  
  Corrections:
  - Artwork entries stay stuck only when the canonical artwork differs, for example after a republish. Same-version artwork added elsewhere does complete them.
  - The 'pays gas after a stale consent' risk is mostly handled. The 'Mint authorization expired.' rejection is classified and cleared (walletSendGuard.ts:56).
  - Background polling is one 3-attempt burst per entry at most every 30 s, and only on focus. Cost is minor.
  - The mint fix can be client-only. createdAt is set after prepare, so createdAt + 30 min bounds the signed deadline. Expire hashless (or receipt-less) mint intents after about 35 min when the chain shows the room unminted.
  - Scope getPending() to the current account.
  - Artwork needs its own time-based 'start over' policy, accepting that a late old setRoomTokenURI could still land on-chain.
  - Reach is small: about 11 collectors ever, and the code has been live since Oct 20.
- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: an unhashed entry, or a hash that never gets a receipt, permanently blocks Collect & Lock or Add artwork for that room on that device. Five corrections:
  
  (1) The consent-expiry hole (fix step 5) is mostly handled already. If consent is accepted after the 30-minute deadline, the wallet's gas simulation fails with 'Mint authorization expired.' classifyWalletRpcRejection (walletSendGuard.ts:56, used at client.ts:343-345) turns that into WalletRequestNotSubmittedError('authorization-expired'). That error removes the entry and shows 'This collection approval expired. Try again to prepare a new approval' (roomWalletError.ts:14). Gas is paid only if the wallet skips simulation or the user overrides its warning. Step 5 is optional polish, not a hole.
  
  (2) A new API field isn't strictly needed. createdAt is stamped after consent, which comes after prepare, so createdAt + 30 min + a margin already falls after the server deadline, apart from client clock skew. Adding deadline to RoomMintPrepareResponse is cleaner but optional. Expiring early is low-risk because the contract allows only one token per room ('Room already minted.'). The worst case is a reverted second transaction, never a double mint.
  
  (3) 'A late old artwork request is harmless' overstates it. An older setRoomTokenURI that mines late would overwrite newer on-chain artwork. The game stays consistent because fresh refresh follows the chain, but the NFT would show the older art. The 'start a new artwork approval' offer should warn about this.
  
  (4) The polling cost is minor. Bursts are limited to one per entry per 30 s and only while visible with the matching account. Unhashed entries skip the receipt RPC. Each refresh costs 3 RPC calls for an unminted room and 5 for a minted one.
  
  (5) Impact is medium, not high. The failure is permanent and the only workaround is clearing site data, which also drops local drafts. But it only affects wallet holders on mobile wallet hops or non-4001 provider errors, and only 11 real NFTs exist.
  
  Effort stays medium. The change touches a new 'expired' status, the lifecycle, UI copy, the unit tests, and the 25-case × 4-profile recovery browser matrix.

### F382: Lost Songs start a new server session on every room entry; after about 32 rooms in 30 minutes a player can't collect songs

- **Area:** Bugs and data integrity: API, storage and realtime
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Each time a player walks into a room that hides a Lost Song they haven't found, the game opens a new 30-minute 'play session' on the server, even when re-entering a room they just left. The server allows only 32 open sessions per player and 5,000 for the whole game. An explorer who crosses 33 song rooms in half an hour sees 'Song progress is unavailable', and on a busy day everyone does. Reusing the open session for the same room fixes it.

**Technical detail.**

Client: LostSongPlayController.update() calls getProof for the current Lost Song room (src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:38-47). getProof caches only the most recent room (68). Leaving to a room without a song clears it (43), and every new context POSTs /api/lost-songs/play ('Starts early on entry', 71-84). Server: src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:88-98 inserts a session with a 30-minute expiry (90). The insert happens only if the identity has fewer than 32 unexpired, unfound sessions (94) and fewer than 5,000 are active worldwide (95). Otherwise it returns 429 'Too many active Lost Song play sessions' (98). The client maps that to 'Song progress is unavailable. Touch the song to retry' and retries every 5 s (lostSongs.ts:76-82). A find needs a valid session (routes.ts:106-110), so the song cannot be saved until old sessions expire, up to 30 minutes. Walking back and forth between two song rooms 33 times trips the per-player cap. The worldwide cap is shared fate: per-network limits are 120 plays a minute (routes.ts:31-36), so 2 networks × 120 × 30 min = 7,200, which is over 5,000. Two connections, or ordinary traffic of about 170 room entries a minute, lock every player out. Fix: before inserting, reuse the identity's existing unexpired, unfound session for the same (room_id, room_version, expanded_room_id), using index lost_song_session_identity, and return a fresh token for it. Keep the per-identity cap but drop the global COUNT(*) gate (or make it per network). Optionally shorten expiry to about 10 minutes. Add a test that enters the same room 40 times and gets one session back.

**Evidence.**
- src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:43 — leaving a song room drops the proof
- src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:68-72 — only the latest room is cached; a new /play session starts on entry
- src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:82 — a 429 surfaces as 'Song progress is unavailable'
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:90 — sessions last 30 minutes
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:94-95 — cap of 32 unfound per player and 5,000 worldwide
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:98 — returns 429 when the insert was skipped

**Fact-check (confirmed).**

Checked against main 2d540764. Every cited line is correct.

Client: OverworldLostSongController.update() (src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:38-47) sets proof = null whenever getContext() returns null (line 43). getProof (66-85) keeps only one proof, keyed by JSON.stringify([target, userId]) (67-68). Any new key, or a proof that was cleared, POSTs /api/lost-songs/play again (71). A failure sets retryAfter to now + 5 s and shows 'Song progress is unavailable. Touch the song to retry.' (79-82). After that, update() starts another /play every 5 s on its own.

getContext (src/scenes/overworld/lostSongContext.ts:16-29) returns null in a room without a lost_song object, and also whenever canPlay() is false. canPlay includes !gameFeelController.isDeathPending() (src/scenes/overworld/composition/player.ts:205). The death phase lasts 180 ms (gameFeel.ts:2), and update() runs from finalize() every frame with a 100 ms throttle (framePipeline.ts:296). So the 100 ms throttle will almost always land one tick inside the death window, and the proof is cleared on each death. The finding misses this amplifier. A new server session starts not only on each room re-entry but on each respawn in a song room. A player who dies 33 times in one hard, unfound song room within 30 minutes hits the cap without ever leaving the room.

Server: src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/routes.ts:89-98 always inserts a new row with a 30-minute expiry (line 90). The insert is gated on fewer than 32 unexpired, unfound rows for the identity (93-94) and fewer than 5,000 unexpired rows in total, found ones included (95). If either gate fails, the route returns 429 'Too many active Lost Song play sessions' (98). /find needs a valid unexpired session (106-109). There is no reuse path. The existing test routes.test.ts:109 proves the cap: it plays the same target 32 times and the 33rd play gets 429.

Global cap: guestRunIdentity (src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/identity.ts:10-16) accepts any client-chosen X-Guest-User-Id and recovery token. That means the per-identity cap of 32 does nothing against an attacker. The only real limit is 120 plays per minute per network, where a network is an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64 (routes.ts:34, rateLimit.ts:22-34). 120 × 30 = 3,600 sessions per network, so two IPs push past 5,000 and lock out every player's Lost Song saving for up to 30 minutes. The trusted-origin check is no barrier to a non-browser client. Organic traffic reaching 5,000 ('on a busy day everyone does') is overstated for current traffic. The deliberate cheap DoS is real.

Not covered by any prior item: only F144 (the feature itself, DONE) mentions Lost Songs, and nothing in prior_findings.json addresses session caps.

Fix notes:
- Reusing a session is compatible with assertLostSongPickupProof (validation.ts:46-52), since an older started_at only loosens the timing bound.
- Only token_hash is stored, so a reuse must UPDATE token_hash with a new token (and ideally started_at). That matches the finding's 'fresh token'.
- The client should also keep the proof through death-pending, or cache proofs per room key in a Map, so respawns and re-entries stop calling /play.
- The global COUNT(*) gate should become per-network or be removed.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** [PR #294](https://github.com/songadaymann/wamp/pull/294), API Worker `073f68a2` (no migration). Two tabs in the same song room each refresh the session's token, so one may need a second touch. [Receipt](wamp-round2-security-and-step1-2026-10-22.md).

### F390: The admin 'clear room' tool fails on every claimed room since Worlds launched, and no builder account can be deleted

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Classroom accounts and Worlds: routes added since the F209 fix)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F205

**Summary.** The Worlds launch added a database rule that a room's ownership record can never be deleted. Deleting a room tries to delete that record automatically, so the whole delete is rolled back. Since September 4 the admin endpoint for removing a bad room has been failing for every room anyone has claimed. The same rule also blocks deleting any builder's account, which teachers will need for end-of-year cleanup (F212). A small database change lets the automatic delete through while still blocking direct edits.

**Technical detail.**

Migration 0045_worlds_pilot.sql:83-94 creates world_room_claims with `room_id REFERENCES rooms ON DELETE CASCADE` and `first_builder_user_id REFERENCES users ON DELETE SET NULL`. The backfill at 96-99 inserted a claim row for every room that was claimed or published. Every new claim adds another row (worlds/roomMutationIntegration.ts:59-66, 113-121). Triggers at 209-219 abort any DELETE on the table and any UPDATE of first_builder_user_id. D1 enforces foreign keys, and the repo's own tests switch PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON to match (worlds/migration.test.ts:128).

handleAdminRoomClear (admin/routes.ts:263) batches DELETE FROM rooms (line 330, run at 361). The cascade fires the trigger and the whole batch rolls back with a 500.

Reproduced: all 68 migrations replayed into node:sqlite with foreign keys on, one claimed room inserted, then the four DELETEs from the handler. Result: "ABORT World room provenance is permanent", and the room is still present. DELETE FROM users for that builder fails with "World room provenance is immutable" (the SET NULL action hits the update trigger).

The existing test admin/roomClear.test.ts:33-39 builds its own 5-table schema without world_room_claims, so it passes.

Fix:
1. Add migration 0069 that recreates prevent_world_room_provenance_delete with `WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rooms WHERE id = OLD.room_id)`. Verified in node:sqlite: a direct DELETE still aborts and the cascade from DELETE FROM rooms succeeds.
2. Add a similar parent-gone guard to the update trigger for the first_builder_user_id SET NULL case, and test it.
3. Switch roomClear.test.ts to the replay-all-migrations fixture already used in guestRoomDrafts/claims.test.ts:65 and runs/finishDeferral.test.ts:41.

**Evidence.**

- migrations/0045_worlds_pilot.sql:91-93 — claims cascade on room delete and SET NULL on user delete
- migrations/0045_worlds_pilot.sql:96-99 — backfills a claim row for every claimed or published room
- migrations/0045_worlds_pilot.sql:209-219 — triggers abort any delete and any update of first_builder_user_id
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/routes.ts:326-331 — clear batch includes DELETE FROM rooms
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/routes.ts:361 — the batch is atomic, so the whole clear rolls back
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/roomClear.test.ts:33-39 — test schema omits world_room_claims and triggers
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRoomDrafts/claims.test.ts:65 — existing replay-all-migrations test pattern

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** 1. **Account deletion is a future blocker, not a current failure.** The app has no account-deletion code. The only `DELETE FROM users` statements are in the test-reset route and the rollout script. Deleting a user is also blocked by other foreign keys with no ON DELETE action, or with RESTRICT:
     - room_comments (0033:21-22)
     - guestbook (0031:13-14)
     - guest_room_drafts (0037:24-25)
     - guest_draft_claims (0053:4)
     - Worlds owner and submitter keys (0045:47, 117, 136, 170)
     - chat_moderation (0013:12, 23)
  
     Fixing the update trigger alone will not make "delete a builder" work for F212.
  2. **The fix reverses a deliberate design choice.** Provenance is permanent on purpose. The October 3 delivery hit this constraint and chose not to bypass it: it reset the room to a blank, unclaimed snapshot and retired the account, "permanent first-builder provenance is preserved" (checkup-delivery-2026-10-03.md:642). The proposed trigger change would delete provenance whenever a room is deleted. A less invasive fix keeps the triggers and makes admin clear reset the room row with an UPDATE (blank draft, published_json NULL, claimer cleared) instead of a DELETE. Which way to go is Jonathan's call.
  3. **Numbering and fixtures.** Migration 0069 is already taken on current main (0069 through 0073 exist), so the next one is 0074. There are 71 migration files at 2d540764, not 68. For the test fixture, use claims.test.ts:65, which turns on PRAGMA foreign_keys. finishDeferral.test.ts:41 does not.
  4. **Severity.** This is an admin-only moderation tool, and the room restore endpoint is still available. Impact is medium rather than high.
- **partially confirmed.** For every room that has been claimed or published since Sept 4 (which is effectively every room), the admin clear endpoint returns a 500 and the delete rolls back. That includes the busy rooms the F205 part fix was meant to handle; its test used a schema that doesn't match production. This is still true on origin/main 80151ad1.
  
  Impact is medium, not high. The endpoint is an admin tool with no UI caller and is rarely used, and unpublish still works for hiding a bad room.
  
  The account-deletion part is not a current bug. No production path deletes users, the Oct 4 cleanup chose to retire accounts on purpose, and many other RESTRICT/NO ACTION foreign keys (worlds owner, publication and name requests, comments, guestbook, guest draft claims, chat admins and bans) would block deletion anyway. That belongs in F212's design.
  
  Better fix: have the clear reset the room row and keep its claim, or let the cascade through only for wamp-prime claims, so numbered Worlds keep their provenance. Use migration 0072 or higher, and switch roomClear.test.ts to replaying the real migrations.
- **partially confirmed.** Confirmed: admin room clear returns 500 and rolls back for any room that has a world_room_claims row. That includes every room claimed or published before 0045 (backfill) and every claim since, because WORLDS_ENABLED=1. The same failure hits the ENABLE_TEST_RESET reset route and the scripts/remote_rollout_check.mjs cleanup. The F205 part-fix in PR #174 was tested only on a hand-built schema, so 'works on rooms with more than 100 runs' does not hold for claimed rooms.
  
  Fix: add a new migration (next free number, likely after 0071, not 0069) that recreates prevent_world_room_provenance_delete with WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rooms WHERE id = OLD.room_id). Verified in node:sqlite: a direct delete still aborts, the cascade succeeds, and the coordinate can be claimed again. Also switch roomClear.test.ts to the replay-all-migrations fixture with a claimed room.
  
  Drop or downgrade the account-deletion half. No account-deletion path exists, and many other RESTRICT and NO ACTION foreign keys also block DELETE FROM users: worlds.owner, world_publication_requests.submitted_by, world_name_requests, world_ownership_events, chat_admins and chat_bans, room_comments, guestbook_entries, guest_room_drafts and guest_room_draft_claims. Relaxing the update trigger alone does not enable deletion; that belongs in F212's design.
  
  Impact is medium, not high: the endpoint is admin API-only with no UI, and restore or admin edit are workarounds.

### F377: Changing your display name leaves the old name on Expanded Room and Course leaderboards, comments and Explore cards

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and data integrity: API, storage and realtime)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** Renamed players keep their old name on Expanded Room leaderboards and Explore builder credits

**Summary.** When a player renames themselves, the server updates their name in nine places but misses several others that are shown publicly. Expanded Room and Course leaderboards, room comments, Expanded Room credits and Explore builder names keep the old name for good. That's confusing, and it also means a moderator-forced rename of an offensive name doesn't fully take effect.

**Technical detail.**

updateUserProfile (src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:417-479) batches name updates for users, chat_messages, room_runs, room_rush_runs, pvp_match_players, user_stats, rooms (claimer and last publisher) and room_versions. Denormalized name columns that are displayed but never updated: expanded_room_runs.user_display_name (migrations/0037:77; shown by src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/leaderboards.ts:38,166), course_runs.user_display_name (migrations/0010:65; courses/leaderboards.ts:39,163), room_comments.author_display_name (roomComments/store.ts:135,187), expanded_rooms.owner_display_name (expandedRooms/store.ts:417,462), and playable_content_index.builder_display_name, which drives Explore and Room of the Day cards (playableContentIndex/discovery.ts:76) and refreshes only when content changes. That is at least 5 public surfaces, plus expanded_room_versions and course_versions publisher names (0037:36, 0010:27). Fix: append matching UPDATE ... WHERE user_id/owner_user_id/author_user_id = ? statements to the same batch, about 8 statements. Confirm each table has an index on the user column, or add one in a migration so the rename doesn't scan. Longer term, have leaderboard reads JOIN users for the name, as the global board effectively does through user_stats.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:417-479 — the rename updates 9 tables only
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/leaderboards.ts:38,166 — Expanded Room boards show the stored run name
- src/cloudflare/worker/courses/leaderboards.ts:39,163 — Course boards show the stored run name
- src/cloudflare/worker/roomComments/store.ts:135,187 — comments show the stored author name
- src/cloudflare/worker/playableContentIndex/discovery.ts:76 — Explore shows index_row.builder_display_name
- src/cloudflare/worker/auth/store.ts:418 — rename batch: chat_messages, room_runs, room_rush_runs, pvp_match_players, user_stats, rooms, room_versions only
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts:204 — run row stores the display name at run start
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/leaderboards.ts:165 — leaderboard entry uses the stored row.user_display_name
- src/cloudflare/worker/courses/store.ts:331 — owner display name never refreshed: existing.ownerDisplayName ?? actor.displayName
- src/cloudflare/worker/playableContentIndex/store.ts:212 — Explore index takes builder name from expanded.owner_display_name
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/difficulty.ts:379 — discovery shows expandedRoom.ownerDisplayName as the builder

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The bug is real, with corrections:
  - Moderator-forced renames don't exist, so drop that claim. The impact is player-initiated renames, including ones away from offensive names.
  - Standalone-room Explore cards only lag until the next index refresh (a rating or republish). Expanded Room builder credits stay stale permanently, because courses/store.ts keeps existing.ownerDisplayName even on republish.
  - Add the missed snapshot tables daily_rooms.builder_display_name and build_prompt_entries.builder_display_name.
  - The needed indexes already exist, so no migration is required.
  
  Fix: append UPDATEs to the existing rename batch for these columns, all keyed on indexed user columns:
  - expanded_room_runs.user_display_name and course_runs.user_display_name (expanded runs are written to both tables)
  - room_comments.author_display_name and room_comments.builder_display_name
  - expanded_rooms.owner_display_name and courses.owner_display_name
  - expanded_room_versions and course_versions published_by_display_name
  - playable_content_index.builder_display_name WHERE builder_user_id=?
  - optionally daily_rooms and build_prompt_entries
  
  Use the same principal_type guards as the rooms updates, and add a test asserting each board shows the new name after a rename.

### F381: In approval-only Worlds, builders never learn whether their room was approved, rejected, or needs resubmitting

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for builders, Worlds, Jams and schools)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** When a World requires approval, pressing Publish only flashes "Draft saved and submitted for World approval". After that the builder hears nothing: no email, no inbox entry, and no screen showing the request. The reviewer's rejection reason is saved, but only reviewers can read it. If the builder keeps tweaking the room, the request quietly goes stale and the reviewer gets an error when trying to approve. Builders should be told the result and see Waiting / Approved / Needs changes (with the reason) in the editor.

**Technical detail.**

Flow: roomRepository.ts:760-775 catches the 403, saves the draft, POSTs publication-requests, then throws a 409 RoomApiError whose message the editor logs as an error and shows as transient status text (roomSession.ts:811-813). Only reviewers can list requests: publication.ts:28-42 requires canReviewPublications, and the client fetches them only for reviewers (ui/worlds/controller.ts:156). Any later draft save changes draft.updatedAt, so resolve marks the request stale and throws 409 to the reviewer (publication.ts:123-130). Resubmitting stales older requests (publication.ts:72-74). Approve and reject only write world_activity_events (publication.ts:131-200), and the PATCH route sends nothing to the submitter (routes.ts:207-256). The only World emails go to managers (notifications.ts:52-75, called at routes.ts:129 and 196). Approving a join request is also silent (routes.ts:145-159). WorldPublicationRequest.rejectionReason (worlds/model.ts:83-96) has no non-reviewer reader. This loop matters most for the classroom use the Worlds PRD points toward.

Plan, no schema change for steps 1-3. (1) Add the viewer's latest request per room to WorldDetail, or add GET publication-requests?mine=1 filtered by submitted_by_user_id. (2) In the editor, when getActiveWorldId() is set, show a status chip (Waiting for review / Approved vN / Needs changes: reason / Out of date: Resubmit), and warn once that editing withdraws the submission. (3) On a decision, send a sendWorldPublicationDecisionEmail through the existing sendWorldEmail helper, plus a membership-approved email. (4) Optional: a builder_activity entry (see the featured-moments finding for the kind migration).

**Evidence.**

- src/persistence/roomRepository.ts:775 — submission surfaces only as a thrown 'Draft saved and submitted for World approval.'
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:811 — logged as 'Failed to publish room' and shown as status text
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/publication.ts:28-42 — listing requires canReviewPublications
- src/ui/worlds/controller.ts:156 — requests are fetched only for reviewers
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/publication.ts:123-130 — any draft change after submission marks the request stale
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/publication.ts:131-200 — approve/reject write only world_activity_events
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/routes.ts:207-256 — decision route sends no notification to the submitter
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/notifications.ts:52-75 — emails go only to World managers
- src/worlds/model.ts:83-96 — rejectionReason is stored on the request

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: builders get no notification and no screen showing the request, and the rejection reason is visible only to reviewers. But editing after a submission is not quiet. roomRepository.publish saves the draft and then throws, so the editor keeps its old serverDraftUpdatedAt. The builder's next autosave, manual save or Publish press then gets a 409 edit conflict and a false 'This Room Changed Somewhere Else' dialog. Choosing Keep Mine overwrites the draft and stales the pending request. The fix should therefore also return or sync the saved draft record in the approval path (for example a typed 'submitted' result instead of a thrown 409 RoomApiError, plus syncRoomMetadata(saved)), and show the submission as a success state rather than a console.error. Size: steps 1-3 (a viewer request listing, an editor status chip, decision and membership emails) are closer to medium than small. Impact is limited to approval_required Worlds, which are still in pilot.
- **partially confirmed.** Real, but the impact is medium, not high. It only reaches active non-manager members of approval-required numbered Worlds in the admin-granted pilot. Prime is members_publish.
  
  The mechanism also needs correcting. After a submission, RoomRepository.publish() throws away the saved draft record, so roomSession's serverDraftUpdatedAt stays stale and the room stays dirty. The builder's next autosave, or a second Publish press to resubmit, then fails with ROOM_EDIT_CONFLICT and shows a false "This Room Changed Somewhere Else" modal. Choosing Keep Mine silently stales the request. The request does not go stale quietly.
  
  Fix this first, and it is small. Return a typed "submitted" result carrying the saved record, or sync serverDraftUpdatedAt and clear the dirty flag before reporting the submission, and don't log it as "Failed to publish room".
  
  Then:
  - Add a viewer-scoped request status: a mine=1 filter on submitted_by_user_id, or the viewer's latest request per room on WorldDetail.
  - Show an editor chip (Waiting / Approved vN / Needs changes: reason / Out of date: Resubmit) and warn once that editing withdraws the submission.
  - Add submitter emails for decisions and member approval through sendWorldEmail.
  
  The full plan is medium effort.
- **partially confirmed.** The builder-feedback gap is real as described, with two changes.
  
  (a) Rejection reasons never exist in practice. The reviewer's Reject button sends null (controller.ts:268-270), and the queue shows only pending requests. "Needs changes: reason" therefore also needs a reason input on the reviewer's Reject action.
  
  (b) Add the bug the finding missed. roomRepository.publish throws away the record from the draft PUT, so roomSession never updates serverDraftUpdatedAt (only syncRoomMetadata sets it, roomSession.ts:1388) and the room stays dirty. The builder's next save after submitting hits ROOM_EDIT_CONFLICT and shows the "This Room Changed Somewhere Else" modal. Choosing Keep Mine silently stales the submission. Fix: return the saved record with a pending-approval flag (or a typed result) instead of a bare 409. Then syncRoomMetadata, setRoomDirty(false), and show a non-error "Submitted for review" status instead of console.error.
  
  Effort is medium, not small. It covers a viewer-request endpoint or WorldDetail field, the editor chip, the reviewer reason input, decision and membership emails through sendWorldEmail, the session sync, and tests. Impact is medium: the pilot is small, but approval is the default policy for every activated World.

### F391: Wamp-O-Gram fails with 'Request body is too large' for rooms that use about six custom sprites

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Small untested features: Wamp-O-Gram, Playlists, Guestbook, Collections)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Builders who decorate with their own pixel art can't send their room as a Wamp-O-Gram. Every custom sprite is copied into the request, and the server rejects anything over 64 KB, while normal room saves allow 2 MB. The builder fills in the whole form and only then gets a technical error.

**Technical detail.**

The POST body cap is 65,536 bytes (src/cloudflare/worker/wampOGram/routes.ts:31). Room snapshot saves allow 2 MB (core/http.ts:21). The snapshot inlines each custom sprite's pixel array (CustomSpriteDefinition.pixels; roomModel.ts:789) and each custom tile's pixels (customTiles/model.ts:18-26).

I measured with tsx: an empty default room is 8,853 bytes, a fully tiled room 14,133 bytes, and each 32x32 sprite adds about 8.7 KB (3 sprites gave a 34,989-byte request). So about 6 sprites in a busy room, or fewer with custom tiles and composed music, crosses the cap. The library allows 64 sprites (customSprites/model.ts:2). The error surfaces as the raw 413 sentence 'Request body is too large.' (core/http.ts:164-166).

Fix: building the snapshot on the server from roomId (see the guardrail finding) removes the upload entirely. As a stopgap, raise the cap to MAX_ROOM_SNAPSHOT_BODY_BYTES, and have the modal measure JSON.stringify(snapshot).length so it can explain the limit before the user fills in the form.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/wampOGram/routes.ts:31 — maxBytes 65_536
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/http.ts:21 — room snapshots allow 2 MB
- src/cloudflare/worker/core/http.ts:164-166 — 413 'Request body is too large.'
- src/customSprites/model.ts:2 — sprite library up to 64
- src/customTiles/model.ts:18-26 — custom tiles also inline pixel arrays

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F387: Safety preview deploys still send multiplayer to the retired PartyKit server, not the safety Worker

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Dead code: Worker, scripts, configs and docs)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Also covers:** Safety previews still run multiplayer on the old PartyKit host, not the Durable Object production uses

**Summary.** Since Oct 18, live multiplayer runs inside the main Cloudflare Worker. The script that builds safety previews still bakes the old PartyKit address into the game and redeploys the old PartyKit project. Safety previews therefore test the old multiplayer server, not the one players use, and they will lose multiplayer once PartyKit's hosted service shuts down. This is a few-line fix in the script, plus a production check that would catch the same mistake on the live site.

**Technical detail.**

Commit 5d138368 (2026-10-18) switched production presence to the PresenceDurableObject: wrangler.jsonc:35 sets PARTYKIT_HOST 'api.wamp.land', and the safety env at wrangler.jsonc:92 sets it to the safety Worker. scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs was never updated. Lines 8-10 still default SAFETY_PARTYKIT_HOST to 'everybodys-platformer-presence-safety.songadaymann.partykit.dev'. Line 43 bakes that value into the build as VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST. Lines 94-95 run `npm run presence:deploy:safety`, which is `partykit deploy --config partykit.safety.json` (package.json:124). A baked host beats the Worker's runtime host (src/auth/runtimeConfig.ts:45, `bundledHost || runtimePartykitHost`). So previews connect to hosted PartyKit, and the Oct 18 Durable Object adapter is never exercised there: hibernation, alarms, and the PvP checkpoints in src/cloudflare/presence/durableObject.ts. docs/development/safety-backend-foundation.md:21,41,48-67 still tells people to set up that PartyKit project. Fix: delete DEFAULT_SAFETY_PARTYKIT_HOST and leave VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST unset so /api/auth/session supplies the safety Worker host. Remove the presence deploy step and the --skip-presence flag, then delete partykit.safety.json and the npm script. About 20 lines. Same risk in production: smoke_prod.mjs:84-95 computes mainBundleContainsPartyKitHost but never asserts on it. Add `assert(!mainBundleText.includes('partykit.dev'))` so a stale VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST in the Pages dashboard can't silently send live players to the old server. Only you can check the Pages env vars.

**Evidence.**

- scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs:8-10 — default safety host is 'everybodys-platformer-presence-safety.songadaymann.partykit.dev'
- scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs:43 — VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST baked into the preview build
- scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs:94-95 — runs presence:deploy:safety (partykit deploy) on every safety deploy
