- wrangler.jsonc:92 — safety PARTYKIT_HOST is now 'everybodys-platformer-safety.novox-robot.workers.dev' (changed in 5d138368)
- src/auth/runtimeConfig.ts:45 — `const host = bundledHost || runtimePartykitHost;` so the baked host wins
- scripts/smoke_prod.mjs:95 — mainBundleContainsPartyKitHost is computed but never asserted
- docs/development/safety-backend-foundation.md:48 — '## PartyKit Safety Project' still documents the retired setup
- scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs:10 — safety client presence host defaults to a partykit.dev project
- scripts/deploy_safety_branch.mjs:95 — every safety deploy still runs presence:deploy:safety
- package.json:124 — presence:deploy:safety runs partykit deploy --config partykit.safety.json
- wrangler.jsonc:92 — safety Worker's own PARTYKIT_HOST is the safety workers.dev Worker
- src/auth/runtimeConfig.ts:45 — build-time VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST overrides the runtime host
- scripts/remote_rollout_check.mjs:21 — production partykit.dev host already blocked

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Safety previews do bake the hosted PartyKit safety host, which overrides the safety Worker's runtime host, and every non-pages-only safety deploy redeploys that PartyKit project. But alarms, PvP checkpoints and hibernation live in the shared core (partykit/presenceServer.ts) and still run on PartyKit. What previews actually miss is the Cloudflare Worker/DO adapter (src/cloudflare/presence/durableObject.ts) and the safety PRESENCE_ROOMS binding and /parties/* routing. Fix: set VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST to '' explicitly rather than omitting it, because vite.config.ts loadMergedEnv would otherwise pick up env.local/.env values. Drop the presence deploy step, --skip-presence, partykit.safety.json and the presence:deploy:safety script. Update safety-backend-foundation.md, mobile-testing.md:100-111 and frontend-redeploy-and-minting.md:42, which still tells operators to set VITE_PARTYKIT_HOST in Pages to the old production partykit.dev host. In smoke_prod.mjs, replace the uninformative mainBundleContainsPartyKitHost check (the bundle always contains api.wamp.land as the API base) with an assertion that the entry bundle does not contain 'partykit.dev'.

### F386: Rooms that share a custom background each download and decode it, and the slower one can fail and restart

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Builders often reuse one uploaded background across a series of rooms. When two nearby rooms use the same background, each room downloads and decodes its own copy at the same time. For animated backgrounds that can mean hundreds of frames decoded twice. When one copy finishes first, the other room cancels its own download. The game then treats that cancel as an error and throws away the room's half-built preparation, so it has to start over. Share one load per background, and treat that cancel as normal.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism:
- beginFullRoomPreparation creates a fresh CustomBackgroundTexturePreparation for every room whose background texture isn't registered yet (worldStreaming.ts:3739-3742).
- Each preparation starts its own fetch and decode (3781-3793). This bypasses the deduped module-level loader that the focus room and chunk previews use (ensureCustomBackgroundTexture and customBackgroundLoadPromises, src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:227-251).
- When room B reaches finishPreparedCustomTiles after room A has committed the shared texture, it calls customBackgroundPreparation.cancel() (worldStreaming.ts:4029-4035).
- cancel() aborts the in-flight fetch (runtime.ts:322-327, fetch takes the abort signal at :345-349). Room B's own .catch sees a still-current preparation and calls failFullRoomPreparation (3787-3791), which logs 'preparation failed' and cancels the room.
- If instead the decode finishes after cancel, the .then branch can fire while phase === 'custom-background'. queuePreparedBackground reuses that label (4084, mislabelled). That path enqueues an upload whose commit() throws on a cancelled preparation (runtime.ts:287-289), with the same failure.
- The single-room test covers only the uncontested path (worldStreaming.dormantLifecycle.test.ts:97-268).

Cost:
- N rooms sharing a background means N concurrent fetches and N decodes. Animated decode is up to 300 frames (webp.ts:19), each a createImageBitmap plus canvas copy.
- The failed room redoes its runtime shell, terrain, insets and objects. On the predicted path this can arrive late at the seam.

Fix:
1. Add a shared per-id 'decoded, not yet committed' loader (extend customBackgroundLoadPromises) that every preparation awaits.
2. In the .catch, return when preparation.customBackgroundReady is already true or the error is the AbortError from our own cancel.
3. Give queuePreparedBackground its own phase name.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3739-3742 — new CustomBackgroundTexturePreparation per room preparation
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3781-3793 — prepare().catch → failFullRoomPreparation if preparation still current
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4029-4035 — texture now exists → cancel() own preparation, mark ready
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4084 — queuePreparedBackground sets phase 'custom-background' (same label the .then checks)
- src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:322-327 — cancel() aborts the AbortController
- src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:344-349 — fetch uses that abort signal
- src/backgrounds/runtime.ts:227-251 — deduped ensureCustomBackgroundTexture exists but the prepared path doesn't use it
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.dormantLifecycle.test.ts:97 — only a single-room custom-background test

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The failure bug is real and reachable. When a room's preparation reaches finishPreparedCustomTiles after another loader has committed the same background, usually the focus room's deduped ensureCustomBackgroundTexture, it cancels its own loader. If that loader's fetch or body read is still running, the AbortError reaches .catch → failFullRoomPreparation. If its decode finishes inside the queuePreparedBackground window (phase reused as 'custom-background'), commit() throws on the cancelled preparation.
  
  Corrections to the cost:
  - The duplicate network download is largely absorbed by the immutable HTTP cache. The real duplicate cost is decode: up to 9 concurrent copies at world load or teleport, each up to 32M pixels (about 128 MB) for animated backgrounds, and a cancelled copy still decodes every frame.
  - The restart is cheap. Textures are already in the artifact cache. The real harm is a dropped predicted preparation, which can make the seam late, plus a console.error.
  
  Fix:
  - First: guard the .catch and .then with `if (preparation.customBackgroundReady) return;`, about 2 lines.
  - Then: share one decoded-but-uncommitted promise per background id.
  - Renaming the queuePreparedBackground phase means updating dormantLifecycle.test.ts:73.

### F399: Points, XP, badges and creator rewards for a finished run are given after the reply, with no retry if that work fails

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and data integrity: API, storage and realtime)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** To make finishing a run feel fast, the server records the run, answers the player, and only then hands out points, XP, badges, the builder's reward and leaderboard totals. If that later work hits a database error or runs out of time, it is simply dropped. The player keeps the clear but never gets the points, and the failure is barely logged. A small 'to do' row saved together with the run, plus a sweep in the existing timer job, would make sure every reward lands.

**Technical detail.**

scheduleRunRewards (src/cloudflare/worker/runs/deferredRewards.ts:10-27) runs the reward closure in context.waitUntil and on error only logs `run-rewards-failed`. That log line is now 1% sampled (see the log-sampling finding). waitUntil work can continue for at most about 30 s after the response. The file's own comment says this work 'used to take over 100 sequential D1 reads and writes'. The closure in runs/routes.ts:520-549 covers awardRunFinalizePoints, awardRoomCreatorCompletionPoints, upsertUserStats twice and awardRoomRunProgression (XP lanes, badges, activity emails). It is not part of the run batch at routes.ts:409-446. The same pattern is used at src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts:596-597 and src/cloudflare/worker/courses/routes.ts:653-654. Failure example: a transient D1 error in the creator-points step aborts every later step. The finisher's user_stats.total_points, which drives the global leaderboard, stays stale until their next finish. The builder never gets creator points and XP for that clear. Nothing records that the attempt is owed rewards. The repo already has the right pattern: prepareRunGhostArchive is added to the same batch as the run update (routes.ts:443-445; runs/ghostArchive.ts:17-31) and flushed by both the request and the cron (ghostArchive.ts:60-81; worker.ts:344). Fix: add `run_reward_jobs(attempt_id PK, run_kind, flags_json, created_at, done_at, attempts, last_error)`. Insert it in the finalize batch, run the closure from waitUntil, then set done_at. Have scheduled() retry jobs older than 2 minutes, capped at 8 attempts. Points are already idempotent per attempt (INSERT OR IGNORE INTO point_events, runs/points.ts:686,787) and lane events are keyed by source, so retries are designed to be safe. Check that persistProgressIncrement only adds when the lane event is new before turning on retries.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/deferredRewards.ts:3-27 — rewards run after the response; failures are only logged
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/routes.ts:520-549 — points, creator points, stats and progression all inside the deferred closure
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts:596-597 — same deferred pattern
- src/cloudflare/worker/courses/routes.ts:653-654 — same deferred pattern
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghostArchive.ts:17-31,60-81 — existing same-batch outbox plus flush pattern to reuse
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/points.ts:686 — point events are INSERT OR IGNORE, so retries are safe

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real gap, but it existed before the deferral: before F029 the run was saved first, so a failure in the reward work also lost the rewards (the player saw a 500), and the finish can't be retried because it returns 409 once a run is finalized. The finisher's leaderboard total recovers on any later upsertUserStats only if their point_events row was written; if awardRunFinalizePoints failed, those points are lost for good, and so are the creator's points, BXP and trust. Retries can't double-count, because persistProgressIncrement adds only newly inserted events. But they also can't repair XP when the run failed between inserting the lane events and the user_progress UPDATE: the retry finds the events, adds 0, and that XP never reaches the totals. The outbox therefore also needs one of two changes: put each total increment in the same batch as its event insert (the lostSongs/progress.ts:29-35 pattern), or recompute the totals from the event sums. A cron retry must also rebuild the record, scope and creator from the attempt id for all three run kinds and use the stored first-clear and personal-best flags; rank XP will be computed against the leaderboard at retry time. A cheaper first step: retry the closure once inside waitUntil, make event plus total atomic, and write failures to a D1 row rather than the 1%-sampled logs.

### F384: Playlist share names run out after 100 per title, and every emoji or non-English title competes for 'playlist'

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Small untested features: Wamp-O-Gram, Playlists, Guestbook, Collections)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Playlist links are made from the title and are shared across all of WAMP. The server only tries 'favorites', 'favorites-1' and so on up to 'favorites-99', and then refuses with an error. Any title without enough English letters, such as emoji, Japanese or 'Hi', becomes 'playlist'. So only 100 such playlists can ever exist. Each new one also checks the names one at a time, up to 100 database calls.

**Technical detail.**

claimUniquePlaylistSlug (src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:646-668) runs one SELECT per candidate (candidate, then -1 to -99) and then throws 409 'Could not find an available playlist URL name.' Slugs are globally unique (migrations/0035_room_playlists.sql: `slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`).

derivePlaylistSlugBase (src/playlists/model.ts:107-113) returns the fallback 'playlist' whenever the [a-z0-9] slug is shorter than 3 characters. The profile form pre-fills that derived slug into the Share URL box (profileModal.ts:1508-1514), so most users submit it unchanged.

The check-then-insert is not atomic: store.ts:264 checks, then 267-283 inserts. Two players creating the same title at the same moment hit the UNIQUE constraint as an unhandled 500. updateRoomPlaylist reuses the same function (330-333).

Fix, about 20 lines:
1. Try the base slug once. On collision, or always for the 'playlist' fallback, append a random 4-character base36 suffix (1.7M combinations).
2. Insert directly, catch 'UNIQUE constraint failed: room_playlists.slug', and retry up to 3 times.

This replaces up to 100 sequential reads with 1-2 writes.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:646-668 — up to 100 sequential probes, then 409
- src/playlists/model.ts:107-113 — titles with <3 latin slug chars fall back to 'playlist'
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:1508-1514 — client pre-fills the derived slug
- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:264-283 — check-then-insert race on the UNIQUE slug

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The mechanism is broader than the finding says. Because updatePlaylistSlugDraft (profileModal.ts:1508-1515) stops updating once the Share URL box is non-empty, the first typed character locks the slug to 'playlist' for almost every playlist typed in the profile form, not only emoji or non-English titles. The roughly 100-playlist cap and the N+1 sequential SELECTs therefore apply to almost all playlists created through the UI, which makes the bug more urgent.
  
  The fix needs two parts:
  1. Client: track a 'slug edited by user' flag and re-derive the slug from the full title on every input until that flag is set.
  2. Server: try the base slug once, then append a random base36 suffix, insert directly and retry on 'UNIQUE constraint failed' (this also closes the race and avoids the 500).
  
  The race itself is low-probability and secondary.

### F389: Single-room share pictures draw the room wrong: starfield rooms get green hills, custom tiles become blocks, trees are double size

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The picture shown in a link preview for a normal room (wamp.land/r/x/y) is drawn by its own copy of the room-drawing code, and that copy has fallen behind the game in several ways. Rooms with the default starry background show a sunny blue sky and green hills. Tiles that builders drew themselves show as plain colored squares. All 221 trees from the tree pack, and about 220 other objects, are drawn at the wrong size and position: the trees come out twice as big and stick up about 8 tiles higher than in the game. Most of this goes away by having the share code import the game's own small helper functions instead of keeping its own versions.

**Technical detail.**

src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts re-implements the shared model instead of importing it. That is why it drifts:

1. **Default background.** resolvePreviewBackground (roomImageRenderer.ts:245-275) maps the default value 'none' (backgrounds/model.ts:3, roomModel.ts:440) to {kind:'palette', palette: grassland}. getBackgroundGroup('none') then returns a group with 0 layers (roomImageRenderer.ts:211-214), so the card is the grassland sky plus hills. I rendered a 'none' room: pixel(5,5)=#8bcce3 and pixel(5,600)=#4f8b48. In-game, roomSnapshotTexture and roomMetadataRender draw a starfield on #050505 (visuals/starfieldCanvas.ts:2, 32-67).
2. **Custom room tiles.** These use gid 10,000+ (customTiles/model.ts:8). The local getTilesetByGid (roomImageRenderer.ts:831-839) returns null for them, so drawFallbackTile (561-625) paints colored blocks. The file never imports customTiles/model. The abstract API renderer does draw these pixels.
3. **Object size and position.** roomImageRenderer.ts:466-476 sizes objects from source.sw and frameWidth/2, ignoring displayScale and displayOffset. The canonical rect is getRoomMetadataObjectDrawRect (mint/roomMetadataRenderLayout.ts:18-36), and roomSnapshotTexture.ts:659-664 computes the same thing. 224 of 362 objects have displayScale != 1, and 225 have non-zero offsets. Example: tree_pack_oak_05 is 192x240 with scale 0.5 and offset (-48,73). In-game it is 96x120 with its top at y+13. On the card it is 192x240 with its top at y-120.
4. **Background layers.** layer.repeat:false is ignored, so desert gets a seam (backgrounds.ts:140-142; drawn by the loop at 216-234). bgColor is also ignored (jungle_vines, backgrounds.ts:53).

Fix:
- Delete the local resolvePreviewBackground, backgroundPalette, parseSolidBackgroundColor, decodeTileValue, getTilesetByGid and parseCustomSpriteObjectId (about 120 lines, plus roomImageAssets.ts:50-72 parseCustomBackground).
- Import the pure modules instead: resolveRoomBackground (backgrounds/model.ts:181), decodeTileDataValue (config/editorState.ts:186), getTilesetByGid (config/tilesets.ts:1378), getCustomRoomTileDefinitionForGid (customTiles/model.ts:57), parseCustomSpriteObjectId (customSprites/model), and getRoomMetadataObjectDrawRect / getRoomMetadataBackgroundLayerLayout (roomMetadataRenderLayout.ts, imports only config/room). All of them import only config, which dist/_worker.js (292 KB) already bundles.
- Port the starfield LCG to the RGBA buffer.
- Draw custom tiles with the per-pixel loop already in roomPreviewImage.ts:324-359.
- Bump ROOM_IMAGE_RENDERER_VERSION (shareMetadata.ts:10) so crawlers refetch.

Affects every single-room share. normalizeMetadata uses the Pages image unless the room is an Expanded Room (shareMetadata.ts:406-426).

**Evidence.**

- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:245-258 — string backgrounds that are not solid/custom become {kind:'palette'} with backgroundPalette(id), so 'none' gets grassland
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:211-214 — group 'none' has no layers, so only the grassland palette is drawn
- src/backgrounds/model.ts:3 — DEFAULT_ROOM_BACKGROUND = 'none' (starfield in game)
- src/visuals/starfieldCanvas.ts:32-40 — in-game 'none' fills #050505 and scatters stars
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:409-413 — no tileset for the gid goes to drawFallbackTile; there is no custom-tile branch
- src/customTiles/model.ts:8 — CUSTOM_ROOM_TILE_FIRST_GID = 10_000
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:466-476 — dest rect from frameWidth/frameHeight and source.sw*scale; no displayScale/displayOffset
- src/mint/roomMetadataRenderLayout.ts:18-36 — canonical rect applies displayScale and displayOffset
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:216-234 — every background layer tiled at canvas height; repeat:false and bgColor ignored

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** All four drawing errors are real as stated. Only one count in the summary is wrong: besides the 221 tree-pack trees, just 4 other objects have a non-default display scale or offset (swordsman_ai, police_patrolman, policewoman, crate), not "about 220". That makes 225 of 362 in total. The tree error is large at the top (about 8 tiles too high) but only about 1 tile at the bottom. The per-pixel custom-tile loop to reuse is drawCustomRoomTilePreview at roomPreviewImage.ts:~322-357. One addition: jungle_vines, spooky_moon and spooky_mountain have no palette entry, so their cards get grassland sky and hills behind the layers as well as losing bgColor.
- **partially confirmed.** All four mechanisms hold. Corrections: (a) Only 225 objects are affected, not 221 trees plus about 220 others: the 221 tree_pack_* trees (scale 0.5 with offsets) plus swordsman_ai, police_patrolman, policewoman and crate. The DETAIL's 224/225 counts are right; the SUMMARY's "about 220 other objects" is wrong. (b) On the card, oak_05 shares its left edge with the in-game tree (x-96). It is twice as big, sits about 133px (8.3 tiles) higher and extends 96px further right. (c) Importing config's getTilesetByGid changes nothing, since it is the same as the local copy. The real tile fix is a custom-tile branch for gid 10000-10127 using getCustomRoomTileDefinitionForGid plus the per-pixel loop from roomPreviewImage.ts. (d) Rooms with an empty or legacy undefined background also resolve to 'none' (starfield) in the game and to grassland on the card. jungle_vines, spooky_moon and spooky_mountain also get the grassland palette under their layers. (e) roomImageRenderer.test.ts:72-90 tests the exported helpers that would be deleted, so it must be rewritten. Impact is medium: the card is wrong but still shows the room's layout.
- **partially confirmed.** The core defects are real and reproduce: 'none' rooms render with the grassland sky and hills, custom tiles become fallback blocks, objects ignore displayScale and displayOffset, and repeat:false and bgColor are ignored. Correct the scope of the object claim. 225 of 362 objects are mis-sized or mis-placed, but 221 of them are tree_pack trees. Only 4 others are affected: swordsman_ai, police_patrolman and policewoman (scale 1.12–1.25) and crate (offset -8,6). It is not "about 220 other objects". Groups the local palette map lacks (jungle_vines, spooky_moon, spooky_mountain) also get a grassland underlay where the game uses bgColor or #050505. config/editorState.ts does not import only config, but it is already bundled through the '../config' barrel, so the bundle cost is still nil. The fix must also rewrite roomImageRenderer.test.ts, which imports the helpers being deleted. Impact is medium (cosmetic, though broad), not high.

### F396: One failed download silences a sound effect, or swaps a drum for a synthesized stand-in, until the page is reloaded

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F230

**Summary.** If a sound file fails to load once (a train tunnel, a flaky school network), the game remembers the failure for the rest of the session. That effect, which could be the jump sound, never plays again. For room music, a failed drum sample is replaced by a synthesized imitation in every room's song until reload. Retrying after a short wait would let sound recover by itself.

**Technical detail.**

SfxController.loadBuffer marks the entry 'failed' and keeps it unless the failure was an abort (sfx.ts:631-649); every later play() sees status 'failed' and records 'error' (sfx.ts:575-579). Drums: loadRolandMt32DrumSample caches .catch(() => null) in samplePromiseCache (rolandMt32DrumKit.ts:124-132); only the raw bytes promise is evicted on failure (100-111). getPatternDrumSamples substitutes renderDrumSample() for null and caches the whole Map per sample rate forever (patternKit.ts:296-309), and rendered loops are cached by music content key, so the stand-in persists in every room. F023 parallelized the kit but did not add retry. Fix: store failedAt and allow a reload attempt after ~15 s (and on 'online'/pageshow); in the drum kit, don't cache null — cache the stand-in map only for this attempt and invalidate drumSampleCache plus the render cache when a real sample later arrives.

**Evidence.**

- src/audio/sfx.ts:631-649 — failed entry kept unless aborted
- src/audio/sfx.ts:575-579 — later plays return 'error' immediately
- src/music/rolandMt32DrumKit.ts:124-132 — null result cached for the session
- src/music/patternKit.ts:296-309 — kit Map with synthesized stand-ins cached per sample rate

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F401: Room links in Explore, Profile, the new collection shelf and playlists are dead clicks while you're in the editor

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The menu and the bottom-bar Explore button also work in the room editor. If a builder opens Explore, My Rooms, a profile, the new 'collected rooms' shelf or a playlist from the editor and clicks a room, the dialog closes and nothing else happens. The game only knows how to jump to a room when the map is on screen. These links should leave the editor (with its usual save) and then go to the room.

**Technical detail.**

Each room action closes its dialog and then calls getActiveOverworldScene(game)?.jumpToCoordinates(...):
- Explore: exploreModal.ts:663-666, 671-673
- Profile room cards: profileModal.ts:1299-1302
- Playlist items: playlistModal.ts:213
- New collection shelf: profileCollection.ts:133-137 (`close(); const scene = getActiveOverworldScene(game); if (!scene) return;`)

getActiveOverworldScene returns null unless the overworld is active or paused (sceneBridge.ts:337-343). Opening any editor puts it to sleep (flow.ts:437-438), so in the editor the optional chain short-circuits after the dialog has already closed. The menu explicitly works 'independent of which game scene is running' (gameMenu.ts:4), and the footer Explore button is styled for the editor dock (dock-shell.css:79). profileModal's findBuildSpot already shows the right pattern: `(getActiveOverworldScene(game) ?? getActiveEditorScene(game))?.returnToWorld()` (profileModal.ts:308).

Fix: add one helper, openRoomFromAnywhere(game, coordinates, { play }). If an editor is active, await editor.returnToWorld() (which already waits for autosave, F056) and then jump/play. Use it in the four call sites, which also removes four copies of close+jump.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/sceneBridge.ts:337-343 — getActiveOverworldScene returns null while the overworld sleeps
- src/scenes/overworld/flow.ts:437-438 — opening the editor sleeps the overworld
- src/ui/setup/profileCollection.ts:133-137 — close() then `if (!scene) return;`
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:663-666 — close() then optional-chained jump
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:1299-1302 — same pattern for profile room cards
- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts:308 — findBuildSpot already falls back to the editor scene
- src/ui/setup/gameMenu.ts:4 — menu works regardless of active scene

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Explore is not reachable from the editor: its footer button is in #world-navigation, which is hidden outside world mode, and entering the editor closes the Explore modal. So exploreModal.ts:663-673 is not part of the bug. The dead clicks are only on paths that start from the profile modal, which the menu's Profile and My Rooms buttons open in the editor:
  - profile room cards (profileModal.ts:1299-1302)
  - a playlist opened from the profile's playlists tab (playlistModal.ts:211-213)
  - the wallet-only collection shelf (profileCollection.ts:133-137)
  
  The fix cannot be just `await editor.returnToWorld(); jump()`. returnToWorld can stop early (save failure or edit conflict) or wake the CourseComposer instead. The overworld wake is also async (handleWakeAsync) and re-centers on the edited room. So the helper should either pass the target coordinates through the wake data, or wait for the wake to finish and re-check getActiveOverworldScene before jumping. An acceptable smaller alternative is to label or disable room cards with "Leave the editor to visit" while an editor is active.

### F404: Teacher page can lose a new student's one-time password when browser storage is blocked

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Classroom accounts and Worlds: routes added since the F209 fix)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a teacher adds a student with a local real name, the page saves that name in browser storage before showing the one-time temporary password. If storage is blocked, which is common on managed school devices, that save throws. The page then reports 'Failed to create student' even though the account was created, and the password is never shown. Retrying fails as a duplicate, so the teacher has to find the student and reset them.

**Technical detail.**

In createStudent (src/school-admin.ts:156-195), localRoster plus saveLocalRoster() run at lines 178-181, before showCredential at line 188, all inside one try. saveLocalRoster calls window.localStorage.setItem with no guard (503-505), while loadLocalRoster wraps its read in try/catch (491-500). The server returns the temporary password exactly once (school/store.ts:294-358). A retry returns 409 'already in this classroom' (299-301).

The same unguarded call runs in the import and rename paths (school-admin.ts:268, 377).

Fix:
1. Wrap saveLocalRoster in try/catch.
2. Call showCredential before saving the roster.
3. If saving fails, show 'Names could not be saved in this browser'.

**Evidence.**

- src/school-admin.ts:178-181 — roster saved before the credential is shown
- src/school-admin.ts:188 — showCredential runs only after the save
- src/school-admin.ts:503-505 — unguarded localStorage.setItem
- src/school-admin.ts:491-500 — reads are guarded but writes are not
- src/cloudflare/worker/school/store.ts:299-301 — retry returns 409 for the already-created username

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The defect is real: an unguarded localStorage.setItem runs before showCredential inside the same try, so a throw loses the one-time password, and a retry with the same username returns 409. But 'storage blocked on managed school devices' is not a realistic trigger. Those settings block cookies along with storage, so the teacher can't sign in through the api.wamp.land session cookie at all. The plausible triggers are a full localStorage quota on wamp.land (room records the editor stores) or uncommon storage-only settings, such as Firefox dom.storage.enabled=false. The trigger also requires a local name to be entered. The error shown is the raw DOMException message, not 'Failed to create student.' The new row also doesn't appear until a reload, and the fix is to reload and use Reset. The same unguarded call is at line 268 (rename listener, an uncaught exception) and line 377 (import, where a failure is reported even though the rows merged in memory). Fix: call showCredential and renderStudents before saving, and wrap saveLocalRoster in try/catch with a 'names could not be saved in this browser' notice.

### F400: Removing a World builder, or turning down a join request, bans them for good

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Classroom accounts and Worlds: routes added since the F209 fix)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** There is no 'decline' button for join requests, so owners use 'Remove'. The server treats anyone with any membership record as already having a role, so a removed or declined person can never ask to join again, which makes Remove the same as Block. The policy test describes the intended rule (only blocked people can't ask again), but the live code path never reaches it.

**Technical detail.**

mapWorldAccess sets viewerRole from membership_role whenever a membership row exists, whatever its status (worlds/access.ts:107-110). Removed rows keep the role 'builder' (worlds/memberships.ts:207). canRequestMembership requires viewerRole === null (worlds/policies.ts:46-50). policies.test.ts:46-50 asserts the intended rule using viewerRole:null with status 'blocked', a combination production never produces. The client hides the request button when either viewerRole or a status is present (src/ui/worlds/controller.ts:93-97).

The ON CONFLICT branch in requestWorldMembership, which resets non-blocked rows to 'requested' (memberships.ts:106-110), is unreachable for bound users. resolveMembershipAction has no 'decline' action (199-214).

Fix:
1. In mapWorldAccess, set viewerRole to null unless status is active, invited or requested.
2. Add a 'decline' action that sets status to removed.
3. Cover remove followed by re-request in a test.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/access.ts:107-110 — role derived regardless of membership status
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/memberships.ts:207 — remove keeps role 'builder'
- src/worlds/policies.ts:46-50 — re-request requires viewerRole === null
- src/worlds/policies.test.ts:46-50 — test expects only 'blocked' to prevent re-requests
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/memberships.ts:199-214 — no decline action

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** This is real but narrower than claimed. After an owner removes a builder or turns down a join request (using Remove), that person can never ask to join again themselves. Here is the path:
  - mapWorldAccess turns the leftover builder/removed row into viewerRole 'builder' (access.ts:107-110).
  - canRequestMembership requires viewerRole === null (policies.ts:46-50).
  - The client also hides the request button whenever viewerMembershipStatus is set (controller.ts:93-97).
  
  It is not the same as Block. The owner can still re-invite them by email: the invite ON CONFLICT at memberships.ts:63-70 resets removed to invited, and the person can then accept. A blocked row stays blocked.
  
  Fix:
  1. Server: treat removed (and blocked) rows as having no role when deciding whether someone can request to join. The policy's blocked check keeps blocked users out.
  2. Client: show the request button when the status is 'removed', or drive it from the server's canRequestMembership.
  3. Optionally label Remove as "Decline" on requested rows. A new action isn't needed.
  4. Add a test for remove followed by re-request against the real mapping, not just resolveWorldPolicy.

### F397: Playlist entries for Expanded Rooms turn into one stale screen after the builder edits the level

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Small untested features: Wamp-O-Gram, Playlists, Guestbook, Collections)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When you add an Expanded Room (a multi-screen level) to a playlist, the playlist remembers the version of one screen. If the builder later edits and republishes that screen, the playlist stops treating the entry as the full level and plays just that single old screen. The goal may sit on a screen the player can no longer reach. Nothing warns the playlist owner.

**Technical detail.**

addRoomToPlaylist stores only (room_id, room_version) for the clicked cell (src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:432). The expanded target found at add time (397-402) is used only for the duplicate check.

On every read, hydratePlaylistItemsWithExpandedRooms (719-766) loads the current published expanded room. It keeps it only if a cell still has the item's exact pinned version (744-746). Otherwise expandedRoom becomes null and the item becomes a standalone single-cell entry (750-752). hydratePlaylistSummaryCounts makes the same comparison (548-552).

Cell versions change on every republish of that cell, because expanded_room_cells rows carry room_version per expanded-room version (expandedRooms/store.ts:480-500; writeStore.ts:208-228). The semantics are also inconsistent. A matched expanded entry plays the current expanded version (mapExpandedRoomTargetForPlaylistItem uses target.version, 811-813), while standalone rooms stay pinned.

Fix:
1. Add a nullable expanded_room_id column to room_playlist_items and fill it at add time from expandedRoomTarget.
2. On read, resolve by expanded_room_id through loadExpandedRoomTarget, and fall back to the pinned cell only when that expanded room is unpublished or archived.
3. Write a migration that back-fills from current memberships.

Add a test with the discoveryTestDatabase fixture, which already seeds two-cell expanded rooms (runs/discoveryTestDatabase.ts:43-55).

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:397-402,432 — only the clicked cell id+version is stored
- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:744-752 — expanded target dropped unless the pinned cell version still matches
- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:548-552 — counts use the same exact-version match
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/store.ts:480-500 — cells are versioned per expanded-room version
- src/cloudflare/worker/playlists/store.ts:807-821 — matched entries carry the current expanded version (not pinned)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real, but the impact is display and duplicate bookkeeping only, not gameplay. Once the clicked cell and its Expanded Room are republished, the playlist API returns the entry as a standalone room. The list then shows the cell's title, goal and version instead of the Expanded Room's 'N cells' line. The owner can re-add the same Expanded Room as a second entry, and roomCount is inflated. Playback is unaffected. Playlist play jumps to the coordinates, and playSelectedRoom/playSelectedCourse play the current published Expanded Room from the live world summary, so neither the version nor item.expandedRoom is used. The player never gets a single stale screen. Smaller fix, no migration needed: in hydratePlaylistItemsWithExpandedRooms (store.ts:744-746), hydratePlaylistSummaryCounts (store.ts:550) and the add-time duplicate predicate, match a current published membership by roomId alone and drop the exact-version check. Add a two-cell test with the discoveryTestDatabase fixture.

### F392: Badly encoded links (for example /api/rooms/%E0%A4%A) crash into a 500 error instead of a 400

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and data integrity: API, storage and realtime)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Many API routes decode part of the web address, and a broken percent-encoding makes that throw an error the server doesn't expect. Instead of a polite 'bad request', the player or bot gets a 500 'something went wrong' error, and it is counted as a server failure. A one-line change in the shared error handler fixes all of them.

**Technical detail.**

There are 98 decodeURIComponent calls across 17 worker files, and none are guarded. Examples: src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:94 (`decodeURIComponent(segments[2] ?? '')` for every /api/rooms/* request), src/cloudflare/worker.ts:157,165 and 610 (the new profile collection shelf). decodeURIComponent throws URIError on malformed sequences. apiErrorResponse treats any non-HttpError as a 500, logs it as api_error and shows 'Something went wrong on our side' (ops/errors.ts:11-27). Scanners and broken share links therefore look like server faults, which adds noise once error alerting exists. Fix: in apiErrorResponse map `error instanceof URIError` to 400 'Malformed URL.' (one line), or add a safeDecodePathSegment helper that throws HttpError(400). Add a test hitting /api/rooms/%E0%A4%A.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:93-94 — unguarded decodeURIComponent on every room route
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:610 — unguarded decode for /api/profiles/:id/collection
- src/cloudflare/worker/ops/errors.ts:11-27 — non-HttpError becomes a logged 500

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: a malformed percent-escape in a path segment reaches an unguarded decodeURIComponent on /api/rooms/* (rooms/routes.ts:94), on worker.ts:157/165/610 and on about 95 other API sites. apiErrorResponse then turns the error into a logged 500 api_error. Corrections: there are 99 call sites in 18 non-test files, and some are already guarded: customSprites/routes.ts decodeSpriteId (it returns 400 and has a test), customSprites/adminRoutes.ts, and presence/durableObject.ts. The preferred fix is a shared decodePathSegment helper that throws HttpError(400), modeled on decodeSpriteId. A blanket `error instanceof URIError` → 400 in apiErrorResponse also works, but it would hide server-side encodeURIComponent failures (lone surrogates in stored data) as client errors. Add tests for /api/rooms/%E0%A4%A and one declarative route such as /api/rooms/%E0/stats.

### F395: New NFT artwork permanently links to whichever website address the builder happened to be on

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Collect & Lock: room collecting, wallet approvals and the crypto gate)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F244

**Summary.** When a builder adds artwork, the NFT's 'animation' link is built from the address in their browser bar. If they are on a preview link or www.wamp.land, that address goes on-chain for good. Preview links use the real production server and Base mainnet, so this can happen with a real NFT. The 'Play this room' link is already fixed to wamp.land; the animation link should use the same rule.

**Technical detail.**

roomWalletActions.ts:159 passes origin: window.location.origin to buildRoomTokenArtwork. buildMintedRoomAnimationUrl builds the animation_url from options.origin (roomMetadata.ts:1084-1090, used at 405). external_url is deliberately pinned by buildRoomTokenPlayUrl to https://wamp.land (roomTokenLinks.ts:1-8, 'Public room links never inherit preview…'). The historical backfill also pins ORIGIN = 'https://wamp.land' (scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:12). Pages preview hosts (*.wampland.pages.dev) map to PRODUCTION_API_BASE (config/appHosts.ts:39-41), so artwork added from a preview link is a real Base-mainnet write of an ephemeral preview URL, served by stale code forever. Two origins also produce different metadata hashes for identical artwork. Fix (2 lines): add a buildRoomTokenViewerAbsoluteUrl next to buildRoomTokenPlayUrl that uses https://wamp.land, and drop origin from RoomTokenMetadataBuildOptions.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/roomWalletActions.ts:159 — artwork is built with origin: window.location.origin
- src/mint/roomMetadata.ts:1084-1090 — animation_url uses options.origin
- src/mint/roomTokenLinks.ts:1-8 — the play link is pinned to https://wamp.land by design
- src/config/appHosts.ts:39-41 — Pages preview hosts talk to the production API
- scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:12 — backfill pins https://wamp.land, unlike the live flow

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Make animation_url always use https://wamp.land, the same rule external_url already follows. It currently copies window.location.origin. The real risk is limited: a room's owner adds artwork while on a *.wampland.pages.dev preview link, and a working but stale preview URL lands on Base mainnet. The owner can fix this by running Add artwork again from wamp.land, so "permanently" overstates it. The www.wamp.land case and the hash difference are not real problems. The fix is small but touches more than 2 lines. Remove `origin` from RoomTokenMetadataBuildOptions, or ignore it. Build the URL with a wamp.land helper in roomTokenLinks.ts. Then update the test that currently asserts the preview origin (roomTokenLinks.test.ts:35), the backfill script, smoke_mint_network.mjs and the two other unit tests that pass `origin`.

### F405: The NFT artwork backfill tool still makes the old blurry 80x44 images and text-card fallbacks

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F244

**Summary.** The planned one-time fix to give all 11 minted rooms proper artwork would go through a maintenance script and a hidden render page. Both still produce the tiny 80x44 picture and, on failure, the plain text card that tokens 1 and 4 have now. The in-game minting flow was already upgraded to crisp, size-checked artwork. Pointing the script at that same function avoids writing blurry art on-chain a second time, which costs gas each time.

**Technical detail.**

scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:
- Builds a URL to room-preview-render.html (87-92) and drives it with Playwright (94-120, scripts/render-room-preview-data-url.mjs).
- That page renders with tilePixelSize: 2 (src/room-preview-render.ts:49-51), which gives 80x44 pixels.
- The script passes the raw PNG straight to buildRoomTokenMetadata (168), with no pixel-sharp wrapper and no size check.
- With --allow-fallback-image it writes buildFallbackSvg (66-84, 162-166), a 640x352 SVG text card that matches what tokens 1 and 4 carry today.

The in-app path, buildRoomTokenArtwork (src/mint/roomTokenArtwork.ts:20-29), tries tilePixelSize 16, then 8, 4 and 2. It wraps the PNG in a 640x352 SVG with image-rendering:pixelated (11-17) and enforces MAX_ARTWORK_TOKEN_URI_LENGTH = 20,000 so the setRoomTokenURI transaction fits Base's gas cap (5-7). The backfill has no such cap and could submit a transaction that fails or is too costly.

F244 and F237 (OPEN) call for exactly this batch setTokenURI.

Fix:
- Have room-preview-render.ts call buildRoomTokenArtwork (or expose it on window) and return the built tokenUri.
- Drop the SVG text fallback, or gate it behind an explicit flag that also logs.
- Or retire room-preview-render.html (86) and src/room-preview-render.ts (104), which only this script uses (knip.json lists them as entries), and render through the world-tile page on an immutable deployment instead. That removes about 190 lines and one public production page (dist/room-preview-render.html).

**Evidence.**

- scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:87-92 — renders via /room-preview-render.html
- src/room-preview-render.ts:49-51 — renderRoomSnapshotToPngDataUrl(snapshot, { tilePixelSize: 2 })
- scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:66-84 — SVG text-card fallback image
- scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts:162-168 — fallback used, then buildRoomTokenMetadata with the raw data URL, no size cap
- src/mint/roomTokenArtwork.ts:5-29 — in-app artwork: 16→2 px sampling, pixelated SVG wrapper, 20,000-char gas-safe cap

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** scripts/backfill-room-token-metadata.ts and room-preview-render.html/.ts lag behind buildRoomTokenArtwork. They produce a raw 80x44 PNG with no pixelated wrapper and without strictAssets (missing assets are silently dropped), and can fall back to the SVG text card. The F237 write-up (wamp-checkup-2026-10-details.md:5466/5474/5479) still tells the owner to run this tool with --write.
  
  Corrections:
  - **Gas risk:** a gas-cap failure cannot be submitted, because estimateContractGas runs before writeContract and a failure is caught per token. All 11 tokens fit at 80x44, and total fees are about 0.0002-0.0004 ETH. The harm is writing worse permanent art and needing a second round of owner transactions.
  - **Plan of record:** the current plan is the pre-built strict, pixel-sharp unsigned proposals in ignored output/f244-artwork-2026-10-20/unsigned/. The tool that generated them is not committed, so any regeneration after revalidation would fall back to the stale script.
  
  Fix:
  - Make room-preview-render.ts take chainId, contract and tokenId params, call buildRoomTokenArtwork, and expose the tokenUri. Have the backfill use that tokenUri. This needs a Pages deploy or ROOM_PREVIEW_RENDER_ORIGIN pointed at a local or immutable build.
  - Remove --allow-fallback-image, or make it log loudly.
  - Update the F237 write-up to point at the corrected tool or the unsigned proposals.
  - Drop the "world-tile page" retirement option.

### F394: Keyboard focus is pulled out of the wallet cost check when 'Add/update artwork' is started from Room History

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F240

**Summary.** When a room owner clicks 'Add/update artwork' in the Room History dialog, the new cost-check dialog ('Continue to wallet' / 'Not now') appears on top. Keyboard focus is immediately pulled back into the Room History dialog underneath. Tab cycles only through Room History's buttons and Escape closes Room History, so a keyboard-only or screen-reader user cannot reach the wallet buttons. The dialog-focus code should treat the cost check as the top dialog.

**Technical detail.**

historyModal.handleRefreshMetadataClick keeps #room-history-modal open and calls editorScene.refreshMintMetadata() (historyModal.ts:65-77). That runs the wallet flow → requestRoomWalletConsent → requestBusyConfirmation (roomWalletConsent.ts:30-34; roomWalletActions.ts:169-170). requestBusyConfirmation renders in #busy-overlay (z-index --z-busy 135, above --z-modal 40; tokens.css:31, 82) and focuses busyClose (appFeedback.ts:279-283). #busy-overlay is not a `.history-modal` (index.html:47), so installModalFocusManagement still treats Room History as the top dialog:
- Its focusin backstop moves focus back to Room History's first control (modalState.ts:177-185).
- Its capture-phase Tab handler cycles only Room History's controls (modalState.ts:153-173).
- The confirmation's own Escape/Tab handler is attached to busyRoot (appFeedback.ts:275-276), so it never sees keys once focus has left.

Pressing Escape instead closes Room History through its lifecycle handler, leaving the consent dialog open.

Fix: give the confirmation-state busy overlay role=dialog plus a marker the stack recognises, e.g. treat `#busy-overlay[data-busy-state='confirmation']` as the topmost entry in openModalsInStackOrder. Alternatively, have the focus manager skip its backstop while hasPendingDialog() is true. Add a test with Room History open that asserts focus stays on 'Not now'.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/historyModal.ts:65-77 — artwork action runs the wallet flow with Room History still open
- src/ui/roomWalletConsent.ts:30-34 — consent uses requestBusyConfirmation
- src/ui/appFeedback.ts:279-283 — confirmation focuses #btn-busy-close
- index.html:47 — #busy-overlay is 'app-feedback app-busy-overlay', not .history-modal
- src/ui/modalState.ts:177-185 — focusin backstop pulls focus back into the top .history-modal
- src/ui/modalState.ts:153-173 — Tab trap cycles only the top .history-modal
- src/styles/tokens.css:31 — --z-modal: 40; tokens.css:82 --z-busy: 135 (consent drawn above)

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** The core mechanism is correct. One correction: the consent buttons are unreachable by keyboard only while Room History stays open. Escape closes Room History, focus returns to its opener, and native Tab order can then reach #busy-overlay. Mouse and touch always work. The preferred fix is to skip the focus-manager backstop and Tab trap when the event target or active element is inside #busy-overlay[data-busy-state='confirmation'] (or when hasPendingDialog() is true). Adding the busy overlay to MODAL_SELECTOR is riskier because that selector also drives hasBlockingModalOpen, the backdrops and gameplayPause.

### F406: The Worlds window and PvP pop-ups bypass the shared dialog system, so keys, focus and Escape misbehave there

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F175
- **Also covers:** The Worlds window was left out of the shared pop-up system: no focus handling, no pause, and it ignores Readable text

**Summary.** Almost every WAMP pop-up uses one shared system. It pauses the game, hands the keyboard to the menu, keeps Tab inside the pop-up and lets Escape close only the top window. The Worlds window, which every visitor can open, and the PvP challenge and result pop-ups were built separately. While they are open, the game still grabs the arrow keys and Space, Tab wanders behind them, and with PvP, Escape can drop you out of the room you are playing. Putting them on the shared system fixes all of this in a few lines.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: src/ui/modalState.ts:1 hard-codes MODAL_SELECTOR = '.history-modal'. The capture-phase Escape guard (:33-46), the covered-backdrop logic (:50-72) and the focus trap and restore (:114-203) all key off it. So do keyboardFocus.ts:91-97 (game keys yield only when hasBlockingModalOpen()), gameplayPause.ts:63/74 (pause) and inspectInput.ts:117-121 (play-mode Escape returns to the world unless a blocking dialog is open). The Worlds dialog is `<section class="worlds-modal">` (worlds/view.ts:11). Its close button (view.ts:15) also does not match CLOSE_BUTTON_SELECTOR (modalState.ts:2: id/class containing 'close' or aria-label 'Close'). Worlds adds its own always-on document Escape listener (worlds/controller.ts:39-41) and sits at z-index 1200 (worlds.css:3), above every shared dialog (--z-modal 40). Result while Worlds is open: Phaser keeps keyboard.enabled and preventDefault on arrows/Space (keyboardFocus.ts:117-123), so they can't scroll the Worlds list (the F169 symptom). There is no focus trap (the F175 symptom), and any shared dialog opened at the same time, for example via the emailed `/?worlds=mine` links (worker/worlds/notifications.ts:31/47/72), traps focus underneath the Worlds panel. The Worlds button is un-hidden for every visitor once the public GET /api/worlds answers (controller.ts:48-52; worker/worlds/routes.ts:56-61). PvP invite and result dialogs are `.pvp-modal` built in TS (pvpModal.ts:20-22, 109-110) with no Escape handling. In play mode an Escape meant to dismiss them reaches inspectInput and leaves the room (the F168 symptom). performanceSuggestionModal.ts:418-434 keeps a private copy of the blocking-dialog check plus a separate .pvp-modal check because of this split. Related plumbing problem: four separate MutationObserver setups watch the dialog set (modalState.ts:68 and :188, keyboardFocus.ts:133, gameplayPause.ts:74-87). Three of them only observe dialogs that exist at install time (main.ts:206-207 run before setupUI at :230), so dialogs inserted later are invisible to the stack-backdrop sync: the Worlds root and the room-goal intro, whose markup roomGoalIntroModal.ts:52/181 injects in its constructor. Fix: (1) add the `history-modal` class (or widen MODAL_SELECTOR to '.history-modal, .worlds-modal, .pvp-modal[aria-modal]') and aria-label="Close" on the Worlds close button. Delete controller.ts:39-41 and use var(--z-modal) in worlds.css. (2) Have modalState own one body childList observer, like gameplayPause.ts:75-87, and expose a single onDialogsChanged subscription for keyboardFocus, gameplayPause and focus management, which replaces three observer setups (~40 lines). Verify with scripts/smoke_worlds_pilot.ts and smoke_keyboard_bindings.mjs.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/worlds/view.ts:11 — Worlds dialog root is <section class="worlds-modal">, not .history-modal
- src/ui/worlds/view.ts:15 — Worlds close button has no id/class/aria-label the shared guard can find
- src/ui/modalState.ts:1-2 — Escape guard, stack backdrops and focus trap only consider '.history-modal' and 'close'-named buttons
- src/ui/keyboardFocus.ts:91-97 — game keeps arrow/Space capture unless hasBlockingModalOpen()
- src/ui/gameplayPause.ts:63 — pause only reacts to .history-modal dialogs
- src/ui/worlds/controller.ts:39-41 — private document-wide Escape listener, runs even when Worlds is closed
- src/ui/worlds/worlds.css:3 — z-index: 1200 places Worlds above all shared dialogs
- src/ui/worlds/controller.ts:52 — Worlds button shown to every visitor once /api/worlds succeeds
- src/ui/setup/pvpModal.ts:20-22 — PvP invite dialog is a .pvp-modal built in TS with no Escape handling
- src/scenes/overworld/inspectInput.ts:117-121 — play-mode Escape returns to the world unless a .history-modal is open
- src/ui/setup/performanceSuggestionModal.ts:418-434 — duplicate blocking-dialog and pvp-modal checks
- src/main.ts:206-207 — stack-backdrop observer installed before setupUI (main.ts:230) inserts later dialogs
- src/ui/worlds/view.ts:11-12 — custom .worlds-modal, not .history-modal
- src/ui/worlds/view.ts:35-43 — open/close without focus handling
- src/ui/worlds/controller.ts:39-41 — unconditional document Escape listener
- src/ui/worlds/worlds.css:1-9 — z-index 1200

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Scope the finding to the real issues: focus handling and consistency, not key capture, pause or room exit.
  
  Worlds is only reachable in world/browse mode, which has no gameplay key capture, pause or play-mode Escape, and its own Escape listener closes it correctly. The real Worlds problems are:
  - (a) No focus move, Tab trap or focus restore, so Tab reaches the UI behind the panel and the list cannot be arrow-scrolled until something inside it is clicked.
  - (b) It sits at z-index 1200, above the shared dialogs, and is not in their stack. Auto-presenting prompts (guest progress claim, guest room recovery, post-run reminder, performance suggestion) do not check for `.worlds-modal`, so they can open underneath it. The shared focus trap then pulls keyboard focus out of Worlds and into the hidden dialog.
  - (c) Its hard-coded fonts and pixel sizes ignore Readable text.
  
  The PvP Escape problem is mostly moot:
  - The result dialog is followed by an automatic return to the world 450 ms later.
  - The invite focuses Accept, which usually makes the game yield its keys.
  
  The fix:
  1. Make Worlds a `.history-modal` (or add its selector to every place that hard-codes the dialog selector: modalState.ts:1, keyboardFocus.ts:133 and gameplayPause.ts:74/81-82). Give the close button aria-label="Close". Delete controller.ts:39-41, use var(--z-modal), and switch to font and size tokens.
  2. Optionally merge the four private blocking-dialog checks and the observers that only watch dialogs present at install time into a single modalState helper.
  
  Only stack backdrops misses dialogs inserted during setupUI (main.ts:207). Keyboard sync and focus management are installed after setupUI (main.ts:236-237). Verify in the browser; scripts/smoke_worlds_pilot.ts only tests the API.

### F393: Controller players can't press Start on the room intro, which now appears before every timed room

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Bugs and regressions: gameplay, editor and UI)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F148

**Summary.** With a game controller, pressing Play on any timed room opens the intro card (goal plus ghost-race choice), and the game pauses behind it. The controller is ignored while paused, and its Start button is mapped to Restart. The player has to reach for the mouse, keyboard or touch screen every time. Let the A or Start button press the dialog's main button when a controller is connected.

**Technical detail.**

Every published room whose leaderboard ranks by time shows the intro on Play (OverworldPlayScene.ts:2777, supportsGhostRace → ranking mode 'time', runs/ghostRace.ts:21-23). The intro sets roomGoalIntroPauseRequested and pauses the scene (OverworldPlayScene.ts:2722-2723). Gamepad polling runs only on the scene's 'preupdate' (gamepadInput.ts:103-112), so nothing is read while paused. Even unpaused, button 9 (Start) maps to restart and button 0 (A) to jump (gamepadInput.ts:77, 80). The intro closes only through its click handler or modal lifecycle (roomGoalIntroModal.ts:42-44, 63-67).

The Room Rush result and run-rating dialogs have the same gap. F148 shipped pad play but no dialog confirmation, which makes it the weakest input for adaptive-controller users (F178 was merged into F148).

Fix (about 30 lines): add a small game-level ('prestep', fires while scenes are paused) pad watcher. When a pad is connected and the top open `.history-modal` has a [data-autofocus] or primary button, an A/Start rising edge clicks it and B/Back clicks its close button. Reuse OverworldGamepadInput's neutral-arming so the press doesn't also become a jump on resume. The intro already focuses its Start button (roomGoalIntroModal.ts:130).

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:2777 — intro shown for every published time-ranked room
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:2722-2723 — intro pauses the scene
- src/scenes/overworld/gamepadInput.ts:103-112 — pad is polled only on scene preupdate (not while paused)
- src/scenes/overworld/gamepadInput.ts:80 — Start is mapped to restart
- src/ui/setup/roomGoalIntroModal.ts:42-44 — intro starts only from a click on its Start button

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The pad can't confirm the room intro, but that rarely costs a pad player anything. The intro only opens right after a Play click, room selection or sequence Next. Those all use mouse, keyboard or touch, because the pad works only in play mode (OverworldPlayScene.ts:1406-1407). Enter or Space already confirms the focused Start button. The Room Rush result and run-rating dialogs open only in the world view (roomRushResults.ts:98-100, runRatingModal.ts:412), where the pad is ignored anyway. That is part of a broader gap: there is no pad navigation outside play. An intro-only A/Start confirm, scoped to #room-goal-intro-modal on game 'prestep', is a small polish. It lets players switch to the pad one step earlier, but it doesn't make the game pad-only. The neutral-arming the finding asks for already happens: 'resume' resets the pad. Don't build a generic watcher that clicks the primary button of whatever .history-modal is on top. Full pad-only play would mean adding pad room selection and Play in the world view, which is medium effort.

### F402: Share-image server remembers a failed image load forever and keeps every decoded picture in memory

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** If loading a room's uploaded background or a tileset fails once, the share-picture server keeps that failure and draws every later share picture without it until the server restarts. It also keeps every decoded picture in memory with no limit, and an uploaded background can take up to 32 MB once decoded. The game's own copy of this drawing code got the same 'forget failures' fix on October 20; this copy did not.

**Technical detail.**

In src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts, imageDataCache (line 23) is a module-level Map with no size cap.

- **Failures cached.** loadAssetImageData (85-101) and loadCustomBackgroundImageData (113-145) store the pending promise before it settles and never delete it on rejection. A transient failure therefore becomes permanent for the isolate. A failed tileset falls back to colored blocks (roomImageRenderer.ts:434-436); a failed background drops it (205-207). A failed group layer stops all remaining layers (`catch { return; }`, 235-237).
- **No timeout.** The custom-background fetch (130) has no AbortSignal or timeout. The 3.5 s budget (ROOM_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS, roomImageRenderer.ts:49) only covers loading the snapshot. A slow image delivery stalls the og:image response, which crawlers time out on.
- **Full-size decodes.** It asks Cloudflare only for format:'png' (124-128), not a smaller size, and allows decodes up to 8 MP (MAX_CUSTOM_BACKGROUND_DECODE_MP, line 20; used at 148-154). 8 MP is 32 MB of RGBA held forever, against the 128 MB Workers isolate limit. Upload size is capped at 8 MB (backgroundImages/routes.ts:34).

The client copy fixed the identical bug in 3ad1f213 on 2026-10-20 (roomMetadataRender.ts:478-481, imageCache.delete on error). This is a concrete example of a fix landing in one renderer copy and not the other.

Fix (about 20 lines):
- Delete the cache entry on rejection.
- Add signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500) to the background fetch.
- Request cf.image {width: 1200, fit: 'scale-down', format: 'png'}, since the card is 1200 px wide.
- Keep custom-background entries in a small LRU (for example 4) and leave the bounded set of static assets uncapped.

**Evidence.**

- src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts:23 — const imageDataCache = new Map<string, Promise<RoomImageData>>() with no eviction
- src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts:91-101 — promise cached before success, never removed on failure
- src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts:118-145 — custom background fetch, no timeout, rejected promise kept
- src/pages/roomImageAssets.ts:20 — MAX_CUSTOM_BACKGROUND_DECODE_MP = 8 (about 32 MB RGBA per entry)
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.ts:235-237 — one failed background layer aborts the remaining layers
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts:478-481 — client copy deletes the failed entry (fixed 2026-10-20)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core defect is real: the share renderer caches rejected image loads for the life of the Workers isolate (not forever), and the custom-background fetch (roomImageAssets.ts:130) has no timeout and is awaited twice (roomImageRenderer.ts:195 and 322). The 3.5 s budget covers only the snapshot. Tests at roomImageAssets.test.ts:118-139 and 215-235 currently pin the cache-the-failure behavior and must be updated.
  
  The memory part is overstated:
  - Custom backgrounds are validated at ≤1280×768 since 2026-10-16 (validateUpload.ts:22-25), so each decodes to about 3.9 MB, not 32 MB.
  - The 8 MP cap applies only to JPEG; decodePng has no cap.
  - The static set the finding calls bounded and leaves uncapped is actually the larger pool: about 78 MB decoded across about 437 reachable paths.
  
  Recommended fix:
  - Delete the entry on rejection, or keep a short negative-cache TTL.
  - Add AbortSignal.timeout of about 1.5 s to the background fetch.
  - Optionally replace the Map with one byte-budget LRU over all entries.
  - Drop the cf.image width resize, which saves almost nothing for current uploads.
  
  Transient static-asset failures via ASSETS.fetch are unlikely. The realistic trigger is the custom-background path through the API Worker and Images delivery.

### F403: Swing settings 96-100% sound identical to 95% but still count as a different groove

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The swing control goes up to 100%, but the synthesizer and the playhead both stop at 95%, so the top five clicks change nothing a builder can hear. Rooms set to, say, 96% and 100% sound the same, yet the transition logic treats them as different grooves and won't blend them on the beat. Cap the control at 95%.

**Technical detail.**

ROOM_PATTERN_MAX_SWING_PERCENT is 100 (pattern.ts:27) and normalizeRoomPatternSwingPercent clamps to it (pattern.ts:217-222); the swing-up button stays enabled until 100 (musicWorkflow.ts:1120-1124). getStepTimingSec clamps the ratio to 0.95 (patternRenderCore.ts:244) and resolveMusicPlayheadStep does the same (musicPlayhead.ts:51). timingIdentity includes swingPercent (transitionPlan.ts:13), so 96 vs 100 rooms fail the 'compatible' check and get a cut instead of a bar-aligned blend; their content keys also differ, so each gets its own render. Fix: set the max to 95. Normalization then maps stored 96-100 to 95 with no audible change.

**Evidence.**

- src/music/pattern.ts:27 — max swing 100
- src/music/pattern.ts:217-222 — normalizer clamps to 50..100
- src/music/patternRenderCore.ts:244 — renderer clamps swing ratio to 0.95
- src/scenes/editor/musicPlayhead.ts:51 — playhead clamps to 0.95
- src/scenes/editor/musicWorkflow.ts:1120-1124 — swing-up enabled until 100
- src/music/transitionPlan.ts:13 — swing part of timing identity

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F398: Playlist thumbnails show the room's latest version, not the one the playlist plays, and load all at once

- **Area:** Bugs and regressions (reviewer: Gap review: Small untested features: Wamp-O-Gram, Playlists, Guestbook, Collections)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Each room in a playlist is saved at a specific version, and 'Play Playlist' plays that version. But the little preview pictures fetch whatever the room looks like today, so a remade room shows a picture of a level you won't actually play. Clicking a row also takes you to today's version. On phones, every thumbnail is requested at the same moment, one web request per room.

**Technical detail.**

attachRoomPreview and loadRoomPreview (src/ui/setup/playlistModal.ts:263-305) key the cache by `${roomId}:${roomVersion}` (264, 298). But they load through worldRepository.loadPublishedRoom(roomId, coordinates) (301), which returns the current published snapshot (worldRepository.ts:324-341). The current room's image is then cached under the pinned version's key.

Row click calls jumpToCoordinates (213), which goes to the live room. Play passes the pinned roomVersion (361-369).

Every row calls attachRoomPreview during render (242) with no IntersectionObserver, unlike Explore (exploreModal.ts:161-162) and Profile (profileModal.ts:1560-1571). A 50-room playlist fires 50 GETs plus 50 canvas renders when it opens.

Fix: collect visible rows with an IntersectionObserver and call worldRepository.queryRoomSnapshots once per batch, with {kind:'version', roomId, version} references and detail 'overview'. The endpoint already accepts up to 128 references (rooms/routes.ts:105-129; rooms/store.ts:397). Feed the results to loadSharedRenderedRoomPreview. Make row click start the sequence at that entry instead of jumping to the live room.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/playlistModal.ts:298-301 — preview keyed by pinned version but loads current published room
- src/persistence/worldRepository.ts:324-341 — loadPublishedRoom returns the current version
- src/ui/setup/playlistModal.ts:213 — row click jumps to the live room, not the pinned version
- src/ui/setup/playlistModal.ts:361-369 — Play uses the pinned roomVersion
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:105-129 — batched versioned snapshot query with overview detail already exists

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Drop the version-mismatch claim. Playlist playback (roomSequenceController.ts:326-338) jumps to coordinates and plays the live room, so thumbnails, row click and Play already all show the current version. The only real version inconsistency is that row titles come from the pinned version_title while gameplay and images are current, which is a product question about whether playlists should pin versions. The valid defect is that playlistModal.createRoomRow loads every thumbnail eagerly: one uncached full-snapshot GET plus a canvas render per item, and playlist size is unbounded. Fix by copying profileModal's IntersectionObserver pattern (observeRoomPreview/getRoomPreviewObserver with rootMargin 240px). If batching through queryRoomSnapshots, use current_preview references (or keep the version references only if playback is also changed to pin versions), with detail 'overview'. Do not switch thumbnails to {kind:'version'} on their own, because that would make them disagree with what Play loads.

### F407: Anyone signed in can record fake PvP matches against any player, farming XP and rewriting that player's leaderboard name

- **Area:** Gap review: Classroom accounts and Worlds: routes added since the F209 fix
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** high · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The server accepts whatever PvP match result the browser sends. A player can invent a match against any account, including a classroom student who is supposed to be shielded from PvP. They can give themselves the win and XP as often as they like, and write any 32-character text as either player's name on the public leaderboard. The PvP match server, which already exists, should confirm results, and names should be looked up on the server.

**Technical detail.**

handlePvpMatchSubmit (src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:19-25) checks only that the submitter's userId is in body.participants. Everything else comes from the request body: the opponents' userIds, results, hearts and hits, and userDisplayName (normalizeParticipants 275-298, name capped at 32 chars at 291). For every participant it inserts pvp_match_players (83-109) and upserts user_stats with `user_display_name = excluded.user_display_name` (124-149, line 136). It also awards PXP: +20 for a win, +10 draw, +6 loss (15-17, 165-200). The dedupe key includes matchId, so sending a fresh matchId each time defeats it. There is no rate limit.

Effects:
(a) Unlimited PXP. PXP sets player_level (progression/laneEvents.ts:19-36), and level 10 unlocks CryptoPunk avatar generation (avatars/routes.ts:227-233).
(b) The global leaderboard shows user_stats.user_display_name (runs/globalLeaderboards.ts:46). Any player can rename any other player there until that player's next run or publish rebuilds the row (runs/points.ts:465-497). The attacker can then repeat it.
(c) Classroom angle: presence blocks PvP invites to and from students (partykit/presenceServer.ts:939, school flag from the token at 844). The Worker never checks school context, so a stranger can still attach a student's userId to fabricated wins and losses. A student can also set their own public leaderboard name to any text, which gets around the display-name block (auth/routes.ts:537).

PvP party rooms also accept the participant list from the client's configure message (src/partykit/pvpMatchRuntime.ts:45-48).

Fix plan:
1. Make the Worker fetch the authoritative final snapshot from the `pvp:<matchId>` PartyKit room, which persists its state under PVP_STORAGE_KEY (presenceServer.ts:107, 201-205). Reuse the existing internal-token channel: the Worker already sends x-partykit-internal-token (admin/launchStats.ts:1277), and the server already verifies it (presenceServer.ts:796-802). Accept only a match whose status is complete and whose participants actually connected.
2. Ignore client display names and read users.display_name instead.
3. Reject any participant with school context.
4. Add takeRateLimitSlots per user, for example 20 matches per hour.

**Evidence.**
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:20-25 — only checks that the submitter appears in body.participants
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:126-149 — upserts user_stats for every participant; line 136 overwrites user_display_name with the client-supplied name
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:291 — participant display name is free text from the request (32 chars)
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:177-186 — PXP dedupe key is per matchId, so a new matchId awards again
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/globalLeaderboards.ts:46 — leaderboard shows user_stats.user_display_name
- partykit/presenceServer.ts:939 — school block exists only on PvP invites, not on result submission
- src/partykit/pvpMatchRuntime.ts:45-48 — match participants taken from the configuring client's message
- src/cloudflare/worker/avatars/routes.ts:227-233 — player level 10 gate that PXP farming reaches
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:22-25 — only checks that the caller is listed as a participant
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:27-44 — duplicate check is a separate read of a client-chosen matchId
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:113-150 — awards XP and upserts user_stats for every client-listed participant, overwriting user_display_name (136)
- src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:199-271 — validation is shape-only; finalSnapshot passed through (270) and stored (80)
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/globalLeaderboards.ts:44-47 — leaderboard entries use user_stats.user_display_name
- partykit/presenceServer.ts:1274-1283 — the presence object already finalizes the match server-side
- src/cloudflare/presence/durableObject.ts:73 — the presence DO receives the full Env (including DB)
- src/scenes/overworld/pvpArenaController.ts:466-467,517-559 — both clients submit the same match when it completes

**Fact-check (partially confirmed, partially confirmed, confirmed).**

The defect holds exactly as described. Two corrections:

1. The leaderboard rename only shows where the victim's row is displayed: the top 50, the victim's own row, and the "player above you" row.

2. The fix plan needs changing:
   - PvP rooms now run in the API Worker's PresenceDurableObject (env.PRESENCE_ROOMS), not PartyKit, so no internal-token fetch is needed.
   - The room deletes its stored match when the last socket closes (presenceServer.ts:418-423). Clients leave about 450 ms after the match completes. A Worker-side fetch of the final snapshot would therefore race and lose. Instead, have the DO write the completed result to D1 itself in finalizePvpMatch/finalizePvpForfeit, using the server-held identities, display names and connected participants. Turn the client POST into a no-op or read, or keep completed matches for a few minutes.
   - Still reject school participants, and still add a per-user rate limit or a daily PvP PXP cap. Hits in the room are client-reported (pvp:match:hit), so two alt accounts could still farm.

The defect and evidence hold. Three corrections:

1. **Scope of the harm**
   - Forged PvP PXP raises player level and avatar unlocks only. It does not change global leaderboard rank, which uses total_points; PvP gives no points.
   - A forged leaderboard name shows only where the victim's row appears: the top 50, their own row, or as someone's "next above". It lasts until upsertUserStats runs: the victim's next run or publish, or someone clearing one of their rooms.
   - Fake PvP win/loss/draw counts are permanent on the victim's profile, because upsertUserStats never resets the pvp_* columns.

2. **Fix step 1 needs a different mechanism**
   - PvP rooms return 404 to HTTP at two layers (presenceServer.ts:225-228 and presence/durableObject.ts:51-57).
   - A room deletes its stored match once both sockets close (presenceServer.ts:418-424), so a Worker fetching it afterwards would race the deletion.
   - Instead, have the PvP room DO, which already has env.DB (durableObject.ts:73), record the result to D1 when the match finalizes. Or keep the completed snapshot with a TTL and read it through env.PRESENCE_ROOMS.
   - Either way, accept results only for participants who actually connected.

3. **Room checks alone are not enough**
   - The room still trusts hits that clients report, so two colluding accounts could still farm.
   - Keep the per-user rate limit or add a daily PvP XP cap, plus the school-context check and server-side display names (users.display_name).

I checked every evidence line against 2d540764 and tried to refute the finding. I couldn't.

**The route trusts the request body.**
- handlePvpMatchSubmit (src/cloudflare/worker/pvp/routes.ts:19-25) requires only auth with the runs:write scope, plus the caller's userId appearing in body.participants.
- normalizePvpMatchSubmission (204-272) checks shape only: the result must be win or draw, there must be exactly one winner and one loser, and the IDs must be consistent. finalSnapshot is passed through (270) and stored (80).
- normalizeParticipants (274-301) takes the userDisplayName as free text capped at 32 characters (291).
- For every listed participant, the route inserts pvp_match_players (83-109) and calls awardLaneDelta. It awards 20, 10 or 6 PXP (lines 15-17), and the dedupe key `pxp:pvp_match:${matchId}:${userId}` (184) contains the client-chosen matchId.
