- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/weeklyRoomRushStore.ts:68-79 — admin can schedule at most this week plus four
- src/ui/setup/roomRushModal.ts:178-184 — players see 'This week's Rush room has not been chosen yet.' and a disabled button
- src/cloudflare/worker/buildPrompts/store.ts:89-90 — current prompt is null unless a row was hand-entered
- src/ui/setup/buildPrompts.ts:154 — 'No prompt scheduled yet.' copy
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:94-131 — Room of the Day already has an automatic weighted chooser to reuse
- progress.md:638 — 'Build Prompt and Room Rush remain unlaunched'

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The core gap is real. Weekly Rush and Build Prompt are live, but they stay empty until an admin row is written. No cron or automatic fallback exists, unlike Room of the Day.
  
  Corrections:
  (a) Manual picking was a deliberate design (see progress.md:893 and :1361, and the F151 fact-check). Present this as an opt-in fallback for Jonathan to approve, not as a missing piece. The prompt bank needs Jonathan to write or approve the content.
  (b) The work needs a migration for picked_by, which neither table has. It also needs either exporting loadCandidates (private, and limited to played goal rooms) or a new Rush-specific candidate query with a new neighbour-count query.
  (c) Run the fallback from the existing hourly scheduled handler and pre-fill next week's slot several days early, so it appears in Launch Admin for review. Do not pick lazily at Monday 00:00. Rush weeks lock at the first ranked start and prompts lock at the first entry, so a lazy pick leaves almost no override window. For prompts, an override means editing the auto prompt's slug or deleting it, because saving another slug for the same week fails.
  (d) Drop the weekday/weekend difficulty weighting for the hard-only Rush.
  
  The Rush fallback on its own is small. Both together, with a migration, tests and prompt content, are about medium.
- **partially confirmed.** Both events are empty because Jonathan has not launched them yet, on purpose (feature-ledger.md:790, 810; progress.md:893). It is not because they need hand-scheduling every week: Build Prompts can be queued for any future Monday, and Rush five weeks ahead.
  
  Reframe it as a decision for Jonathan. Option A: pre-load a season of prompts and a month of Rush rooms. Option B: an automatic fallback (picked_by='automatic' plus a migration, a stable-room preference and an admin override). Gate the Rush fallback on F203 run checking, because an auto-launched ranked weekly board with public winners widens that open exploit. Auto-picks also need to avoid community rooms likely to be republished, since a locked week pauses on any version change (weeklyRoomRushStore.ts:44-49).
  
  The cheapest fix for "an empty event is worse than none": hide the This Week's Rush button and the Explore Build Prompt button while no event is set.
  
  'No prompt scheduled yet' only appears before the first prompt ever runs. After that, the last closed prompt is shown (buildPrompts/store.ts:168-171).
- **partially confirmed.** Both features are idle by Jonathan's recorded choice (F128 'first theme unset by human choice'; the F151 fact-check chose hand picks), so present this as a decision for him. Build Prompts need no code: admin saves have no future-week limit, so a season of prompts can be scheduled in Launch Admin today. Only the Rush needs an automatic fallback, because hand scheduling stops at this week plus four. That fallback needs a new candidate query: daily loadCandidates is private, requires a goal and a verified clear, and has no type or neighbour filter. It also needs re-pick logic for unlocked weeks whose start room was republished (mapRoomRushWeekPick pauses the week otherwise), a migration if picked_by is wanted, and tests. progress.md:638 is from 10-09; current production state is unverified.

### F428: 'Can you do better?' share links don't let your friend race you: send your ghost with the link

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F142

**Summary.** When you beat a room, the share text says "I beat X in 12.3s. Can you do better?", but the link only opens the room. Your friend never sees your time or your run. WAMP already saves a replay of every verified clear, including guest clears. Adding your run's ID to the link would let your friend race your see-through ghost and try to beat your exact time. That makes every shared clear a personal challenge, and a reason for the friend to share back.

**Technical detail.**

Gap: runShare.ts builds the text 'I beat … in WAMP in {time}. Can you do better?' (runShare.ts:9-15), but buildRunShareUrl → buildAttributedRoomShareUrl strips every parameter except from=share (roomShareLinks.ts:22-27). The ghost endpoint returns only 'top' and 'personal' (ghosts.ts:83-104; RoomGhostResponse at runs/ghostRace.ts:18-20; GhostRaceChoice = 'off'|'top'|'personal' at :7). So the recipient can race the #1 ghost or their own, never the sharer's.

Building blocks already in place: (1) run_ghost_archive keeps every completed verified ordinary-room recording, signed-in and guest (migrations/0063:3-17; prepareRunGhostArchive is called from runs/routes.ts:443 and guestRuns/attempts.ts:179). Guest ghosts are already anonymised as displayName 'Guest' (attempts.ts:170-171). (2) loadArchivedRunGhost(env, attemptId) fetches any archived run by ID (ghostArchive.ts:47-58). (3) loadGhostOption already validates room, version and elapsed time against a leaderboard-style entry (ghosts.ts:54-81). (4) The client knows the attempt ID at finish (goalRuns.ts:828, 1079), and the post-run share sites are runRatingModal.ts:157, 694-695 and 1098-1099.

Smallest shippable version (about 120 lines): add attemptId to PostRunRatingRequestDetail (postRunRatingEvents.ts:11-24). Append &vs=<attemptId> in buildRunShareUrl for time-ranked standalone rooms. Have handleRoomGhosts accept ?vs= and return a third option, challenge: {ghost, reason}, after checking that the archive row's room_id matches and its version is in selection.equivalentRoomVersions. Add 'challenge' to GhostRaceChoice and pre-select it in GhostRaceIntro (ghostRaceIntro.ts:33-60) when the page URL carries vs, labelled 'Beat {name} · 12.34s'. The OG description on /r/x/y can say 'Race {name}'s 12.34s'. Cost: one R2 read per challenge open ($0.36 per million reads, ghostArchiveCosts.ts:14-19). Ghosts are capped at 300 KB (ghostRace.ts:6); a 15 s run at the 250 ms breadcrumb rate is about 60 points, a few KB.

Follow-up on the same rails: the activity inbox reports only a lost #1 (trigger builder_activity_top1, migrations/0055:82-104). A 'Sam passed you on Lava Leap — race their ghost' entry could use this same vs link.

Why it moves retention: an asynchronous rivalry needs no one else online, works for guests (most sharers), and every reply is a new share.

**Evidence.**

- src/social/runShare.ts:9-15 — share text ends 'Can you do better?'
- src/social/roomShareLinks.ts:22-27 — share URL keeps only from=share; no run or ghost reference
- src/runs/ghostRace.ts:7 — GhostRaceChoice is only 'off' | 'top' | 'personal'
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghosts.ts:83-104 — handleRoomGhosts returns only top and personal options
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghostArchive.ts:47-58 — any archived run can be loaded by attemptId
- migrations/0063_run_ghost_archive.sql:3-17 — archive stores every completed room and guest_room recording
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/attempts.ts:168-171 — guest ghosts are built with displayName 'Guest'
- src/progression/postRunRatingEvents.ts:11-24 — post-run detail has no attemptId to put in a link
- src/scenes/overworld/goalRuns.ts:828 — client stores the server attemptId for the run

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Scope: only ordinary rooms with time-ranked goals have archived ghosts. Course, Expanded Room and score-ranked shares can't include a ghost. Guest post-run details already carry guestProgress.attemptId, so only signed-in clears need attemptId added. Add vs only after the clear is saved and verified (guest status 'saved', or the signed-in finish accepted); otherwise the archive row doesn't exist yet. Decide whether fetching any archived run by attemptId is acceptable, since leaderboard attempt IDs are public and today personal ghosts are owner-only, or use a signed vs token. Pass vs through loadRoomGhosts/loadRaceGhost and the Restart refresh in scenes/overworld/ghostRace.ts. Expect about 200-300 lines with tests, not 120.
- **partially confirmed.** The core idea holds, but several details need correcting. Only signed-in ranked runs have an attempt ID when the run finishes (goalRuns.ts:828). Guest attempt IDs arrive later through guestProgress, once a verified save succeeds. Queued, offline or unverified guest clears have no ID, so the share URL must update on GUEST_RUN_PROGRESS_CHANGED, and some guest shares will never carry vs. The feature covers only time-ranked ordinary rooms; course, Expanded Room and score-ranked shares get nothing. The 'challenge' choice must also be threaded through the Restart refresh in scenes/overworld/ghostRace.ts:120-130 and OverworldPlayScene.ts:2739, the race label at ghostRace.ts:96 and the select options in roomGoalIntroModal.ts:197-198. vs has to be cleared when navigating to other rooms, and the OG text adds a D1 read in share/routes.ts. Guest challengers show up as "Guest". The "Race my ghost" share variant was first proposed in F136, which was merged into F142, and dropped from F142's delivery. Realistic size: medium effort, medium impact.
- **partially confirmed.** The idea holds, with these corrections.
  - Guest post-run details already carry the attempt ID (detail.guestProgress.attemptId, refreshed by runRatingModal.getCurrentGuestSaveResult). Only signed-in runs need attemptId added. Guest challenges will read "Beat Guest".
  - Effort is medium, not small. 'challenge' must be threaded through ghostRepository.loadRoomGhosts/loadRaceGhost, the overworld OverworldGhostRaceController restart refresh path (ghostRace.ts:117-140), updateRaceInfo labels, GhostRaceIntro and its index.html option, roomGoalIntroModal, the worker handler, runShare and tests.
  - The server should check room_id and equivalent versions on the D1 archive row before any R2 read, and apply the same moderation/hidden-user filtering the leaderboard rows use.
  - The client must scope or strip ?vs=, because setFocusedCoordinatesInUrl carries it to every room.
  - Label with the server ghost.elapsedMs.
  - The OG description change is optional.

### F429: After beating a room in free play there's no 'Next room' button: offer the next unbeaten room

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F096

**Summary.** When you clear a room you found yourself (not from a playlist), you get a short 'ROOM CLEAR!' card and then nothing tells you where to go next. The 'Next' button exists only inside playlists and Explore's Play All. That part of the earlier clear-feedback fix was deliberately left for later. A 'Keep playing →' button that jumps to a room you haven't beaten would turn one clear into a session.

**Technical detail.**

The clear card from createPostRunClearReward is a timed sting with no actions (rewardStings.ts:188-213). The F096 fact-check says a Next button 'exists today only inside room sequences' and that free-roam Next 'needs new logic to choose the target' (docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10-details.md:3717-3718). The F096 delivery scope explicitly left 'Free-roam destination selection' as separate work (feature-ledger.md:1020). Nothing has been added since.

Building blocks: Explore already has personal sorts 'unbeaten' and 'unvisited' (runs/model.ts:18-28), served by loadRoomDiscovery(difficulty, sort, limit) (runRepository.ts:188-194). requestExploreQueueStart turns a result list into a Play All sequence with the existing room-sequence HUD and Next button (exploreQueueEvents.ts:15-37). Guests can't use personal sorts (401 at difficulty.ts:281-283), but their clears are stored locally with roomCoordinates (guestRunProgress.ts:11-25), so the 'popular' list (public-cached) can be filtered on the client.

Smallest version (about 100 lines, client only): on a free-roam clear, prefetch one discovery page: 'unbeaten' for signed-in players, 'popular' minus local clears for guests, excluding the room just cleared and, if possible, matching its difficulty. Add a 'Keep playing →' action to the clear card (or a small chip that stays until the player moves). On tap, call requestExploreQueueStart({mode:'play', entries, sourceLabel:'Keep playing'}). Cost: one discovery request per clear (48-row page), no new Worker code.

Why: the moment after a clear is when a player is most engaged. Today they must open Explore or walk off blind, and the many single-room visitors from shared links end their session there.

**Evidence.**

- src/progression/rewardStings.ts:188-213 — clear card has no actions
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10-details.md:3717-3718 — Next exists only in sequences; free-roam Next needs new target logic
- feature-ledger.md:1020 — F096 scope left free-roam destination selection as separate work
- src/runs/model.ts:18-28 — discovery sorts include 'unbeaten' and 'unvisited'
- src/ui/setup/exploreQueueEvents.ts:15-37 — existing call that starts a Play All sequence from discovery entries
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/difficulty.ts:281-283 — personal sorts require sign-in (guest path must filter locally)
- src/progression/guestRunProgress.ts:11-25 — guest clears keep roomCoordinates for local filtering

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: free-roam clears offer no specific next room, and F096 deliberately left this out. The details need correcting:
  1. Signed-in players see the ROOM CLEAR card only on their first clear of a room version (goalRuns.ts:1036-1050). Guests see it on every clear for 2.6 s.
  2. The sting layer has pointer-events: none (rewards-xp.css:10), so it cannot take a button without new renderer and CSS work. Host the action in a persistent chip instead. The PostRunReminderController chip (#post-run-reminder, postRunReminder.ts) already follows this pattern.
  3. 'unbeaten' and 'unvisited' run the legacy full-world path with a per-viewer state lookup and a private, no-store response (difficulty.ts:284-306 and 420-433). Fetch on tap, not on every clear.
  4. Hide the action while a room sequence is active; RoomSequenceController needs a small public flag or event for this.
  5. Players can already walk into neighbouring rooms, so the gap is a targeted suggestion, not a total dead end.
  6. Rate it medium impact and medium effort; about 100 lines is optimistic.
- **partially confirmed.** The action can't go on the clear card: the sting layer has pointer-events:none, the card disappears after about 2.6 s, and signed-in players only get it on their first clear of a version. Build it as a persistent 'Keep playing →' chip shown in play-world after any goal clear when no room sequence is active. Also give the guest claim modal's existing 'Keep Playing' button (runRatingModal.ts:1033) a real destination. Fetch the target on tap, not on every clear: 'unbeaten' for signed-in players, 'popular' minus local clears for guests, with a fallback to any difficulty because many levels have no label. Lower the impact to medium: the overworld already lets players walk into neighbouring rooms, and nothing measures free-roam clears or sessions ending after shared links (F127 is open).
- **partially confirmed.** Real and unbuilt, but the build is wrong as described:
  - The reward sting can't take an action. It is `pointer-events: none`, `role=status` and hides itself after 1.55-2.6 s. Build a separate persistent 'Keep playing' HUD chip, triggered from the run-complete path. Signed-in players see the clear card only on a first clear (goalRuns.ts:1036).
  - Hide the chip when `body.dataset.roomSequenceActive==='true'`, for co-op and assisted runs, and in Room Rush.
  - Fetch the destination lazily: 'unbeaten' for signed-in players, Popular minus local clears for guests.
  - Start the run with `requestRoomSequenceStart` and its own label (`requestExploreQueueStart` hardcodes 'Play All').
  - Also wire the guest claim modal's dismiss-only 'Keep Playing' button (runRatingModal.ts:1033) to the same destination.
  
  Size and impact:
  - About 200-350 lines with tests and phone checks, not 100. Effort stays medium.
  - Impact is medium, not high: neighbouring rooms are already walkable and there is no return-visit data.

### F435: The world map doesn't show which rooms you've already beaten

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The map marks rooms where you found a Lost Song, but not rooms you've cleared. Players can't see their progress across the world or spot the unbeaten rooms right next to them. A small 'beaten' mark on each cleared room would make the map a progress board and a to-do list. The server already tracks clears per player; it just never sends them to the map.

**Technical detail.**

roomCells.ts only has a hook for found Lost Songs (host.hasFoundLostSong, :24). It draws a gold inset frame only for those (:102-104). There is no cleared, visited or beaten state anywhere in the map cell renderer.

Building blocks: the server already computes per-viewer visited, completed and rated state from room_runs (loadDiscoveryViewerRoomStates, runs/discoveryViewerStates.ts:20-60) to power Explore's 'unbeaten' sort. The Lost Song feature already shows the exact client pattern needed: a paged ID list endpoint (lostSongs/progress.ts:6-16, 512 IDs per page) and a once-per-session cached Set (lostSongs/service.ts:66-82) that the map reads synchronously. Guest clears are stored locally with roomCoordinates (guestRunProgress.ts:11-25).

Smallest version (about 150 lines): GET /api/me/cleared-rooms returns DISTINCT room_id FROM room_runs WHERE user_id=? AND result='completed' with accepted verification, paged like Lost Songs. Add a ClearedRoomService that mirrors LostSongService and merges guest records. Add hasClearedRoom to the room-cell host. Draw a corner tick in browse mode, using a shape rather than only a colour for colour-blind players (see F179). Optionally show 'Beaten 34 rooms' in the existing HUD counter row next to 'Songs N'.

Why: spatial progress is the cheapest completionist hook, and it uses the map, which is WAMP's main navigation surface.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/roomCells.ts:24 — map host exposes only hasFoundLostSong
- src/scenes/overworld/roomCells.ts:102-104 — only found Lost Songs get a map marker
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/discoveryViewerStates.ts:20-60 — per-viewer completed state is already computed from room_runs
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/progress.ts:6-16 — paged ID-list endpoint pattern to copy
- src/lostSongs/service.ts:66-82 — once-per-session cached Set pattern
- src/progression/guestRunProgress.ts:11-25 — guest clears keep roomCoordinates

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F433: Players are never told Lost Songs exist, how many there are, or where to look

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F144

**Summary.** The Lost Song hunt is hidden from players. The 'Songs' counter stays invisible until you find your first one, the only explanation is in the builders' object picker, and there's no 'found 12 of 87'. The map only marks songs you've already found. Showing the total, a short first-time hint, and an Explore filter for rooms with a song you haven't found would turn a hidden easter egg into a world-wide hunt.

**Technical detail.**

The counter is hidden while total is 0 (ui/setup/lostSongs.ts:12-15), and it only ever shows found count ('Songs N'). The only copy about Lost Songs is builder-facing: 'Hide a Lost Song for explorers…' (index.html:862). The map marks only found rooms (roomCells.ts:102-104). No table or summary records which published rooms contain a song. The world summary query has no such column (rooms/worldSummaries.ts:12-43), and neither does the trigger-maintained world_tile_published_room_summaries (migrations/0042:4-16, triggers at :65-160). The data exists inside published_json, which is where targets.ts:41-43 finds the song. Rewards already exist: 5 XP per find, capped at 10 XP finds per day (lostSongs/model.ts:4-5), and badges at 1/10/100 (lostSongs/progress.ts:33-36).

Smallest version: (1) migration adds has_lost_song to world_tile_published_room_summaries and the playable_content_index member rows, computed in the existing triggers with EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM json_each(NEW.published_json,'$.placedObjects') WHERE json_extract(value,'$.id')='lost_song'), plus a backfill. (2) GET /api/lost-songs/total returns a public-cached count, minus the viewer's own rooms client-side. The counter shows 'Songs 12/87' and is always visible once the total is above 0. (3) Add a 'Lost Songs' discovery sort: rooms with has_lost_song, excluding found ones client-side. (4) Optional hot/cold hint: a faint cassette outline on unfound-song rooms only at close browse zoom, so the hunt stays a search rather than a checklist. (5) A one-line tooltip the first time a player enters a room with a song.

Why: a collectathon needs a visible denominator to pull players onward, and it sends traffic to the builders who hid songs. It also gives Jonathan a number showing whether builders use the feature at all.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/lostSongs.ts:12-15 — counter hidden at 0 and shows only found count
- index.html:862 — the only Lost Song copy is in the builder object picker
- src/scenes/overworld/roomCells.ts:102-104 — map marks only already-found songs
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/worldSummaries.ts:12-43 — room summaries carry no Lost Song flag
- migrations/0042_world_tile_published_room_summaries.sql:4-16 — summary table has no Lost Song column
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/targets.ts:41-43 — song placement is available in published_json
- src/cloudflare/worker/lostSongs/progress.ts:33-36 — 1/10/100 badges already exist to aim players at

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real gap, but narrower than "never told". Signed-in profiles already show "Lost Songs found: 0", and the cassette is visible in rooms, with a toast when it is picked up. What is missing is a world total, any explanation before the first find, and any way to find rooms that have songs. Song placement is at targets.ts:35-36, not :41-43. Only world_tile_published_room_summaries is maintained by triggers. Those three triggers have to be dropped and recreated to add a column. playable_content_index is maintained in Worker code (playableContentIndex/store.ts). Recommended order:
  1. Compute the total of published song cells in maintenance/hourly.ts and serve it as one public cached value. The server subtracts the viewer's own song rooms. Show "Songs N/M" plus a one-time tooltip the first time a player reaches a room with a cassette. No migration is needed for this, and the number also measures adoption.
  2. Only if adoption justifies it: add a has_lost_song column through the migration and Worker index code, and a discovery sort. For signed-in users, exclude found rooms on the server with NOT EXISTS against user_lost_songs. Filter on the client only for guests.

### F434: The person who receives a Wamp-O-Gram never sees the sender's message, and the link preview isn't the postcard

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Gap review: Small untested features: Wamp-O-Gram, Playlists, Guestbook, Collections)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** The sender writes a To/From note and a message, and sees a nice postcard while making it. The recipient opens the link and lands in the room with one status line made from the title and names. The message is never shown. The image in the link preview is also a plain room picture, not the postcard. Showing the postcard as a card before play, with a 'Send one back' button, would complete the feature and give it a way to spread.

**Technical detail.**

loadWampOGramLaunchFromCurrentUrl (src/wampOGram/launch.ts:30-47) builds statusMessage from recipientName, senderName/creatorDisplayName and the title only. record.message is never read anywhere on the client after load (a grep for wampOGram in the scenes and UI finds only the editor modal).

The 240-character message (model.ts:10) shows up only in the og:description (shareMetadata.ts:323), which many apps truncate or hide. The client postcard renderer draws title, To, message and From (render.ts:110-144). But the og:image is /api/wamp-o-grams/:slug/preview.png (shareMetadata.ts:248), which runs the plain room renderer renderRoomSharePreviewPng (wampOGram/routes.ts:101). So the unfurl never looks like the card the sender designed.

Fix, reusing existing pieces:
1. Add a small WampOGramIntro controller on the playlistIntroModal pattern (createModalLifecycle, playlistIntroModal.ts:43-47 and 60-75). It opens on Boot handoff and shows renderWampOGramPostcardToCanvas(record.roomSnapshot, record) (render.ts:16-45) with Play, Reply ('Make one back' opens the editor and clicks #btn-wamp-o-gram, as firstPublishModal.ts:206 already does), and Visit the real room.
2. In the worker preview, draw the postcard frame (the paper and stripes from drawPostcardPaper) around the room render, so the unfurl reads as a postcard.

About 120 new lines. There is no backend change apart from the frame.

**Evidence.**

- src/wampOGram/launch.ts:30-47 — statusMessage uses title/recipient/sender; message is never used
- src/wampOGram/render.ts:110-144 — sender's preview postcard draws the message the recipient never sees
- src/pages/shareMetadata.ts:239-250 — og:image points at the server preview.png
- src/cloudflare/worker/wampOGram/routes.ts:101 — preview.png is the plain room render, not the postcard
- src/ui/setup/playlistIntroModal.ts:43-47,60-75 — reusable intro-card lifecycle pattern

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: the recipient never sees record.message in the app. launch.ts uses only the title and names, and only as a transient status line. The message reaches only og:description (shareMetadata.ts:324). og:image is the plain room render (routes.ts:65,101). Three corrections to the fix:
  (a) The worker preview renderer has no text or font capability. Adding the paper frame gives stripes but no To, From or message text, so it won't match the client postcard without adding a bitmap font.
  (b) 'Make one back' can't simply click #btn-wamp-o-gram as firstPublishModal does. That button and WampOGramModal need the recipient's own EditorScene room and sign-in, and the recipient is playing someone else's draft copy in OverworldPlayScene. The reply needs a sign-in plus an editable-room flow, or should be cut down to 'Build your own'.
  (c) The effort is above about 120 lines: modal HTML, CSS, controller, LazyModal and Boot handoff wiring, and tests. An intro card with Play and Visit room alone is small.
- **partially confirmed.** The game never shows the sender's message: the recipient gets a 4.2-second status line with the title and names (launch.ts:34-46; OverworldPlayScene.ts:2005-2008). The link preview does include the message as og:description, which Slack, Discord, WhatsApp and X show, and the sender can download the postcard PNG. So "never sees" holds only inside the game and on apps that hide descriptions, such as iMessage.
  
  The worthwhile fix is a boot-time WampOGram intro card using the playlistIntroModal pattern. It shows renderWampOGramPostcardToCanvas(record.roomSnapshot, record) with a Play button, and must not stack on the Welcome or room-goal modals (as in F093). That part is small.
  
  "Make one back" cannot just click #btn-wamp-o-gram. That needs an active EditorScene on the viewer's own room (wampOGramModal.ts:149-156) and a signed-in account with the rooms:write scope. So the button has to send the recipient through sign-in and building or claiming a room, or be cut back to "Make your own".
  
  Drop or deprioritise the worker frame. roomPreviewImage.ts has no text drawing, so the link preview image still could not show To, From or the message. The room render also fills y 18 to 612 of 630, so the frame needs a new layout. The result would be cosmetic, not a postcard.
- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: the recipient sees only a 4.2 s status line with the title and names (launch.ts:34-46; OverworldPlayScene.ts:2005-2008), never the message, and og:image is the plain room render (routes.ts:65/101).
  
  Corrections:
  - The message does reach Slack, Discord and X unfurls through og:description (shareMetadata.ts:324). The sender can also download the real postcard PNG.
  - "Make one back" cannot just click #btn-wamp-o-gram. The modal needs an active editor scene and sign-in (wampOGramModal.ts:149, :226), and the recipient is usually a guest playing a draft copy of the sender's room. Use a "Make your own" exit to the world or build flow instead, or add a sign-in plus own-room routing step.
  - The worker "frame" only adds colored edges. The room fills 1080x594 of the 1200x630 image, and the worker renderer cannot draw text. A real postcard unfurl needs a re-layout plus a bitmap font, or uploading the client-rendered PNG at create time (R2 plus a route). Treat that as a separate medium item.
  
  Scope this item to a lazily loaded intro card on the Wamp-O-Gram launch with Play, Visit room and Make your own: about 150-250 lines including the HTML, CSS, LazyModal and budget entry, the boot-to-UI bridge, and tests. Impact is medium.

### F432: No way to follow a builder you like and hear when they publish something new

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F123

**Summary.** If you love someone's rooms, the only way to find their next one is to check their profile again by hand. A 'Follow' button on profiles, plus an inbox note when a followed builder publishes, would give players a reason to come back. It would also give builders an audience that grows over time. The activity inbox, weekly email and profile pages already exist, so this mostly connects existing pieces.

**Technical detail.**

There is no follow table or route (no 'follow' match in migrations or the worker). The activity inbox is fed only by triggers for completions, ratings, comments and #1 changes, and its kind column is a CHECK enum: 'completion','rating','comment','top1','dethroned' (migrations/0055_builder_activity.sql:7; src/activity/model.ts:1). The weekly digest queues only for users who already have builder activity that week (emails.ts:62-71, via emailActivityExistsSql at store.ts:43-47), so people who only play never get one.

Building blocks: the profile modal already has Copy Link and Activity buttons where a Follow button fits (index.html:2848-2850). Builder discovery sorts exist ('alphabet','rooms','recent', runs/model.ts:30). The inbox UI, unread counts and email outbox with leases and unsubscribe tokens are all in activity/. publishRoom (rooms/store.ts:983) and the expanded-room publish path are single hook points.

Smallest version: (1) migration user_follows(follower_user_id, builder_user_id, created_at, PK both) plus follow_activity(id, recipient, builder, content_type, content_id, version, created_at). Use a new table because SQLite can't widen the CHECK on builder_activity without a rebuild. (2) POST/DELETE /api/follows/:userId and GET /api/follows, rate-limited. (3) After a first publish (not republish; F201's republish rules show why), fan out at most N rows per follower per day. (4) The inbox merges follow_activity rows as 'X published a new room'. Add an Explore 'Following' chip that filters newest by followed builder IDs. (5) The digest adds a 'New from builders you follow' section and drops the builder-activity-only eligibility gate. About 300-400 lines across Worker and UI.

Why: it is the standard UGC retention loop (players return for creators; creators publish more because they have an audience). It also makes the F123 builder notifications two-way.

**Evidence.**

- migrations/0055_builder_activity.sql:7 — activity kinds are a fixed CHECK list; no follow or new-room kind
- src/activity/model.ts:1 — client ActivityKind has no follow-related kind
- src/cloudflare/worker/activity/emails.ts:62-71 — weekly digest queues only when the user has builder activity
- index.html:2848-2850 — profile header Activity / Copy Link buttons (where Follow fits)
- src/runs/model.ts:30 — builder discovery sorts exist to reuse for a Following filter
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:983 — publishRoom is the single hook for fan-out

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** Real and not built, but impact is medium rather than high. With the current community size, Explore Newest and the 'recent' builder sort already show most new rooms, so follow notifications would be rare until there are more builders. The design also needs three changes. First, weekly_digest is opt-in and off by default, so removing the builder-activity gate alone won't reach players; prompt them to opt in when they first follow someone. Second, a 'Following' Explore filter is per viewer, so it has to skip the shared public discovery cache. Third, fan-out has to cover course and Expanded Room publishing as well as publishRoom. Expect more than 300-400 lines once tests are included; effort is still medium.
- **partially confirmed.** The gap and the building blocks are real. Three parts of the proposed design need changing:
  (a) Don't add a follow_activity table with fan-out at publish time. Store only user_follows and build "new from builders you follow" when it is read, by joining user_follows with playable_content_index on builder_user_id and first_published_at. That one query covers rooms, courses and expanded rooms, needs no per-follower cap, and only picks up first publishes. Hooking only publishRoom would miss publishCourse (courses/store.ts:354) and expanded-room publishes.
  (b) Merging this into the activity inbox needs a second unseen cursor, or a separate "Following" section, because unread state is one seen_id compared with builder_activity.id (activity/store.ts:54/72/107).
  (c) The Explore 'Following' chip needs its own private, uncached endpoint. Room discovery has no builder filter, and its public cache must not see viewer data (discoveryPublicCache.ts:6).
  The digest part only reaches players who have an email account. xp-badges-ratings-prd.md:1099 records follow/feed as an open owner question, so get the owner's decision before building.
  Effort: medium for an MVP (follow button, user_follows, rate-limited POST/DELETE/GET, a read-time Following list in the inbox). Large for the full five-part spec with digest and Explore changes, well over 300-400 lines with tests.

### F431: Idea: give touch players a 'whole room' view button; the code for it already exists, only the button is missing

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Mobile play on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Upright phones show only about half of a room's width at a time, so players can't see what's ahead. Keyboard and gamepad players can flip to a whole-room view mid-run (the 9 key or a gamepad button), but touch players can't. The game already has a touch 'camera toggle' action wired in. Adding one small button to the touch controls would let phone players look around.

**Technical detail.**

Portrait zoom is twice the fit zoom (OverworldPlayScene.ts:381 MOBILE_PORTRAIT_PLAY_CAMERA_ZOOM_MULTIPLIER = 2), and the fit padding is 16 (composition/settings.ts:9). On a 390px phone, fit = (390-16)/640 = 0.584, so zoom is about 1.17. That shows about 334 of the room's 640 world pixels, roughly 21 of 40 tiles. A 360px Android phone sees about 335px.

The toggle exists end to end:
- TouchActionName includes 'cameraToggle' (touchControls.ts:3).
- framePipeline.ts:246 consumes it, and cameraController.toggleCameraMode switches follow/inspect (cameraController.ts:142-152).
- The keyboard binds Digit9 (keyBindings.ts:10), the gamepad uses button 11, and the mann.cool parent maps '9'.
- But portraitPlayControls binds only jump/slash/shoot/stop/restart (:147-162), and nothing calls pressTouchAction('cameraToggle').

Settings has a 'Whole room' camera style (index.html:3291-3292), but it is a buried, permanent choice, not a quick look.

Build: add a 44px 'View' button to the portrait console header next to Stop/Restart and to the landscape overlay top row. Its click calls pressTouchAction('cameraToggle'). Optionally offer a phone zoom choice (Close / Normal / Wide) that reuses the existing multiplier clamping, normalizeMobilePortraitCameraZoomMultiplier at OverworldPlayScene.ts:3218-3230. Players would get the same look-ahead desktop players have, at about 30 lines.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/mobile/touchControls.ts:3 — 'cameraToggle' is a touch action
- src/scenes/overworld/framePipeline.ts:246 — the frame loop consumes it
- src/scenes/overworld/cameraController.ts:142-152 — toggle between follow and whole-room view
- src/ui/mobile/portraitPlayControls.ts:147-162 — no button presses cameraToggle
- src/settings/keyBindings.ts:10 — keyboard has camera on Digit9
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:381 — portrait zoom multiplier 2
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/settings.ts:9 — fit padding 16
- index.html:3291-3292 — 'Whole room' only as a Settings choice

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Don't wire a button to the existing 'cameraToggle'. That action only switches between follow and inspect, keeps the same 2x portrait zoom, and leaves the camera frozen at half the room's width. The actual whole-room view is the 'room' camera style path (isRoomCameraFixed → syncRoomCamera in cameraController.ts:60-109, run every frame from framePipeline.ts:159).
  
  Build:
  1. Add a session-only room-view override (for example a flag in the camera controller or comfortSettings that is not saved to localStorage) and have isRoomCameraFixed honor it.
  2. Add a 44px 'Room' toggle button to the portrait console and the landscape overlay that flips this flag.
  3. Clear the flag on stop, room change, or when the button is pressed again.
  4. Optionally reuse normalizeMobilePortraitCameraZoomMultiplier for a Close/Normal/Wide choice.
  
  The keyboard/gamepad '9' toggle does not show the whole room either; it only stops the camera following. So the premise that this matches desktop behavior is wrong: on desktop the whole room is already visible.

### F430: Finding a Lost Song gives '+5 XP' and nothing musical: let each find add that room's song to your profile Mixtape

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F234

**Summary.** The Lost Song is a golden cassette, but picking it up just shows 'Lost Song found! +5 player XP.' No music plays and nothing is saved except a count. Each find could 'record' the room's own builder-made music into a Mixtape tab on your profile, where you and visitors can play it back. That ties the hunt to music and to Song A Day, and credits the builder who composed it.

**Technical detail.**

The pickup status is only text: 'Lost Song found!' plus '+5 player XP.' (scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:115). The profile shows only a number, 'Lost Songs found' (profileModalProgressRenderer.ts:160-162). Server progress is just a list of room IDs with found_at (user_lost_songs, migrations/0061:33-43; lostSongs/progress.ts:6-16).

Building blocks: every room snapshot carries builder-composed music (persistence/roomModel.ts:138, music: RoomMusic | null). RoomMusicController.playArrangement(music, {mode}) plays any RoomMusic: pattern, phrase arrangement or stems (music/controller.ts:191-254). The profile modal already has tabs (index.html:2884-2888) and the same paged room-ID list used for progress.

Smallest version: (1) On pickup, change the toast to '♪ Added "{room title}" by {builder} to your Mixtape'. (2) Add a profile 'Mixtape' tab listing found rooms (titles from world summaries), each with ▶. ▶ loads the published snapshot and calls playArrangement(snapshot.music, {mode:'world-play'}), skipping rooms with no music. (3) Optionally show builders 'Your song was collected 14 times'. Start with pattern-music rooms, because arranged rooms still need 26-28 phrase fetches (open F222). A Song A Day variant, where each find unlocks a real song from Jonathan's catalogue, would need a song list feed; none exists in the repo.

Why: it gives the collectathon a reward players can hear and share, and it makes room music part of player identity. It complements the open F234 (music credit and remix), which covers the in-room credit but not keeping a collection.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/lostSongs.ts:115 — pickup reward is only a status line and XP
- src/ui/setup/profileModalProgressRenderer.ts:160-162 — profile shows only a count of songs
- migrations/0061_lost_songs.sql:33-43 — finds stored as room IDs, ready to list
- src/persistence/roomModel.ts:138 — every room snapshot carries builder-composed music
- src/music/controller.ts:191-254 — playArrangement can play any room's music
- index.html:2884-2888 — profile tab bar where a Mixtape tab fits

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Keep the idea, with five corrections.
  1. **The pickup is completely silent.** collection.ts:61-63 skips the collect effect and SFX. Adding a cassette sound and the room title and builder to the toast is a small first step.
  2. **A public view needs new work.** The progress API is owner-only (lostSongs/routes.ts:44-48), so letting visitors see your list needs a new public endpoint and a privacy decision.
  3. **Use the existing endpoints.**
     - Titles and builders: the batch POST /api/rooms/snapshots/query with detail 'overview'.
     - Playback: the cacheable GET /api/rooms/:id/versions/:room_version, using the room_version already stored in user_lost_songs, rather than the latest published snapshot.
  4. **Check how many finds have music first.** Room music defaults to null (roomModel.ts:443). Measure what share of Lost Song rooms have music before building the tab. Cells of expanded rooms and courses play a source room's music.
  5. **Coordinate with world music.** Profile playback shares the global controller and the 'world-play' mode with OverworldRoomMusicPlaybackController. That controller won't restart the room's music afterwards unless it is reset or given a separate mode or restore hook.

### F442: No badges reward the daily and weekly loops, flawless clears, or exploring many builders' rooms

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** There are only eight player badges: first, 10 and 100 clears; first, 10 and 100 Lost Songs; top 10; and #1. Nothing rewards playing Room of the Day regularly, entering a Build Prompt, running the weekly Rush, beating a room without dying, or exploring many different builders' rooms. Those are the behaviours WAMP most wants, and the data for all of them is already recorded. Five or six new badges are a few lines each.

**Technical detail.**

Player badges in BADGE_DEFINITIONS: player_first_clear, first/10/100 Lost Songs, 10/100 clears, top10, top1 (progression/badgesTrophies.ts:46-79). Builders get prompt credit only for winning (builder_prompt_winner, :80-83). The XP PRD's player catalog also lists 'no-death clear', 'first course clear' and 'difficult-room top 10', and says badges should count 'only on unique, non-owned rooms' (xp-badges-ratings-prd.md:816-825). None of these are built.

Data already present: Room of the Day clears are pxp_events with event_type='daily_clear' and source_id=date (daily/store.ts:181, 242-249). Weekly Rush runs carry event_week (migrations/0062:14-20). Build Prompt entries live in build_prompt_entries (0058:14). Deaths and verification are on room_runs. Builder identity per room is available for a distinct-builders count.

Smallest version: add to syncUserBadges (badgesTrophies.ts:353-410) using the existing upsertBadgeAward (:282-321): 'Daily Regular' (Room of the Day cleared on 7 different days; not consecutive, per the PRD's no-streak rule), 'Prompt Entrant' (first Build Prompt entry), 'Flawless' (0-death verified clear of a non-owned room rated medium or harder), 'Globetrotter' (cleared rooms by 10 and 50 different builders), and 'Rush Runner' (finished a weekly Rush). Hold Rush Runner until F203's Rush checks land, since Rush runs are unverified. The badge sting and profile rendering already exist (rewardStings.ts:277-286). About 80 lines plus tests.

Why: badges are the cheapest way to point players at the newer loops. 'Globetrotter' directly serves the PRD's first goal of playing other people's rooms.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/badgesTrophies.ts:46-79 — only eight player badges exist
- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/badgesTrophies.ts:80-83 — Build Prompt credit only for winners
- docs/product/xp-badges-ratings-prd.md:816-825 — planned no-death / course / difficult-room badges not built
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:181 — daily clears are queryable pxp_events by date
- migrations/0062_weekly_room_rush.sql:14-20 — weekly Rush runs carry event_week
- src/cloudflare/worker/progression/badgesTrophies.ts:353-410 — syncUserBadges is the single place to add awards

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The badges are real gaps, the data exists and the work is small. But award Daily Regular and Prompt Entrant at the event (awardDailyClear and prompt entry), as Lost Songs and Prompt Winner are already awarded, not in syncUserBadges. That function runs after every run finish and rating and already makes about 20 D1 calls. In the sync, skip the Globetrotter and Flawless queries once the badge is held. Prompt Entrant is a builder badge. Flawless needs a chosen difficulty source. Rush Runner waits for F203. syncUserBadges spans lines 353-430. Badges only appear after they are earned: the profile shows 3 and the summary keeps the 6 most recent, with no list of unearned badges. So the claim that these badges steer players to the newer loops needs a small locked-badge list too. Without it, they are surprise rewards, and the impact is lower than medium.

### F443: Room of the Day says 'Beaten 3 of the last 7' but gives no way to play the 4 you missed

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F129

**Summary.** The daily panel counts how many of the last seven daily levels you've beaten, but only links to today's. The missed ones are just a number. A 'Play the ones you missed' button would let a player catch up when they return after a few days. That matches the design rule that missing a day should feel soft, not punishing, and it reuses the existing Play All sequence.

**Technical detail.**

The panel renders 'Beaten {n} of the last 7' (ui/setup/dailyRoom.ts:156), and its only play link is /today (:151). The server reads the last 7 picks but selects only date, target_type, content_id, version and legacy_course_id (daily/store.ts:178). The response type exposes only those fields (daily/model.ts:31), even though daily_rooms stores room_x, room_y and title (DailyRow, store.ts:16-21). The 7-day tally counts a pick only when cleared on its own UTC date (daily/guestProgress.ts:9; server pxp_events source_id=date at store.ts:181), so the gap can never close.

The XP PRD asks to 'make loss feel soft' and to 'avoid "you missed a day, start over from zero" punishment' (xp-badges-ratings-prd.md:757-760).

Smallest version (about 60 lines): add room_x, room_y, title and cell_count to the history SELECT and recentPicks. In the modal, list missed days and add a 'Play missed days (4)' button that calls requestRoomSequenceStart (roomSequenceEvents.ts:20-37) with those entries, including expandedRoomId and version fields. Optionally show 'caught up' ticks for late clears without awarding the daily PXP, so the bonus still rewards same-day play.

Why: returning players get a ready-made 5-level session of vetted community rooms, and each daily pick's builder gets a longer tail of plays than one UTC day.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/dailyRoom.ts:156 — 'Beaten N of the last 7' with no way to play the missed ones
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:178 — history query omits coordinates and title
- src/daily/model.ts:31 — recentPicks exposes only date/type/id/version
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:16-21 — daily_rooms already stores room_x, room_y and title
- src/daily/guestProgress.ts:9 — only same-day clears count
- docs/product/xp-badges-ratings-prd.md:757-760 — make loss feel soft, no start-over punishment
- src/ui/setup/roomSequenceEvents.ts:20-37 — existing sequence start API

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The missed picks can already be played. Every daily pick goes into featured_rooms with featured_at (store.ts:131-138), and Explore opens on Featured sort, ordered by featured_at DESC, with Play All. So the gap is discoverability and filtering, not access. The smallest fix is a "Catch up on recent picks" link from the daily modal to Explore's Featured sort. The full "Play missed days" version also needs:
  - the signed-in viewer response to return which dates were completed, not only completedLast7 (store.ts:180-182 returns a count);
  - an availability check for each history row, like dailyPickAvailable at store.ts:140, so removed or ineligible past picks are left out, as Build Prompt does;
  - the history SELECT to add room_id, room_version, target_key, room_x/room_y, title and cell_count.
  
  The play link is set at dailyRoom.ts:153, not :151. Expect about 100-150 lines including tests, not 60.

### F439: Guests and classroom players can't communicate in the world at all: add a small set of emotes

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Speech bubbles are blocked for guests, chat-banned players and classroom accounts, so most visitors standing next to each other can't even say hi. A handful of fixed emotes (wave, heart, GG, '!', laugh) contain no typed text, so there's nothing to moderate. They would let anyone greet, cheer or thank another player. Emotes are already on the product roadmap and reuse the speech-bubble system that exists today.

**Technical detail.**

The presence server drops room-chat bubbles unless canSendRoomChat, which requires source 'auth' and roomChat 'ok' (partykit/presenceServer.ts:874-877; src/presence/identityToken.ts:239-241). The client refuses early with 'unauthenticated' or 'restricted' (src/presence/roomChat.ts:207-215). F131's write-up notes guests are most visitors, so in-world interaction is limited to a minority. The PRD lists 'Emotes / gestures' under v2 (docs/product/product-requirements.md:457), and v3 is still unchecked (:869). No emote code exists in src.

Building blocks: the bubble transport and renderer already handle per-user transient messages: 6 s lifetime, 1 s rate limit (chat/roomChatModel.ts:3-6), the room-scoped broadcast filter (presenceServer.ts:899-912), and Phaser bubbles keyed by userId (scenes/overworld/roomChat.ts:35-67).

Smallest version (about 150 lines): add a RoomChatEmoteMessage {type:'room-chat:emote', emoteId} with a closed enum of 6-8 IDs. Validate the ID on the server and reuse lastRoomChatSentAt for the rate limit. Gate sending on 'not chat-banned' instead of source==='auth', so guests can emote. Keep canReceiveRoomChat as is for school accounts, or allow emotes from classmates only, which keeps F208's protection. Render the emote as an icon bubble through the existing controller, and add 1-6 number keys plus a small touch tray button. The payload is about 40 bytes, so there's no moderation queue and no word filter (F191) dependency.

Why: shared-world presence is WAMP's core promise (product-requirements.md:445-451). Today two guests in the same room are mute ghosts to each other. A wave or 'GG' after a co-op plate (F152) or a duel is the cheapest social glue available.

**Evidence.**

- partykit/presenceServer.ts:874-877 — guests, chat-banned players and classroom accounts cannot send bubbles
- src/presence/identityToken.ts:239-245 — send requires source 'auth'; school accounts cannot receive
- src/presence/roomChat.ts:207-215 — client refuses unauthenticated or restricted senders
- src/chat/roomChatModel.ts:3-6 — existing 140-char / 6 s / 1 s bubble limits to reuse
- src/scenes/overworld/roomChat.ts:35-67 — per-user bubble renderer to reuse for emote icons
- docs/product/product-requirements.md:457 — 'Emotes / gestures' planned; :869 still unchecked

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** In the proposed smallest version, only guests gain the ability to emote, since school and chat-banned accounts stay blocked. Allowing emotes between classmates only needs a new classroom ID claim, because today's token carries just roomChat:'school'. Opening emotes to students at all is a policy decision on top of F208. The simplest build has the server map a closed emoteId enum to fixed strings or glyphs and reuse the existing room-chat broadcast and bubble renderer. It needs a PartyKit deploy as well as Pages. Expect low to medium payoff, given unknown same-room co-presence among guests.

### F437: Duck the room music under reward stings so level-ups and #1 moments land

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Room music and audio)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** When a level-up or leaderboard jingle plays, the room's loop keeps going at full level underneath. It is usually in a different key and tempo, and on its own bus it is slightly louder than the jingle. Briefly lowering the music for the length of the jingle, as console games do, makes these moments feel like a reward instead of a clash. The audio engine already has the controls for this.

**Technical detail.**

Levels: music bus gain is 0.82 × 0.6 × volume = 0.49 (controller.ts:1029-1031); stingers are 0.76-0.80 × GLOBAL_SFX_VOLUME_MULTIPLIER 0.55 ≈ 0.42-0.44 (sfx.ts:84, 336-365). Building blocks: RoomMusicController.setPlaybackDuck ramps the music bus (controller.ts:440-448) but has a single owner today, the room video's 0/1 mute (roomVideo/frameController.ts:534-545). Plan: change it to named duck sources multiplied together (setDuck('video', 0) and setDuck('sting', 0.35)); in RewardStingController.showNext set the sting duck when sfxCue starts and release it after durationMs (ui/setup/rewardStings.ts:111-117; durations from progression/rewardStings.ts:85-91), using a ~80 ms attack and ~400 ms release. Optionally the same for goal-success and the death beat. Small, no new assets.

**Evidence.**

- src/music/controller.ts:440-448 — setPlaybackDuck ramps the music master
- src/music/controller.ts:1029-1031 — music master = 0.82 × 0.6 × volume × duck
- src/roomVideo/frameController.ts:534-545 — the only duck owner is video mute
- src/audio/sfx.ts:84 — effects trimmed by 0.55
- src/ui/setup/rewardStings.ts:111-117 — sting cue and card timer
- src/progression/rewardStings.ts:85-91 — sting durations

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Real and small, but the plan needs three changes. The 'louder than the jingle' claim is only gain arithmetic, not measured loudness. Apply the duck when the sting voice actually starts, not when the card shows: progression stingers lazy-load and can start up to 1.5 s late, and playSfx returns nothing, even when it skips the cue because SFX is muted, set to 0 or the tab is hidden. Hold the duck across queued stings until REWARD_STINGS_IDLE_EVENT or the voice ends. Use the shared musicBus from F229 (src/audio/engine.ts) and add a release time constant to setPlaybackDuck, since it is fixed at 0.02 s today.

### F438: Empty rooms feel dead even though WAMP has recordings of everyone who played them: show recent runs as faint ghosts

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F142

**Summary.** When nobody else is online, every room is empty, yet WAMP has stored a replay of every verified clear. Replaying the two or three most recent runs in a room as faint, named ghosts would make the world feel lived in all day. It would also teach routes and show that real people play these rooms. The ghost-race player and the recording archive already exist.

**Technical detail.**

Building blocks: run_ghost_archive has an index on (room_id, room_version, created_at DESC) (migrations/0063:19-20), so 'latest 3 runs in this room version' is one index seek. loadArchivedRunGhost reads one by ID (ghostArchive.ts:47-58). GhostRacePlayback samples a recording over time (runs/ghostRace.ts:99). OverworldGhostRaceController already draws a presentation-only sprite with alpha 0.42 and a tint, outside Arcade physics, presence, combat and objectives (scenes/overworld/ghostRace.ts:27-70). The PRD's multiplayer promise is that 'seeing a dozen tiny characters bouncing through a room feels alive' (product-requirements.md:450), which today happens only when people happen to be online.

Smallest version: GET /api/rooms/:id/ghosts/recent?version= returns up to 3 archived runs from the last 14 days by distinct users, labelled with the stored display name ('Guest' for guests, attempts.ts:170). Wrap it in loadAnonymousPublicCache (core/publicCache.ts:20) with a 10-minute TTL, so a busy room costs at most about 18 R2 reads and 18 D1 usage writes per hour (recordGhostArchiveOperation writes one D1 row per download, ghostArchiveCosts.ts:20-25). On the client, generalise OverworldGhostRaceController to N looping sprites at alpha 0.25. Show them only in play mode, only when presence reports no live players in the room, and hide them once a timed run or ghost race starts. Add a Comfort toggle ('Show recorded players'). Limits: recordings exist only for time-ranked standalone rooms (supportsGhostRace, runs/ghostRace.ts:21-23).

Why: WAMP's social pitch fails during quiet hours. Asynchronous presence costs pennies and uses data already being paid for.

**Evidence.**

- migrations/0063_run_ghost_archive.sql:19-20 — index on (room_id, room_version, created_at DESC) supports 'recent runs here'
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghostArchive.ts:47-58 — archived ghost loader
- src/runs/ghostRace.ts:99 — GhostRacePlayback reusable for looping playback
- src/scenes/overworld/ghostRace.ts:67 — existing presentation-only ghost sprite (alpha 0.42, tint, no physics)
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/ghostArchiveCosts.ts:14-25 — R2 read cost and per-download D1 usage write (cache needed)
- docs/product/product-requirements.md:450 — 'Presence is the feature — … feels alive'

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The idea is valid but has narrow reach today. Recordings exist only for time-ranked standalone rooms since early October: 51 recordings across about 975 rooms on 2026-10-09. They are not "every verified clear", and some are unverified 'not_required' room runs. Corrections to the plan:
  - Show ambient ghosts only while the current goal run is not 'qualified'. Goal rooms create a practice run as soon as you enter, and the automatic #1 race ghost already covers qualified runs. Hand off cleanly to that race ghost.
  - Have the endpoint require EXISTS in room_runs for source='room'. Admin invalidation deletes room_runs rows but leaves run_ghost_archive untouched, so invalidated cheat runs would otherwise replay.
  - Resolve the current display name rather than the name stored in the payload.
  - Use the leaderboard family's equivalentRoomVersions, not only the exact room version.
  - Note that the edge cache is per data center (still negligible cost) and that guests (NULL user_id) cannot be deduped by user.
  Impact is low until the archive grows.

### F440: Keep downloaded rooms on the device so returning players don't re-download their neighbourhood

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Every visit downloads every nearby room again, through a request that browsers and the CDN are told never to store. Each request names an exact room version that never changes. The game already has a proven on-device cache for world-map tiles. Reusing it for room data would let returning players start playing in their usual area before the network answers, and it would cut database reads on the server.

**Technical detail.**

Today:
- previewCache.ensureRoomSnapshotsBatch sends version-pinned references to POST /api/rooms/snapshots/query (previewCache.ts:151-245). The references carry roomId, coordinates, state and updatedAt.
- The response is 'private, no-store' (rooms/routes.ts:128).
- The only client cache is the in-memory sharedRoomSnapshotCache (256 entries) and the per-session previewCache, both lost on reload.
- The first checkup noted that the arrival-room snapshot batch follows the chunk summary on the startup critical path.

Building blocks:
- worldTiles/byteCache.ts already implements CacheStorage plus an IndexedDB LRU with a byte budget and content-hash keys.
- buildSharedRoomSnapshotKey(roomId, version, state, updatedAt) (sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:6-13) is already an immutable key.
- ensureRoomSnapshotsBatch already filters references against local caches (165-189), so a persistent tier can slot in there.

Plan:
1. Persist full-detail published snapshots (not drafts or construction previews) under that key with a ~10–20 MB budget.
2. Check the persistent tier before building references.
3. Write through after normalisation.

Benefit: returning players get their arrival room and neighbours from disk, so the first playable frame no longer waits on a D1-backed POST, and each revisit saves one Worker+D1 read per room. It fits naturally after the over-cloning fix, because the normalised object becomes the single stored copy.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/previewCache.ts:151-245 — ensureRoomSnapshotsBatch builds version-pinned references and only checks in-memory caches
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:128 — snapshot query responses are private, no-store
- src/persistence/sharedRoomSnapshotCache.ts:6-13 — immutable roomId:version:state:updatedAt key already exists
- src/scenes/overworld/worldTiles/byteCache.ts:59-73 — reusable CacheStorage + IDB LRU with byte budget

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The idea is valid and has not been built: room snapshots live only in memory and are lost on reload. Reframe the benefit, though. Browse startup is no longer gated on the snapshot batch, because the production tile cutover at 100% defers it (worldStreaming.ts:899). A persistent tier would save one snapshot POST (about 0.1-0.4 s) on the first Play entry of a session and on the dynamic overlay fill-in, plus a small number of batched primary-key D1 reads. 'private, no-store' is irrelevant because the endpoint is a POST. byteCache.ts is a pattern to copy, not a drop-in: it is specific to tile Blobs and URLs with SHA-256 checks, so it would need generalising or a sibling JSON IDB store. Add a client schema version to the persisted key, persist only published full-detail snapshots, and keep the existing missing/changed-reference checks.

### F444: Three finished GameJew prize avatars (green, purple, yellow) ship in every deploy but no player can wear them

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Dead code: Worker, scripts, configs and docs)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** A contributor added three more colour versions of the GameJew jam-prize character in August. Only the red one was ever switched on, so the other three (712 KB) download to the server with every release and nobody can use them. They are nearly ready to use: each needs one small file renamed and a few lines of setup. They could become prizes for weekly Build Prompt winners through the same 'entitlement' system the red one uses.

**Technical detail.**

Files: public/assets/player/gamejew-{green,purple,yellow}/ hold 711,899 bytes in total, added in b8f5d68c (2026-08-05, KamiSawZe) and recompressed in 3c8db344. No reference exists anywhere in src, html, scripts or docs (`rg 'gamejew-(green|purple|yellow)'` finds nothing). src/player/avatar/registry.ts:188-196 registers only GAMEJEW_RED via createDefaultCompatibleAvatarPack, and :210-214 builds the pack map. Why they would fail as is: createDefaultCompatibleAtlasAssets (registry.ts:125-139) loads PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json, but each unused pack ships PlayerCombatSheet.json instead (77,954 bytes, the wrong file) next to PlayerCombatActionsSheet.png. gamejew-red/PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json is byte-identical to default/PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json (`cmp`), and gamejew-green/PlayerSheet.json is byte-identical to gamejew-red/PlayerSheet.json, so the frame layout matches. Steps to enable, all reusing existing pieces: (1) Copy the 6 KB default PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json into each folder and delete the three wrong PlayerCombatSheet.json files (234 KB). (2) Add three createDefaultCompatibleAvatarPack entries in registry.ts. (3) Add them to ENTITLEMENT_GATED_AVATAR_IDS (src/player/avatar/unlocks.ts:37-39). (4) Grant them through user_avatar_entitlements (avatars/entitlements.ts), for example automatically to build_prompt_winners from the weekly Build Prompt (F128). Also add a GameJew provenance and licence line to ASSETS.md; it currently has none for any gamejew pack. If you don't want them, delete the three folders instead and save 712 KB per deploy.

**Evidence.**

- src/player/avatar/registry.ts:188-196 — only GAMEJEW_RED_PLAYER_PACK is created
- src/player/avatar/registry.ts:136-139 — packs load PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json, which the green/purple/yellow folders lack
- src/player/avatar/unlocks.ts:37-39 — ENTITLEMENT_GATED_AVATAR_IDS holds only gamejew-red
- src/cloudflare/worker/avatars/entitlements.ts:8-24 — existing per-user avatar entitlement lookup to reuse
- ASSETS.md:25 — provenance covers CryptoPunks; no entry for any GameJew pack

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: three finished, unreferenced GameJew variants, each with the wrong combat JSON, can be enabled by copying default/PlayerCombatActionsSheet.json and registering and gating them in registry.ts and unlocks.ts.
  
  Two corrections:
  - No code grants avatar entitlements today. Red was granted by hand, and entitlements.ts only reads. Prizes for Build Prompt winners need a new INSERT OR IGNORE INTO user_avatar_entitlements in the settleExpiredBuildPrompts batch (buildPrompts/store.ts:139-161), plus a decision on which colour goes to which rank.
  - The waste is negligible. Pages uploads by content hash and no client fetches these files, so '712 KB per deploy' overstates what deleting them saves.
  
  Also extend getChoiceRank (unlocks.ts:130) and registry.test.ts. The ASSETS.md licence line needs Jonathan to confirm the contributor's terms.

### F441: Multiplayer has one mode (Arena Duel): add a live head-to-head race through a goal room

- **Area:** Ideas: players (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for players)
- **Type:** idea · **impact:** low · **effort:** large

**Summary.** The Multiplayer menu offers a single choice, a sword duel. The multiplayer system was built for more modes, and racing is already on the roadmap. A 'Race' mode would invite another online player into a goal room with a shared countdown, and the first to reach the exit wins. Many people will find it more approachable than combat, and it reuses the duel's invite, countdown and results screens.

**Technical detail.**

MultiplayerModeId is only 'arena' (multiplayer/model.ts:10), and MULTIPLAYER_MODE_DEFINITIONS registers one mode (:110-114). The framework already models what a race needs: category 'cooperative' and camera 'free_roam' (unused anywhere, :11-12), per-mode goals {room, course} switches (:56-59) that the scene honours during matches (OverworldPlayScene.ts:2789-2794, :4024), and per-mode damage rules (:17-24). The HUD shows a two-step 'Choose Mode' picker for one card (scenes/overworld/hud.ts:975-1000). The PRD lists 'Racing' under multiplayer v2 (product-requirements.md:461).

What's missing: match resolution is hearts-only. finalizePvpMatch picks the winner by eliminated or alive participants (partykit/pvpMatchRuntime.ts:200-218).

Smallest version: a 'race' definition (goals.room=true, playerDamage/sword/gun false, lockToStartRoom true, countdown reused). Add a 'pvp:goal-complete' client message carrying elapsed time. The runtime finalises on the first finisher with the existing 350 ms draw window, and the existing result submission records win/loss. Allow guests to race unranked. Ranked results should stay signed-in only, as for duels, because they're client-reported (see F203's warning about unchecked Rush runs). Roughly 300-500 lines across PartyKit runtime, model and client.

Why: racing is the most natural live social mode for a platformer, and it fits players who don't enjoy fighting. Rank this below the async ideas, because it needs two people online at the same time.

**Evidence.**

- src/multiplayer/model.ts:10 — MultiplayerModeId is only 'arena'
- src/multiplayer/model.ts:11-12 — 'cooperative' category and 'free_roam' camera exist but are unused
- src/multiplayer/model.ts:56-59 — per-mode goal switches already modelled
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:2789-2794 — scene honours match goal policy
- src/partykit/pvpMatchRuntime.ts:200-218 — results are decided by hearts only
- src/scenes/overworld/hud.ts:975-1000 — mode picker iterates a one-item list
- docs/product/product-requirements.md:461 — Racing planned

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The idea is real and the framework evidence is correct, but the scope needs three corrections.
  
  (a) The roadmap item at product-requirements.md:461 is async ghost racing, which already shipped (F142, PR #77/#80). A live race is a new proposal, not a planned item.
  
  (b) It is not "mostly reuse". 'arena' is hardcoded in 9 files, including:
  - pvpArenaController.ts:174, which rejects other modes
  - the worker route routes.ts:211-213/262, which rejects any mode other than 'arena'
  - the hearts-based status and result payload
  
  A race also needs:
  - a shared start point instead of the opposite-side PvP spawn
  - the room-goal intro suppressed during the countdown
  - per-goal-type rules (limit it to reach-exit/checkpoint goals at first)
  - its own stats instead of pvp_wins/losses and PvP XP
  - a brand-new guest path, since guests are blocked at pvpArenaController.ts:186-193
  
  A realistic size is about 700-1,000 lines plus tests, not 300-500.
  
  (c) Duel results are already client-reported through an unverified submit route. Gating ranked races to signed-in players is not an integrity control. Reuse the F199 ranked-trace verification if race results count for anything.
  
  Impact is low-medium, because it needs two players online at the same time in the same area.

### F447: Builders aren't told when their room is Featured, Room of the Day, or a Build Prompt winner, and a quick republish silently un-features it

- **Area:** Ideas: builders (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for builders, Worlds, Jams and schools)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F123

**Summary.** Being featured is the biggest compliment a builder can get, but the in-game Activity inbox never mentions it. Room of the Day sends an email only to people who found and ticked an opt-in box, and admin features and prompt wins send nothing. Because Featured is tied to one exact version, fixing a typo afterwards quietly removes the room from Featured, and the builder never knew it was there. Add these moments to the inbox and keep Featured across gameplay-identical republishes.

**Technical detail.**

The activity kinds are fixed to completion, rating, comment, top1 and dethroned (migrations/0055_builder_activity.sql:7, source_kind :12), and the visibility filter accepts only those sources (activity/store.ts:20-23). Featured rows are written in three places, none of which creates an activity entry: the admin pin (admin/routes.ts:456-470), the Room of the Day pick (daily/store.ts:132) and prompt settlement (buildPrompts/store.ts:150-155). The Room of the Day email needs daily_features=1 (daily/emails.ts:15), which defaults to 0 (0057_daily_rooms.sql:28). Prompt entrants who don't win get no results notice; settlement runs from the scheduled handler (worker.ts:360). The index joins featured_rooms on the exact current version (playableContentIndex/store.ts:151-158), so any republish drops Featured.

Plan. (1) Migration: rebuild builder_activity with kinds 'featured', 'daily', 'prompt_result' and source_kind 'feature'. The table is small and the rebuild can be shared with other new kinds (neighbor, world decision, remix). (2) Insert rows in the three write sites and in settleExpiredBuildPrompts: winners get their rank, and other entrants get "Results are in: N entries". (3) Extend activityDescription (activity/model.ts:31-37). (4) In the publish flow, warn "This room is Featured. Changing gameplay will remove it", and match featured_rooms by fingerprint group (room_version_facts) so title and music edits keep the pin. Size: about 120 lines plus a migration.

**Evidence.**

- migrations/0055_builder_activity.sql:7 — activity kinds exclude featured/daily/prompt results
- src/cloudflare/worker/activity/store.ts:20-23 — inbox visibility limited to bxp/pxp/comment/guest sources
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/routes.ts:456 — admin feature pin writes featured_rooms only
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/store.ts:132 — Room of the Day writes featured_rooms only
- src/cloudflare/worker/buildPrompts/store.ts:150 — prompt winners featured, no entrant notice
- src/cloudflare/worker/daily/emails.ts:15 — RotD email only when daily_features = 1
- migrations/0057_daily_rooms.sql:28 — daily_features defaults to 0
- src/cloudflare/worker/playableContentIndex/store.ts:151-158 — Featured matches exact version, so republish drops it

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: Featured, Room of the Day and prompt results never reach the Activity inbox, the Room of the Day email is opt-in and off by default, and a republish removes Featured and the same day's Room of the Day without warning. Three corrections:
  (a) A builder's first prompt win does show a generic "Prompt Winner" badge sting via rewardStingCatchup. It names neither the room nor the rank, and repeat wins get nothing. The Room of the Day modal shows "Your level is Room of the Day!" only if the builder opens it.
  (b) Clearing the pin on republish is a deliberate F125 decision (feature-ledger.md:1007, "pins the reviewed whole-level version"). The fingerprint carry-over should not ship by default: the fingerprint leaves out the title, music and background, room_version_facts is filled lazily so a SQL join can't use it, and expanded rooms are harder. Ship the publish warning, which also covers the Room of the Day becoming unavailable. Make carry-over a separate decision for Jonathan, and if it is approved, do it in TypeScript at publish time and require the title to be unchanged.
  (c) Add the inbox rows with AFTER INSERT/UPDATE triggers on featured_rooms and build_prompts.settled_at, following the 0055 trigger pattern, instead of editing the three write sites. The table rebuild must also recreate the 0055 triggers and views and the 0066 index, and needs a sentinel system actor for the NOT NULL actor_user_id and the generated-user filter.

### F451: Room stats and the death map go blank whenever a builder republishes, even after only a title or music change

- **Area:** Ideas: builders (reviewer: Obvious feature ideas for builders, Worlds, Jams and schools)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F124

**Summary.** A builder's play numbers (players, clear rate, deaths) and the death map belong to one exact published version. Any republish, even renaming the room or swapping its music, resets the profile card to "No finished attempts yet" and empties the death map. There is also no way to see whether a real change made the room easier or harder. The leaderboard already knows which versions play the same, so insights should use that grouping and show a before/after comparison when gameplay did change.

**Technical detail.**

Mechanism: insights/store.ts:18 joins attempts with `a.version_key = owners.version_key` (exact version only). insights/routes.ts:21 defaults to the current published version. The modal only ever shows "published vN" (roomInsights.ts:134), and profile cards print insightSummaryText (profileModalRoomRenderer.ts:93-95), which returns 'No finished attempts yet' when attempts=0 (insights/model.ts:25). Leaderboards and ghosts already merge gameplay-identical versions: roomLeaderboardAggregation.ts:17-50 returns equivalentRoomVersions, used by ghosts.ts:99-100. The fingerprint excludes title, background, music, lighting and weather (roomVersionLineage.ts:235-257). The History modal already labels "Same as vN" (historyModal.ts:426). Builders republish often: the ledger notes a live 215-version history for room 2,1 (feature-ledger.md:857).

Plan. (1) Server: for contentType 'room', read fingerprints from room_version_facts (migration 0064, already filled for leaderboards) and expand the requested version to its equivalent set. Change selectionCte so each requested row carries a group key and matches `version_key IN (equivalents)`, aggregating by group. Apply the same mapping in attachRoomInsights (profile/discovery, 40 targets per batch) with one extra room_version_facts query per batch. (2) Client: the modal also requests the previous gameplay-different version (routes.ts:39-40 already accepts ?version=) and shows two columns, e.g. "v12 now: 18% clear, 6.1 deaths vs v11: 42%, 2.3", plus a version toggle on the death map. (3) Expanded Rooms keep exact-version stats until they have a lineage. Size: about 80 server lines and 60 client lines; extend insights/store.test.ts with a title-only republish case.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/insights/store.ts:18 — attempts joined on exact version_key only
- src/cloudflare/worker/insights/routes.ts:21 — defaults to current published version
- src/ui/setup/roomInsights.ts:134 — modal shows only 'published vN', no comparison
- src/insights/model.ts:25 — 'No finished attempts yet' when the new version has no attempts
- src/ui/setup/profileModalRoomRenderer.ts:93-95 — profile card prints per-version insights
