Focus loss: toggleMusicPhraseAudition calls requestRender immediately and again after the render resolves (musicWorkflow.ts:683-697, 733), and selectArrangementSlot calls requestRender (musicWorkflow.ts:666-675); the focused button is removed, so document.activeElement falls back to body and Enter cannot stop the audition. Fix: (1) return early from both panel renders when music mode is inactive or the panel is hidden; (2) keyed reconciliation: keep a Map<phraseId, entry> / slot buttons and only update class/aria/text; (3) if a rebuild is unavoidable, restore focus by data-room-music-phrase-audition / data-room-music-arrangement-slot. Keyboard test: Tab to a ▶ preview, press Enter twice, expect start then stop.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/musicUi.ts:238-295 — full replaceChildren of every library entry per render
- src/scenes/editor/musicUi.ts:86-166 — slot-count buttons and whole slot grid recreated per render
- src/scenes/editor/musicWorkflow.ts:1253-1255 — panels rendered unconditionally from renderUi
- src/scenes/editor/musicWorkflow.ts:683-697 — audition toggle requests a render right away (and again at 733)
- src/scenes/editor/musicWorkflow.ts:666-675 — selecting a slot requests a render
- src/scenes/editor/musicPhraseOrchestrator.ts:294-307 — Load More appends 24 items per page
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1218-1250 — lighting/weather slider handlers call renderEditorUi per change
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:1900-1906 — renderEditorUi always calls renderMusicUi

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F471: Error messages in Explore, Leaderboard, Profile and 9 other menus are never announced to screen readers

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F180

**Summary.** When Explore, a profile or a leaderboard fails to load, a red message with a 'Try again' button appears, but screen readers don't announce it. A blind player just finds an empty list. 12 of the 13 menu error boxes have this problem. Fix: mark the shared error box as an alert, which is a one-line change in the helper every menu uses.

**Technical detail.**

index.html has 13 `.history-modal-error` banners. Only #guest-progress-status (:3035) has role=status/aria-live. The others are silent: :2382 room history, :2397 wamp-o-gram, :2494 leaderboard, :2645 room rush, :2838 explore, :2852 profile, :2947 playlist, :3012 phrase save, :3050 run rating, :3138 sign text, :3172 guestbook and :3584 chat moderation. renderFriendlyError (src/ui/friendlyError.ts:13-30) un-hides the element, inserts the text and a 'Try again' button, but sets no role and moves no focus. Combined with the deferred-dialog focus regression, an Explore load failure is completely invisible to assistive tech. Loading states (Explore 'Loading…', profile load) also have no aria-busy. Fix: in renderFriendlyError, call `element.setAttribute('role', 'alert')` before inserting the text (covers the 4 callers), and add role='alert' to the static banners in index.html. Optionally set aria-busy on #explore-list and profile panels while loading.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:2838 — explore-modal-error has no role/aria-live
- index.html:2494 — leaderboard-modal-error has no role/aria-live
- index.html:2852 — profile-modal-error has no role/aria-live
- index.html:3035 — only guest-progress-status is a live region
- src/ui/friendlyError.ts:13-30 — renderFriendlyError shows text and retry without role or focus
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:1287-1289 — Explore errors go through renderFriendlyError

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** 12 of the 13 banners do lack live-region semantics, but only 4 menus (Explore, Leaderboard, Profile, Playlist) go through renderFriendlyError. The other 8 have their own setStatus or setError code. Four of those (room rush, guestbook, chat moderation, wamp-o-gram) also show progress and success messages, so a blanket static role="alert" would read those out assertively. The fix:
  - role="alert" in renderFriendlyError.
  - Static role="alert" on the 4 error-only banners: room-history, phrase-save, run-rating, sign-text.
  - In the 4 mixed-tone banners, switch the role by tone inside their setStatus, or keep a role="status" region that isn't toggled with display:none.
  - Optional: aria-busy on the Explore and Profile lists, following the activityInbox pattern.

### F478: The main menu button doesn't say whether the menu is open, and Escape doesn't close the menu

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F168

**Summary.** The hamburger menu holds Settings, Controls, sign-in and the 'Paused' notice, but its button never tells screen readers whether it's open, and pressing Escape doesn't close it. Every other pop-up closes with Escape. Keyboard players have to Tab back to the button to close it. Fix: report the open state and close on Escape.

**Technical detail.**

index.html:162 `<button id="menu-toggle" aria-label="Menu">` has no aria-expanded or aria-controls. auth/client.ts:179-188 only toggles #auth-panel.menu-open and closes on outside click. None of the 17 `classList.remove('menu-open')` sites is keyboard-driven (they are in gameMenu.ts, controllers.ts, leaderboardModal.ts and others), and installDialogEscapeGuard (modalState.ts:33-48) only considers .history-modal. While the menu is open, gameplayPause.ts:63 pauses solo play and shows #game-pause-status inside the menu (index.html:169), so the player is stuck in a paused state that Escape does not undo. Fix: in the toggle handler, set aria-expanded and aria-controls='menu-body'. Add a document keydown for Escape that closes menu-open when it is open, calls preventDefault, and focuses #menu-toggle. Include the menu in the Escape guard so the key isn't also handled by the game.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:162 — menu-toggle has aria-label only, no aria-expanded
- src/auth/client.ts:179-188 — toggle and outside-click close; no keyboard close
- src/ui/gameplayPause.ts:63 — menu-open pauses gameplay
- src/ui/modalState.ts:33-48 — Escape guard only knows .history-modal dialogs

**Fact-check.**

- **confirmed.** No correction.

### F477: Tabbing to a player's name makes it fade to near-invisible, with no focus ring

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Every clickable player name (leaderboards, Explore builders, collectors, chat, build prompts) turns light green when hovered or reached with Tab, and its focus outline is removed. On the cream panels that green is about 2:1 contrast, so the name nearly disappears at the moment a keyboard player lands on it. In Explore, the builder name turns pale blue (1.75:1). Fix: keep the text dark and add a visible ring or highlight.

**Technical detail.**

base.css:979-984 sets `.profile-trigger:hover, .profile-trigger:focus-visible { color: var(--accent-cool) /* #5dc16b */; text-decoration: underline; outline: none; }`. Computed contrast is 2.05:1 on #fff3db and 2.17:1 on #fffaf0. createProfileTriggerElement (profileEvents.ts:61-65) applies the class at 9 call sites: leaderboardModal x3, globalLeaderboardPanel x2, exploreModal, buildPrompts, chat/panel and profileCollection. collectionAttribution.ts:78 also adds it to 'Collected by' names. In Explore, explore-room-cards.css:184-188 overrides it further. The builder name goes from sky-deep #2c5071 (7.66:1) to sky #79ccde (1.75:1 on paper) with outline:none. This fails WCAG 2.4.7 (focus visible) in practice and 1.4.3 for the focused text. Fix (2 rules): keep color ink, remove outline:none, and use `outline: 2px solid var(--wamp-ink); outline-offset: 2px` or `background: var(--wamp-yellow)` for focus-visible. Keep the colour change only on hover if wanted, with a colour of at least 4.5:1 such as --wamp-green #277b30 (4.82:1).

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/base.css:979-984 — profile-trigger hover/focus: #5dc16b text, outline none
- src/styles/sections/modals/leaderboard-profile-explore/explore-room-cards.css:184-188 — builder name focus: sky text, outline none
- src/ui/setup/profileEvents.ts:61-65 — every openable player name gets class profile-trigger
- src/ui/setup/collectionAttribution.ts:78 — collector names also use profile-trigger

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Only some player names are affected, not every one. Leaderboard names (5 of the 9 createProfileTriggerElement sites) keep ink or sky-deep text on focus because more specific #leaderboard-modal rules win. They get an underline and no ring. The build-prompt "by X" button keeps ink text and its background turns sky on focus. The real defect is in four places:
  - Chat author names: #5dc16b on cream, 2.05:1. An underline still appears.
  - Explore room-card builder names: sky #79ccde on paper, 1.75:1. They are already underlined, so focus only changes the colour.
  - Profile-collection builder links (.collection-person): #5dc16b, about 2:1, colour change only.
  - 'Collected by' names (.collection-person): same as above.
  The last two are crypto-gated, so only wallet holders see them. The fix stays two CSS rules: base.css:979-984 and explore-room-cards.css:184-188. Use an ink outline for :focus-visible, and on hover keep a colour of at least 4.5:1, or none.

### F472: Explore room cards read as one long run-on button, and key explanations only exist as mouse-hover tooltips

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Each Explore card is a fake button with real buttons (builder and collector names) inside it, so screen readers read the whole card as one long label and skip the inner buttons. The five rating stars are read as 'black star' five times. Explanations of 'Protected', 'Co-op plates', 'Est.' difficulty, 'Popular' and why some sorts are disabled are only hover tooltips, which phones and tablets never show. One tooltip shows a raw computer timestamp. Fix: give each card a real 'Go to room' button, hide the decorative stars, and show the explanations as visible text.

**Technical detail.**

exploreModal.ts:659-673 (and the guest card at :591-607) builds a `div role="button" tabindex=0` and then appends real buttons inside it: the builder name (createBuilderRow :943-967 → createProfileTriggerElement) and 'Collected by' names (collectionAttribution.ts:74-82, via collectionAttributionSlot at exploreModal.ts:727). Children of role=button are presentational, so the accessible name becomes e.g. 'Preview <title> Co-op plates Featured Protected Built by X Collected by Y Played by 12 ★★★★★ 4.2 stars · 3 ratings Est. Medium Trophy room', and the nested buttons are not exposed. The stars are 5 '★' spans (exploreModal.ts:985) with no aria-hidden, even though the label next to them already says '4.2 stars'. Title-only explanations: roomProtection.ts:16 ('Only the owner can edit a protected cell.'), exploreModal.ts:704 (co-op), :1016 ('Estimated from N players' first clears'), :404 (Popular), :402 (disabled personal sorts: 'Sign in to sort…'), and collectionAttribution.ts:71, which interpolates the ISO ownerSyncedAt (e.g. 2026-10-20T14:03:22.123Z, set at worker mint/service.ts:292). Fix: make the card an <article> whose title is an <h3> containing a <button> (the open action), with the builder/collector buttons as siblings, so there is no nesting. aria-hidden the stars container. Render one short visible explainer line or a tappable 'i' toggle for badges, add a visible 'Sign in to use' note under disabled sorts, and format the date with toLocaleDateString.

**Evidence.**

- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:659-673 — card is div role=button with click/keydown handlers
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:943-967 — builder-name <button> appended inside the card
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:985 — five '★' spans, not aria-hidden
- src/ui/roomProtection.ts:16 — protection explained only in title tooltip
- src/ui/setup/exploreModal.ts:402-404 — disabled-sort and Popular explanations only in title
- src/ui/setup/collectionAttribution.ts:71 — tooltip shows raw ISO timestamp

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claims hold in renderEntry (exploreModal.ts:659-673): the role=button card holds a nested builder <button> (:726, :943-967) and, for wallet holders, 'Collected by' buttons (:727). The stars are not aria-hidden (:985), and the protected, co-op, Est., Popular and signed-out-sort explanations exist only as title tooltips. While signed out the sort button is disabled, so the visible setError at :222-224 never fires.
  
  Corrections:
  - The guest card (:591-607) has no nested buttons. Its only problem is the run-on name.
  - The 'Collected by' buttons and the raw ISO ownerSyncedAt tooltip (collectionAttribution.ts:71) appear only behind the wallet gate, so few visitors see them.
  - Nested buttons can still be reached with Tab. The breakage is in screen-reader browse/touch modes and in the card's accessible name.
  - profileModalRoomRenderer.ts:176 has the same unhidden-star pattern, so include it.
  
  Fix:
  - Use a real <button> for the open action and keep the card click for pointer users.
  - Keep the .explore-room-card class, because the smoke tests select it.
  - Add aria-hidden to the star containers.
  - Add a visible 'Sign in to use these sorts' note.
  - Format the date with toLocaleDateString.

### F476: Stylesheets outside src/styles skip all style checks; Worlds and Bug Report ignore Readable and Large text

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: UI, styles and pages)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F171

**Summary.** The Readable font and Large text settings work by changing a few shared style values. A handful of newer style files live outside the styles folder, where the automatic checks don't look. Among them are the Worlds window, the Bug Report window and the guest-recording notice. Those files hard-code the pixel font and small sizes, so players who switched on Readable or Large text still get small pixel text there. Moving these files into the checked folder and using the shared values fixes it and keeps the checks honest.

**Technical detail.**

Both style guards only scan src/styles: check_shared_styles.mjs:7 (palette, font-stack and token ownership) and check_style_cascade.mjs:39 (stylelint !important ceilings, @layer ownership, named z-index roles). Eight sheets live elsewhere: src/ui/worlds/worlds.css (100 lines), src/bugReports/reporter.css, src/analytics/replay/notice.css, src/auth/emailCodeDialog.css, src/jam.css, src/admin/{replays,bugReports}.css and src/admin/launch/replayModal.css. Three ship in the game through TS imports (worlds/view.ts:1, bugReports/reporter.ts:6, analytics/replay/recorder.ts:7). None of the eight uses @layer, so their rules beat every layered rule in main.css whatever the specificity. Readable/Large text work only by swapping --font-ui, --font-display and --ui-text-* (tokens.css:156-175). worlds.css hard-codes font-family "HomeVideo" (:19), "Early GameBoy" 16px (:46-47) and 12px (:55). reporter.css hard-codes 12px and 14px 'HomeVideo' (:7-8, :18). notice.css:1 uses 12px generic monospace for the guest session-recording consent notice. Stacking is likewise literal: worlds.css:3 z-index 1200, reporter.css:1 10002, notice.css:1 10001, bypassing the --z-* roles the cascade check enforces. 45 hex literals equal to palette tokens slip past the F113 palette check: worlds.css 17, reporter.css 10, jam.css 8, emailCodeDialog.css 7, admin/bugReports.css 3. Fix (small): move worlds.css, reporter.css and notice.css under src/styles/sections (still imported lazily from their TS, as editor-bundle.css is) inside `@layer components`. Replace font literals with var(--font-ui)/var(--font-display), px sizes with var(--ui-text-*), and z-index with var(--z-modal)/var(--z-toast)/var(--z-critical). Then widen both guards to scan src/**/*.css with an explicit allowlist for the standalone admin and jam pages.

**Evidence.**

- scripts/check_shared_styles.mjs:7 — palette/font guard reads only ../src/styles/
- scripts/check_style_cascade.mjs:39 — cascade/!important/z-index guard lints only 'src/styles/**/*.css'
- src/ui/worlds/worlds.css:19 — Worlds panel font-family hard-coded to "HomeVideo"
- src/ui/worlds/worlds.css:46-47 — Worlds title fixed to "Early GameBoy" 16px
- src/bugReports/reporter.css:8 — bug-report notes field fixed to 14px 'HomeVideo'
- src/bugReports/reporter.css:1 — z-index: 10002 literal, unlayered
- src/analytics/replay/notice.css:1 — recording notice: z-index 10001, 12px monospace, hard-coded colours
- src/styles/tokens.css:156-175 — Readable and Large text only swap --font-* and --ui-text-* tokens

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The real defect is narrower.
  - **Worlds:** the panel ignores Readable entirely, and ignores Large only for kicker, meta, title and pill text.
  - **Bug Report:** ignores Large for its 12px paragraphs, status line and 16px phone title. It ignores Readable only in the notes textarea.
  - **Recording notice:** ignores only Large. It uses generic monospace, not the pixel font.
  
  Font mapping in the fix: "HomeVideo", monospace should become var(--font-home-short) or var(--font-ui), and "Early GameBoy", monospace should become var(--font-label). Using var(--font-display) would swap in Super Mario Bros. NES and change the look. Sizes should use var(--ui-text-small, 12px) and var(--ui-text-title, 16px) so the defaults stay byte-identical.
  
  Wrapping these files in `@layer components` changes precedence, because unlayered rules currently beat every layer. The simplest fix keeps the files where they are, swaps literals for tokens, and points both guards at these three paths. Allowlist jam.css and the admin sheets, which have their own look on purpose. Leave the z-index literals alone, or add a deliberate top role; don't fold them into --z-toast or --z-critical without a stacking check.

### F475: Settings: four choice groups have no name (two are both just 'Auto'), Audio is buried 7th of 9, and 'Option-drag' is Mac-only wording

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F180

**Summary.** Performance, Frame rate, Builder Experience and Panning Style are radio choices with no group label, so a screen reader hears 'Auto, 1 of 3' twice with no idea which setting it is. Volume, the setting people look for most, is the 7th of 9 sections, below Bug reports. Panning is labelled 'Option-drag', which Windows and Chromebook players don't have (it's Alt there). Fix: group the choices properly, move Audio to the top, and name the key per platform.

**Technical detail.**

index.html:3313-3415: the Performance (3314), Frame rate (3349), Builder Experience (3388) and Panning Style (3407) groups are `<section><div class=settings-section-title>` + `<div class=settings-choice-group>` with no fieldset/legend and no role=radiogroup with aria-labelledby. Both Performance (3317) and Frame rate (3352) open with an option named 'Auto'. The Comfort section's Camera group (fieldset + legend) already shows the right pattern, and Comfort and Assist use aria-labelledby. Section order: Comfort, Assist, Performance, Bug reports, Frame rate, Comments, Audio, Builder Experience, Panning Style. Frame rate is split from Performance by Bug reports. 'Option-drag' appears at index.html:3411 and in the Controls dialog at :3438, while inspectInput.ts:433 reads altKey, which is Alt on non-Mac keyboards. Fix: convert the four groups to fieldset/legend (reuse .settings-comfort-camera styles). Reorder to Audio, Text and Comfort, Assist, Camera, Performance + Frame rate (merged), Building (Builder Experience + Panning), Comments, Bug reports. Render the label as 'Option-drag' or 'Alt-drag' from navigator.userAgentData?.platform or navigator.platform.

**Evidence.**

- index.html:3314 — Performance radio group: div title, no fieldset/legend
- index.html:3349 — Frame rate radio group: div title, no fieldset/legend
- index.html:3317 and 3352 — both groups start with an option named 'Auto'
- index.html:3375 — Audio section is 7th of 9
- index.html:3411, 3438 — 'Option-drag' label shown to all platforms
- src/scenes/overworld/inspectInput.ts:433 — panning actually checks altKey

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The markup, line numbers, section order and Option/Alt mismatch are all correct. The screen-reader symptom is overstated. Each radio's label wraps its title and description, so the two "Auto" options are announced with different full names ("Auto Balances smooth play…" vs "Auto Uses about 60 fps…"), and browse mode reads the visible section title first.
  
  The real gap is that the four radio groups (Performance, Frame rate, Builder Experience, Panning Style) have no group name when someone tabs or arrows into them. The fix is to wrap each in a fieldset/legend like the Camera group, or add role=radiogroup with aria-labelledby.
  
  The Option/Alt problem is wording only. Space-drag and middle-drag already pan on every platform. Relabel the option per platform, or label it "Option/Alt-drag" the same way the editor writes "Cmd/Ctrl". Do this in both Settings (3411) and the Controls dialog (3438).
  
  Moving Audio first and putting Frame rate next to Performance is a sensible, safe reorder, since bindings find the radios by name. The larger regrouping the reviewer proposed is optional.

### F474: Readable and Large text don't reach in-world comments, chat bubbles, ghost names or goal labels

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F171

**Summary.** The new Readable font and Large text options change menus and three kinds of map labels, but most text drawn inside the game world doesn't follow them. That includes room comments, chat speech bubbles, race-ghost names, goal marker labels and floating effect text. Those are the most text-heavy things players read in a room, and they stay at fixed small sizes in the original fonts. Fix: hook each of them up to the existing text-preference helper.

**Technical detail.**

bindCanvasTextPreferences (src/settings/textPreferences.ts:24-41) is called for only 3 of 30 Phaser text objects: browseOverlays.ts, roomCells.ts and liveObjects/npcNameLabel.ts. The unbound texts use fixed world-space sizes: room comment pins (roomComments.ts:796-834: 11px count, 10px header, 11px body, 9px meta), in-play comment popovers (roomCommentsPlayPresentationController.ts:106-122: 11/12/10px), chat bubbles (roomChat.ts:517-519, 12px), ghost labels (presence.ts:1215-1217, 11px Courier New), goal-marker labels (goalMarkers.ts:90-92, 12px) and FX text (fx/controller.ts:262-264, 12px). On-screen size also depends on camera zoom, so at browse zoom the 9-11px comment text is smaller still. Fix: call bindCanvasTextPreferences(label, family, size) after each add.text, one line per site. Where layout depends on text height (redrawRenderedComment in roomCommentsPlayPresentationController.ts already measures it), subscribe to settings changes and re-run the redraw.

**Evidence.**

- src/settings/textPreferences.ts:24-41 — helper exists; used by 3 label types
- src/scenes/overworld/roomComments.ts:796-834 — comment texts at 9-11px, unbound
- src/scenes/overworld/roomCommentsPlayPresentationController.ts:106-122 — popover texts 10-12px, unbound
- src/scenes/overworld/roomChat.ts:517-519 — chat bubble 12px, unbound
- src/scenes/overworld/presence.ts:1215-1217 — ghost label 11px Courier New, unbound
- src/scenes/overworld/goalMarkers.ts:90-92 — goal labels 12px, unbound

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The real gap is text size, not font. Comments, chat and comment popovers already use IBM Plex Mono (the Readable font). Ghost, goal and FX labels use Courier New. Readable and Large never change their size.
  
  Browse comment markers are already counter-scaled to 0.82–1.38x on screen (badgeOverlays.ts:66-81), so they do not get smaller at browse zoom. Play-world labels look small only on small viewports, mainly the phone 'room' camera (zoom about 0.6). On desktop (zoom about 2.2) they show at 22-30px.
  
  Add the browse danmaku (roomComments.ts:1161/1170, 13px/8px) and the remaining browseOverlays labels (8-12px) to the list.
  
  Effort by group:
  - Ghost, goal and FX: one line each. FX can just call resolveTextSize once at spawn.
  - Chat bubble and play comment popover: bind the texts and re-run redrawBubble / redrawRenderedComment when settings change.
  - Browse comment text panel, compact count and danmaku: replace the hard-coded y offsets (24/56), heights (72/28) and fixedHeight 21 with measured layout before binding. Otherwise Large makes body and meta overlap.
  
  The helper is at textPreferences.ts:27-44.

### F470: Desktop editor squeezes 'Scramble' and 'Rectangle' to 7px, and shrinks Publish to 8px on tablets and small laptops

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F117

**Summary.** In the editor's top bar, two tool labels are drawn at 7px by default. On screens 1250px wide or less (iPads in landscape, small laptops), the big Publish button, the builder's main action, drops to 8px text, smaller than every other button around it. Only players who turn on Readable or Large text get relief. Fix: shorten or wrap the two labels, and keep Publish at least as large as its neighbours.

**Technical detail.**

dock-shell.css:198-202 sets `.editor-shell-tools [data-tool='randomize'|'rect'] .tool-label` to var(--ui-text-small, 7px), in IBM Plex Mono bold via --editor-ui-font (tokens.css:144). Every other chunky label uses 10px (dock-shell.css:174). button-roles.css:73-76: under @media (max-width: 1250px) the lg Publish label (index.html:1463, data-button-size='lg', SMB NES font) is set to var(--ui-text-small, 8px). Above 1250px it is 16px and gets a 1.5fr column (button-roles.css:60-70). So the primary action shrinks below its secondary neighbours at exactly the widths where tablets use this desktop/tablet dock. Fix: use 'Mix'/'Rect' or allow two-line labels at 10px. In the ≤1250px query, keep Publish at 12px (HomeVideo) or 16px NES on its own row instead of 8px.

**Evidence.**

- src/styles/sections/editor/dock-shell.css:198-202 — Scramble/Rectangle labels at 7px default
- src/styles/sections/editor/dock-shell.css:174 — other chunky labels 10px
- src/styles/sections/button-roles.css:73-76 — Publish label 8px at max-width 1250px
- index.html:1463 — Publish is the lg primary button

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Both labels are real, but the scope and the reasoning need correcting.
  
  1. Scramble and Rectangle are drawn at 7px in uppercase IBM Plex Mono. The font is forced by typography.css:9-11 through --editor-button-font. The other tool labels are 9px (tools.css:226-230), not 10px. This happens on every editor layout, phones included, because editorPhoneDock.ts:100 moves the tools.
     - Fix: shorten Rectangle to "Rect".
     - Or keep 9px where the column is wide enough, and use 7px only at narrow widths.
     - Two-line wrapping does not help single words.
  2. Publish drops to 8px Super Mario Bros. NES at 1250px wide and below, phones included (editorPhoneDock.ts:94). On screen it is not smaller than its neighbours: 8px NES caps are 7px tall, the same as 10px Plex caps, and the all-caps label is wider.
     - What it does lose is primary emphasis: it gets an equal column and the same green as Test.
     - The 8px was a deliberate F114 choice, checked by the label-fit audit, and it sits on the font's pixel grid.
     - Changing it means a layout change, such as giving Publish its own row with a 16px label, and re-running the button-role audits. Simply resizing it to 12px would go off-grid and would not fit with the drawer open.

### F469: About 30 editor instructions tell phone builders to 'Click', 'press Escape' or 'move the mouse'

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Building on phones and tablets)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Many of the hints the editor shows while you build are written for a mouse and keyboard, for example: 'Move the mouse and click to place tiles, or press Esc to cancel'. On a phone there's no Escape key, so these hints point at actions that don't exist. Only one message (pressure-plate linking) is reworded for touch today. One small helper could adjust them all.

**Technical detail.**

User-visible status and hint strings with Click, Escape or mouse, counted with grep: objectMoveController.ts:96, 119, 232; tools.ts:119, 165, 230; EditorScene.ts:933, 1741; editorDockShell.ts:716 ('Click the room to place the spawn point. Press Escape to cancel.'); viewModel.ts:169-177 (5 marker hints); inspector.ts:1266, 1267, 1302; inspectorViewModel.ts:92; editRuntime.ts:3192; courseEditor/objectInspector.ts:897-909 (4); CourseEditorScene.ts:948-954 (4), 2975, 3083; paletteController.ts:919. That is 30 strings, not counting tooltips. Only phoneInspector.ts:69 rewrites Click→Tap, and only for the pressure-link prompt. Escape is the only stated way to cancel in these messages; the touch equivalents are switching tools, tapping empty space, or the Show/Hide button that turns into Cancel. Fix (small): add a pointerCopy(desktop, touch) helper keyed on getDeviceLayoutState().coarsePointer, or route every setStatusText call through a single Click→Tap / Escape→'tap Cancel' transform. Name the real touch cancel in each case (e.g., 'tap Cancel' for spawn placement, 'pick another tool' for paste).

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/editor/tools.ts:119 — 'Copy preview active. Move the mouse and click to place tiles, or press Esc to cancel.'
- src/ui/setup/editorDockShell.ts:716 — 'Click the room to place the spawn point. Press Escape to cancel.'
- src/scenes/editor/objectMoveController.ts:96 — 'Release to place; Escape cancels.'
- src/scenes/editor/viewModel.ts:169-177 — five 'Click the canvas…' marker hints
- src/scenes/editor/phoneInspector.ts:69 — the only Click→Tap rewrite, limited to pressure linking

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The mismatch shows up mainly on tablets, not phones. On phones, most of these strings are never displayed. The editor status line (#editor-room-feedback) is display:none on phones (retro-skin.css:194). The spawn instruction is written into a markers popover that start-spawn closes. The goal-placement hints sit in a drawer that auto-collapses on phones. Phone-visible cases are limited to paletteController.ts:919 (empty object panel), and the pressure-link prompt is already rewritten. On tablets (deviceClass 'tablet'), the status line is visible and shows 'Move the mouse... press Esc', 'Escape cancels' and similar. Key the copy helper on touchPrimary or deviceClass rather than coarsePointer, which is also true for touchscreen laptops that have keyboards. The phone side deserves its own note: phone builders get no status feedback at all for copy/paste, move and practice-start, because the status line is hidden.

### F468: 'Collect' now means both coin pickups and owning a room; 'My Rooms' opens a tab called 'Levels'

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Design, UX and accessibility)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F246

**Summary.** For wallet holders, a profile shows 'Collectibles: 412' (coins picked up) right next to a 'Collection' tab (rooms they own), and rooms use 'Collect Race' goals while the owner button says 'Collect & Lock'. The same rooms are called 'Protected' in Explore but 'Lock' on the button. Separately, the menu's 'My Rooms' opens a tab labelled 'Levels', and Explore mixes 'rooms' and 'challenge levels'. The wallet balance is shown with all 18 decimal places. Fix: pick one word per idea and use it everywhere.

**Technical detail.**

Existing gameplay vocabulary includes goal types 'Collect Target' and 'Collect Race' (goals/goalDefinitions.ts:88, :141), the profile stat 'Collectibles' with a coin icon (profileModalProgressRenderer.ts:155-157), the builder cap 'Collectibles' (:265-267) and editor goal help (editorDockShell.ts:171-172). The ownership feature added 'Collect & Lock' (index.html:265, ownerCollectionReminder.ts:80), the 'Collection' tab (index.html:2885), 'View collectible' (profileCollection.ts:82, index.html:266) and 'Collected by' (collectionAttribution.ts:75). Status uses 'Protected' / 'N/M cells protected' (roomProtection.ts:7). gameMenu.ts:39 opens the 'rooms' tab from the 'My Rooms' button (index.html:179), but that tab is labelled 'Levels' (index.html:2884) and its empty state says 'No published rooms yet.' (:2898). Explore empty states say 'challenge levels' (exploreModal.ts:1253-1259). roomWalletCost.ts:28 prints the balance via formatRoomEth with full wei precision (e.g. '0.012345678901234567 ETH'). Fix: (a) keep 'Collect' for ownership as F246 proposes, but rename the coin stat and cap to 'Coins' or 'Pickups'; or use 'Own / Owned rooms' for the NFT feature. (b) Use 'Locked' everywhere instead of 'Protected' to match 'Collect & Lock'. (c) Rename the Levels tab to 'Rooms' and use 'rooms' in the Explore empty states. (d) Round the balance to 4-6 significant digits for display.

**Evidence.**

- src/goals/goalDefinitions.ts:88, 141 — 'Collect Target' / 'Collect Race' gameplay goals
- src/ui/setup/profileModalProgressRenderer.ts:155-157 — 'Collectibles' stat with coin icon
- index.html:265 — 'Collect & Lock' room action; index.html:2885 — 'Collection' profile tab
- src/ui/roomProtection.ts:7 — 'Protected' label for the same state
- index.html:179 / src/ui/setup/gameMenu.ts:39 — 'My Rooms' opens the 'rooms' tab
- index.html:2884 — that tab is labelled 'Levels'
- src/mint/roomWalletCost.ts:28 — balance printed with 18-digit precision

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Leave the gameplay word 'Collectibles' alone: it covers gems, keys, potions and Lost Songs, not just coins. Rename only the two wallet-only ownership labels, for example 'Collection' tab to 'Collected Rooms' and 'View collectible' to 'View collected room'. That stays within F246's 'Collect & Lock' decision. Rename the profile 'Levels' tab (index.html:2884) to 'Rooms' to match 'My Rooms' and its own empty state. Round the wallet balance in roomWalletCostMessage (roomWalletCost.ts:30, not :28) to about 6 decimals, rounding down so the balance never looks bigger than it is. The low-balance check already compares exact bigint values, and the test at roomWalletCost.test.ts:11 pins full precision for formatRoomEth, so add a separate display formatter instead of changing formatRoomEth. Drop the Explore 'challenge levels' change: those sorts really do include only rooms with goals. Treat 'Protected' vs 'Locked' as optional: hudViewModel.ts:464 deliberately shows 'Protected' to visitors without a wallet.

### F479: Visitors without a wallet still download NFT owner addresses and token IDs whenever they tap a room

- **Area:** Design, UX and accessibility (reviewer: Gap review: Collect & Lock: room collecting, wallet approvals and the crypto gate)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F246

**Summary.** Jonathan's rule says crypto-only data such as owner addresses must not be fetched for visitors without a wallet. Every visitor who selects a room downloads its full summary, which includes the NFT owner's wallet address, token ID, contract and artwork hash. Nothing on screen shows these to non-wallet visitors, so they are simply not needed. Separately, the 'Protected' Explore sort is shown to everyone. The team decided 'protected' is not crypto, but a list of rooms filtered by 'was collected as an NFT' is a judgement call for Jonathan.

**Technical detail.**

Selecting any published room calls hudState.ensureSelectedOwnershipLoaded (hudState.ts:343-365) → loadRoomOwnershipDetails → GET /api/rooms/:id/summary (composition/ui.ts:226-233). The worker summary carries 8 minted* fields: chain, contract, tokenId, owner wallet, synced-at, metadata version/updated/hash (rooms/store.ts:624-631). It is publicly cached for anonymous visitors (rooms/routes.ts:151-170). For visitors without a wallet, hudViewModel only needs isMinted and claimer. Edit rights for a signed-in owner on a wallet-less device can come from summary.permissions.canSaveDraft, as roomOwnershipEdit.ts:44-47 already does. Fix: the client appends crypto=1 only when hasCryptoWallet(); otherwise the server returns a 'protected' boolean and omits the minted* fields. That gives a separate cache key, so there is no cache mixing.

Related: the editor's idle status builds 'Collected & Locked · Token #N' and 'Owner: 0x…' text unconditionally (roomSession.ts:420-455). It is hidden only by a regex filter at render time (editor/chrome.ts:113, /token|mint|NFT|wallet|on-chain|owner:|owned by|collect(?: room| & lock)/). Any new crypto wording that misses the regex would leak, so branching on hasCryptoWallet() in getIdleStatusDetails is sturdier.

Protected sort: index.html:2828 has no data-crypto, and exploreModal.ts:391 shows it whenever the API advertises it. Badges ('Protected', 'n/m cells protected') are useful to non-wallet builders because they explain why a room can't be edited. A sort that lists only collected rooms is closer to a marketplace view. Decide whether to add data-crypto to that one button.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/hudState.ts:363-365 — every room selection loads ownership details
- src/scenes/overworld/composition/ui.ts:226-233 — that call fetches the full room summary
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/store.ts:624-631 — the summary includes owner wallet, token id, contract and metadata hash
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:166-169 — anonymous summaries are publicly cached for 20 s
- src/scenes/editor/chrome.ts:113 — crypto status is hidden by a regex, not at the source
- src/scenes/editor/roomSession.ts:420-455 — idle status always builds token/owner text
- index.html:2828 — Protected sort button has no data-crypto

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** This is payload hygiene against the literal rule, not a user-facing defect. No extra request, RPC or quota is spent and nothing is displayed, so the skill's reason for the rule does not apply. A complete fix must strip minted* fields from /summary, /current and GET /api/rooms/:id (and the ownership refresh) for non-wallet visitors. It must also replace the client logic that keys off those fields: hudViewModel.ts:270-273 viewerOwnsMintedRoom uses mintedOwnerWalletAddress without a wallet gate, and EditorScene.ts:1385, roomSession.ts:1130/1200/1205 and viewModel.ts:63/147 use mintedTokenId. They would switch to a 'protected' boolean plus permissions.canSaveDraft. That is medium effort. The editor-status regex currently catches all crypto wording, so moving the check to getIdleStatusDetails is optional hardening. The Protected Explore sort is a decision already shipped and documented in PR #275, so it is a question for Jonathan, not a defect.

### F483: main isn't protected: a PR was merged before its checks finished, failed lint, and auto-deployed

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** Nothing on GitHub stops a pull request from being merged before CI finishes or while CI is red. On October 20, PR #268 was merged 25 seconds after its checks started. Its lint check then failed, and main stayed red for two hours. Cloudflare Pages builds main automatically, so that unchecked code went live. Turn on branch protection that requires the Quality checks.

**Technical detail.**

`gh api repos/songadaymann/wamp/branches/main/protection` returns 404 'Branch not protected'.

Timeline for PR #268 (00c3bb61, 'Let Jimothy face both ways, step-jump, and wander'):
- Its PR run 39445619022 started at 2026-10-20T15:08:08Z.
- The PR was merged at 15:08:33Z by its author. The status rollup now shows quality: FAILURE (1 failed, 11 passed).
- The main push run 39445688395 failed `npm run lint` with 'File has too many lines (2351). Maximum allowed is 2342 max-lines' for src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects.ts (pinned at eslint.config.js:12).
- Main stayed red until 254eea33, which passed CI at 17:09Z.

Pages builds main on every push (docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md:518 describes 'the automatic main Pages build'), so the red commit reached production. That bypassed the `npm run check` gate that scripts/deploy_prod.mjs:46-48 applies to manual deploys. Two outside contributors merge into this repo (#185/#222 and #268), so this isn't hypothetical.

This time it was only a size-ratchet error. The same path would ship a failing test or a broken build.

Fix:
1. Add a GitHub ruleset on main: require a pull request; require the status checks `quality` and `mobile-smoke` (others stay advisory until the flakes in the browser-check finding are fixed); block force-push.
2. Optionally point the Pages production branch at a `release` branch that deploy_prod.mjs fast-forwards after its checks.

**Evidence.**

- gh api repos/songadaymann/wamp/branches/main/protection — HTTP 404 'Branch not protected'
- gh pr view 268 — mergedAt 2026-10-20T15:08:33Z; statusCheckRollup quality: FAILURE
- gh run 39445619022 — PR run created 15:08:08Z, conclusion failure (quality)
- gh run 39445688395 --log-failed — 'File has too many lines (2351). Maximum allowed is 2342  max-lines'
- eslint.config.js:12 — 'src/scenes/overworld/liveObjects.ts': 2342
- gh run list main — 00c3bb61 failure at 15:08:35Z, next success 254eea33 at 17:09:21Z
- scripts/deploy_prod.mjs:46-48 — manual deploys run `npm run check`; Pages auto-build does not
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md:518 — 'the automatic main Pages build finished afterward and replaced custom-domain asset references'
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:3-6 — checks run on pull_request and push, but nothing requires them

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Main has no branch protection or ruleset, and PR #268 was merged 25 seconds after its checks started while `quality` then failed on lint (liveObjects.ts 2351 > 2342), leaving main red from 15:08Z to about 17:19Z.
  
  That red commit did not go live. Both Cloudflare Pages production builds for 00c3bb61 reported "Build failed", most likely because of the production-only `world-tiles:release:check --strict` prebuild guard tripping on the Jimothy asset-catalog change. The site stayed on the previous build until 254eea33.
  
  The real gap is narrower: the Pages auto-build on main runs only tsc, vite build and the world-tile guard. A commit that fails only lint, unit tests or browser smokes would go live.
  
  Recommended fix:
  - Add a ruleset that requires the `quality` (and optionally `mobile-smoke`) status checks before merge.
  - Put the repo owner on the bypass list, or don't require PRs for admins. Claude delivery lanes push "Record ... delivery" commits straight to main.
  - Optionally make the Pages build command, or a release branch, depend on green CI.
  
  The contributors in question are one write-access collaborator (KamiSawZe), not two outside contributors.
- **partially confirmed.** The core gap is real. main has no branch protection or ruleset, and a write collaborator (KamiSawZe, the only outside contributor) merged PR #268 25 seconds after its checks started. Its lint failure left main red for about 2 hours.
  
  The commit did not go live, though. Both Cloudflare Pages builds of 00c3bb61 (wamp and wampland) failed. The production Pages prebuild runs the strict world-tile asset-contract guard, and #268 changed the Jimothy catalog entry. That guard most likely blocked the build; tsc passes on that commit. #268 reached production only inside 254eea33, after CI had passed.
  
  The Pages auto-build already gates on tsc, vite build and the world-tile release guard. What it skips is lint, unit tests and the smoke checks, so the residual risk is a failing test shipping, not a broken build.
  
  It has happened once in about 80 main merges this week, with zero player impact. Of the other red main runs, #281 was an admin-lane merge with cancelled PR jobs, and #248 and #284 were post-merge flakes that protection would not catch.
  
  Revised fix: add a main ruleset that requires the `quality` and `mobile-smoke` checks before merging PRs, with the songadaymann admin account as a bypass actor. Without that bypass, the agent lanes' direct "Record F... delivery" pushes to main would be blocked. This restrains write collaborators like the #268 case. Optionally, also have the agent lanes wait for green checks before running `gh pr merge`.
- **partially confirmed.** The repository facts are right: main is unprotected, and PR #268 was merged 25 s after its checks started and turned main red for 2 h. But the commit did NOT reach production. Both production Pages builds of 00c3bb61 failed. The prebuild step's strict world-tile asset-contract check (scripts/check_pages_release.mjs, then world_tile_asset_contract_check.ts --strict) blocked them, because the PR changed GAME_OBJECTS, and docs/review/wamp-wallet-recovery-2026-10-20.md:104 records the block. A broken build can't ship either, since the Pages build runs tsc and vite and a failure leaves the last deployment live.
  
  The real exposure is narrower: code that compiles but fails lint, tests or smoke could auto-deploy if one write collaborator, or an agent, merges early. In about 100 merges this happened once, and production was not affected. Recommended fix: add a ruleset on main that requires only the `quality` check, gives the repo admin a bypass (the owner pushes "Record ..." commits directly), and blocks force-push. Leave mobile-smoke advisory, because it failed on main after #284 even though it passed on the PR. A possible alternative is to run lint and test in the production-only prebuild.

**2026-10-22 delivered.** Created with `POST /repos/songadaymann/wamp/rulesets`: `required_status_checks` (`quality`, `mobile-smoke`, integration 15368 = GitHub Actions, not strict) and `non_fast_forward` on `refs/heads/main`, with bypass actor RepositoryRole 5 (Admin), mode `always`. `GET /repos/songadaymann/wamp/rules/branches/main` lists both rules. Write collaborators (KamiSawZe) can no longer merge before those two checks pass. The other browser checks stay advisory; F482's console-noise flakes are still open. ### F485: Pinned Node version (.nvmrc = 20) can't run about 60 test files; the tests and CI need Node 22

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The repo's .nvmrc file tells tools and AI agents to use Node 20.19.4, and nobody has changed it since the first commit. About 60 test files use Node's built-in SQLite, which only exists from Node 22.5. Under the pinned version those files crash before any test runs, while CI quietly uses Node 22. Pin Node 22 in one place and have CI read that same file.

**Technical detail.**

.nvmrc:1 = `20.19.4`, last touched by 67e3e7f8 (2026-03-09, Initial commit). Every CI job sets `node-version: 22` by hand (quality.yml:16 and 17 copies), so CI never notices. 25 test files import `node:sqlite` directly (for example guestRuns/progress.test.ts:2 and mint/roomMetadataCacheCli.test.ts:3). So does the shared fixture activity/testDatabase.ts:2, which activity/*, runs/discoveryTestDatabase.ts and collections/testDatabase.ts reuse. That makes about 61 test files that need Node 22.5 or later.

Verified: running vitest under ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.19.4 on activity/store.test.ts and guestRuns/progress.test.ts makes both suites FAIL with `Error: No such built-in module: node:sqlite`. ESLint 10 also requires ^20.19 || ^22.13 || >=24 (node_modules/eslint/package.json:237). The owner's agent memory already carries a 'use Node 22' gotcha, which is a symptom of this.

Fix (about 10 minutes):
1. Set .nvmrc to 22.22.0, the version used locally and in CI.
2. Add `"engines": {"node": ">=22.13"}` to package.json.
3. Replace `node-version: 22` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc` in all quality.yml and world-map-health.yml jobs, so local and CI can't drift again.
4. Optional: pass `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning` via vitest execArgv. Each run prints 61 SQLite warnings (122 lines) into the logs agents read.

**Evidence.**

- .nvmrc:1 — `20.19.4`; git log shows only the initial commit 67e3e7f8 (2026-03-09)
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:16 — `node-version: 22` (repeated in every job)
- src/cloudflare/worker/activity/testDatabase.ts:2 — `import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'` in the shared fixture
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/progress.test.ts:2 — direct node:sqlite import
- vitest run under Node v20.19.4 — 'FAIL ... Error: No such built-in module: node:sqlite' for both suites
- node_modules/eslint/package.json:237 — engines ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **confirmed.** No correction.
- **partially confirmed.** Real tooling defect: .nvmrc pins 20.19.4, and 61 of the 609 test files transitively need node:sqlite (Node 22.5 or later), while CI hardcodes 22 in 16 setup-node blocks (15 in quality.yml, 1 in world-map-health.yml). The ESLint engines line does not show breakage, since 20.19.4 satisfies ^20.19.0. A better supporting fact is that the direct devDependency miniflare 4.20260730.0 requires Node >=22. The 'use Node 22' memory gotcha comes from shells defaulting to Node 23, not from .nvmrc. The fix should note that Cloudflare Pages (the wampland project auto-builds main) reads .nvmrc unless NODE_VERSION is set, so bumping it also moves production front-end builds from 20.19.4 to 22. Check the first Pages build afterwards. Impact is contributor and agent-only (an agent already hit this in docs/2026-07-29-gameplay-performance-plan.md:82), so medium rather than high.
- **partially confirmed.** Real and worth doing, with these corrections:
  - `node:sqlite` works without a flag only from Node 22.13, not 22.5.
  - CI pins `node-version: 22` 16 times: 15 in quality.yml and 1 in world-map-health.yml.
  - The ESLint engines range accepts 20.19.4, so it supports the >=22.13 floor but is not evidence that the current pin fails.
  - Changing .nvmrc also changes the Node version Cloudflare Pages uses for both automatic wamp and wampland production builds (from 20.19.4 to 22.22.0, unless a dashboard NODE_VERSION overrides it). The PR should say so and confirm both Pages build checks pass.
  
  Impact is medium, not high. The trap affects only developer and agent tooling, and an agent already hit it (docs/2026-07-29-gameplay-performance-plan.md:82).

**2026-10-22 delivered.** PR #289. [Receipt](wamp-round2-security-and-step1-2026-10-22.md).

### F487: Riskiest write paths barely tested: Expanded Room editing 0%, room save/publish 15%, agent tokens, Worlds

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F064
- **Also covers:** Worlds Worker has 2,581 lines but only two test files, and the room-clear test uses a fake schema that hides a production failure

**Summary.** About 45% of the code runs under tests. Run-finishing and multiplayer code are well covered, at over 80%. But four risky areas are thin: the server code that creates, saves and publishes Expanded Rooms has no tests at all, and the main room save/publish route file is 15% covered. The check that rejects revoked or disabled AI-agent tokens is never tested, and the Worlds classroom routes are at 0% even though Worlds is switched on in production. Add route-level tests using the existing SQLite fixture, and set coverage floors for these folders so coverage can't slide back.

**Technical detail.**

Ran the full suite with v8 coverage (reports written to scratch; 609 files and 5,232 tests, all passing): 44.8% of lines over 1,047 files. Per-file line coverage:
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts: 0/122. This covers create, draft save, publish, unpublish and cell add/remove. Cell add/remove is where minted rooms are kept from being absorbed: loadProtectedMintedRoomIds at :391, used at :232.
- expandedRooms/runRoutes.ts: 74/186 (39.8%).
- rooms/routes.ts: 32/219 (14.6%). handleRoomRequest at :87 routes claim, save and publish.
- courses/store.ts: 10%; courses/routes.ts: 33.7%.
- agents/routes.ts: 0/84 and agents/store.ts: 7/51. loadAgentTokenAuth (:302-339) is the gate for bot writes, and its revoked/inactive rejection at :339 is never executed.
- worlds/routes.ts 0/127, memberships.ts 0/67, publication.ts 0/67. Worlds is live: WORLDS_ENABLED="1" at wrangler.jsonc:41.
- src/auth/client.ts: 184/711 (25.9%). F064 covered the extracted auth-state module, not the client.

Well covered: worker/runs 84%, presence 83.5%, mint worker 79%. partykit/presenceServer.ts is 80.8% covered but excluded from the repo's coverage include (vitest.config.ts:12 covers only src/**).

CI browser smokes replay recorded API responses (scripts/lib/apiFixtures.mjs:1-7), so they never execute these Worker routes. CI runs `npm run test` without coverage (quality.yml:21), and vitest.config.ts has no thresholds.

Fix:
1. Write route tests on activity/testDatabase.ts fixture(), which applies the real migrations in about 59 ms. Cover:
   - Expanded Room publish, and cell add/remove refusing protected minted cells, plus non-owner 403.
   - rooms/routes save with a stale base and publish limits.
   - Agent token revoked, agent disabled, and missing scope.
   - Worlds invite/accept and publication approve/reject.
2. Add `coverage.thresholds` per glob (for example worker/runs/** 80, worker/expandedRooms/** 60, worker/agents/** 70) plus a CI coverage step. The full coverage run took 86 s against 44 s without coverage.
3. Add partykit/** to the coverage include.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts:155-206 — handleExpandedRoomCellAdd: auth, published-version and duplicate checks, then saveCourseDraft; 0% covered
- src/cloudflare/worker/expandedRooms/editorRoutes.ts:232 and :391-424 — minted-room protection lookup used when removing cells; 0% covered
- src/cloudflare/worker/agents/store.ts:339 — `if (!row || row.revoked_at || row.agent_is_active !== 1) return null;` never executed by tests
- src/cloudflare/worker/rooms/routes.ts:87 — handleRoomRequest; 14.6% line coverage
- wrangler.jsonc:41 — "WORLDS_ENABLED": "1" while worlds/routes.ts, memberships.ts and publication.ts are at 0%
- vitest.config.ts:9-13 — coverage include only src/**/*.ts, no thresholds
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:21 — CI runs `npm run test` without coverage
- scripts/lib/apiFixtures.mjs:1-7 — browser smokes replay recorded API responses instead of running the Worker
- src/cloudflare/worker/worlds/access.test.ts:82-100 — hand-built users/rooms tables plus migration 0045 only
- src/cloudflare/worker/admin/roomClear.test.ts:33-39 — ad-hoc schema without world_room_claims
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRoomDrafts/claims.test.ts:65 — existing replay-all-migrations loop
- src/cloudflare/worker/runs/finishDeferral.test.ts:41 — the same loop copied again

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** Seven corrections:
  
  (1) CI does run the real Worker. Service smokes (smoke_collections_service, smoke_room_protection_service, smoke_mint_network_service, smoke_wallet_auth_service, smoke_map_capture_service) run the bundled Worker in Miniflare on native D1, and three of them seed it with activity/testDatabase.ts. None of them calls room publish, the Expanded Room editor, agents or Worlds. scripts/smoke_worlds_pilot.ts (`smoke:worlds:local`) exercises the Worlds join, membership, publication and settings routes, but only by hand against a local Worker, not in CI. Reuse these harnesses instead of describing CI as only replaying recorded responses.
  
  (2) Room save is already partly tested. rooms/store saveDraft runs 33 times, and the stale-base guard assertDraftUnchangedSince is tested in editConflict.test.ts. The real gap is publishRoom (rooms/store.ts:989), revertRoom and setCanonicalRoomVersion, which run 0 times.
  
  (3) The Expanded Room gap includes courses/store.ts: createCourseDraft, saveCourseDraft, publishCourse and unpublishCourse run 0 times. The cheapest first test is the pure getExpandedRoomCellRemovalError.
  
  (4) agents/store.ts:339 does run, 4 times, but only through `!row`. The revoked_at and agent_is_active operands are never evaluated.
  
  (5) No folder matches "presence 83.5%": src/presence is 78% and worker/presence is 3.4%. The reviewer's 1,047-file/44.8% run had partykit added to the coverage include; the repo's own config gives about 1,046 files and 44.6%.
  
  (6) Split the merged claim into its own small defect item. Admin room clear (admin/routes.ts:330) aborts in production on the world_room_claims provenance trigger for any claimed room. Fix it, and switch roomClear.test.ts to the migrated fixture.
  
  (7) "Worlds classroom routes" is mislabeled: these are the Worlds pilot routes; classroom code lives under worker/school.
- **partially confirmed.** Room save is not part of the gap. saveDraft runs 33 times in tests, and the stale-base check (assertDraftUnchangedSince, rooms/store.ts:844) has its own tests in editConflict.test.ts. Most of rooms/routes.ts is request dispatch, while the logic lives in rooms/store.ts, which is 49% covered. The real room gap is publish and revert: publishRoom (store.ts:989), revertRoom (:1162) and appendWorldPublishStatements all have 0 calls. So drop "rooms/routes save with a stale base" from the fix and test publish and revert instead.
  
  Worlds is the numbered-Worlds pilot, not "classroom" routes. Its routes, memberships and publication only serve Worlds created through admin complimentary grants, so few real users reach them. The WAMP 0 claim/publish integration, by contrast, runs on every room write.
  
  The merged room-clear sub-claim is a concrete, unlisted production bug that should get its own item. POST /api/admin/rooms/:id/clear deletes the room row, which cascades into world_room_claims (0045:91), whose BEFORE DELETE trigger aborts (0045:215-219). The clear therefore fails on all 607 backfilled rooms and on every room claimed since. The bug is still on origin/main 80151ad1. The fix should either delete only runs, versions and points without deleting the rooms row, or reset the room in place. Add a regression test on fixture() with a world_room_claims row.
  
  Measured coverage is 44.6% over 1,046 files, not 44.8% over 1,047.
- **partially confirmed.** The coverage figures are accurate. Corrections:
  (a) Agent tokens: agents/store.ts:339 runs. Only the `!row` operand is exercised (branch hits [4,0,0]); the revoked and inactive operands and the success path are never evaluated.
  (b) Expanded Rooms: editorRoutes.ts create, save and publish are thin wrappers over courses/store.ts (10%) and courses/routes.ts. The real gap is courses/store. Minted protection applies only to cell removal (cell add has no minted check). The rule is the pure function getExpandedRoomCellRemovalError (src/expandedRooms/model.ts:177), which is untested and can be unit-tested cheaply.
  (c) Rooms: rooms/routes.ts is a dispatcher. Save and publish logic is in commandCore.ts (83%) and rooms/store.ts (49%). The stale-base rule is already tested in rooms/editConflict.test.ts, so route tests mainly add auth, scope and origin wiring.
  (d) Worlds: a manual end-to-end smoke exists (scripts/smoke_worlds_pilot.ts, `npm run smoke:worlds:local`) but is not in CI. migration.test.ts covers SQL-level publication approval.
  (e) Add a concrete defect: admin room clear (admin/routes.ts:330 here; :346 on main 80151ad1) deletes the room. That cascades into world_room_claims, whose BEFORE DELETE trigger in 0045:215-219 aborts with 'World room provenance is permanent' (reproduced in node:sqlite). Every claimed or published room has a claim row, so clear fails on essentially every real room. roomClear.test.ts's hand-built schema hides this.
  Do first: fix room clear and move its test to fixture(); then the agent-token gate tests, the removal-rule unit test, a courses/store save/publish test, and Worlds route tests or Worlds smoke in CI; then thresholds.

### F480: 48 of 69 smoke and probe scripts never run in CI, and at least five are broken on main

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Dead code: Worker, scripts, configs and docs)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Also covers:** 40 of 62 smoke tests never run in CI, and wiring in a new one takes edits in six places

**Summary.** Only 21 of the 69 browser and probe test scripts run automatically. The rest are only run by hand, so they quietly break when the UI changes. Three were flagged as broken on Oct 11 and are still broken. I found a fourth that has been broken since Oct 2 because the email-code pop-up it waits for no longer exists, and a fifth that can't start at all because it needs a library that isn't installed. A cheap automatic check that the IDs the smokes use still exist would have caught the Oct 2 break.

**Technical detail.**

Count: scripts/ has 69 smoke/probe files. 21 are exercised by .github/workflows/quality.yml, directly or through scripts/mobile_smoke_ci.mjs: mobile_smoke, assist, auth_state, chat_identity, collections(+service), dom_contract, expanded_leaderboards, gameplay_pause, keyboard_bindings, map_capture(+service), mint_network(+service), room_artwork, room_ownership, room_protection(+service), wallet_auth(+service) and worker_safety_probes. The other 48 only run by hand. Known broken: docs/review/wamp-split-colliders-phone-ci-2026-10-11.md:37-40 lists smoke_editor_dock, smoke_editor_history and smoke_police_enemies as stale on main, unfixed 10 days later. Newly broken: scripts/smoke_wallet_email_link_modal.mjs:113 waits for `#email-code-modal:not(.hidden)` and :125 for it to hide. Commit 5a79b35b (2026-10-02) replaced that modal with an inline panel (index.html:190 `id="auth-email-code"`). No element with id email-code-modal exists in index.html or src, so the smoke times out. It has no npm script and only knip.json references it. Cannot run: scripts/remote_rollout_check.mjs:3 imports { Wallet } from 'ethers', which is not a dependency; knip reports it as unlisted and `npm ls ethers` is empty. A static scan of every smoke's `#id` selectors against index.html and src/**/*.ts flagged email-code-modal as the only absence that is actually awaited. Fix plan: (1) Extend scripts/smoke_dom_contract.mjs, already in CI, to scan scripts/smoke_*.mjs for `#id` selectors and getElementById strings and fail when an ID exists nowhere in index.html or src. About 30 lines. (2) Give each script a status header (ci / nightly / manual / retired) and add a nightly workflow that runs the manual replay-capable smokes with --skip-build. (3) Fix or delete the five broken scripts. remote_rollout_check also targets the retired PartyKit host (see the PartyKit finding).

**Evidence.**

- scripts/smoke_wallet_email_link_modal.mjs:113 — await page.locator('#email-code-modal:not(.hidden)').waitFor()
- index.html:190 — email code UI is now <div id="auth-email-code">; no #email-code-modal anywhere (changed in 5a79b35b)
- docs/review/wamp-split-colliders-phone-ci-2026-10-11.md:37-40 — smoke_editor_dock, smoke_editor_history, smoke_police_enemies stale on main
- scripts/remote_rollout_check.mjs:3 — import { Wallet } from 'ethers'; ethers is not installed
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:30-31 — CI runs smoke:dom-contract and smoke:worker-safety; most smokes are absent
- scripts/mobile_smoke_ci.mjs:34 — 16 `args.has('--x-only')` flags OR-ed to decide whether to skip the base smoke
- scripts/mobile_smoke_ci.mjs:43-149 — 14 near-identical spawnSync blocks, one per feature smoke
- scripts/smoke_first_publish.mjs (head) — default base http://127.0.0.1:3033; not invoked by quality.yml or mobile_smoke_ci.mjs
- scripts/smoke_editor_touch.mjs (head) — default base http://127.0.0.1:3031, 'Synthetic fixtures are local only'
- src/config/executableEntryContract.test.ts:142 — 'keeps Knip synchronized with every executable and build-time root'
- scripts/remote_rollout_check.mjs:3 — import { Wallet } from 'ethers' (not in package.json; node_modules/ethers missing)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** 48 of 69 smoke and probe scripts never run in CI (the count is right), but three are confirmed or likely broken on main, not five. smoke_wallet_email_link_modal waits on #email-code-modal, which 5a79b35b removed; the fix is to wait on #auth-email-code. smoke_editor_history's tablet Back button covers Undo (Oct 19 receipt). smoke_police_enemies is still stale (untouched since August). smoke_editor_dock was fixed on Oct 16 (F112) and its receipt says it passes. remote_rollout_check is not a smoke, and its missing `ethers` is already documented as a manual prerequisite in docs/development/architecture.md:61-63.
  
  The cheap fix is to extend smoke_dom_contract.mjs to scan scripts/smoke_*.mjs for '#id' and getElementById strings, with an allowlist for intentional assertAbsent/count()==0 IDs (#rotate-gate, #install-help-modal, #btn-install-help-open, #btn-editor-drawer-close, #btn-room-goal-intro-close).
