### F482: Browser checks fail at random in about 4% of CI runs, mostly on harmless console noise

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** In the last 100 CI runs, 4 had to be re-run because a browser check failed and then passed on exactly the same code. The checks treat any console error as a failure, so an aborted chat poll or a Safari 'connection reset' fails the run. Each flake costs 10-15 minutes, and it tempts an agent to 'fix' a bug that isn't there. Share one console-error filter across the checks, stop logging aborted chat polls as errors, and make un-recorded API calls fail cleanly.

**Technical detail.**

`gh run list` (100 runs, 2026-10-18 to 10-21) shows 5 runs with attempt 2. The first-attempt failures:
- 39560743143 assist-mode: `'Failed to poll chat messages AbortError: signal is aborted without reason'`.
- 39299465410 gameplay-pause: three WebKit `'Failed to load resource: Error receiving data: Connection reset by peer'`.
- 39415155266 auth-state: `["Context is stopped"]`.
- 39305050781 mobile-smoke.
All four passed on re-run of the same SHA.

Why this happens:
- src/ui/chat/panel.ts:375 calls `console.error('Failed to poll chat messages', error)` even for AbortError.
- smoke_assist.mjs:61 collects every console error and :94/:138 `assert.deepEqual(errors, [])`. smoke_gameplay_pause.mjs:52-53 and :178 do the same.
- 46 scripts hand-roll their own `page.on('console')` collectors. Only smoke_auth_state.mjs:114-131 filters teardown noise.
- The assist-mode log also shows vite `http proxy error ... ECONNREFUSED` for /api/chat/messages and /api/guest-activity/heartbeat. vite.config.ts:122-127 proxies /api to localhost:8787 and `vite preview` inherits server.proxy, so a request that slips past the Playwright route hits a dead port and fails nondeterministically.

Fix:
1. panel.ts: return quietly when `error.name === 'AbortError'`.
2. Add scripts/lib/consoleErrors.mjs: one collector with a short allowlist for transport noise (resource 'Connection reset by peer', teardown 'Context is stopped'). Use it in the 46 scripts.
3. Set `preview: { proxy: {} }` for the smoke build, or have apiFixtures answer un-recorded /api with a deterministic 503 recorded in `report().misses`.
4. Have mobile_smoke_ci.mjs retry a failed child once and print FLAKY, so flakes are visible but don't block.

**Evidence.**

- gh run 39560743143 attempt 1 — assist-mode AssertionError, actual: 'Failed to poll chat messages AbortError: signal is aborted without reason'
- gh run 39299465410 attempt 1 — gameplay-pause: 3x 'Failed to load resource: Error receiving data: Connection reset by peer'
- gh run 39415155266 attempt 1 — auth-state AssertionError ["Context is stopped"]
- src/ui/chat/panel.ts:375 — console.error('Failed to poll chat messages', error) for every failure including aborts
- scripts/smoke_assist.mjs:61 — every console error pushed to errors; :138 assert.deepEqual(errors, [])
- scripts/smoke_gameplay_pause.mjs:52-53,178 — same strict console assertion
- scripts/smoke_auth_state.mjs:114-131 — the only script that filters teardown noise
- vite.config.ts:122-127 — /api proxied to http://localhost:8787 (inherited by vite preview in CI)

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** CI flakes are real: 4 of the last 90 Quality runs failed and then passed on the same SHA (~4.4%), and all four failed strict console-error assertions. The main avoidable cause is new. Since #267 (254eea33), src/api/pageReadLifetime.ts aborts every apiRequest GET on pagehide/beforeunload. The background-read catch blocks that call console.error then log AbortError during page teardown. panel.ts:375 is the periodic one that tripped smoke_assist, and about 15 other `Failed to load ...` sites can do the same.
  
  Fix:
  (a) Add a shared isAbortError helper and skip page-lifetime aborts in those catch blocks, not only in the chat panel.
  (b) Use one shared collector in the ~14 scripts that CI runs. It should record m.location().url. Any teardown filter should apply only during a navigation or close window, as smoke_auth_state does. Do not use a global allowlist for 'Connection reset by peer' or 'Context is stopped': the root cause of 'Context is stopped' is still unproven, and the repo's review docs record that no error was filtered.
  (c) `preview.proxy: {}` is optional hygiene. The requests that reach the vite proxy are unload/keepalive requests that Playwright does not route; apiFixtures already returns a 404 for un-recorded /api requests and lists them in misses.
  (d) An optional retry-once with a FLAKY label would also cover the non-console timeout flakes, such as mobile-smoke mann.cool in 39702059313.

### F486: progress.md and feature-ledger.md grew 6x since Oct 3, copy each other, and 71% of commits edit them

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Dead code: Worker, scripts, configs and docs)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F061

**Summary.** The two running log files at the top of the repo went from about 95 KB and 61 KB on Oct 3 to 586 KB and 352 KB today. About half of progress.md is a word-for-word copy of the ledger. Nearly three out of four commits edit the top of these same two files, so two lanes working in parallel will keep colliding, and every AI session that reads them wastes a lot of context. Keep the ledger to one line per feature, stop committing progress.md (it is already in .gitignore), and archive the history once.

**Technical detail.**

Size: progress.md is 585,768 bytes / 2,594 lines. On Oct 3 it was 95,133 bytes (`git show $(git rev-list -1 --before='2026-10-03 23:59' HEAD):progress.md | wc -c`); F061 cited 78 KB. feature-ledger.md is 351,945 bytes, up from 61,186. The checklist details file is another 1,029,512 bytes. Duplication: 137 of progress.md's 273 `## ` sections, 182,231 bytes in all, are byte-identical to sections in feature-ledger.md. Both files start with the same heading, '## 2026-10-21 — F246 owner collection reminder' (line 1 of each). Churn: 301 of the 426 non-merge commits since Oct 3 (71%) modify progress.md or feature-ledger.md, nearly always by prepending at line 1, so any two concurrent PRs conflict. Tracking contradiction: .gitignore:15 lists progress.md, but the file is tracked; it was force-added again in 9db8b42c on 2026-09-04. Fix plan, all small: (1) Move the current progress.md once to docs/history/progress-2026.md, then `git rm --cached progress.md` so the .gitignore entry takes effect and it stays a local scratch log. (2) Make feature-ledger.md one table row per feature: date, F-ID, PR, receipt link. The long prose already lives in docs/review/<receipt>.md. (3) To end conflicts for good, write per-PR fragment files such as docs/ledger.d/<date>-<slug>.md and concatenate them in a script. (4) The AGENTS.md from F061 should point at the receipts, not at these logs. Payoff: about 770 KB less for agents to read, and no conflicts between parallel lanes on these files.

**Evidence.**

- progress.md:1 — '## 2026-10-21 — F246 owner collection reminder', the same heading as feature-ledger.md:1
- feature-ledger.md:1 — the same entry duplicated; 137 of 273 progress.md sections are byte-identical to ledger sections
- .gitignore:15 — 'progress.md' is ignored, yet `git ls-files progress.md` shows it tracked
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10-details.md:6680 — F061 measured progress.md at 78 KB; it is now 585,768 bytes

**Fact-checks (3 independent reviewers).**

- **partially confirmed.** The sizes, the 137 copied sections, the 71% churn and the .gitignore contradiction are all accurate. The corrections:
  - **Duplication.** It is 50% of progress.md by section count but only 31% by bytes (182 KB).
  - **Where commits edit.** The first changed hunk is at line 1 in 47% of commits and within the first 20 lines in 76%, not "nearly always at line 1".
  - **Conflicts.** Conflicts are a growing risk rather than a frequent event: only 2 of 190 merges since Oct 3 needed a hand-resolved change here (e2d7d0ad, 2808b5d9).
  - **Fix step (4).** Drop it. The F061 AGENTS.md was declined ("won't do", 2026-10-13).
  - **Fix step (1).** When moving progress.md to docs/history/, also update the evidence pointers in docs/development/ghost-run-archive.md:25 and docs/development/checkup-delivery-2026-10-03.md:108 and :289.
  - **Fix step (2).** Archive the ledger prose before cutting it to one row per feature. Only 135 of 225 sections link a receipt.
  - **Codex skill.** Update ~/.codex/skills/develop-web-game/SKILL.md (lines 28 and 135-137), which tells every Codex session to read both files. Otherwise the habit continues.
  - **Ratings.** Impact is medium (developer workflow only), effort small.
- **partially confirmed.** The core facts hold: about 6x growth since Oct 3, 137 identical sections (about 182 KB), a tracked file that .gitignore lists, and roughly two thirds to three quarters of commits touching the files. Four things need correcting:
  
  1. **Mechanism.** Commits did not 'nearly always prepend at line 1'. Until about Oct 19 entries were appended at the end of each file, and since then they are prepended at the top. Only about 41-44% of commits since Oct 3 begin their edit at line 1. Both styles insert at one fixed point, so concurrent branches still conflict.
     - Evidence: merges e2d7d0ad and 2808b5d9 needed hand-resolved hunks in these files.
     - Evidence: f16decd0 wiped 1,599 lines of progress.md by accident, and e62e4eb3 restored them.
     - The churn figure is 302/450 (67%) when counted from Oct 3 00:00, or 298/418 (71%) with `--since=2026-10-03`.
  2. **Impact.** Medium, not high. Nothing reaches players or builders; this is agent and merge workflow only.
  3. **Missing step: the Codex skill.** ~/.codex/skills/develop-web-game/SKILL.md (lines 28 and 133-139) tells every agent to read both files and keep updating them. Unless that skill changes to read only the head and write ledger fragments, agents will recreate the pattern.
  4. **Missing step: doc pointers and F061.** Five docs name progress.md as their evidence location: checkup-delivery-2026-10-03.md:108 and 289, ghost-run-archive.md:25, asset-intake-rules.md:293, and 2026-07-29-gameplay-performance-plan.md:75. Repoint them at the archived copy. Also merge the archive step with F061's open 'archive progress.md to docs/history' sub-item instead of tracking it twice.
- **partially confirmed.** The numbers hold, give or take: 298 of 418 commits (71%) and 137 identical sections (182 KB). Narrow the fix. Move the existing progress.md and feature-ledger.md history once into docs/history/. Then write each delivery note in one file only, and make the other file a short index. Untracking progress.md (`git rm --cached`) is only safe together with an edit to ~/.codex/skills/develop-web-game/SKILL.md:28/133-138: that skill tells agents to read both files, and the tracked progress.md is how handoffs reach separate Codex worktrees. Drop step (4), because F061's AGENTS.md was declined as won't do on 2026-10-13. Per-PR ledger fragment files (step 3) change the workflow for every lane, so that part is medium effort. Impact is medium, not high: conflicts take a minute to fix and players never see this.

### F498: The file-size limits were never lowered after this week's big refactors: the two largest files can regrow by 2,000 lines unnoticed

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Superfluous and duplicated code: scenes and game runtime)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F067
- **Also covers:** File-size ratchet never tightens: shrunk files can regrow by 2,500 lines with no lint error

**Summary.** The lint rule that stops big files from growing has a fixed limit per file, and it is only useful if the limit is lowered when a file shrinks. This week's refactors cut OverworldPlayScene by about 1,200 lines and worldStreaming by about 800, but the limits were not changed. Those two files can now grow back by 2,000 lines without lint noticing. Meanwhile seven other files sit at exactly their limit, so any added line fails lint. A tiny script that tightens every limit to the file's current size, run in CI, would fix both.

**Technical detail.**

OVERSIZED_FILE_LINES (eslint.config.js:6-27) counts non-blank lines (`skipBlankLines: true`, line 70). Current non-blank counts against the caps: OverworldPlayScene 5,128 vs 6,355 (1,227 headroom). worldStreaming 4,972 vs 5,765 (793). runs/difficulty 1,616 vs 1,762 (146). CourseEditorScene 3,328 vs 3,464 (136). EditorScene 1,888 vs 1,984 (96). rooms/store 1,754 vs 1,819 (65). Total slack across the list is 2,512 lines. git log -L shows the caps last moved on 2026-10-14 (aafc986e). The extractions came after: ba02037f (OverworldPlayScene −1,773/+725), 3f9389bd (−225/+60) and 969b5f83 (worldStreaming −971/+164), all on 2026-10-19. At the other end, swordsmanController, worldTiles/controller, earlyWorldTileBootstrap.classic, profileModal, musicPatternEditor, musicWorkflow and autotiling/solver have 0 headroom, and uiBridge 3, editRuntime 6, liveObjects 9. Fix: add scripts/ratchet-max-lines.mjs (about 25 lines). It counts non-blank lines per listed file. With --write it rewrites each cap to min(cap, actual); in CI it fails when cap > actual + 10. It also deletes entries that drop under MAX_LINES (1500). Run it once now to lock in the F066 gains.

**Evidence.**

- eslint.config.js:7 — 'src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts': 6355 (file has 5,128 non-blank lines)
- eslint.config.js:8 — worldStreaming cap 5765 (file has 4,972 non-blank lines)
- eslint.config.js:9 — CourseEditorScene cap 3464 (3,328 non-blank)
- eslint.config.js:14 — EditorScene cap 1984 (1,888 non-blank)
- eslint.config.js:70 — max-lines counts with skipBlankLines: true
- eslint.config.js:11 — swordsmanController cap 2608 equals its 2,608 non-blank lines (0 headroom)
- eslint.config.js:3-4 — 'lower a number when you split a file (F067)'
- eslint.config.js:7 — 'src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts': 6355 (file now 5,128 non-blank lines)
- eslint.config.js:8 — 'src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts': 5765 (file now 4,972)
- eslint.config.js:14 — 'src/scenes/EditorScene.ts': 1984 (file now 1,888)
- git show a9dabba8 -- src/ui/setup/profileModal.ts — logic extracted to profileCollection.ts to stay at the 1,556 pin

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds. The F066 refactors on 2026-10-19 (ba02037f, 3f9389bd, 969b5f83) never lowered the file-size caps, which still date from aafc986e on 2026-10-14. That leaves 2,512 lines of slack: OverworldPlayScene 1,227, worldStreaming 793, difficulty 146, CourseEditorScene 136, EditorScene 96, rooms/store 65. Drop the claim that the seven files at their exact cap are a problem: being pinned at current size is the stated design, and the script would not change it. The fix is to set each cap to min(cap, current non-blank count) now: 5128, 4972, 3328, 1888, 1754, 1616, and so on. Optionally add a `--write` ratchet script, plus a check in lint or CI that fails when a cap is more than ~10 lines above the file's size and names the number to change. Do not delete entries that fall under 1,500. musicWorkflow (1488) and roomComments (1483) are pinned below the default, and removing their entries would loosen them.

### F497: The dead-code report keeps growing because nothing enforces it (481 to 513 unused exports in 17 days)

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Dead code: game client)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The project has a dead-code scanner (knip), but it only prints a report and isn't part of the automatic checks, so the pile keeps growing. Most of what it flags in the game client is harmless: about 480 items are marked 'shared' but only used inside their own file. Once those are fixed and the truly dead items in this review are removed, the scanner can run in CI and stop new dead code from arriving.

**Technical detail.**

package.json:17 defines `"dead-code:report": "knip --no-exit-code"`. .github/workflows/quality.yml runs lint, styles, test, typecheck, build, size, assets, DOM contract and worker-safety, but never knip. The ledger records the baseline growing: '481 unused exports, 256 types' (feature-ledger.md:1032, commit 71ae8bda on 2026-10-04), against 513 exports and 279 types in today's report. That is 32 more exports and 23 more types.

Client breakdown (src without src/cloudflare, plus partykit), classified by reference counting:
- 418 exports and 245 types flagged.
- 480 (292 exports, 188 types) are used inside their own file only, so the fix is to delete the `export` keyword. That is mechanical and can be scripted.
- 95 (64 exports, 31 types) have no reference anywhere; they are covered by the other findings here.
- 86 are barrel re-exports or same-name collisions (see the alias-barrel finding).
- 3 duplicate exports: audio/assetUrl.ts resolveAudioAssetUrl and resolveSfxAssetUrl, courses/model.ts MAX_EXPANDED_ROOM_CELLS and MAX_COURSE_ROOMS, jam/model.ts JAM_ROOM_CLAIM_OPEN_AT and DEFAULT_JAM_SUBMISSIONS_OPEN_AT.

What knip cannot see, and this review had to find another way: exports used only by their own tests. The vitest plugin makes every test file an entry, so a transitive pass found about 1,450 lines of test-only or dead top-level code that knip does not flag. It also misses public class methods and hidden-but-present UI.

Plan: (1) one PR that drops the 480 needless exports; (2) delete the dead groups from this review; (3) add `knip --include exports,types,files,duplicates` to quality.yml with a small ignore list for test harnesses (presenceServer.testHarness.ts, worldStreaming.testHarness.ts, sceneCapabilityRegistry.testSupport.ts, roomWalletTestFixtures.ts). Optionally, (4) add a vitest-excluded knip run (`--production`) to catch exports reachable only from tests.

**Evidence.**

- package.json:17 — knip runs with --no-exit-code (report only)
- feature-ledger.md:1032 — 2026-10-04 baseline of 481 unused exports and 256 types
- src/vite-env.d.ts:19-67 — window hook declarations show the dynamic-use surface knip cannot see

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Replace plan steps (1) and (3) with this:
  1. Set `ignoreExportsUsedInFile: true` in knip.json. This is one config line, not a 480-site PR.
  2. Add a baseline ratchet to quality.yml. Run knip with `--reporter json --include exports,types,files`, compare the result with a committed baseline list of symbols and paths, and fail only on new items. The baseline is 163 exports and 69 types after the flag. That way the gate can go in now instead of waiting for about 230 remaining items to be triaged.
  3. Add src/cloudflare/worker/collections/testDatabase.ts to `ignore`, or turn its string-loaded fixture into an entry. Leave out `duplicates`, or delete the 3 intentional aliases first.
  4. Update docs/development/architecture.md:53-54 and the closeout note, which both say knip stays report-only.
  5. Drop the `--production` idea unless entries are marked with `!` first; today it reports no exports. Also drop the harness ignore entries that knip never flags.
  
  The client count of exports used only in their own file is 465 by knip's measure, not 480. Overlaps F067 item (4), whose Knip part was left not done.

### F489: scripts/ is outside type checking and real linting; two scripts already disagree with the game's types

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** TypeScript only checks the src/ folder. That leaves the 17 TypeScript files in scripts/ unchecked, including 7 test files and the Worker safety check that CI runs. Checking them now turns up real drift: one smoke test's fake world loader is missing 4 methods, and the safety probe builds an out-of-date room object. Meanwhile the 69 .mjs scripts named in the lint command get zero lint rules, because ESLint only parses them. Add a tsconfig for scripts and lint the whole folder with a basic rule set.

**Technical detail.**

tsconfig.json includes only `src/**/*` and `partykit/presenceServer.ts`. Type-checking scripts/*.ts with a scratch tsconfig that extends the repo's:
- scripts/live_construction_play_smoke.ts:24: 'Class ProbeWorldRepository incorrectly implements interface WorldRepository', missing loadCompactWorldChunkWindow, loadWorldTileConfig, loadWorldTileManifest and queryRoomSnapshots. This is the npm script smoke:live-construction-play (package.json:66).
- scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts:264: `placedObjects.push({ id, x, y })` is missing the now-required instanceId. This file runs in CI as smoke:worker-safety.
- reconcile-room-token-cache.ts:47: replaceAll needs lib ES2021, but the target is ES2020.
- The remaining errors are TS7016: missing types for the .mjs helpers the vitest files import.

Linting:
- `eslint --print-config scripts/mobile_smoke.mjs` reports 0 enabled rules. The rules block at eslint.config.js:40 matches only *.ts, and the .mjs block at :83-85 just spreads disableTypeChecked.
- package.json:18 lists 74 script paths by hand (69 .mjs, 5 .ts). 53 other script code files aren't listed at all, including 12 .ts files such as worker_safety_probes.ts.

Fix:
1. Add scripts/tsconfig.json (extends root, lib ES2022, include scripts/**/*.ts; allowJs with .d.ts for the shared .mjs helpers) and `tsc -p scripts` in typecheck.
2. Change lint to `eslint src partykit scripts`, with js recommended rules (no-undef with node globals, no-unused-vars) for .mjs.
3. Fix the two drifted fakes.
This deletes the 2,000-character lint command.

**Evidence.**

- tsconfig.json:24 — "include": ["src/**/*", "partykit/presenceServer.ts"]
- scripts/live_construction_play_smoke.ts:24 — `class ProbeWorldRepository implements WorldRepository` (tsc: missing 4 members)
- scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts:264 — badObject.placedObjects.push({ id: 'not-a-real-object', x: 10, y: 10 }) (tsc: instanceId missing)
- eslint.config.js:40 — rules apply to ['src/**/*.ts', 'partykit/**/*.ts', 'scripts/**/*.ts'] only
- eslint.config.js:83-85 — .mjs block is only ...tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked
- eslint --print-config scripts/mobile_smoke.mjs — 0 enabled rules
- package.json:18 — lint lists 74 script files by hand

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The core claim holds: scripts/ is never type-checked, its .mjs files get zero lint rules, and the lint command names files by hand (2,606 characters, 74 named, 53 missing). Five corrections:
  - **Line numbers.** tsconfig include is line 22, not 24.
  - **Runtime effect.** The two drifts are type-only. live_construction_play_smoke passes at runtime because its fake's missing methods are never called. The safety probe still fails for the intended reason (Unknown object id), since the server does not validate instanceId.
  - **Error count.** Scripts produce about 45 tsc errors, not "two drifts plus TS7016":
    - 8 TS2307 from vitest `?query` imports
    - 4 TS5097 from `.ts` import extensions
    - about 20 implicit-any and shape errors in two test files
    - the scripts tsconfig also needs allowImportingTsExtensions, lib ES2021 or later, and a `declare module '*.mjs?*'`
  - **Stronger evidence to lead with.** scripts/smoke_editor_touch.mjs:62-70, 100, 106 and 112 call `updateEditorState`, which it never imports; it has been broken since PR #255. The file is already in the lint list, and no-undef would have caught it.
  - **Lint setup.** The .mjs rule block needs browser and Node globals, plus @eslint/js and globals as new devDependencies. A probe found 24 no-undef hits (12 of them this bug) and 4 unused vars, so the rollout is small.

### F490: Startup code grew 30 KB in a week with nothing to flag it until the budget breaks; the size check needs per-change attribution and more boundaries

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Load time, bundle and assets)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F024

**Summary.** Startup code went from 630.7 KB on Oct 14 to 660.7 KB now, with only 9 KB left before the 670 KB limit. The check prints one total, so nobody saw which changes added the weight. Most of the growth came from wallet features and a code reorganization. Printing what each change added, and blocking known-heavy modules from startup, would stop the creep earlier.

**Technical detail.**

I built 23 consecutive main commits (45d3b6f4 → a9dabba8) in a scratch copy and ran scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs on each. Oct 14 → Oct 18 was +11.9 KB in many small steps (630.7 → 642.6 per receipts). Oct 18 → 21 was +18.1 KB: assist mode #247 +2.2, keyboard/auth state #248-#250 +1.1, overworld composition refactor #252-#254 +4.1 (8 new composition/* files, 59 KB minified, about 9.3 KB br in-bundle against 6.5 KB removed from OverworldPlayScene), editor state #255 +0.7, map capture #261 +0.5, ownership refresh #264 +1.2, wallet recovery #267 +5.3, collection pricing and approvals #270-#272 +1.3, owner pricing #277 +1.5. The check (scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs:14) compares one total against 670 KB, and its only structural guards are the 18 deferred menus and room-data independence (:34-48). Fix: (1) commit a small baseline (per-chunk brotli plus module list from output/build/chunk-graph.json) and have size:check print the modules that entered boot and the chunks that grew versus the baseline, so every PR shows its cost. (2) Add a boot-forbidden list next to deferredControllers: src/mint/roomMetadataRender.ts, src/mint/roomWallet*, src/auth/wallet*, src/ui/setup/ownerCollectionReminder.ts, @tonaljs/chord-type, src/debug/*, src/main/resourceDebug.ts. (3) After the fixes in this review land, lower BUDGET_KB to about 610 so the headroom stays meaningful.

**Evidence.**

- scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs:14 — a single BUDGET_KB = 670 total
- scripts/check_bundle_budget.mjs:34 — the only structural guards: 18 deferred controllers and room-data independence
- docs/review/wamp-remaining-dialogs-2026-10-14.md:31 — 630.7 KB brotli across fifteen startup files on Oct 14
- Scratch builds: 45d3b6f4 642.6 KB, ba02037f 648.9, 254eea33 657.7, a9dabba8 659.2; current dist 660.7 KB across 18 files

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Startup JavaScript grew 30 KB in a week: 630.7 KB on Oct 14 to 660.7 KB now, with 9.3 KB left before the 670 KB limit. The check already prints the 8 largest files and the total. What it lacks is per-module or per-change attribution. Wallet and mint work explains about 9 KB of the growth (#267 alone moved startup from 15 to 18 files and added about 4.6-5.3 KB), and the overworld composition refactor about 4 KB. The rest came from many small features.
  
  Recommended fixes:
  1. Have the vite plugin record each module's rendered size, and have size:check print which modules entered startup compared with main's build in CI, plus a top-modules table. Avoid a committed baseline keyed on hashed chunk names, which would cause merge conflicts.
  2. Add a boot-forbidden list only as each heavy module is moved out of startup. Today every listed module is in startup (roomMetadataRender, wallet transaction/auth/recovery, ownerCollectionReminder, mobilePerformanceProfiler, resourceDebug, and chord-type in room-data). Keep the small startup watcher src/main/roomWalletRecovery.ts and its lifecycle allowed, and forbid only the heavy check and transaction modules.
  3. Ratchet BUDGET_KB down after those moves land.

### F488: Room Video swaps out the editor's save/load methods at runtime, hidden from readers and tests

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** medium
- **Related round-1 item:** F062

**Summary.** The YouTube room-video feature works by replacing some of the editor's own functions while the editor loads. One of them produces the room data that gets saved and published. Anyone reading or changing the editor, including an AI agent, can't see this from the editor files, and no test checks that a room's video survives a save. A routine refactor could silently delete builders' videos. Make the video an ordinary part of the editor's room data and add a save/load test.

**Technical detail.**

The patches:
- src/roomVideo/editing.ts:193-216 replaces EditorEditRuntime.prototype.reset, applyRoomSnapshot and exportRoomSnapshot. exportRoomSnapshot has 48 references in 9 files, including the draft save session (roomSession.ts, 7 refs) and both editor scenes.
- src/roomVideo/sceneHooks.ts:53-95 replaces EditorScene.prototype.update and create, and CourseEditorScene.prototype.update, create (twice) and renderUi.
- sceneHooks.ts:26-51 wraps CourseEditorScene's `scene.input.on`, so the video can swallow pointer events before the editor's handlers run. EditorScene instead calls roomVideoPointerDown directly (editor/interaction.ts:704), so the two editors use two different mechanisms.
- The hooks are installed from editorSceneLoader.ts:17.

frontend frames.ts:84-127 reads private scene state through `as unknown as` casts:
- EditorScene.editRuntime, `private readonly` at EditorScene.ts:173.
- OverworldPlayScene.mode and currentRoomCoordinates, private at :526 and :529.
- CourseEditorScene.musicModeActive, a private getter at :308.
Renaming any of these compiles cleanly; the video then silently stops syncing.

F062 built a typed, runtime-checked scene capability registry (src/ui/setup/sceneCapabilityRegistry.ts) for exactly this. Room Video (8a56f131, 2026-10-13) landed alongside it and bypasses it, as do the unchecked scene casts in ui/setup/roomInsights.ts:54 and bugReports/gameContext.ts:41.

Tests: only roomVideo/model.test.ts and access.test.ts exist. No test calls installRoomVideoEditing, so the editRuntime tests run against un-patched behavior.

Fix:
1. Store video in EditorEditRuntime itself (RoomSnapshot already has `video?` at persistence/roomModel.ts:140), so apply/export handle it natively.
2. Have each scene call a RoomVideoController from create/update, typed through the capability registry.
3. Delete sceneHooks.ts (96 lines) and the prototype block in editing.ts.
4. Add an apply-then-export round-trip test.
5. Add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule banning assignment to `*.prototype.*` in src/.

**Evidence.**

- src/roomVideo/editing.ts:193-216 — prototype.reset, applyRoomSnapshot and exportRoomSnapshot reassigned to wrappers
- src/roomVideo/sceneHooks.ts:53-57 — hookUpdate replaces sceneClass.prototype.update
- src/roomVideo/sceneHooks.ts:26-51 — wrapInput replaces scene.input.on to intercept pointerdown/move/up
- src/roomVideo/sceneHooks.ts:70-95 — course.prototype.create (x2), renderUi and editor.prototype.create replaced
- src/scenes/editorSceneLoader.ts:17 — roomVideo.installRoomVideoEditorHooks(editor.EditorScene, courseEditor.CourseEditorScene)
- src/roomVideo/frames.ts:84 — `scene as unknown as EditorVideoScene` reads editRuntime, roomId, musicModeActive
- src/scenes/EditorScene.ts:173 — `private readonly editRuntime: EditorEditRuntime`
- src/scenes/OverworldPlayScene.ts:526-529 — private mode and currentRoomCoordinates read by frames.ts:127
- src/ui/setup/roomInsights.ts:54 — getScene(key) as unknown as InsightScene, bypassing the capability registry
- src/persistence/roomModel.ts:140 — `video?: RoomVideo | null` already part of RoomSnapshot

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The risk is narrower than claimed. Renaming or removing the three patched EditorEditRuntime methods already fails typecheck, because editing.ts uses the typed prototype. A builder's video would be lost without warning only if:
  - a new snapshot-export path skips exportRoomSnapshot;
  - apply or export gains a parameter that the wrappers drop;
  - EditorEditRuntime is used before the editor loader installs the hooks.
  
  The private-field casts in frames.ts can silently stop the video from displaying or syncing, but they do not lose data.
  
  The fix plan needs three changes:
  - The prototype patching was a deliberate workaround for the F067 max-lines ratchet (commit 8a56f131). editRuntime.ts has only 6 lines of headroom (3281/3287), so keep the video logic in src/roomVideo and add only explicit call lines in reset, apply and export.
  - Use direct typed calls or accessors from the scenes rather than the UI capability registry, which only covers public methods the UI calls.
  - The ESLint ban must also catch aliased assignments like `const prototype = X.prototype; prototype.reset = ...`.
  
  Do the apply→export→reset round-trip test first. It is the cheapest and most valuable piece.

### F484: No test checks that the renderers draw the same room the same way; the abstract server renderer has no tests at all

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Gap review: Room-to-image renderers: several separate implementations drawing the same room)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** medium · **effort:** small

**Summary.** All the mismatches in this review (wrong background, missing custom tiles, wrong tree size, dropped sprites) slipped through because nothing compares the different drawing paths. The 838-line server renderer for Expanded Rooms and postcards is never run by any test. One test room that uses every feature, checked against each renderer, would catch future drift as soon as it happens.

**Technical detail.**

Current coverage:
- No *.test.ts imports src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts. routes.metadata.test.ts only asserts image URLs (lines 47-78).
- The Wamp-O-Gram preview route is untested; the only test touching wampOGram routes is school/restrictions.contract.test.ts.
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.test.ts (44-195) covers grassland, solid, custom-sprite and flip cases, but not 'none', custom tiles, displayScale/displayOffset, repeat:false or background-layer objects.
- mint/roomMetadataRender.test.ts checks the 'parity helpers', but only roomMetadataRender calls them.

The infrastructure is already there: roomImageRenderer.test.ts has createEnv with a fake ASSETS binding and a pixelAt helper (26-40), and the source art is in public/assets.

Plan (about 150 lines):
1. Add a fixture 'feature room' with:
   - background 'none'
   - one custom tile at gid 10000
   - one custom sprite
   - tree_pack_oak_05 on the background layer (scale 0.5, offset -48,73)
   - jimothy (NPC)
   - a desert variant
2. For the RGBA server renderer(s), assert sampled pixels:
   - the sky pixel is near #050505 for 'none'
   - the custom tile's pixel colors appear
   - the tree's bounding box equals getRoomMetadataObjectDrawRect scaled to 27 px per tile
3. For the two canvas renderers, run with a recording mock 2D context and assert the drawImage destination rects equal the same helper.

This turns 'parity' from a comment into a guard. Once the shared geometry module exists (later finding), most assertions become one-liners.

**Evidence.**

- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.test.ts:26-40 — existing fake ASSETS env and pixelAt helper to build on
- src/pages/roomImageRenderer.test.ts:71-90 — background tests cover solid/custom/grassland, not 'none'
- src/cloudflare/worker/share/routes.metadata.test.ts:58-62 — only checks the image URL path and query, never pixels
- src/mint/roomMetadataRender.test.ts:8 — 'room metadata renderer parity helpers' tested in isolation

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The coverage gap is real. No test renders with src/cloudflare/worker/share/roomPreviewImage.ts or runs the Wamp-O-Gram preview.png route; routes.metadata.test.ts only loads the module indirectly. Pages renderer tests miss 'none', custom tiles, displayScale/offset and background-layer objects.
  
  Two parts of the plan need changing:
  (a) The worker renderer deliberately draws placeholder shapes. It skips background-layer objects and ignores displayScale/displayOffset, so exact tree-rect parity can only be asserted for the Pages renderer and the two canvas renderers (mint/roomMetadataRender.ts and visuals/roomSnapshotTexture.ts). For the worker renderer, assert background colour, custom-tile pixel colours and that background-layer decor appears.
  (b) Several assertions fail today: Pages renders 'none' as grassland and has no custom tiles or display scale; the worker renders 'none' as #070b16 with stars and drops background-layer objects. Ship the fixture test together with those fixes, or with it.fails/todo markers, not as a standalone green guard.
  
  Mock-context tests to extend already exist in roomMetadataRender.retry.test.ts:10-16 and roomSnapshotTexture.rows.test.ts:36-51.

### F491: `npm run check` and CI run different checks, and check type-checks the project twice

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** defect · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F061

**Summary.** Agents and the deploy script treat `npm run check` as 'the same checks CI runs', but the two lists differ. CI also runs the Worker safety probes, while check also verifies the audio files, which CI never checks. On top of that, check runs the full TypeScript compile twice, wasting about 20 seconds per run and up to a minute on a cold machine. Make CI run `npm run check` itself, and drop the duplicate compile.

**Technical detail.**

package.json:8 defines check as: styles, lint, test, typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`, :7), dom-contract, world-tiles types, build, size, png, trees and audio. But build (package.json:27) is `tsc && vite build && ...`, which repeats the same no-emit compile.

Measured locally: tsc 64 s cold and 19 s warm ('Check time 13.74s'), lint 42 s, vitest 44 s, styles 1 s, DOM contract 0.4 s. In CI's quality job (276 s total): lint 51 s, test 99 s, typecheck 22 s, build 44 s, png check 19 s.

The drift:
- quality.yml:18-31 runs smoke:worker-safety (:31) and the world-tile asset contract (:28-29), but not assets:audio:check (no 'audio' anywhere in quality.yml). A PR that swaps an audio file without updating src/music/audioAssetManifest.json passes CI, even though the check is a pure hash compare (scripts/build_audio_assets.mjs:15-22, no ffmpeg needed).
- `check` lacks smoke:worker-safety (package.json:64, a 386-line probe of CORS, room snapshot validation and Room Rush), yet scripts/deploy_prod.mjs:46-48 says it runs 'the same checks here'.

Fix:
1. Make build `vite build && node scripts/build_pages_worker.mjs`, keeping tsc only in typecheck.
2. Turn scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts into a vitest file under src/cloudflare/worker/ (it already uses node:assert), so `npm test` covers it.
3. Replace quality.yml's step list with `npm run check`, plus the network-only asset-contract step.

**Evidence.**

- package.json:7 — "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
- package.json:8 — check runs typecheck and then build, and includes assets:audio:check but not smoke:worker-safety
- package.json:27 — "build": "tsc && vite build && node scripts/build_pages_worker.mjs"
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:18-31 — CI step list includes smoke:worker-safety (:31), no audio check
- scripts/build_audio_assets.mjs:15-22 — --check only compares SHA-256 hashes against the manifest
- scripts/deploy_prod.mjs:46-48 — 'CI may still be running ... so run the same checks here'
- local timings — tsc 64 s cold / 19 s warm, lint 42 s, vitest 44 s; CI quality job 276 s

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Keep `tsc` in `build`. It is the only type gate for the Cloudflare Pages auto-build of main (`npm ci && npm run build`), deploy_prod --skip-check, deploy_safety_branch and the service smokes. Remove the redundant `npm run typecheck` step from `check` and from quality.yml instead. That saves about 15-20 s per local check (CI shows 15 s for typecheck). It does not shorten CI overall, because the quality job (207 s) is far shorter than mint-network (752 s) and mobile-smoke (714 s).
  
  To close the drift with the least churn:
  - Add `npm run assets:audio:check` to quality.yml (a hash compare of files tracked in git, about 1 s).
  - Add `npm run smoke:worker-safety` to `check` (about 1 s), or move it into a vitest file and update the entry in knip.json:114.
  - Make the deploy_prod.mjs:46 comment and frontend-redeploy-and-minting.md:11 match what `check` actually runs.
  
  Replacing CI's step list with a single `npm run check` is optional and loses per-step visibility. Severity is low: a worker-safety regression is still caught by CI on PR and main, and a mismatched audio asset is caught at the next deploy_prod.

### F493: Docs agents read first are stale or huge: presence still 'PartyKit', checklist title at line 67, logs 6x

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small
- **Related round-1 item:** F061

**Summary.** The README and architecture notes still say live multiplayer runs on PartyKit, but it now runs inside the game's own Cloudflare Worker. The master checklist opens with 66 lines of dated status updates before its title, and its 'Progress' line says 172 done while 175 items are ticked. The two running logs, progress.md and feature-ledger.md, have grown about sixfold since October 3, to 586 KB and 352 KB, which is too big to read in one pass. Move the status updates into their own log, check the progress number automatically, and fix the presence docs.

**Technical detail.**

Presence docs:
- README.md:11 says 'PartyKit for realtime presence'.
- docs/development/architecture.md:3 and :29-30 describe PartyKit hosting and PartyKit validating the signing secret.
- In production, presence is PresenceDurableObject: bound in wrangler.jsonc:7, exported from src/cloudflare/worker.ts:3, with the adapter src/cloudflare/presence/durableObject.ts wrapping partykit/presenceServer.ts.

The checklist, docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md (518 lines, 154 KB):
- The H1 is at line 67, after 52 dated '**October…' status paragraphs.
- Line 95 says 'Progress: 172 of 216 done.', but 175 items are `- [x]` and the status paragraphs say 'master175/216'.
- Line 120 asks agents to update the count by hand.

Logs:
- progress.md: 86,698 B on 2026-10-03, now 585,768 B (2,594 lines). It is ignored at .gitignore:15 yet still tracked.
- feature-ledger.md: 58,725 B, now 351,945 B.
- docs/review holds 133 files (2.1 MB); the details file alone is 1.03 MB.

Competing 'current' plans: docs/README.md:26 links performance-code-health-roadmap.md, which calls itself 'the canonical implementation tracker' (line 3), and docs/development/refactor-plan-2026-08-13.md:3 says 'This is the current implementation plan'.

The stray tracked .cursor/debug-843bc4.log, noted in the F061 fact-check, is still there.

Fix:
1. Move the status paragraphs to docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10-log.md, leaving the checklist header as title, how-to and progress.
2. Add a vitest that counts `- [x]` lines and fails if the Progress line disagrees.
3. Label the June-August plans 'Historical' in docs/README.md.
4. Update the README and architecture presence sections (Durable Object in the API Worker; `dev:presence` still uses partykit dev).
5. Rotate progress.md and feature-ledger.md monthly into docs/history/, keeping the current file at 20 KB or less.
This doesn't touch the AGENTS.md question Jonathan declined.

**Evidence.**

- README.md:11 — '- PartyKit for realtime presence'
- docs/development/architecture.md:29-30 — 'partykit/presenceServer.ts handles realtime ... PartyKit validates the shared signing secret'
- wrangler.jsonc:7 — durable_objects PRESENCE_ROOMS -> PresenceDurableObject
- src/cloudflare/worker.ts:3 — export { PresenceDurableObject } from './presence/durableObject'
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md:67 — '# WAMP Checkup (October 2026)' after 66 lines of status paragraphs
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md:95 — '**Progress: 172 of 216 done.**' (175 items ticked)
- docs/review/wamp-checkup-2026-10.md:120 — instructs agents to update the progress count by hand
- docs/performance-code-health-roadmap.md:3 — 'This is the canonical implementation tracker for the June 10 and July 13 audits'
- docs/development/refactor-plan-2026-08-13.md:3 — 'This is the current implementation plan'
- .gitignore:15 — progress.md ignored but tracked; wc -c progress.md = 585,768

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Most claims hold, with these corrections:
  - Only 33 dated status paragraphs (66 lines) sit above the H1. The other 19 are between the H1 and "How to use", so the move should take all 52. The H1 moves down two lines with nearly every checklist commit: line 1 on Oct 17, line 67 at 2d540764, line 71 on latest main 80151ad1.
  - The 172-vs-175 Progress mismatch is already fixed on 80151ad1, where the line says 182 and 182 items are ticked. Git history still shows the count disagreeing with the ticks in about half of the last 40 checklist commits, so the vitest guard remains justified.
  - docs/review has 136 files totaling 2.96 MB, not 133 files and 2.1 MB.
  - The log growth baseline is 78.5 KB (progress.md) and 56.7 KB (feature-ledger.md) at 7371df9a, or 95 KB and 61 KB by the end of Oct 3. Growth is about 6-7x and 6x. progress.md is newest-first, which blunts the "too big to read in one pass" point.
  - The "competing current plans" claim is overstated. The roadmap is canonical only for the June/July audits, and the August refactor plan is scoped to one proposal and not linked from docs/README.md. Labelling them historical is optional tidying.
  - The log rotation to docs/history, the ignored-but-tracked progress.md and the .cursor debug log were already proposed in F061, which Jonathan declined. Treat those parts as optional, or ask him first.
  - The new, worthwhile parts are:
    - fixing the stale presence lines in README.md:11 and docs/development/architecture.md:3,29-30 (presence is PresenceDurableObject in the API Worker on api.wamp.land; dev:presence and presence:deploy:safety still use the partykit CLI);
    - moving the status paragraphs out of the checklist;

### F492: Database test fakes are copy-pasted 21 times, with 12 hand-typed copies of the rooms table

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** medium

**Summary.** Server tests need a stand-in for Cloudflare's D1 database. A good shared helper exists that builds the real schema from the migrations, but 20 other test files each carry their own fake, about 825 lines in total. 17 files also type out their own table definitions; the rooms table alone is retyped 12 times, each with only 2 to 11 of its real 33 columns. When the schema changes, these tests can keep passing against tables that no longer match production. Make the shared helper the standard and move the copies onto it.

**Technical detail.**

Copies: 20 `implements D1PreparedStatement` and 12 `implements D1Database` classes across 20 src test files, plus MockStatement/MockD1Database in scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts (166 lines). Brace-matching measures 825 lines in 21 files.

Schemas: 41 CREATE TABLE statements in 17 test files. Compared with the schema produced by applying all 71 migrations:
- The rooms copies have 2-11 of 33 columns; admin/roomClear.test.ts has 2.
- users copies have 1-3 of 10 columns.
- runs/leaderboards.test.ts has room_runs with 11 of 24 columns.
- mint/roomMetadataCacheCli.test.ts:20 adds a `title` column that production's rooms table doesn't have.

The right pattern already exists: activity/testDatabase.ts:7-32 (Statement/Database over node:sqlite), and the fixture() that follows applies every migrations/*.sql, which takes 59 ms per fresh database. runs/discoveryTestDatabase.ts and collections/testDatabase.ts already reuse it. Six files re-implement that migrations loop instead (for example guestRuns/progress.test.ts:51-56).

Fix:
1. Move Statement/Database and `createMigratedD1({ skip?: string[] })` to src/cloudflare/worker/testing/sqliteD1.ts.
2. Replace the 20 copies; keep a hand schema only where a test deliberately exercises a pre-migration state (the *Migration.test.ts files).
3. To keep speed, cache the concatenated migration SQL per worker.
Net: about 700 fewer lines, and schema drift becomes a test failure instead of a silent pass.

**Evidence.**

- src/cloudflare/worker/activity/testDatabase.ts:7-32 — shared Statement/Database over node:sqlite; fixture() applies every migrations/*.sql
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/progress.test.ts:22-38 — another private Statement and Database class
- src/cloudflare/worker/guestRuns/progress.test.ts:51-56 — re-implements the migrations loop in beforeEach
- src/mint/roomMetadataCacheCli.test.ts:20 — hand-typed rooms table with a `title` column production lacks
- scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts:24-28 — MockStatement/MockD1Database, a 21st copy
- schema comparison script — rooms hand-typed 12x with 2-11 of 33 real columns; 41 CREATE TABLE in 17 test files

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Narrow the claim to about 20 test files that run a real node:sqlite database. These are the 11 `implements` copies plus about 9 object-literal fakes such as roomClear, lostSongs/routes, expandedRooms/leaderboards, publishedGoalIssuesSql, bugReports, guestReplay, routes.limits and pruneExpired. Exclude the 9 canned or recording mocks (worldTiles/service, routes and store; roomComments/routes; t14ContractTestSupport; auth/store; music/store; gameJams; scripts/worker_safety_probes.ts). They intentionally script results or assert SQL shape, so a migrated database cannot replace them.
  
  The shared createMigratedD1() must support:
  - opt-in hooks: failAt/loseReply/beforeBatch, round-trip counting, and query/binding recording
  - meta.changes on run and batch results
  - D1's 100-bound-parameter limit
  - a blank variant with no seed rows
  
  Then migrate the files that hand-type a base schema and apply a single migration on top: worlds/access, worldTiles/reconciliation, worldTiles/health, worldTileRenderer/stateMachine, customSprites/catalogStore, lostSongs, maintenance/pruneExpired, guestReplay and roomClear. Keep hand schemas in the 4 *Migration tests, in ops.test (d1_migrations), and in the mint CLI test, where the `title` column is a harmless sentinel that the CLI never queries.
  
  Expect about 250-300 fewer lines, not about 700. The schema-drift benefit is preventive: no test passes falsely today.
  
  The migrations loop in guestRuns/progress.test.ts is at :89-94, not :51-56.

### F496: Streaming tests skip the constructor, so the game code carries test-only workarounds

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** 59 test setups build the streaming controller without running its constructor and then patch in the pieces they need. To survive that, the real game code has about a dozen 'in case this is missing' checks on fields that always exist, including one branch that exists only for an old test helper. Building the controller normally in tests would let those checks go, and the tests would then catch real wiring mistakes.

**Technical detail.**

The harness: createWorldStreamingHarness (worldStreaming.testHarness.ts:12-48) uses Object.create(prototype). It, or direct Object.create, appears 59 times across 9 test files (lifecycle 21, transitionHydration 10, dormantLifecycle 9, preparation 9, dynamicOverlayFallback 5, and others).

Production guards that exist only for partial objects:
- this.performanceAdvisorExactSnapshotRequestsByRoomId ??= new Map() (worldStreaming.ts:1489), plus ?. on the same always-initialised map (1531, 1546, 1951)
- pendingFullRoomPreparationsById?. (1949)
- playableRoomSnapshot*ById?.delete (3587-3589)
- fullRoomReleaseAtById?. (4320)
- getResolvedPerformancePolicy computes a 'legacyHarnessProfile' with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(this, 'getEffectivePerformanceProfile') on every call. It also uses this.options.getMode?.(), this.localPlayPressure?.profile and frameWorkCoordinator.hasQueuedWorkAtPriority?.() (3203-3222).

These hide real failures: a genuinely missing map or option silently does nothing in production.

Fix:
1. Add a createTestWorldStreamingController(overrides) factory that calls the real constructor with fake scene, repository and callbacks. The constructor already takes everything through options.
2. Migrate the 9 files.
3. Delete the guards and the hasOwnProperty branch.

**Evidence.**

- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.testHarness.ts:12-14 — Object.create(OverworldWorldStreamingController.prototype)
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1489 — ??= on an always-initialised field
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1949-1951 — optional chaining on always-present maps
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3205-3216 — legacyHarnessProfile hasOwnProperty hack in production
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3587-3589 — ?.delete on always-present maps

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The guards are dead code in production, not code that hides real failures. The required options are enforced by TypeScript and every guarded map is a class-field initialiser, so the "silently does nothing in production" path cannot happen. The setups span 8 test files (59 setups), plus commentReadiness.test.ts, which calls prototype methods directly. The proportionate fix is small, and covers all the guards including the `?.` on hasQueuedWorkAtPriority:
  - have createWorldStreamingHarness pre-initialise the always-present fields and a default FrameWorkCoordinator;
  - give the partial test options the two required callbacks;
  - switch the three lifecycle tests at lines 150, 738 and 918 from the getEffectivePerformanceProfile own-property override to options.getPerformanceProfile;
  - then delete the guards and the hasOwnProperty branch.
  Moving all 59 setups onto the real constructor is optional. It would need Phaser and repository fakes, and would not stop tests from swapping private collaborators for partial mocks.

### F495: Split the 5,357-line streaming file into four modules and lower its line limit

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Gap review: World streaming client: the largest file in the repo, never reviewed)
- **Type:** cleanup · **impact:** low · **effort:** large

**Summary.** worldStreaming.ts is still the largest file in the game and mixes five separate jobs. Its lint line limit was never lowered after the presenter was split out, so it can grow by almost 800 more lines without anyone noticing. Lower the limit to today's size, then move the four largest self-contained parts into their own files.

**Technical detail.**

Ratchet: eslint.config.js:8 allows 5,765 non-blank lines. The file now has 4,972 (5,357 total, 385 blank), so it has 793 lines of silent headroom since #254.

Self-contained clusters, by line range:
1. Startup and dynamic-overlay orchestration, about 650 lines: refreshAround 758-1052, plus loadDistantPreviewsProgressively, mergeDeferredDynamicOverlays, scheduleDynamicOverlayRetry and requestFullPreviewUpgradeIfNeeded at 2797-3150. Move to worldStreamingStartup.ts.
2. Transition snapshot requests, performance-advisor exact-snapshot events, summary recovery and portal ownership, about 520 lines: 1321-1840. Move to transitionSnapshotRequests.ts.
3. Predicted-destination intent, about 180 lines: 3486-3623 plus clearPredictedPlayableRoomForTransition at 1698-1731. Move to predictedDestination.ts as pure functions. That makes the misprediction above unit-testable without the Object.create harness.
4. The full-room preparation pipeline, about 1,000 lines: 3625-4632, beginFullRoomPreparation through rollback and cancel. Move to fullRoomPreparationPipeline.ts.
5. The teardown pipeline, about 520 lines: 4732-5180 plus destroyFullRoom at 5251-5315. Move to fullRoomTeardownPipeline.ts.

Items 4 and 5 can share the state maps through a small 'stream state' object passed to each module. What remains is a coordinator of about 1,500 lines, under the default MAX_LINES (eslint.config.js:5).

Order: tighten the ratchet now (one-line change), then extract 3, 2, 5 and 4 in that order, smallest risk first, ratcheting down after each.

**Evidence.**

- eslint.config.js:8 — 'src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts': 5765 (skipBlankLines)
- eslint.config.js:5 — MAX_LINES = 1500
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:758 — refreshAround starts the startup cluster
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:1321 — transition snapshot request cluster begins
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3486 — predicted-destination helpers begin
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:3625 — preparation pipeline begins
- src/scenes/overworld/worldStreaming.ts:4732 — teardown pipeline begins

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** Ratchet: the problem covers several files, not only this one. Re-pin every stale OVERSIZED_FILE_LINES entry (OverworldPlayScene 6355→5128 has 1,227 lines of headroom; worldStreaming 5765→4972; difficulty.ts, CourseEditorScene, EditorScene and rooms/store.ts are also stale). Add a lint-config check that fails when a pin is more than a small margin above the file's real non-blank count, so the next split cannot leave headroom again. This part is small effort.
  Split: the proposed extractions would leave about 2,287 non-blank lines, not about 1,500, so the file would still need a pin. The list has five clusters, not four, and clusters 2 and 3 overlap at 1698-1731. Only estimateTimeToSeamMs and the hysteresis check, about 60 lines, can become pure functions. Preparation and teardown are coupled in both directions and share predicted-intent, artifact-cache and presenter state, so they would need a real shared-state interface or a single scheduler module, not a small state object. refreshAround is the main refresh entry, not startup-only, and belongs in the coordinator. The ~6,000 lines of Object.create-harness tests that reach private members would also need rewriting. Realistic scope: extract the pure seam-ETA helper and the teardown pipeline first, and ratchet the pin down after each step.

### F494: Each push runs 18 CI jobs that each reinstall browsers and rebuild the game: 106 runner-min, 12.6 min wait

- **Area:** Code health, tests and tooling (reviewer: Code health, tests and tooling for AI agents)
- **Type:** improvement · **impact:** low · **effort:** small

**Summary.** The Quality workflow has 16 near-identical browser-check jobs, and every one of them installs dependencies and Playwright and then builds the whole game again. On the latest main push, about 27 of the 106 runner-minutes went to repeating that setup, and the two slowest jobs made everyone wait 12.6 minutes for a result. Build once and share the build, cache the browsers, split the two slowest jobs, and cancel runs that a newer push has replaced.

**Technical detail.**

quality.yml is 326 lines. The jobs at :33, :53, :72, :91, :110, :129, :148, :167, :189 (matrix x4), :215, :234, :256, :282 and :306 each repeat checkout, setup-node, `npm ci` and `npx playwright install --with-deps` (14 copies). `npm run smoke:mobile:ci` is invoked 17 times, only 3 of them with --skip-build. mobile_smoke_ci.mjs:19-25 runs a full `vite build` unless --skip-build, so each push makes 17 smoke builds plus the quality job's own build.

Timings from run 39664022786 (main, 2026-10-21 19:42:49 to 19:55:26Z):
- 18 jobs, 6,369 job-seconds.
- Playwright install: 36-59 s per job, about 774 s total.
- npm ci: 13-25 s per job, about 366 s total.
- Each vite build is at most about 30 s; map-capture's whole smoke:mobile:ci step took 39 s.
- Repeated setup and builds come to roughly 27 min.

Wall time is set by two jobs:
- mint-network, 754 s: three sequential smoke:mobile:ci calls of 50, 357 and 208 s.
- mobile-smoke, 717 s: chromium and then webkit, 638 s.

There is no `concurrency:` key, so outdated PR runs keep going; 8 of the last 60 runs were cancelled by hand. Runners also warn that actions/checkout@v4 and setup-node@v4 run on deprecated Node 20.

Fix:
1. Add a `build-smoke` job that builds once and uploads dist-mobile-smoke as an artifact.
2. Replace the 16 jobs with one `smoke` job whose `strategy.matrix.suite` comes from a single list (see the smoke-registry finding). It downloads the artifact and runs with --skip-build.
3. Cache ~/.cache/ms-playwright keyed on the Playwright version.
4. Split mobile-smoke by engine, and mint-network into its three steps.
5. Add `concurrency: {group: quality-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}}`.

Expected result: about 27 runner-min saved per push, and wall time of about 7-8 min (the next-longest job, keyboard-controls, takes 433 s). The workflow file shrinks by about 200 lines.

**Evidence.**

- .github/workflows/quality.yml:33-52 — mobile-smoke job: checkout, setup-node, npm ci, playwright install (:44), smoke:mobile:ci (:45); same block repeated at :53, :72, :91, :110, :129, :148, :167, :189, :215, :234, :256, :282, :306
- scripts/mobile_smoke_ci.mjs:19-25 — vite build into dist-mobile-smoke unless --skip-build
- gh run 39664022786 jobs — 18 jobs, 6,369 job-seconds; mint-network 754 s, mobile-smoke 717 s (smoke step 638 s), Playwright install 36-59 s per job
- grep -c 'npx playwright install' quality.yml = 14; smoke:mobile:ci = 17; skip-build = 3
- .github/workflows/quality.yml:1-6 — no concurrency group
- gh run list (60 runs) — 44 success, 8 failure, 8 cancelled

**Fact-check.**

- **partially confirmed.** The workflow is duplicated as described, but the fix saves about 0-3 runner-minutes per push, not 27. That doesn't matter much anyway: the repo is public, so runner minutes are free. The only real gain is wall time.
  
  Dropped:
  - Build-once with a shared artifact. The smoke build takes about 16 s, and a needs: build-smoke edge adds about 45-60 s to the critical path.
  - Caching ~/.cache/ms-playwright. Browser downloads take about 7 s per job; the 33-40 s apt `--with-deps` phase stays.
  
  Do instead:
  1. Add `concurrency: {group: quality-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}}`.
  2. Split mint-network into its ownership and artwork steps and mobile-smoke by `--engine`, each job doing its own 16 s build.
  3. Bump actions/checkout and setup-node past the Node 20 versions.
  4. Optionally, turn the 14 job definitions into one matrix list (`fail-fast: false`, per-suite service step, timeout and artifact path).
  
  Expected wall time is about 8.5 min, down from 12.6, because collection-costs at 509 s becomes the longest job; keyboard-controls at 433 s is not. Keep the total job count at 20 or under to avoid GitHub Free's concurrent-job limit.
